search_summary.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

course_info.title: People, Propaganda and Profit: Understanding Media in China (Online)
course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: Definitely don't pick this if you're not from the mainland. A lot of your grade depends on class participation, but you won't really have much to say if you've never been exposed to China media in your life. Also cause a lot of it is class participation, you also need to be good at public speaking.
reviews.translated_content: Definitely don't pick this if you're not from the mainland. A lot of your grade depends on class participation, but you won't really have much to say if you've never been exposed to China media in your life. Also cause a lot of it is class participation, you also need to be good at public speaking.

reviews.content: 老师讲课很有意思，任务比较轻松，期中有一个project设计分析报纸，给分很好，但是tutorial上要准备主题发言而且平时也要积极表达，占比很高，tutorial特别重要
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer’s classes are very interesting, and the tasks are relatively light. There was a mid-term project involving the design and analysis of newspapers, and the grading was good. However, you need to prepare thematic speeches for tutorials and participate actively in regular discussions; these count for a high proportion of the grade, so tutorials are especially important.

reviews.content: tutor不好，她给分看起来是乱来的。workload不大，但不合理不公平。
reviews.translated_content: The tutor is not good; her grading seems arbitrary. The workload isn’t heavy, but it’s unreasonable and unfair.

reviews.content: 两份essay（一份midterm一份final）给分还好但instructions不太明确， 一个group presentation（groupmate和topic在tutorial里面抽签）
reviews.translated_content: There are two essays (one for midterm, one for final). Grading is okay, but the instructions aren’t very clear. There is also one group presentation (groupmates and topics are drawn by lot in the tutorial).

reviews.content: lecture线上好摸鱼，tutorial占比差不多一半，平时要积极发言，final essay一篇，midterm project设计报纸加report说明，还有一个pre，wl一般给分fair
reviews.translated_content: It’s easy to slack off during the online lectures. Tutorials account for nearly half of the grade, so you need to participate actively. There is one final essay, a midterm project involving newspaper design plus an explanatory report, and a presentation. The workload is average, and the grading is fair.

reviews.content: wl中等不算特别少但是很有意思，是能让人产生一些观念和对世界的理解方式上的改变。tutorial的参与度很重要，积极发言很能拉好感。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is moderate, not particularly light, but it’s very interesting. It can change your perspectives and understanding of the world. Participation in tutorials is important; speaking up actively really helps make a good impression.

reviews.content: 轻松好grade，上课内容也不算枯燥，online上课很舒服
reviews.translated_content: Relaxed and easy to get a good grade. The class content is not boring either, and online classes are comfortable.

reviews.content: 挺有意思的，整体压力不大，做project写essay为主
reviews.translated_content: Quite interesting. The overall pressure is not high, and the assessment is mainly based on projects and essays.

reviews.content: 好龟CC 只要认真准备presentation和mid project final essay基本能无痛Ａ减 教授人超nice可爱
reviews.translated_content: GPA-friendly Common Core course. As long as you prepare seriously for the presentation, mid-term project, and final essay, you can basically get an A- without much pain. The professor is super nice and cute.

reviews.content: workload比较低，A range 好拿，tutorial就是讨论和轮流prez
reviews.translated_content: The workload is relatively low, and an A-range grade is easy to obtain. Tutorials consist of discussions and rotating presentations.

search_summary.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

course_info.title: Curing the Chinese: Medicine and Society in Modern China (Online)
course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: 内容总体上是历史学+社会学 如果是历史爱好者感觉没必要这里头历史含量实在不高感觉没有中国古代史有意思 网课基本一直挂机tut要说点话因为有participation计分 因为本人文科脑袋essay写的很顺手 个人在这门课的wl不大比较轻松 没有去抢发言最后是B+ 最后强调不要用ai写作！！！
reviews.translated_content: The content is basically history plus sociology. If you are a history enthusiast, you might feel it’s unnecessary because the historical content is actually not that high; I don’t think it’s as interesting as ancient Chinese history. For the online classes, I mostly just kept the window open. In tutorials, you have to speak up because participation is graded. As someone with a humanities background, I found writing essays quite easy. My personal workload in this course was low and relatively relaxed. I didn’t fight for speaking turns and ended up with a B+. Finally, I emphasize: do not use AI for writing!!!

reviews.content: workload稍稍有点大，写Essay真是抓破脑袋，但是课程内容很有趣，关于历史，最后给分也不错，A
reviews.translated_content: The workload is slightly heavy; writing the essay was really head-scratching. But the course content is interesting, focusing on history, and the grading was also good: an A.

reviews.content: 上zoom课很无聊，基本上都没在听。attendance 计1分，打字没有分，说话才有加分。还有就是不要用AI写作，有人被教授骂了。
reviews.translated_content: Attending Zoom classes is very boring; basically, I didn’t listen at all. Attendance counts for 1 mark; typing gets no marks, only speaking earns extra points. Also, do not use AI for writing; someone was scolded by the professor for it.

reviews.content: 上zoom lecture和tutorial回答问题会加participation，两个field trip都是A range但最后还是只拿了B+ 应该是被final paper拖低了。整体workload适中吧
reviews.translated_content: Answering questions during Zoom lectures and tutorials boosts your participation grade. Both field trips were graded in the A range, but I still only got a B+ overall; my final paper probably dragged my grade down. The workload was moderate.

reviews.content: 讲中医跟西医在华史，挺有趣的。reading不少，但不用看。wl还行，essay抓不着门道，但还是混了个A-。
reviews.translated_content: It covers traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine in modern Chinese history, which is quite interesting. There’s quite a bit of reading, but you don’t need to read it. The workload is fine; I couldn’t quite figure out the essay requirements, but still managed to scrape an A-.

search_summary.title: Dunhuang and the Silk Road: Art, Culture and Trade (Online)

course_info.title: Dunhuang and the Silk Road: Art, Culture and Trade (Online)

reviews.content: workload大。有两个essay，分别1000words和3000words。虽然是online但还是每周有lecture和tutorial，每周tutorial前有作业要做完讨论。有个midterm quiz，这个是开卷的难度低。最后还有final group presentation，不能与essay选的topic相同。
reviews.translated_content: Heavy workload. There are two essays, 1000 words and 3000 words respectively. Although it’s online, there are lectures and tutorials every week, and you must complete assignments before each weekly tutorial for discussion. There’s a midterm quiz, which is open-book and low difficulty. Finally, there’s a final group presentation, and the topic cannot be the same as the one chosen for the essays.

reviews.content: 没听过课很少去tutorial的线上cc，但是和敦煌有关的内容还是很有趣，教授和tutor的英文似乎都不太好，但是人超nice，wl个人认为很小：一篇论文（分两part提交）一个quiz（线上quiz你懂的）一个gp pre，哪怕参与分占比很高（）最后也A-～
reviews.translated_content: I rarely attended lectures or tutorials for this online Common Core course, but the content related to Dunhuang was quite interesting. The professor and tutor’s English didn’t seem very good, but they were super nice. In my opinion, the workload was very light: one paper (submitted in two parts), one quiz (you know how online quizzes go), and one group project presentation. Even though participation marks carried a high weight, I still ended up with an A-.

reviews.content: 整个课，prof，tutor都很chill，给人一种非常佛系的感觉，但是essay有3000字，写的有点崩溃。不过跟着prof和tutor走，多拿bonus，好好做gp，写essay就问题不大
reviews.translated_content: The whole course, including the professor and tutor, is very chill, giving a very laid-back vibe. However, the essay is 3,000 words long, which was a bit overwhelming. That said, if you follow the professor and tutor, earn bonus marks, and put effort into the group project, the essay shouldn’t be a big problem.

reviews.content: workload不算大 而且有很多加bonus的机会 教授和tutor人都很好 期中的quiz好好复习（会有review ppt）essay好好写就能好龟
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy, and there are many opportunities for bonus marks. The professor and tutor are very nice people. If you revise properly for the midterm quiz (there will be review slides) and write the essay well, you can get a good grade.

search_summary.requirement: You may add up to two fully online Common Core (CC) courses. And your enrollment must comply with the requirements of CC and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

course_info.title: Mothering China: From the Womb to the Nation (Online)
course_info.requirement: You may add up to two fully online Common Core (CC) courses. And your enrollment must comply with the requirements of CC and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: I didnt answer any questions in the lecture. Just prepare for the tutorials and speak twice every tutorial. For the podcast, MUST cosnult carol frequently. Got A+ at last.
reviews.translated_content: I didnt answer any questions in the lecture. Just prepare for the tutorials and speak twice every tutorial. For the podcast, MUST cosnult carol frequently. Got A+ at last.

reviews.content: 卷人多，碰到free rider煞笔队友哪怕前期tut reading都读上课都发言也没用，最后B+烂了。虽然lecturer和tutor都很好，如果要冲分一定要找好靠谱队友准备好所有pre和最后播客
reviews.translated_content: There are many highly competitive students. If you get stuck with free-riding teammates, it doesn’t help even if you did the tutorial readings and participated in class early on; I ended up with a disappointing B+. Although the lecturer and tutor are both nice, if you want a high grade, you must find reliable teammates and prepare thoroughly for all presentations and the final podcast.

reviews.content: Its vey boring, I wont suggest to take it unless ur very intersted in gender studies. Youll need to participate for no reason just to get grades and tell generic lies. You dont even get to interact with your group that much and the end just to grind a day before submission.
reviews.translated_content: It’s very boring. I wouldn’t suggest taking it unless you’re very interested in gender studies. You’ll need to participate for no reason just to get grades and tell generic lies. You don’t even get to interact with your group that much, and in the end, you just have to grind a day before submission.

reviews.content: 精心设计的课程，深入浅出，案例和素材的选择都非常好，很有趣味性和启发性。老师认真耐心，总是给学生很多鼓励支持和帮助。但由于是online cc，和groupmate的沟通更困难，也更容易组到free rider
reviews.translated_content: A carefully designed course that explains complex ideas simply. The choice of cases and materials is excellent, making it very interesting and inspiring. The teacher is serious and patient, always giving students much encouragement, support, and help. However, since it is an online Common Core course, communication with group mates is more difficult, and it is easier to end up with free riders.

reviews.content: wl我觉得很小，说是三个pre但其实都完全based on gp content所以念稿子就好，每个pre你花十分钟准备就行。tutor和prof都不错的，这学期意外遇到了很靠谱的队友，幸福。这门课就是很吃队友，队友好的话可以过得非常开心轻松。
reviews.translated_content: I think the workload is very small. Although there are three presentations, they are entirely based on the group project content, so you can just read from a script. Ten minutes of preparation per presentation is enough. Both the tutor and professor are nice. This semester I unexpectedly met reliable teammates, which was a blessing. This course really depends on your teammates; if they are good, you can have a very happy and relaxed time.

reviews.content: 课程前面一段时间wl比较小，后期一个月wl很大，每个星期都要做pre，我是在找到的队友都很靠谱的情况下，依然觉得后期的wl挺大的，但是上课内容还算有趣。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is relatively small in the early part of the course, but becomes very heavy in the last month. You have to do a presentation every week. Even though I found reliable teammates, I still felt the workload in the later stage was quite heavy, but the class content was fairly interesting.

reviews.content: Same as CCCH9054
reviews.translated_content: Same as CCCH9054

reviews.content: 遇到了特别划水的组友，但是老师和tutor都很supportive，老师不仅教我怎么写论文还专门安慰了我，特别有人文关怀，最后也给我了bonus grade
reviews.translated_content: I encountered groupmates who slacked off terribly, but both the teacher and tutor were very supportive. The teacher not only taught me how to write the essay but also specifically comforted me, showing great humanistic care. In the end, she even gave me a bonus grade.

reviews.content: 快跑给分根本是玄学，有些明显做的不太好的朋友拿了A，也可能是prof的标准比较奇怪，反正不推荐。
reviews.translated_content: Stay away. The grading is opaque and unpredictable; some friends who clearly didn’t do very well got an A. Maybe the professor’s standards are just strange. Anyway, not recommended.

reviews.content: 快點走！ 找一個醫生來教政策，根本自己也分身不暇。小組討論一部份人能高分是因為那個醫生去交流，然後他說，早前present的小組都能很高成績🙄🙄🙄 ，然後他就說之後的小組他會很嚴格，請問這他m 的公平嗎！ 所以你們要高分就早點做，最好第一組present因為他會給你很高分！他的評分準則完全是個迷，他提供的handbook 所謂的評分準則也是模棱兩可。 課堂上教的和她想要做的present和poster完全不是同一回事 🙄🙄🙄🙄🙄 還騙說 上年度一半人A一半兩B ,根本不是那麼一回事 ，想要在這裏拿高分 去求求神明會更加實際
reviews.translated_content: Run away quickly! Finding a doctor to teach policy means he's stretched too thin himself. Some people in the group discussions got high grades because that doctor went to exchange activities, and then he said the groups that presented earlier could get very high scores 🙄🙄🙄. Then he said he would be very strict with later groups. Is this f***ing fair?! So if you want a high grade, do it early; ideally, present as the first group because he will give you a very high score! His grading criteria are completely a mystery, and the so-called grading criteria in the handbook he provided are ambiguous. What was taught in class and what he wanted for the presentation and poster were completely different things 🙄🙄🙄🙄🙄. He also lied, saying that half the class got As and half got Bs last year, which was not the case at all. If you want a high grade here, praying to the gods would be more practical.

reviews.content: 还好吧全程没认真过 都是水的 最后A-，不过组员很重要
reviews.translated_content: It was okay. I wasn't serious throughout the whole course; everything was lightweight. I still got an A-, but your group members are important.

reviews.content:
教授感觉很忙的样子，三个月下来有一个半月都是TA在代课。评分标准非常迷，给的手册里面都是很飘渺的标准。上课前有一堆资料让你看（我没看），但是都不是很有用的样子。Group project 感觉一般，好多护理系的提前抱团。有个半强制的探访老人活动（生病没去），要根据采访内容和施政报告做poster，同样意义不明。
* 如果你是DSE考生且知道LS（通识）这门课的话，你就按照LS的标准来写他的作业，至少不会大错。（本人DSE LS 5**这门课B+，我猜是我这个组靠后pre所以低分的原因（摊手））
reviews.translated_content: The professor seemed very busy; over the three months, the TA taught about half the classes. The grading criteria were very confusing—the handbook provided vague standards. There was a lot of pre-class reading material (which I didn’t read), but it didn’t seem very useful. The group project was average; many nursing students formed groups early on. There was a semi-mandatory elderly home visit activity (I missed it due to illness) that required making a poster based on interview content and policy reports, which also felt pointless. If you are a DSE student familiar with Liberal Studies (LS), write your assignments according to LS standards, and you should at least avoid major mistakes. (I got 5** in DSE LS but only a B+ in this course; I guess my group’s low score was because we presented later in the sequence (shrug).)

reviews.content: 给分玄学，课程要记participation但参与机会不多，探访老人活动的内容跟后续的poster制作关系不大
reviews.translated_content: Grading is opaque and unpredictable. The course requires recording participation, but there aren’t many opportunities to participate. The content of the elderly-visiting activity has little relevance to the subsequent poster production.

course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: 不知道是不是网课的原因，我一个理科生感觉学的有点累。教学组的英语水平好像不是很好，有点影响学习热情
reviews.translated_content: I’m not sure if it was because of online classes, but as a science student, I found it a bit tiring. The teaching team’s English proficiency doesn’t seem very good, which somewhat affected my enthusiasm for learning.

reviews.content: 我这一学期是online所以field trip取消了，field trip report也换成了reading reflective essay，总体lecture进度不算很快，讲的东西也都很有意思，尤其是推荐的阅读都挺好看的～ tutor人很好会帮忙看essay，wl也不是很大，lecture不计attendance而且跟最后gp work和essay的关联也不大，所以上课溜号也问题不大hhh有两个quiz（但是quiz之前tutor会把quiz内容过一遍所以不用担心） gp work的时候可以抱建院大佬大腿，我组友是马来西亚建院华人，所以gpw体验还不错。另外essay最好提前一些写，写完问问tutor建议也很棒。 我周围人好像都是A或者A-，不知道有没有A+，总体来讲是一门wl小grade靓的课，不要犹豫大胆来选吧～
reviews.translated_content: I took this course online this semester, so the field trip was cancelled and the field trip report was replaced by a reading reflective essay. Overall, the lecture pace wasn’t too fast, and the topics were interesting, especially the recommended readings, which were quite enjoyable. The tutor is very nice and helps review essays. The workload isn’t heavy, attendance isn’t taken for lectures, and there isn’t much connection between lectures and the final group work or essays, so zoning out in class isn’t a big problem haha. There are two quizzes, but the tutor goes through the quiz content beforehand, so no need to worry. For the group work, you can rely on strong students from the Faculty of Architecture; my teammate was a Chinese-Malaysian student from Architecture, so the group work experience was quite good. Also, it’s best to start the essay early, and asking the tutor for feedback after finishing is very helpful. People around me seem to have gotten A or A-, I’m not sure if anyone got A+. Overall, it’s a low-workload course with good grades, so don’t hesitate—go for it!

reviews.content: Field trip  很有趣，小组作业因为可以两人一组所以相对来说社恐友好。我们那个tutor几乎一直没怎么给我们的pre提意见，数次发邮件问他有没有什么意见他也没怎么回，搞得我中途一度很慌，不过后来结果还不错…我前几节课摸鱼太放飞自我了，so后期很努力，幸好勉强弥补了
reviews.translated_content: The field trip was very interesting. Since the group assignment allowed pairs, it was relatively friendly for those very uncomfortable with social participation. Our tutor hardly gave any feedback on our presentation; even after emailing several times to ask for comments, he barely replied, which made me panic for a while. However, the final result turned out quite well... I slacked off too much in the first few lessons, so I worked very hard later on and fortunately managed to make up for it.

reviews.content: remote+没有field trip之后workload更小了 改成了一个400字的reading essay。tutor人超好 每次都把文章的outline发给他审核
reviews.translated_content: After switching to remote learning and cancelling the field trip, the workload became even lighter. It was changed to a 400-word reading essay. The tutor is super nice; I sent him the outline of my essay for review every time.

reviews.content: 良心好课 特别是对建院的学生来说，可以拓广知识面，了解中国传统建筑知识。tutor们也都很nice
reviews.translated_content: A genuinely worthwhile course, especially for students from the Faculty of Architecture. It broadens your knowledge and helps you understand traditional Chinese architecture. The tutors are also very nice.

reviews.content: 教授超好，也很好🐢，wl也不算大，就我的tutor叫Freddie Wong的有点拉了
reviews.translated_content: The professor is super nice, and the grading is generous. The workload isn’t heavy either. It’s just that my tutor, Freddie Wong, was a bit disappointing.

reviews.content: 挺有趣味性的一门课，但不建议尚未习惯英文教学的y1小朋友食用。
reviews.translated_content: A quite interesting course, but I wouldn’t recommend it for Year 1 students who aren’t yet used to English-medium teaching.

reviews.content: 内容很有意思不会无聊的类型 理科生也能轻松handle 最后选了个比较挑战的project题目感觉也做得很好 不知道大佬怎么拿A+的啊 我认识的基本上都是A啊
reviews.translated_content: The content is interesting and not boring. Science students can handle it easily. I chose a more challenging project topic at the end and felt I did quite well. I don’t know how the top students manage to get A+; most people I know got As.

reviews.content: lecturer是建院大佬，但他不怎么上课，都是tutor上的，tutor上的课十分无聊。上课听不懂没关系，tutorial听懂就能应付所有assessment。reading有点多，但可以水过去。给分好。
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer is a top expert from the Faculty of Architecture, but he rarely taught; classes were mostly conducted by tutors, and the tutorials were very boring. It doesn’t matter if you don’t understand the lectures; as long as you understand the tutorials, you can handle all the assessments. There was quite a lot of reading, but you could coast through it. The grading was good.

reviews.content: 相对有趣的一门课，lecture对于只要不是特别讨厌建筑类知识的同学应该都不会太无聊，wl正常，有field trip report（19-20sem2线上所以是reading report），group project，1500字大essay和两个小quiz，quiz很简单只要好好听tutorial即可。教授和TA人都很好，可以把assignment发过去请求帮忙修改。认真上的话A range不难
reviews.translated_content: A relatively interesting course. Lectures shouldn’t be too boring for anyone who doesn’t particularly dislike architecture-related knowledge. The workload is normal. There is a field trip report (in Sem 2 of 2019–20, it was online, so it became a reading report), a group project, a 1,500-word major essay, and two small quizzes. The quizzes are very simple as long as you listen well in tutorials. The professor and TA are very nice; you can send them your assignments and ask for help with revisions. If you take it seriously, getting an A-range grade isn’t hard.

reviews.content: Workload大，慎选
reviews.translated_content: Heavy workload, choose with caution.

reviews.content: 烂龟
reviews.translated_content: Harsh grading.

reviews.content: 英語水平要求較高 wl小
reviews.translated_content: Requires a high level of English proficiency. Low workload.

reviews.content: 挺好的
reviews.translated_content: It’s pretty good.

reviews.content: 可能关于中国现代史、中国城市（小区、单位）的部分内容对于内地同学来说比较明显；Term Paper 3000字还是比较需要投入的～
reviews.translated_content: The sections on modern Chinese history and Chinese urban communities (residential compounds, work units) may be quite obvious to students from the mainland. The 3,000-word term paper still requires a considerable investment of effort.

reviews.content: 略无聊，给分还好
reviews.translated_content: A bit boring, but grading is okay.

reviews.content: workload较大，一个presentation，两篇800字reflective journal，一篇2500字final paper（或5000字group project），还有半开卷的final exam lecture会讲中国近代史，也会讲中国的城市问题（土地所有权，遗产保护，交通情况等），内容丰富。 tutorial主要是presentation和group discussion，和local交流想法会比较有收获。 个人认为还是很适合内地生的一门课。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is relatively heavy: one presentation, two 800-word reflective journals, one 2,500-word final paper (or a 5,000-word group project), plus a semi-open-book final exam. Lectures cover modern Chinese history as well as urban issues in China (land ownership, heritage conservation, transport, etc.), so the content is rich. Tutorials mainly involve presentations and group discussions; exchanging ideas with local Hong Kong students can be quite rewarding. Personally, I think this course is very suitable for students from Mainland China.

reviews.content: 19-20 spring课程全为网课，所以授课效果不怎么样，课程内容不算特别有用但还好吧，当时选不上其他ccch所以选了这个，期末简单复习一下笔记即可，会有两张单面A4的cheat sheet，最后A-还比较满意
reviews.translated_content: In spring 2019–20, all classes were online, so the teaching effectiveness wasn't great. The course content wasn't particularly useful, but it was acceptable. I chose this because I couldn't enrol in other CCCH courses. For the final, just reviewing your notes is enough. You're allowed two single-sided A4 cheat sheets. I ended up with an A-, which I was fairly satisfied with.

reviews.content: Nice！！
reviews.translated_content: Nice！！

reviews.content: Lecture內容很雜的一堂課,essay一篇佔40%,建議寫作好的同學上,final exam佔30%,考點就主要幾個,有很多past paper可以參考
reviews.translated_content: The lecture content is quite scattered. One essay accounts for 40%, so it’s recommended for students who are good at writing. The final exam accounts for 30%; the key testing points are limited to a few main topics, and there are many past papers for reference.

reviews.translated_content: quite good

reviews.content: 讲中国思想，对于文科生来说高中历史会有涉猎，不是很难，wl还可以
reviews.translated_content: It covers Chinese thought. For humanities students, this overlaps with high school history, so it’s not very difficult. The workload is manageable.

course_info.title: Ideas and Images of the West in Late Imperial China

reviews.content: 真的蛮无聊的 高中历史课的感觉 中外文化交流 每当遇到有趣的问题宋老师就不深入下去了 觉得也没学到啥cultural studies的本领 essay50%自选题目 我写了晚清翻译小说 自己觉得还OK 结果总分B+也不知道为啥
reviews.translated_content: It’s really quite boring, feeling like a high school history class on cultural exchanges between China and the West. Whenever an interesting question came up, Professor Song wouldn’t go into depth. I feel like I didn’t learn much in the way of cultural studies skills. The essay was worth 50% with a self-chosen topic; I wrote about late-Qing translated novels. I thought it was OK, but I got a B+ overall and don’t know why.

reviews.content: 课程内容虽说有许多干货，但个人觉得确实有点无聊。宋刚老师为人真的特别好，能提供一些新的视角和有趣知识（还会在课上放电影）。考核的话，Lecture考勤占10%，Tutorial一共四次小组presentation占40%（每年都是指定的题目），再就是自选题目essay占50%。自选题目的essay可以找教授和助教多聊聊，让他们帮忙看outline或者推荐一些reading。最后A-
reviews.translated_content: Although the course content has a lot of substantive material, I personally found it a bit boring. Professor Song Gang is genuinely a very nice person. He provides new perspectives and interesting knowledge (and even shows movies in class). For assessment, lecture attendance counts for 10%, four group presentations in tutorials count for 40% (with set topics each year), and a self-chosen topic essay counts for 50%. For the self-chosen essay, you can chat more with the professor and TAs, ask them to review your outline, or recommend some readings. I got an A-.

reviews.content: 很多presentation，但是评分很不错，tutor也很好
reviews.translated_content: There are many presentations, but the grading is quite good, and the tutor is also very nice.

reviews.content: 还算好🐢
reviews.translated_content: The grading is fairly favourable.

reviews.content: 应该是一个presentation（35%？忘了）一篇essay（50%），剩下的是tutorial discussion。Professor非常儒雅，上课也有interaction；tutor也会对每个发言进行回应。对于DSE没有学过历史的人来说也不用害怕，毕竟大头在essay上，选个自己感兴趣的方面研究就好了。我写的是西方传教士对于中国晚清艺术史的影响，写了大概两个星期，看了不少资料慢慢写的，最后essay A+，overall是A。
reviews.translated_content: There should be one presentation (35%? I forgot), one essay (50%), and the rest is tutorial discussion. The professor is very refined, and there is interaction in class; the tutor also responds to every comment. Those who didn’t take history in the DSE don’t need to worry, since the essay carries the most weight—just choose a topic you’re interested in and research it. I wrote about the influence of Western missionaries on late Qing Chinese art history, spent about two weeks reading plenty of sources and writing slowly, and finally got an A+ for the essay, with an overall grade of A.

reviews.content: 课程无聊透顶，但是wl小，需要非常仔细地准备presentation和essay，tutorial最好去听一听
reviews.translated_content: The course is utterly boring, but the workload is small. You need to prepare very carefully for the presentation and essay. It’s best to attend the tutorials.

reviews.content:
lecture attendance + group 30 min pre with 10 min Q&A + 2500 essay
好prof好tutor好🐢
reviews.translated_content: Lecture attendance + group 30-min presentation with 10-min Q&A + 2500-word essay. Good professor, good tutor, generous grading.

reviews.content: prof人还可以就是很无聊，tutor给人印象不是很好（给我们presentation指出问题，但是我觉得我们已经解释了是他没在听）final essay选题是明清中西音乐交流，自认为写得还行没想到只有B
reviews.translated_content: The prof is okay but very boring. The tutor left a bad impression (he pointed out issues with our presentation, but I felt we had already explained them and he just wasn’t listening). The final essay topic was musical exchange between China and the West during the Ming and Qing dynasties. I thought I wrote it reasonably well, but unexpectedly only got a B.

reviews.content: 还不错的历史课 教授确实很博学 内容有趣 不过studio太忙了没空慢慢准备占大头的presentation（除非有很强的队友带）和essay…tutor感觉印象不太好
reviews.translated_content: A decent history course. The professor is indeed very knowledgeable and the content is interesting. However, the studio sessions were too busy, leaving no time to slowly prepare for the heavily weighted presentation (unless you have very strong teammates to carry you) and essay... I didn’t have a good impression of the tutor.

reviews.content: 很不公平 tutorial grp那个时间段报的人少就导致grp pre只能两个人一组，别的组三四个人😅两个人负责三十分钟的pre 社恐人真的累了。还有，扣十分就没A range了，但那些作业评分都蛮主观的 比如essay和pre。只能说付出的努力不成正比吧
reviews.translated_content: Very unfair. Because fewer people signed up for that tutorial group time slot, our group presentation could only be done by two people, while other groups had three or four. Two people responsible for a 30-minute presentation—someone with social anxiety is really exhausted. Also, losing 10 marks means missing out on the A range, but the grading for assignments like essays and presentations is quite subjective. I can only say that the effort put in was not proportional to the result.

course_info.title: The Chinese Cultural Revolution
course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: A well-organized course对于有一定学术水平的同学来说，这门课能够给予的知识是极其有限的（但是反过头来看所有CC都这样，所以也不能说是一个缺点，只能说大家在知识方面不要抱有过高期望），所谓重塑世界观啊啥的确实可能言重了，平时多关注一下相关知识就可以避免世界观突然被重塑了,何况这门课多是事实的描述而非价值的判断与传递，并不会有人刻意想重塑你的世界观。 但是这门课传达出的学术态度是端正的，其中有一篇reading有很大篇幅是用来描述所使用的methodology，是与统计密切相关的，而这与政治科学本身的精神是相契合的，所以对于教授观点偏激所作出的批评是不成立的，要么是自己的视野过于狭隘，要么是出于民族主义自尊心不容许别人做出批评，要么是出于一种“因为世界不都是光明的所以我们的历史是不可指摘的”的怪异逻辑，这些都是脱离论域的人身攻击或者诉诸结果的逻辑谬误，我觉得加在老师身上是不恰当的，而且要注意，具备这样社会科学学术素养的老师，其实是在中文学院工作的。 另外，对于想上这门课的同学来说，上课的体验比较一般，因为教室很大，而且王老师的英语配合上有点问题的音响有点闹耳朵；workload不是非常大，但是是细水长流的，reading不多，但是每周都要花时间准备tuto（有几周要看电影，有两周要debate，有的时候要分析电影文本或者文章文本），期末要做一个project（这个是我认为相当不错的项目，因为历史已经离我们远去，要想再次捕捉它的痕迹，用亲人的oral history的方式再好不过了）以及一个final essay exam（其实很简单，就是提炼一下几个reading的观点，把文章的结构提前布好就OK了），需要集中的时间来准备；给分我觉得也是挺好的，每个项目都认真准备（每周花一至两个小时准备tuto，tuto上发言要有质量，project可以用汉字，final注意和reading相联系），其实拿A很简单，我这门课除了上面所说的也没花太多时间和精力，最后A，来划水一学期然后拿不到A的就别喷了，随便去哪个课都不会给A的，至于已经很努力但是没有A的，可能是tuto上比较羞涩，这个自己多练习就好，可以对稿念的。 最后，爽姐真的很nice，去看她中文学院的介绍图片，简直是白月光呀！
reviews.translated_content: A well-organized course. For students with a certain level of academic ability, the knowledge this course provides is extremely limited (but looking back, all Common Core courses are like this, so it’s not necessarily a drawback; just don’t have overly high expectations regarding content). Claims about “reshaping your worldview” may be exaggerated; staying informed about related topics can prevent any sudden shock to your worldview. Moreover, this course mostly describes facts rather than transmitting value judgments, so no one is deliberately trying to reshape your worldview.  However, the academic attitude conveyed by this course is sound. One reading spends a large portion describing its methodology, which is closely related to statistics and aligns with the spirit of political science. Therefore, criticisms based on the professor’s allegedly radical views are unfounded; they stem either from narrow-mindedness, nationalist pride that refuses criticism, or a strange logic that “because the world isn’t all bright, our history is beyond reproach.” These are ad hominem attacks or logical fallacies outside the scope of argument, and I find them inappropriate when directed at the teacher. Note that a teacher with this level of social-science academic literacy actually works in the School of Chinese.  Additionally, for students considering this course, the classroom experience is average because the lecture hall is large, and Professor Wang’s English combined with faulty speakers is hard on the ears. The workload isn’t huge, but it’s steady. There aren’t many readings, but you need to spend time each week preparing for tutorials (some weeks involve watching films, two weeks require debates, and sometimes you analyse film or article texts). At the end, there is a project (which I think is excellent, since history is distant, and using oral history from relatives is a great way to recapture its traces) and a final essay exam (actually quite simple: just distil points from several readings and outline the structure in advance), which requires concentrated preparation.  I think the grading is quite good. If you prepare carefully for each component (spend 1–2 hours weekly on tutorial prep, contribute quality comments in tutorials, write the project in Chinese if you prefer, and link your final to the readings), getting an A is easy. Apart from what I mentioned, I didn’t spend much time or effort on this course and still got an A. Anyone who coasts through the semester and doesn’t get an A shouldn’t complain; you won’t get an A in just any course. As for those who worked hard but didn’t get an A, you might have been too shy in tutorials; just practise more—you can even read from a script.  Finally, Shuang Jie is really nice. Check out her profile picture on the School of Chinese website; she’s absolutely radiant!

reviews.content: 怎么说，文革的资料是截了一半的，五百多页的文章就截了五十多页还把关键信息给漏掉，就比如刘少奇提议大放国债完全避而不谈，并且选的片段立场很鲜明，再说文章你好歹查一下作者的成分吧，你选的那些作者一个成分比一个逆天，杨绛拿出来说话就算了，杨小凯一个澳大利亚的基督徒的小作文有啥可以拿出来说的呀？关键是原文两百多页你就找了20页，然后一本正经地说要critical 然后还有叶永烈，一个科幻作家写的人物传记还奉为圭臬？王洪文一个月用15吨煤炭是吧。资料是断章取义的，道貌是岸然的，立场是鲜明的，思维却是critical的，只能说分还是不错的，所以应该是hk在宣传反动思想的一门课
reviews.translated_content: How should I put this? The Cultural Revolution materials were heavily truncated. A 500-plus-page article was cut down to just over 50 pages, with key information omitted. For instance, it completely avoided mentioning Liu Shaoqi’s proposal to issue large amounts of national debt. Moreover, the selected excerpts have a very clear bias. Also, you should at least check the authors’ backgrounds; the ones chosen are increasingly absurd. It’s one thing to cite Yang Jiang, but what is there to say about Yang Xiaokai’s little essay as an Australian Christian? The key point is that out of more than 200 pages of original text, only 20 pages were selected, yet the instructor solemnly claimed we needed to be critical. And Ye Yonglie, a science-fiction writer’s biographical work, was treated as the gold standard? Wang Hongwen used 15 tons of coal in a month, right? The materials are taken out of context, the moral posturing is hypocritical, the stance is obvious, yet the thinking is supposedly “critical.” I can only say the grade was decent, so this must be a course for HKU to promote reactionary ideology.

reviews.content: 作为一门CC课，这门课专注于讲述和分析历史事件本身，而对背后的理论领域，即各种意识形态交锋的真正战场少有涉足。对于想深入了解文革的同学，我建议从工人运动史的普遍性和中国革命的具体性两个方面来思考：文革其实是了解当代马克思主义困境的一个很好的切入点，这涉及到一个至今还没能从实践上解决的，但却有关人类命运的问题：革命之后是什么？早在1844年，马克思就警告我们要“避免建立起一个与个人对立的抽象的社会”。我们这代人应当对这句话有着前辈们不可能预见的理解，因为“只有我们这一代人，才忍受着名曰共产主义的‘反资本主义’型的彻底的资本主义”。我们问自己，一个工人国家是如何转化到了自己的对立面？人和自由是可能的吗？我们是不是总要碰到一个反对个人自由的新形式的国家暴政？我们为自由的斗争是否一定要以一种专制而告终？在革命生死存亡的关头，不同阶级对党的压力导致党内不同阶层从不同阶级的利益出发来确定自己的“社会主义”愿望。然而唯一有能力施加真正社会主义压力的阶级——工人阶级却是最软弱，最无组织，最无力施加这种压力的阶级。以上是文革作为普遍的历史的一部分生发出来的思考，我个人建议感兴趣的同学可以仔细地考察1917年11月的俄国革命，关注我们的时代唯一一个成功的工人革命是如何在人性的自由中开启了一个崭新的时代，但却以国家资本主义反革命告终。具体到包括文革在内的整个中国革命，我个人建议好好研究CCP本身的性质，特别是从政党实质是本阶级的代表这个角度思考。弄清了这个问题，也就弄清了整个中国革命的性质。在这个框架下，诸如文革的起源，不同势力的此消彼长乃至文革注定的结局等一系列问题也就迎刃而解了。此外个人建议好好阅读杨曦光在1968年所写的「中国向何处去」，思考为什么这篇文章一经发出会招致包括文革派在内的一众官僚的强烈反应，有助于理解文革的实质。当然了以上都是我们站在如今的视角高高地审视历史，这门课个人认为最有价值的是提供了千千万万身为普通人的亲历者的视角，身处历史之中的人们很难像如今的我们一样理解革命。“人们创造历史，但并非是在自己创造的环境中。在这个过程中，他们既改变了环境，也改变了自身”。
reviews.translated_content: As a Common Core course, this class focuses on narrating and analysing historical events themselves, with little engagement in the underlying theoretical arena—the true battlefield of clashing ideologies. For students who want to understand the Cultural Revolution in depth, I suggest thinking from two perspectives: the universality of labour movement history and the specificity of the Chinese revolution. The Cultural Revolution is actually a good entry point for understanding the contemporary dilemma of Marxism, which involves a question concerning human destiny that has yet to be resolved in practice: What comes after revolution? As early as 1844, Marx warned us to 'avoid establishing an abstract society opposed to the individual.' Our generation should have an understanding of this sentence that our predecessors could not have foreseen, because 'only our generation endures thorough capitalism in the guise of “anti-capitalist” communism.' We ask ourselves: How did a workers' state transform into its opposite? Are people and freedom possible? Must we always encounter a new form of state tyranny opposing individual liberty? Must our struggle for freedom inevitably end in despotism? At critical moments of life and death for the revolution, pressure from different classes on the Party led different factions within the Party to define their 'socialist' aspirations based on the interests of different classes. However, the only class capable of exerting genuine socialist pressure—the working class—was the weakest, least organised, and least able to exert such pressure. These are reflections arising from viewing the Cultural Revolution as part of universal history. Personally, I suggest interested students carefully examine the Russian Revolution of November 1917, observing how the only successful workers' revolution of our time opened a new era in human freedom but ended in state capitalist counter-revolution. Regarding the entire Chinese revolution, including the Cultural Revolution, I personally suggest studying the nature of the CCP itself, especially from the perspective that a party is essentially the representative of its class. Clarifying this issue clarifies the nature of the entire Chinese revolution. Within this framework, questions such as the origins of the Cultural Revolution, the ebb and flow of different forces, and the inevitable outcome of the Cultural Revolution become easy to resolve. Additionally, I personally recommend reading Yang Xiguang's 1968 article 'Whither China?', and considering why this article provoked strong reactions from bureaucrats, including the Cultural Revolution faction, upon its release. This helps in understanding the essence of the Cultural Revolution. Of course, all of the above is us looking down on history from today's perspective. In my opinion, the most valuable aspect of this course is providing the perspectives of countless ordinary people who experienced it. People living within history find it hard to understand revolution as we do today. 'Men make their own history, but they do not make it as they please; they do not make it under self-selected circumstances, but under circumstances existing already, given and transmitted from the past. In this process, they change both their circumstances and themselves.'

reviews.content: 好好学了，只有B+，没吹的那么好
reviews.translated_content: I studied hard but only got a B+. It's not as good as people claim.

reviews.content: A 爱这门课永远 哪怕改革变成线下了wl大的问题大家也说了 但我想说 真正的好课是你在上完之后会一直怀念的 会和prof和tutor处成朋友的 会在结课的时候结课照片和感言刷遍朋友圈的 这门课是我为数不多的能带给我深刻思考的cc课 关于死亡 政治 暴力 人性 感慨万千 无须多言 能在我大学四年中上到这样一门课是我的幸运
reviews.translated_content: A. Love this course forever. Even though the reform changed it to offline and everyone has mentioned the high workload issue, I want to say that a truly good course is one you will miss constantly after finishing it. You become friends with the prof and tutor. At the end of the course, graduation photos and testimonials flood your social media feed. This is one of the few CC courses that gave me profound thoughts on death, politics, violence, and human nature. Words cannot express my feelings. It was my fortune to take such a course during my four years of university.

reviews.content: 非常好的CCCH9005……虽然wl是很大没错，平时的Tutorial都需要读reading➕准备发言，期末是闭卷手写Essay，但是上完之后真的感觉非常有意义，能够极大地拓宽你的眼界和视角，让你重新审视历史事件，包括看待研究方法和问题。两位老师都是专业能力强且非常有人格魅力的人，在她们身上真的学到了很多，这门课值得我用很长时间去怀念。关于闭卷手写这点我Final前有问过Prof. Wang，她说了一句话让我印象很深：只有你记在脑子里的东西才是别人拿不走的。听到之后我久久不能平息，之后就很认真地去准备essay了。可能是由于本人写Essay水平比较低（个人原因），最后拿到了A-，课友拿到了A+，但我们都觉得在这门课上，知识永远大于分数。总体来说，还是非常非常好的课，会跟每一届入学的学弟学妹推荐的好课。
reviews.translated_content: CCCH9005 is an excellent course... although the workload is indeed heavy, requiring reading and preparation for speaking in regular tutorials, and the final is a closed-book handwritten essay, I truly felt it was very meaningful after completing it. It greatly broadened my horizons and perspective, allowing me to re-examine historical events, including research methods and questions. Both instructors are highly professional and charismatic; I learned a lot from them, and this is a course worth remembering for a long time. Regarding the closed-book handwritten aspect, I asked Prof. Wang before the final, and she said something that left a deep impression on me: 'Only what you keep in your mind cannot be taken away by others.' Hearing this calmed me down, and I prepared for the essay very seriously afterwards. Possibly due to my own relatively low essay-writing ability (personal reason), I ended up with an A-, while a classmate got an A+, but we both felt that in this course, knowledge always outweighs grades. Overall, it is still a very, very good course, one that I would recommend to every cohort of junior students.

reviews.content: wl大 个人偏见极其严重 不按照教授的想法来就分数不高👎完全没有任何理性的讨论可言
reviews.translated_content: Heavy workload. Extremely biased personally. If you don’t follow the professor’s ideas, you won’t get high marks 👎. There is absolutely no room for rational discussion.

reviews.content: 好课，教授内地人，文革期间自己在北京搞地下艺术，自由派反中共的倾向是肯定有的，也非常熟悉CCP propganda，瑕不掩瑜，摆正心态听。以史为镜，可以看到一部分官场的本质和现实、群众心理的走向。
reviews.translated_content: Good course. The professor is from the mainland and engaged in underground art in Beijing during the Cultural Revolution. He definitely has liberal, anti-CCP tendencies and is very familiar with CCP propaganda. The flaws don’t outweigh the merits; just keep an open mind when listening. Using history as a mirror, you can see part of the essence and reality of officialdom, as well as trends in mass psychology.

reviews.content: 感觉出龟很魔幻，本来以为很高最后也一般
reviews.translated_content: The grade release was surreal. I thought it would be high, but it turned out to be just average.

reviews.content: 看到这门课明年还有我就放心了
reviews.translated_content: I’m relieved to see that this course is still offered next year.

reviews.content:
The Professor is nice and the tutor is also chill. However this class was very competitive when I took it. A lot of exchnage students were taking this course for some reason. Avg workload(3 Psets,1 presentation).
The worst part about this course is the participation marks, the prof said you have to raise questions in class to get the marks, so everybody is just competing to ask questions even though she does not mark anything down or ask for anybody's names! She claimed that she remembers people's faces and gives participation grade based on that!! 
The grade is quite disappointing: I got close to full mark for all assignments(48/50) and I'd say the presentation went quite well. In the end only got A-! not even an A!

reviews.translated_content: FBE students will find it easy to pick up, as it overlaps significantly with Econ1220. The workload is light.

reviews.content:
Totally a scam!!!
本身我的grade是A，結果二月office email我說grade改成B了！還不提供原因！完全scam！！！

reviews.translated_content: Totally a scam!!! My original grade was an A, but in February they emailed me from the office saying it had been changed to a B! They didn’t even provide a reason! Total scam!!! Don’t take this course...

reviews.content: 換了教授, 課程由 Quantitative base 變成了 Qualitative base, 說白了就是要實用計算的部份沒了, 對自己essay 文筆有信心的同學才建議上, problem set 變成了3次essay, 會在奇奇怪怪的地方扣分
reviews.translated_content: The professor changed, and the course shifted from a quantitative base to a qualitative base. To put it plainly, the practical calculation parts are gone. It’s only recommended for students who are confident in their essay writing skills. The problem sets have been replaced by three essays, and marks are deducted in strange places.

reviews.content: 教授很厉害，人称坑U宏观守门员，感觉在某些intuition方面比1220和2220讲得还好。内容特别友好，tutorial会手把手教各种econ概念，所以应该很适合商院以外对经济（尤其中国经济）感兴趣的同学。整体内容算是对中国经济提供了一种见解吧，尤其印象深刻的是对90年代通胀和改开以来高增长的解释。个人感觉给分还行，不过估计A和A+得essay写得细致才行。
reviews.translated_content: The professor is impressive, known as the gatekeeper of macroeconomics at this trap of a university. I feel he explains certain intuitions better than in ECON1220 and ECON2220. The content is very accessible, and the tutorials teach various economic concepts step-by-step, so it should be suitable for students outside the Business School who are interested in economics (especially the Chinese economy). Overall, the content offers insights into the Chinese economy; I was particularly impressed by the explanations of inflation in the 1990s and high growth since the reform and opening-up. Personally, I think the grading is okay, but getting an A or A+ probably requires writing detailed essays.

reviews.content: 超級好🐢! 3份problem set都很簡單，上tutorial就幾乎給答案了。個人覺得group project做好就可以好🐢。（A+）
reviews.translated_content: Super generous grading! All three problem sets are very easy; the tutorials practically give you the answers. Personally, I think if you do well on the group project, you’ll get a good grade. (A+)

reviews.content: 选的人的确很多 商学院的学生会占一定优势
reviews.translated_content: There are indeed many students enrolled. Business School students have a certain advantage.

reviews.content: 极其文科生友好的一门课，内容包括高中中国近代经济史外加一小部分econ相关知识。wl不大，一个pre,一篇essay（gp），三个来自于ppt的problemset，一个takehome的midterm。prof说problemset可以讨论，只要答案不是一模一样就可以。tutor是Gloria,非常nice，tutorial准备的也很用心。用点心就能好龟的一门课。推荐
reviews.translated_content: A course extremely friendly to humanities students. The content covers modern Chinese economic history from high school plus a small amount of economics knowledge. The workload isn’t heavy: one presentation, one essay (group project), three problem sets based on the PPTs, and one take-home midterm. The professor said we could discuss the problem sets as long as the answers weren’t exactly identical. The tutor is Gloria, who is very nice and prepared thoroughly for tutorials. It’s a course where you can get a good grade if you put in a bit of effort. Recommended.

reviews.content: Workload was okay. Required reading was quite interesting.
reviews.translated_content: Workload was okay. Required reading was quite interesting.

Yr1第一门cc就给我留下trauma了😭，问了一圈yr3/4的也说是他们上过最难的cc。wl很大，lecture是不能用电子产品的，考勤是随机的，mcq quiz是有的，final 是闭卷手写essay的，1000的Analytical Essay是要求非常critical的，reading是极多的，tutor Jessica是极mean的，tut是必须参加强制发言的，但讨论氛围是极压抑的，每次去上tut简直都是酷刑，每次上完都要吃点东西缓缓的程度。group presentation居然成了整个tutorial最享受的时光（因为tutor只给下面听众施压了），出分是b-的😊，只能寄希望于后面再选一门ccch来cover掉这门了。
reviews.translated_content: RUN!!! My first Common Core course in Year 1 left me with trauma 😭. I asked around, and even Year 3/4 students said it was the hardest CC they had taken. Huge workload. Lectures ban electronic devices. Attendance checks are random. There are MCQ quizzes. The final is a closed-book handwritten essay. The 1000-word Analytical Essay requires a very critical approach. Reading load is extremely heavy. Tutor Jessica is extremely mean. Tutorial attendance is mandatory with forced participation, but the discussion atmosphere is extremely oppressive. Every tutorial feels like torture; I need to eat something afterwards to recover. Surprisingly, the group presentation became the most enjoyable part of the tutorial (because the tutor only pressured the audience below). Got a B- 😊. I can only hope to take another CCCH course later to cover this one.

reviews.content: Honestly this course was quite challenging as I thought as I do not have a background in poli sci/history and the workload is hectic. there are tutorials final exam presentation group project + an impromptu quiz...which is about basically all the required readings in the course. peter is very chill and nice but the negative reviews i have seen about jh is mostly true...jh does give out tricky questions, doesn't give much guidance on essays, interrupts group presentations but as long as you say something during tutorials she will give you some sort of credit I guess...overall A- but I wouldn't recommend because this took up sm of my time

reviews.content: 整个班上貌似只有一个内地生....因此tutorial上可以体验舌战群儒的快感！课程内容基本上是国际政治导论但基本不会涉及较多的术语，基本与中国周边国际问题有关。 今年换了一个漂亮的韩国小姐姐当讲师，workload与过去相比略少，但仍然不少。 一学期上完收获颇丰，感觉是最好帮助理解中国的课了。 Group project自动分组，且一组很多人，比较难以掌控局面。但只要final essay写好且字数够（最少2000），给分貌似还不错。最后A-
reviews.translated_content: There seemed to be only one student from Mainland China in the whole class... so in tutorials you could experience the thrill of debating against many opponents! The course content is basically an introduction to international politics but rarely uses much terminology; it mostly relates to international issues around China. This year we had a pretty Korean female instructor. The workload was slightly less than before, but still considerable. I gained a lot after finishing the semester; I feel it was the course that best helped me understand China. The group project used automatic grouping with many members per group, making it harder to manage the situation. But as long as you write a good final essay with sufficient length (at least 2000 words), the grading seems decent. I ended up with an A-.

reviews.content:
Kinda wanted to rebut the negative review left today. Have to agree with the prof perspective (Chill and nice) but lowkey Jessica Hun aint that bad...trickey questions, yes, but the questions are basically either reading or lecture related and it kinda requires comprehensive understanding of the topic, which is required in the course outlines. Workload is big but allows you to gain insight of how China interacts with other countries by doing the course papers and group projects. Regarding the cantonese part, perhaps the local isn't that fluent in English? Coz on my end she always held the tutorial sessions in English.

Overall, mid-heavy workload, interesting topic. Finals require you to write essays about the readings (which is reasonable for a non-politics major student). Choose when you want to get a glimpse of how modern china interacts in world politics. (Good grades for good effort, got a A- thinking id get a B range)

reviews.content: 没有enroll上，所以全程只能旁听...因为她明年就要退休了呜呜呜。教授是何式凝老师，社工系的，主要研究性和性别议题，写过很多书，有关于男同的，有关于她自己的，也有一些边缘群体和角落的。她上课真的很热忱，也真的能感受到她想要把理念和知识传递的真诚。这个课程从毛时代一直推进到当代，探讨关于家庭、爱在不同语境下的变化和深入剖析不同时代下的不同困境。 看到有朋友说政治化倾向比较浓，但是恰恰觉得没有，课堂里有放过她的学生拍的内地人在香港的身份认同的微电影，她也觉得多元化的观点都可以被讨论。我作为一个旁听的学生，她也经常下课之后问到我作为内地学生在香港的感受，让我不要担心，不要害怕，总还是有温暖的人在的。 她其实自己会觉得自己在港大教授里也是边缘的角色（专注教学，无意晋升），而或许也是她自己明白作为边缘的感受，因此也就对边缘更加关注。实在感谢她眼睛和话语里的那份光，在这个很空洞的时代，依旧给到自己那份关于学者的力量，关于很多理念“依旧会有空间”的力量。
reviews.translated_content: I couldn’t enrol, so I sat in on the entire course... She is retiring next year, which is sad. The professor is Ho Shik-ngin from the Department of Social Work and Social Administration. She mainly researches sexuality and gender issues and has written many books, including topics on gay men, her own experiences, and marginalised groups. She is truly passionate in class, and you can genuinely feel her sincerity in wanting to convey her ideas and knowledge. The course progresses from the Mao era to the present, exploring how family and love change in different contexts and deeply analysing the dilemmas of different eras. Some friends said the course is heavily politicised, but I felt the opposite. In class, we watched a micro-film made by her students about mainlanders’ identity in Hong Kong, and she believes diverse viewpoints can be discussed. As an auditing student, she often asked me after class about my feelings as a mainland student in Hong Kong, telling me not to worry or be afraid, as there are still warm-hearted people around. She actually sees herself as a marginal figure among HKU professors (focused on teaching with no intention of promotion). Perhaps because she understands the feeling of being on the margins, she pays more attention to marginalised groups. I am truly grateful for the light in her eyes and words. In this hollow era, she still gives us the strength of a scholar and the power of the belief that “there will still be space” for many ideas.

course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: wl不大，需要和同一个tut session的人组队做pre和拍3min小视频，但tut总共只有两节。上课的内容都是中国社会的热点话题，比如教育（双减）、医疗、扶贫、婚姻（三孩）、养老。除了GP，会有两次开卷的小quiz+一篇essay，essay和GP的话题要一致，且是与课堂内容相关的即可。3个TA+PROF都是大陆人，人也都很nice。属于是一门对内地生极其友好，但对local和foreigner比较痛苦的课2333（不过local和foreigner挺多的）。GP只有B-，但最后还是拿A
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy. You need to team up with people from the same tutorial session for a presentation and to film a 3-minute video, but there are only two tutorials in total. The lecture content covers hot topics in Chinese society, such as education (the “double reduction” policy), healthcare, poverty alleviation, marriage (the three-child policy), and elderly care. Besides the group project, there are two open-book quizzes and one essay; the essay and group project topics must align and relate to the course content. The three TAs and the professor are all from Mainland China, and they are very nice. This is a course that is extremely friendly to students from Mainland China, but quite painful for local and foreign students haha (though there are plenty of local and foreign students). I only got a B- on the group project, but still ended up with an A.

reviews.content: wl: 整体不大。一共要写九个150字左右对这节课的reveiw, 但是是写了就给满分，所以压力不大；两个in-class quiz,考前一周复习ppt问题不大，且上学期第二个quiz前lecturer给花了重点范围；有一个gp,video+pre,这个略费时，但更多取决于组员如何。gp是每个tutorial gp（10人左右）内组队，如果提前找好了队友建议报同一个tutorial。tutorial一共三节，内容约等于无，很多是在讨论gp. 最后一个essay.     课程：个人感觉lecture不算非常有趣，可能因为我是内地生对课上讲的中国社会问题都非常熟悉了，lecturer也没有讲很多新颖观点，更多是介绍性，有时略无聊。我听课听起来比较轻松，甚至偶尔觉得不听也行，如果想了解中国社会问题，比如教育医疗养老等等，还是不错的。  给分：我最后有A+，应该是有拉curve, 两次quiz 都B+，gp, essay都是A，我觉得给分是fair 且挺不错的。教授和TA也都人美心善很好沟通。
reviews.translated_content: Workload: Not heavy overall. You need to write nine reviews of about 150 words each for this class, but you get full marks just for writing them, so the pressure is low. There are two in-class quizzes; reviewing the slides a week before the exam is sufficient, and last semester, the lecturer highlighted key areas before the second quiz. There is one group project involving a video and presentation, which is slightly time-consuming, but it depends largely on your teammates. Group projects are formed within each tutorial group (about 10 people), so if you find teammates early, I suggest signing up for the same tutorial. There are only three tutorials, and the content is virtually nonexistent, mostly discussing the group project. Finally, there is an essay.  Course: Personally, I don’t find the lectures very interesting, possibly because as a student from Mainland China, I am already very familiar with the social issues in China discussed in class. The lecturer didn’t present many novel viewpoints, mostly introductory material, which was sometimes a bit boring. I found listening to the lectures relatively easy, even occasionally feeling that I could skip them. However, if you want to understand social issues in China, such as education, healthcare, and elderly care, it’s still worthwhile.  Grading: I ended up with an A+. There was likely a curve applied. I got B+ on both quizzes, and As on the group project and essay. I think the grading was fair and quite good. Both the professor and the TA are kind, beautiful, and easy to communicate with.

reviews.content: 课程内容对于内地生应该很熟悉，tutorial方式很轻松，香港tutor人挺好，功课遇到问题都能问。lec除了quiz那两天记得去就行，quiz是开卷的只需要把ppt上的东西抄下来就能拿A，考验你用ctrl+f的能力。小组作业分组方式有点随机，和抽签差不多，不过一组有6-7个人，每人负责的东西很少，wl很小，有2个freeride了都能A，Essay字数很少很轻松B+，overall A，推荐
reviews.translated_content: Students from Mainland China should find the course content very familiar. The tutorials are very relaxed, and the Hong Kong tutor is nice; you can ask them whenever you have problems with assignments. For lectures, you only need to attend on the two quiz days. The quizzes are open-book; you can get an A just by copying what’s on the slides, so it really tests your Ctrl+F skills. The group allocation for the group project is a bit random, almost like drawing lots, but there are 6–7 people per group, so each person has very little to do. The workload is small. Even with two free-riders in the group, we could still get an A. The essay word count is low and easy; I got a B+. Overall A. Recommended.

reviews.content: overall B+，不是那种轻松a range的课。这门课挺看重essay写作水平的，GP最好做的有亮点。我是社院的，上学期专业课essay拿了a-，这门课term essay只有b，大家可以衡量下。
reviews.translated_content: Overall B+. This isn’t one of those easy courses where you can coast to an A-range grade. The course places significant weight on essay-writing skills, and your group project should ideally have some standout features. I’m from the Faculty of Social Sciences; last semester I got an A- on essays in my major courses, but only a B on the term essay for this course. You can take that into consideration.

reviews.content: 三年下来选过最烂的cc，见过嘴最硬的tutor
reviews.translated_content: The worst Common Core course I've chosen in three years, and I've met the most stubborn tutor.

reviews.content: wl略大，每周之后都有discussion question（150字+），还有final presentation和final essay。教授和tutors人很nice，会尊重来自不同国家或地区学生的观点，并且他们提出问题都会及时解决。课上呈现了一些中国基本的社会问题。我认为如果感兴趣+付出努力的话就可以A+。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is slightly heavy. There are discussion questions (150+ words) every week, plus a final presentation and a final essay. The professor and tutors are very nice; they respect students’ viewpoints from different countries or regions, and they resolve any questions raised promptly. The class covered some basic social issues in China. I think if you are interested and put in the effort, you can get an A+.

reviews.content: 其實wl不算小，quiz給分很迷，而且挺多人會cheating然後拿A+…有點點不公平吧。gp花了很多心血，最後發揮很不錯，video有被誇，結果被判半離題，只有B+。反而individual essay糊里糊塗A+了。overall沒A，估計兩次quiz影響很大，臨場寫作文差的可以跑了。
reviews.translated_content: Actually, the workload isn’t small. The quiz grading is very confusing, and quite a few people cheat and get A+... It’s a bit unfair. I put a lot of effort into the group project and performed quite well; the video was praised, but it was judged as half off-topic, resulting in only a B+. On the other hand, I somehow got an A+ on the individual essay. I didn’t get an A overall; I estimate the two quizzes had a big impact. Those who are poor at impromptu essay writing should stay away.

reviews.content: 为什么没有21-22的选项啊，课还行，差点以为要烂，结果A-。
reviews.translated_content: Why isn’t there an option for 21-22? The course is okay; I almost thought I would fail, but ended up with an A-.

reviews.content: 一般 讨厌prez
reviews.translated_content: Average. I hate presentations.

reviews.content: 教授很nice，tutor也很乐于助人。阅读不算多，有一个group video，group presentation，individual essay要做，给分很好。
reviews.translated_content: The professor is very nice, and the tutor is also very helpful. The reading load isn’t heavy. There’s a group video, a group presentation, and an individual essay to complete. Grading is generous.

search_summary.title: Hong Kong: Becoming a Chinese Global City

course_info.title: Hong Kong: Becoming a Chinese Global City

reviews.content: 内容：很好地介绍了香港的殖民历史渊源，提供了对香港当代社会问题的一些见解。参与课程能够从不同的视角，理解所处的社会正在发生的一切，以及我们作为青年可以做什么。 授课：Lecturer Gary Wong 讲课很快，一节课PPT多的有八九十页，一直不停留。不保持专注容易跟不上。Tutorial主要是小组分享，tutor会提供点评，互动性还不错。 任务：Reflective Essay需要一些创新意识，选择有代表性的香港话题，注意多引用文献（笔者大一不会引用文献，因此成绩不好）。Tutorial presentation以及Term project可能有很多local队友，但他们很友好，建议有更多的朋辈之间的讨论。最后的Report任务量小大，一人要写1500-2000字。
reviews.translated_content: Content: It provides a good introduction to Hong Kong’s colonial historical roots and offers insights into contemporary social issues in Hong Kong. Taking this course allows you to understand what is happening in our society from different perspectives and what we as young people can do. Teaching: Lecturer Gary Wong speaks very fast; some lectures have 80–90 slides of PPT without pausing. It’s easy to fall behind if you don’t stay focused. Tutorials are mainly for group sharing, where the tutor provides feedback; the interaction is quite good. Assignments: The Reflective Essay requires some creativity. Choose a representative Hong Kong topic and make sure to cite many references (as a Year 1 student, I didn’t know how to cite properly, so my grade was poor). For the Tutorial presentation and Term project, you may have many local Hong Kong student teammates, but they are friendly. I suggest having more peer discussions. The final Report workload is manageable; each person needs to write 1500–2000 words.

reviews.content: Workload 不大，grade中等
reviews.translated_content: The workload is not heavy, and the grades are average.

reviews.content: work load还好，很好龟
reviews.translated_content: The workload is manageable, and it’s easy to get a good grade.

reviews.content: 适合想了解香港历史的同学 内地生少，要和local组队 主要围绕几场香港的社会movement，如果立场偏红，可能受不了 wl不算大
reviews.translated_content: Suitable for students who want to understand Hong Kong’s history. There are few students from Mainland China, and you’ll need to form groups with local Hong Kong students. The course mainly revolves around several social movements in Hong Kong; if your political stance leans pro-Beijing, you might find it hard to tolerate. The workload isn’t heavy.

course_info.title: People, Propaganda and Profit: Understanding Media in China

reviews.content: 不错！prof对中国的看法还是相对客观没有很bias 给分fair 努力能Arange
reviews.translated_content: Not bad! The professor’s views on China are relatively objective and not very biased. The grading is fair. With effort, you can get an A-range grade.

reviews.content: 期中画报纸封面+几百字分析占30% A，期末一篇一千字essay占40% A-，participation占30%，我应该算是比较积极的那种，最后A-，可以说给分fair吧。 这门课如果有兴趣真的很好很好，能学到很多，不论是lec还是tut设置都很合理，通过这门课认识了一些很有见解的local朋友！很喜欢和大家讨论！（btw我因为另一门课的作业，采访了prof，算是后来还有点私下交流吧，她真的好温柔好温柔！！冲！！我打算搜罗她其他的课去上了！！
reviews.translated_content: The midterm (designing a newspaper cover plus a few hundred words of analysis) accounts for 30% (A), the final (a 1,000-word essay) accounts for 40% (A-), and participation accounts for 30%. I was quite active, and I ended up with an A-, so I'd say the grading is fair. If you're interested, this course is really, really good. You can learn a lot, and both the lecture and tutorial structures are very reasonable. I met some insightful local friends through this course! I really enjoyed discussing with everyone! (By the way, because of an assignment in another course, I interviewed the prof, so we had some private communication later on. She is truly, truly gentle!! Go for it!! I plan to look for her other courses to take!!)

reviews.content: 理科生，对课程内容非常感兴趣，学得很开心，对中国媒体有了体系化的思考。期中是设计河南日报和南方都市报的版面并阐释理由，然后进行对比分析。期末是自选主题写2000-2500字的论文。两篇都认真写了，然后找writing center改了几次，幸运地都拿了A，overall也是A。美中不足的是线上tutorial感觉没有氛围，很多时候会不自觉地划水，没能体会到更有价值的讨论。
reviews.translated_content: As a science student, I was very interested in the course content and enjoyed learning. It gave me a systematic way of thinking about Chinese media. The midterm involved designing layouts for Henan Daily and Southern Metropolis Daily, explaining the rationale, and then conducting a comparative analysis. The final was a self-chosen topic essay of [REDACTED_PHONE] words. I wrote both seriously and had the Writing Centre review them several times. Fortunately, I got an A for both, and an A overall. The only downside was that the online tutorials lacked atmosphere; I often found myself coasting unintentionally and didn’t experience more valuable discussions.

reviews.content: 付出回报不成正比
reviews.translated_content: The effort required is disproportionate to the return.

reviews.content: 对中国媒体的分析框架很实用，assessment主要是写essay。感觉能学到很多东西，不过pf了不知道给分如何
reviews.translated_content: The analytical framework for Chinese media is very practical, and the assessments are mainly essays. I feel like I learned a lot, but since I took it pass/fail, I don’t know how the grading works.

reviews.content: wl小，midterm和final各一篇essay，给龟也不错，tutor很热情每次发言都会肯定你给你很大的信心，感觉基本上tuto有说过话participation的分也不会低
reviews.translated_content: Light workload, one essay each for the midterm and final. The grading is decent too. The tutor is enthusiastic and affirms every contribution, giving you a lot of confidence. I feel that as long as you speak up in tutorials, your participation score won’t be low.

reviews.content: 主要是介绍中国内地新闻界的情况，老师人不错，对新闻感兴趣的应该会觉得lecture有趣，本人则觉得偏学术，听起来有点走神。两篇essay一个presentation，wl ok，认真做给分不错。
reviews.translated_content: It mainly introduces the situation of the mainland Chinese news industry. The teacher is nice; those interested in journalism will likely find the lectures interesting. I personally found it rather academic and zoned out a bit. There are two essays and one presentation. The workload is OK, and if you put in the effort, the grading is good.

reviews.content: 课程给龟挺fair，教授三观很正很中立，tutorial质量高，课程内容略显无聊，reading比较重要要好好看
reviews.translated_content: The grading is quite fair. The professor has very sound and neutral values. The tutorials are high quality. The course content is slightly boring, and the readings are quite important, so make sure you read them carefully.

reviews.content: 这门课给分靓!grading算是挺公平的，我的midterm essay拿了A+，final report拿了A，在FR比重大的情况下最后出了个A，还是挺开心的，也能对媒体环境有些不错的反思。
reviews.translated_content: The grading for this course is great! The grading seems quite fair. I got an A+ on my midterm essay and an A on my final report. Even though the final report carried a heavy weight, I still ended up with an A, which made me quite happy. It also allowed for some good reflection on the media environment.

reviews.content: 对于我个人来说，这门课算是给分好＋wl不大＋有意思。整个学期的wl是做一个报纸封面的project再加一篇final文章。然后讲tutorial需要准备一次20min的pre，平时要有一定participation。 内容主要是讲中国新闻，话题是有趣的，但线上上课感觉不如线下好玩。
reviews.translated_content: For me personally, this course offers good grades, a manageable workload, and is interesting. The semester’s workload consists of a newspaper-front-page project plus a final essay. For the tutorial, you need to prepare one 20-minute presentation, and regular participation is required. The content focuses mainly on Chinese news; the topics are interesting, but online classes felt less fun than face-to-face ones.

reviews.content: 大概就是讲了佛教的核心教义，然后各个角度与儒家的对比。sum term 需要注意1.所有session都要求出勤 2.时间很紧，quiz完就要准备pre，然后最后几天要写2000-3000字essay，本人只用了3天因为pre完去长沙玩了一圈（如果能吃辣的话笨萝卜还可以）。楼上说的，用中文文献写英语的问题其实是有的，主要体现在要找佛经（推荐cbeta）等等，但是英文的汉学家也很多所以问题不大。
reviews.translated_content: It basically covers the core doctrines of Buddhism and then compares them with Confucianism from various angles. For the summer term, note: 1. Attendance is required for every session. 2. The schedule is tight: after the quiz, you need to prepare for your presentation, and then in the last few days you have to write a [REDACTED_PHONE]-word essay. I only spent three days on mine because I went to Changsha for a trip after my presentation (if you can handle spicy food, Benluobo is decent). As mentioned above, there is indeed an issue with using Chinese sources to write in English, mainly because you need to locate Buddhist sutras (I recommend CBETA), but since there are many English-speaking Sinologists, it’s not a major problem.

reviews.content: 好课以及好龟课！wl 中等，Tutor人超好给龟也大方！quiz考炸了（below median)，最后都有A，（感觉主要是靠论文拉回来的）。论文有一个小tips: 尽量找新颖小众的话题来写，实在想不到再去参考给的list。tutor说每学期论文大部分人看起来都是一样的，很难区分给分。还有一个小组pre，是按照个人表现评分的，不用担心free rider。课程内容比较简单，对佛学感兴趣的非常推荐！
绝世好课！事少龟好，quiz都是mcq不算很难认真过几遍ppt基本都会写，gp不用担心freerider因为是按individual的表现给分。另外tutor Terence人特别好 非常supportive
reviews.translated_content: An absolutely excellent course! Low workload and generous grading. The quizzes are all multiple-choice and not very difficult; if you go through the PowerPoint slides a few times, you’ll basically be able to answer them. You don’t need to worry about free riders in the group project because grading is based on individual performance. Also, the tutor Terence is a very nice person and extremely supportive.

reviews.content: 好课，说着要记考勤其实只需要拿着app在教室门口打个卡就可以撤。essay和pre全用AI➕降重，最后也有A-。事情很少给分还不错，建议上。
reviews.translated_content: Good course. Although they say attendance will be recorded, you only need to clock in with the app at the classroom door and can then leave. I used AI plus paraphrasing for both the essay and the presentation, and still ended up with an A-. There isn't much work, the grading is decent, and I recommend taking it.

reviews.content: 为什么indian也可以上这个课。。好诡异。。然后tutor你还我A+，why why why？每一项都是very good然后没有a+。。。
reviews.translated_content: Why can Indian students take this course...? It’s so weird... And tutor, give me back my A+! Why, why, why? Every item was marked “very good,” yet I didn’t get an A+...

reviews.content: 这门课内容很充实，教授和Tutor也都很友善。但是线上教学一定程度上阻碍了学生与老师之间的交流，所以感觉tutorial的线上质量并不是非常高（tutor也是这么说的）。这门课wl并不大，但也不是一门水课，所以选择时请谨慎。个人认为这门课更加适合对佛学、历史和中国文化有一定了解的同学（线下版是有期中考试的，期末还有一篇2500字的essay）。最后的prez和essay也需要有一定的critical thinking和new ideas。主观感觉tutor更加欢迎大二以上的学生。大一cc小白最后得分A-。
reviews.translated_content: This course has substantial content, and both the professor and tutor are very friendly. However, online teaching somewhat hindered interaction between students and teachers, so I felt the quality of the online tutorials was not very high (the tutor said the same). The workload isn’t heavy, but it’s not an easy course either, so please choose with caution. Personally, I think this course is better suited for students who already have some understanding of Buddhism, history, and Chinese culture (the in-person version has a midterm exam, and the final includes a 2,500-word essay). The final presentation and essay also require a certain level of critical thinking and new ideas. Subjectively, I feel the tutor welcomes second-year students and above more. As a first-year Common Core beginner, I ended up with an A-.

reviews.content: 很烂 很烂 很烂 教授上课只会读ppt 下面的人死气沉沉 给分也不fair 不知道今年是怎么了 😅
reviews.translated_content: Terrible, terrible, terrible. The professor just reads off the slides in class, the audience is lifeless, and the grading isn’t fair either. Not sure what happened this year 😅

reviews.content: summer term上的课，想水的话还是很容易的，只需保证每次lecture，tutorial都出席。前两周几乎不用干什么事情，然后quiz复习一下即可，除此之外就是pre和2000-3000字的essay。个人感觉因为summer的时间略紧凑，essay的参考文献可能很难非常翔实，不过最后还是很好龟的！综合wl和grade，我觉得summer上这门非常合适。
reviews.translated_content: This was a summer term course. It’s quite easy to coast through if you want to; you just need to ensure attendance at every lecture and tutorial. You hardly need to do anything in the first two weeks, and then you just revise for the quiz. Apart from that, there is only a presentation and a [REDACTED_PHONE]-word essay. Personally, I feel that because the summer schedule is slightly compact, it might be hard to make the references in the essay very comprehensive, but in the end, the grading was very favourable! Considering the workload and grades, I think taking this course in the summer is very suitable.

reviews.content: tutor很棒！她會帶著學生冥想,真的可以讓人沈浸其中。workload不算大，lecture有些無聊，如果對buddhism沒有很大興趣的同學不建議選這課。grade沒有傳說中這麼好，depends on個人的essay輸出質量
reviews.translated_content: The tutor is great! She leads students in meditation, which really allows you to immerse yourself. The workload isn’t heavy. Some lectures are boring; if you aren’t very interested in Buddhism, I don’t recommend taking this course. The grades aren’t as good as rumours suggest; it depends on the quality of your individual essay output.

reviews.content: 有点chur
reviews.translated_content: A bit demanding.

reviews.content: Good course, got an A range, definitely recommended. Put not just discipline, but also interest in it. Found not just historical facts from this, but motivation and spirit from it, especially during the Thousand Schools of Thoughts. Really recommended
reviews.translated_content: Good course, got an A range, definitely recommended. Put not just discipline, but also interest in it. Found not just historical facts from this, but motivation and spirit from it, especially during the Thousand Schools of Thoughts. Really recommended

reviews.content: 这是门新课。发现是两位王老师教就直接选了。讲座内容其实就和高中中国历史差不多，爱和会在课上让我们过足皇帝瘾。Tutorial wl还是很大的，每周要准备稿子演讲。最后作文很短，比较轻松。整门课的主题是“暴政的升级”，最大的优点就是reading选的很有品味，能从不同的学术方法中获取很多东西，本文科生也是受益匪浅。最后A+。
reviews.translated_content: This is a new course. I enrolled as soon as I saw it was taught by two instructors surnamed Wang. The lecture content is actually similar to high-school Chinese history, and Prof. Ai and Prof. Hui let us fully indulge our ‘emperor fantasies’ in class. The tutorial workload is quite heavy; you need to prepare scripts for weekly speeches. The final essay is short and relatively relaxed. The theme of the whole course is ‘the escalation of tyranny’. Its biggest strength is the tasteful selection of readings, from which you can gain a lot through different academic approaches. As a humanities student, I benefited greatly. Got an A+ in the end.

reviews.content: 无敌好老师 下课找老师问问题可以感觉到老师为了这么课真的做了很多功夫 也特别乐意解决学生的问题 a range推推
reviews.translated_content: An absolutely excellent instructor. If you ask them questions after class, you can tell they put a lot of effort into this course and are especially willing to help students with their problems. I got an A-range grade; highly recommended.

reviews.content: wl不算大，final改成回家写essay也很友好。lecture和每周tutorial都很有意思。好龟
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy, and it was very friendly of them to change the final to a take-home essay. Both the lectures and weekly tutorials are quite interesting. Generous grading.

reviews.content: 不错 挺轻松

reviews.translated_content: The course covers ancient Chinese astrology, traditional Chinese medicine and herbalism, hydraulic engineering, and more. There is a large volume of knowledge and many obscure terms. The tutorials are very lightweight.

reviews.content: 水了一個a-，prof 是PPT reader ，不用上課，找好組友做prez 和寫essay就行
reviews.translated_content: Coasted to an A-. The professor just reads off the slides. You don’t need to attend lectures; just find good teammates for the presentation and essay.

reviews.content: 有趣好玩
reviews.translated_content: Interesting and fun.

reviews.content:
Lecture: 主要由Peiyi執教，內地老師，有點緊張但很熱情，口語一般，PPT reader。一次Guest lecture是enrichment，一次是mid-term essay可選的主題之一。

Tutorial: Gabrie負責我的class，給的意見平平，如何令她歡心很重要（）小組作業選擇的主題可以定生死，請慎重考慮！！！

Workload: 大。個人部分兩次Essay（謎一般的標準），一次closed book Mid-term test（吃複習記憶力），一次open book Pop quiz，小組部分Video（需要剪輯），video proposal，storyboard（需要畫畫），peer review，PPT & presentation

不要被Prof和Tutor的友善及課上的放鬆氛圍騙了，不然看到Mid-term最後一題二選一essay的一個定義來自reading material一個來自PPT不起眼的小角落的模糊配圖你就老實了。此外，非常重要的選擇組員和選擇小組作業主題的環節要求在幾十分鐘內完成，實在是風險大。

整體評價: 不吃專業，但吃人際互動能力，選groupmate和Tutor搞好關係很重要。本人雖然小組和個人essay都在B range，但Test和Quiz高分，最後還是回到了A-。再次強調小組主題請謹慎選擇！
reviews.translated_content: Lecture: Mainly taught by Peiyi, a mainland China instructor. She is a bit nervous but enthusiastic, her spoken English is average, and she just reads off the slides. One guest lecture was for enrichment, and another was one of the optional topics for the midterm essay. Tutorial: Gabrie was responsible for my class. Her feedback was mediocre; knowing how to please her is important. The topic chosen for the group project can determine your fate, so please consider it carefully!!! Workload: Heavy. Individual components include two essays (with mysterious standards), one closed-book midterm test (tests memorisation), and one open-book pop quiz. Group components include a video (requires editing), video proposal, storyboard (requires drawing), peer review, and PPT & presentation. Don’t be fooled by the friendliness of the professor and tutor and the relaxed atmosphere in class. Otherwise, when you see that one definition in the final optional essay question of the midterm comes from the reading material and the other from an obscure image in a corner of the PPT, you’ll be humbled. Also, the very important steps of choosing groupmates and selecting the group project topic must be completed within tens of minutes, which is highly risky. Overall evaluation: It doesn’t require specific major knowledge, but it does require interpersonal skills. Choosing groupmates and building a good relationship with the tutor are important. Although my group and individual essays were in the B range, I scored highly on the test and quiz, so I ended up with an A-. Again, please choose your group topic carefully!

reviews.content: 不是很推荐，教授讲课很催眠，英文烫嘴，ppt reader，但是lecture不强制出席。wl比较大，feedback给得挺多的但是要求不明确，local tutor态度一般，不适合来水课的同学。
reviews.translated_content: Not highly recommended. The professor’s lectures are very soporific, his English is awkward, and he just reads off the slides, but lecture attendance is not mandatory. The workload is rather heavy. Although there is plenty of feedback, the requirements are unclear. The local tutor’s attitude is average. This course is not suitable for students looking for an easy ride.

reviews.content: good course. Prof. is very nice. TA is very helpful.
reviews.translated_content: good course. Prof. is very nice. TA is very helpful.

reviews.content: 不推荐，今年好像wl多了不少，tutor水平一般，避雷
reviews.translated_content: Not recommended. The workload seems to have increased significantly this year, and the tutors are average. Avoid this course.

reviews.content: 不计attendance，wl比较小，有两个quiz和两个essay和一个gp，没有大考试。出分B+，总体感觉凑活。guest lecture很有趣。tutor平常看着很严但是人其实挺好的，quiz请假或者补作业材料都不会难为你
reviews.translated_content: Attendance is not counted, and the workload is relatively light. There are two quizzes, two essays, and a group project, with no major exam. I received a B+, and overall it feels passable. The guest lectures are interesting. The tutor seems strict at first glance but is actually quite nice; they won't make things difficult if you request leave for a quiz or submit make-up materials.
