reviews.content: run
reviews.translated_content: Stay away.

reviews.content: Chad退休了，换了一个年轻老师，但后面教授可能还会换。整体workload略大，一学期两次essay加两次辩论。essay一次要写2500word，需要严格按要求一步步写，不然分会很低；辩论建议提前组好3人小队，每次都做好充足的准备。平时会组织coffee tutorial，也会有两次有关essay的线上tutorial。我第一次essay没按要求写，但最后龟也还可以。学期末教授会选出十个人课堂辩论，这些人龟会很高。如果对哲学不感兴趣也不想辩论的朋友建议润
reviews.translated_content: Chad has retired and been replaced by a younger instructor, though the professor might change again later. The overall workload is slightly heavy: two essays and two debates per semester. Each essay is 2,500 words and must follow the requirements step by step, otherwise your grade will be very low. For the debates, I recommend forming a three-person team early and preparing thoroughly each time. There are occasional coffee tutorials, plus two online tutorials focused on the essays. I didn’t follow the requirements for my first essay, but my grade was still acceptable. At the end of the semester, the professor selects ten students for an in-class debate; those students receive very high grades. If you’re not interested in philosophy or debating, I suggest you stay away.

reviews.content: The lecture content was quite difficult for me to follow and understand as I had no prior background knowledge in Chinese history or philosophy or even philosophy in general. However, overall the grade was pretty ok.
reviews.translated_content: The lecture content was quite difficult for me to follow and understand as I had no prior background knowledge in Chinese history or philosophy or even philosophy in general. However, overall the grade was pretty ok.

reviews.content: 一门讲诸子百家的课。Chad是认真做学问的那种老师，对中国古代哲学有很多自己独到的见解，而且人超好 超耐心负责，会额外组织coffee tutorial给同学答疑。wl不大，期中期末两篇paper，原来tutorial上有debate 由于网课原因tutorial取消，debate变成voluntary。课程设计很成体系，edx/mooc上有录好的网课，老师还编了一本textbook。只要认真学就会很有收获，给分也会很不错。总之 非常推荐！
reviews.translated_content: A course on the various schools of Chinese philosophy. Chad is a serious scholar with many unique insights into ancient Chinese philosophy. He is also extremely nice, patient, and responsible, and organises extra coffee tutorials to answer students' questions. The workload is not heavy; there are two papers for the midterm and final. There used to be debates in tutorials, but these were cancelled due to online classes and made voluntary. The course design is very systematic: there are recorded online lectures on edX/MOOC, and the teacher even compiled a textbook. If you study seriously, you will gain a lot, and the grading will be quite good. In short, highly recommended!

reviews.content: 感觉workload比较小，但是要拿A或A+的话，很需要之前对于中国古代思想的祭奠。文科生应该比较轻松，理科生慎选。
reviews.translated_content: The workload seems relatively light, but if you want an A or A+, you really need a solid foundation in ancient Chinese thought. It should be quite relaxed for humanities students, but science students should choose with caution.

reviews.content: A very fruitful course, Chad really loves teaching and has a lot of insights. You can’t miss it if you love Chinese philosophy (especially political and moral philosophy). Be active and you will have many chances to talk to him in person in his coffee tutorial.
reviews.translated_content: A very fruitful course, Chad really loves teaching and has a lot of insights. You can’t miss it if you love Chinese philosophy (especially political and moral philosophy). Be active and you will have many chances to talk to him in person in his coffee tutorial.

reviews.content: wl有点大，很努力的在准备每次debate和essay，龟是A
reviews.translated_content: The workload is a bit heavy. I worked hard preparing for every debate and essay. My grade was an A.

reviews.content: 能找到好队友非常重要！辩论没人能划水。自由分（三人一组），需要报同一个 Tutorial Group。辩论没人教，每次双方都有备而来，非常辛苦。Essay 就是辩论稿，也非常难写。不过 Online Course 和课本的质量很高，有外面没有的独到观点，决定读的话一定要认真看，会很有收获。
reviews.translated_content: Finding good teammates is crucial! No one can coast during the debates. The peer-assessment component is done in groups of three, and you must register for the same tutorial group. No one teaches you how to debate; both sides come fully prepared each time, which is very exhausting. The essay is essentially your debate script, and it’s also very difficult to write. However, the online course materials and textbook are of high quality, offering unique perspectives you won’t find elsewhere. If you decide to take this course, make sure to read them carefully; you’ll gain a lot.

reviews.content: wl巨大。mid 和final都有essay，需要很多准备。两次debate，很麻烦，很吃队友。新的教授英文很费劲，lecture也讲的不好，debate的feedback根本讲不明白。慎选。
reviews.translated_content: Huge workload. Both the midterm and final involve essays, requiring a lot of preparation. There are two debates, which are troublesome and heavily dependent on your teammates. The new professor struggles with English, delivers poor lectures, and the feedback on the debates is incomprehensible. Choose with caution.

reviews.content: workload低 online gp只看个人，跟组队也没啥关系（虽然组队是钦点的，同一个tuto的随机分） 龟还行 就quiz有点chur，看不看reading和做不做的对题没太大关系 tuto很nice
reviews.translated_content: Low workload. The online group project depends only on individual effort and has little to do with your team (although teams were assigned, randomly within the same tutorial). The grading is okay. Only the quizzes are a bit demanding; whether you do the readings or get the questions right doesn’t seem to matter much. The tutor is very nice.

reviews.content: Easy class, light workload. I am a law student but I would say this course doesn't require much prior law knowledge. Lecture attendance is optional, and pick Sarah for your tutorials for an easy time. Just do the final essay well, focus heavily on readings for one specific topic (+ do your own research) and you will do well. Choose one topic to cover in detail and forget about the rest. A grade
教授很好，风趣幽默，好龟
reviews.translated_content: The professor is great, witty and humorous, and the grading is generous.

reviews.content: 涵盖的内容不少，法律经济政治都有涉猎，我个人比较感兴趣。80％的得分来源于期末2000字论文+录视频对论文做presentation，剩下20应该是平时的attendance。wl算正常，但把论文都放到revision week去做会很扑街。
reviews.translated_content: Covers a lot of content, touching on law, economics, and politics, which I personally find interesting. 80% of the grade comes from a 2000-word final essay plus a video presentation of the essay, and the remaining 20% is likely for attendance. The workload is normal, but leaving the essay until Reading Week will lead to disaster.

reviews.content: 本人FBE学生 第一节课开始就有点云里雾里的跟不上教授在讲什么了。。。因为没有介绍课是要做什么的 一直都没听太懂 加上男lecturer有点ppt reader导致经常犯困 tut会点名发言 有2篇essay和1个单独pre 最后实在顶不住了late drop了  这门课不是给非law学生上的。。。
reviews.translated_content: I’m a Business School student. From the first lecture, I was a bit confused and couldn’t keep up with what the professor was talking about... Because there was no introduction to what the course required, I never really understood it. Plus, the male lecturer is a bit of a slide-reader, which often made me sleepy. Tutorials require roll call and speaking. There are two essays and one individual presentation. I eventually couldn’t handle it and late-dropped the course. This course isn’t designed for non-Law students...

reviews.content: tutor好人，好🐢，tutorial多发言，essay认真写，最后A。
reviews.translated_content: The tutor is nice and grading is generous. Speak up more in tutorials, write your essay carefully, and you will get an A in the end.

reviews.content: law院开的课，挺偏文的，如果对自己essay能力不是很自信的话慎选。两次essay得分都是23/30，除此之外还看tut发言情况和一个prez（有质量发言的那种orz网课听不清问题我吃了不少亏233）
reviews.translated_content: This is a course offered by the Faculty of Law, so it leans heavily towards humanities. Choose with caution if you're not very confident in your essay-writing skills. I scored 23/30 on both essays. Other assessment components include tutorial participation and a presentation (the kind where quality contributions matter). I suffered quite a bit because I couldn't hear the questions clearly during online classes, haha.

reviews.content: real boring course. lectures require logbook written almost every time. a lot of presentations in the tutorials
reviews.translated_content: real boring course. lectures require logbook written almost every time. a lot of presentations in the tutorials

reviews.content: 课程涵盖内容广泛，readings读不读关系不大，tutorial跟tutor好好沟通是关键。
reviews.translated_content: The course covers a wide range of content. Whether you do the readings doesn’t matter much; the key is to communicate well with your tutor in tutorials.

reviews.content: 好课，wl 不大，教授讲的有意思，但涉猎范围较广，需要对法律政治经济多方面都有一定储备，跟课才更丝滑。为tut 准备pre的时间较多，幸好组里法学学姐带飞
reviews.translated_content: Good course. The workload is not heavy, and the professor lectures in an interesting way. However, the scope is broad, so you need some background knowledge in law, politics, and economics to follow the class smoothly. Preparing presentations for tutorials takes a lot of time; fortunately, a senior student in my group who studied law carried the team.

reviews.content: law院生，B+，lecture不强制参加，讲课有意思也没意思，个人很喜欢刘庄老师的课，虽然没拿到Arange。正常上课，wl巨巨巨巨巨小，就最后一篇essay，可能会有那种很小的presentation。总之这门课没花我什么什么时间，可以接受它给分玄学（因为就一篇essay定胜负）。
reviews.translated_content: Law student here, got a B+. Lecture attendance is not mandatory. The lectures were interesting and uninteresting at the same time. I personally really enjoyed Prof Liu Zhuang’s classes, even though I didn’t get an A-range grade. Regular classes, extremely light workload—just one final essay, and maybe a very small presentation. In short, this course didn’t take much of my time. I can accept that the grading is opaque and unpredictable (since it’s just one essay that decides everything).

reviews.content: 这学期第一次开的cc，课程内容主要讲了内地和香港历史上的联系，两边政治、经济、金融体系（占大部分）的区别和关系，对于FBE学生还是比较友好的，可能上完FINA2330之后对一些知识点的理解会更快一点，但就算没有这门课的基础也是没有问题的。我认为这门课还是比较有用的，尤其是对于打算在香港从事金融行业的同学，了解QDII, QFII, Stock Connect (North/Southbound)等这些连接内地和香港金融体系的渠道对实习初期去看懂一些趋势是很有帮助的。上课讲的东西大部分时间确实比较无聊，Lec没有出勤记录。Tutorial attendance占25%，缺过一节，基本每次tut稳定发言1-2次；Group project占35%，pre+report，每个小组六人合作完成一个课题研究最后一节课上演讲，得分没有公布，但是感觉不错。Final占40%，选择和小essay，因为第一次开没有pp，背lec ppt和tut material就完事了，最后A。
reviews.translated_content: This was the first time this Common Core course was offered this semester. The content mainly covered the historical connections between mainland China and Hong Kong, and the differences and relationships between their political, economic, and financial systems (which accounted for the majority). It is relatively friendly for FBE students; having taken FINA2330 might help you understand some points faster, but it’s not a problem if you haven’t. I think this course is quite useful, especially for students planning to work in finance in Hong Kong. Understanding channels connecting the mainland and Hong Kong financial systems, such as QDII, QFII, and Stock Connect (North/Southbound), is very helpful for understanding trends during the early stages of an internship. Most of the lecture content is indeed quite boring. There is no attendance record for lectures. Tutorial attendance accounts for 25%. I missed one session and generally spoke 1–2 times steadily in each tutorial. The group project accounts for 35%, involving a presentation and a report. Each group of six collaborates on a research topic and presents in the last class. Scores were not published, but it felt good. The final exam accounts for 40%, consisting of multiple-choice questions and short essays. Since it was the first offering, there were no past papers, so just memorizing the lecture PPTs and tutorial materials was enough. I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: 烂中烂 wl巨大无比 每周有一堆reading tutorial记participation 每节课三到四个问题都特别难 给的准备时间特别少 课堂大家竞争很激烈 report花时间很多 要求很高 还有Final group meeting 回答教授犀利的问题 lecture 内容很多很杂 对非商科生很不友好 Final 要写essay还有10道mc 没有pp 考两小时 还不知道给🐢咋样
reviews.translated_content: One of the worst of the worst. The workload is huge. Every week there’s a bunch of reading, tutorials count participation, and every class has three to four questions that are particularly difficult with very little preparation time given. Competition in class is fierce. Reports take a lot of time and have high requirements. There’s also a final group meeting where you answer the professor’s sharp questions. Lecture content is abundant and messy, very unfriendly to non-business students. The final requires an essay and 10 multiple-choice questions. There are no past papers, the exam lasts two hours, and I still don’t know how the grading is.

reviews.content: 神人教授，攻击性极强无比，对于gp要求非常高 学期中一个group project outline交上去被一顿攻击，说是研究不充分，没有呈现出小组已经有的研究结果…… 怀着passion选的课然后已经赤了一坨大石，极其无语 期末再来追评
reviews.translated_content: The professor is a real character—extremely aggressive—and has very high requirements for the group project. In the middle of the semester, I submitted a group project outline and got attacked for it, being told the research was insufficient and that we hadn’t presented the results our group already had... I chose this course with passion, but now I’m carrying a huge burden. Seriously speechless. Will add a follow-up review after the finals.

reviews.content:
中肯的来说不懂金融政治经济的可以不要选了。想知道课程框架可以看一楼。
考试：30分mc（考10题陈述题选哪几条对） 70分SQ essay 
没提示（唯一可能就是说不用记数据和事实，因为事实自然会从分析里出来，但是考的不是资料分析题），没pp，没有送分题，不考记数据，但很多数据图。教授说Lecture里很多slides你认真听课的话就知道那个slide跳过了不用考，但教授停在一个数据图上走来走去讲了15分钟课。当然讲得很有深度很有例子，但很多人没听。我看他讲了那么久，但我没有slide文字辅助跟不上。Lecture内容很多长难句，考验备课，希望因为exam然后拿A的人一下就碎了。Tutorial reading的内容也会考SQ essay问题。问时事背后的分析，经济原因。
Tutorial：（需要拍TA上课的内容要考，不上载moodle。TA性格挺好）
tutorial问的问题很难，问完给你10分钟和其他人讨论，可以看到很多人都用ai来gen回答，当然也有大神一下子就讨论了。问题读了reading你不一定能回答上来，reading有几个链接，给我最深印象就是第一个星期要读一个官方文件很多页，但TA讲了概要之后，问的问题和文件没那么大关系，可能有一题有关系。问题主要就是要你用思维去想一个有深度的分析香港和大陆的经济发展。没思维的人跟不上。
Lec：
教授讲第一课讲了很多堂课，期间几次取消课，
最后没教完第七课，需要加一个星期回去上课（本来以为有考试提示，老师说没出完考卷），剩下11天要考试了。总共7个file，第一个file第一堂课70多页，之后加到100多页，讲香港经济review。
group project：
超自由自定经济相关课题写report，很多人写的topic feedback是和课件撞内容了、内容广泛，不是不可以但是要大部分内容有深度分析。
要教授feedback才知道写的对不对头，但group project大纲 feedback虽然很中肯（没用心+不够深度，反馈根据每段内容写了很多字，很多问句），但是每次课堂上email说好给的feedback的日期一拖再拖，最后剩下短时间ddl收到feedback发现要大改。（可能因为组多？）。很考验有否有实力的队友，考验teamwork，present其实是最后一个星期要问所有人知不知道整份写了什么概念内容，为什么这么写。

教授：希望大家读cc不是为了水和高grade，而是去认真学，认真扩展视野额外知识。很中肯，送给想选这课的你。
如果你选这课过了半个sem的水日子，就完蛋咯。

对一楼课程内容很有兴趣的人可以读，有大湾区，货币政策等等，挺有深度。
reviews.translated_content: To be fair, if you don’t understand finance, politics, or economics, you might want to skip this course. You can check the first post for the course framework. Exam: 30 marks MC (10 statements, select which ones are correct), 70 marks SQ essay. No hints (the only possible hint is that you don’t need to memorise data and facts, as facts naturally emerge from analysis, but the exam isn’t a data-analysis question type). No past papers, no easy-mark questions. It doesn’t test rote memorisation of data, but there are many data charts. The professor said that if you listen carefully to the lecture, you’ll know which slides are skipped and won’t be tested, but he stopped at a data chart, walked back and forth, and lectured for 15 minutes. Of course, the depth and examples were great, but many people didn’t listen. I watched him speak for so long, but without text on the slides to support me, I couldn’t keep up. The lecture content has many long, complex sentences, testing your preparation. Those hoping to get an A just by cramming for the exam will shatter. Tutorial reading content will also appear in SQ essay questions, asking for analysis behind current events and economic reasons. Tutorial: (You need to photograph what the TA covers in class as it will be tested; it’s not uploaded to Moodle. The TA has a nice personality.) The questions asked in tutorials are difficult. After asking, they give you 10 minutes to discuss with others. You can see many people using AI to generate answers, though some experts can discuss immediately. Reading the material doesn’t guarantee you can answer; the readings have several links. The deepest impression was the first week, where we had to read an official document of many pages, but after the TA summarised it, the questions asked weren’t closely related to the document, maybe only one question was. The questions mainly require you to use critical thinking to provide a deep analysis of Hong Kong and mainland China’s economic development. Those without this mindset can’t keep up. Lecture: The professor spent many classes on the first lesson, cancelling class several times. In the end, he didn’t finish Lesson 7, requiring an extra week of make-up classes (I thought there would be exam hints, but the teacher said the exam paper wasn’t finished). With 11 days left before the exam. There are 7 files in total; the first file for the first class is over 70 pages, later increasing to over 100 pages, reviewing Hong Kong’s economy. Group project: Extremely free choice of economics-related topics for a report. Many people’s topic feedback indicated overlap with courseware content and broad scope. It’s not forbidden, but most content requires deep analysis. You need the professor’s feedback to know if you’re on the right track. Although the group project outline feedback was fair (not diligent + insufficient depth; the feedback included many words and questions based on each paragraph), the dates promised via email for feedback in class were delayed repeatedly. Finally, receiving feedback with a short deadline remaining revealed the need for major revisions. (Maybe because there were many groups?) It really tests whether you have capable teammates and teamwork. The presentation is actually in the last week, asking everyone if they know the concepts written in the entire report and why it was written that way. Professor: He hopes everyone takes Common Core courses not to coast and get easy grades, but to learn seriously and broaden their horizons with additional knowledge. Very fair advice for those considering this course. If you spend the first half of the semester coasting in this course, you’re done for. Those interested in the course content mentioned in the first post can read it; it covers the Greater Bay Area, monetary policy, etc., and is quite deep.

reviews.content: wl巨大无比，每节tutorial需要抢着发言（participation占30%）；group project和教授约了好几次meeting，写了非常多内容，很考验组队。final前lec基本没去过，四天速通所有内容lec资料全部背过基本就能好🐢。final选择不太确定，大题也有一些没完全写出来最后还是A了。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is huge. You need to fight to speak up in every tutorial (participation accounts for 30%). For the group project, we scheduled several meetings with the professor and wrote a lot of content, which really tests your team dynamics. I basically skipped lectures before the final; cramming through all the lecture materials in four days and memorizing them is enough to get a good grade. I wasn’t sure about some multiple-choice questions in the final, and didn’t fully complete some long-answer questions, but I still got an A in the end.

reviews.content: 要用五百元買map，可以同group一齊買，3張ws，要畫map。個人覺得非常輕鬆，自己係理科人，DSE無讀geog+平時無行山都覺得無問題（風景超靚，好玩）。有條3分鐘既片要拍，一個人可以做到既workload，分了十二份，可想言之有多簡單。group project 同 ws hea 做，最後A range!  Tutor 選擇除Nixon/Vincent 外，水到爆。
reviews.translated_content: You need to buy a map for HK$500, which you can split with your group. There are three worksheets that require drawing maps. I found it very relaxing; as a science student who didn’t study geography in the DSE and doesn’t usually go hiking, I had no problems (the scenery is beautiful and it’s fun). There is a 3-minute video to shoot, which is a manageable workload for one person. Since the work was divided into twelve parts, you can imagine how simple it was. We coasted through the group project and worksheets, and I ended up with an A-range grade. Except for Nixon and Vincent, the tutors are incredibly easy-going.

reviews.content: 沒有final 會看各種地圖和會寫和這course標題相關聯的essay 就能A range
reviews.translated_content: There is no final exam. You look at various maps and write essays related to the course title, and you can get an A-range grade.

reviews.content: 喜欢行山郊游的必不可错过。对体能有一定要求，但是挺好玩的，风景很好

reviews.content: Fun course, with 2-3 field trips, 3 worksheets and a project video

reviews.content: 选tutor时要慎重 不会粤语建议选Vincent 其他tutor field trip全程粤语 写邮件申诉也无用 btw爬山很累 不喜爬山的要慎重

The other tutors use Cantonese exclusively during the field trip, and emailing to appeal is useless. By the way, the hiking is tiring; if you don’t like hiking, choose with caution.

reviews.content: chill tutor KT Liu 很自由 爬山少了 不會很累
reviews.translated_content: Chill tutor KT Liu. Very free and easy. Fewer hiking trips, so it’s not too tiring.

reviews.content: wl有点大 3个worksheet还有field trip不过挺好玩的 要买地图，听说是可以大家一起买不过我没有，hku找那些人买是可以打折，小组作业拍视频 剪辑很辛苦，最后a-
reviews.translated_content: The workload is a bit heavy: three worksheets and a field trip, though the trip was quite fun. You need to buy a map; I heard you can buy it together with others to get a discount, but I didn’t do that. Buying from certain people at HKU can get you a discount. The group assignment involves filming and editing a video, which was very tough. I ended up with an A-.

reviews.content: 不 会 粤 语 快 跑 这 课 全 是 港 人 自 己 玩
reviews.translated_content: If you don’t speak Cantonese, run away. This course is entirely for Hong Kong locals to play among themselves.

reviews.content: 这节课全是local，是一个认识local的好机会，但建议会粤语的参加。wl小，只有3个field trip worksheet和一个12人一起做的3min视频。field trip是mandatory的，默认讲粤语，今年是魔鬼山，鹤咀，芝加哥大学香港校园和盐田梓。需要去政府花约470hkd买地图以完成worksheet，这应该就是workload最大的一部分。喜欢爬山，看自然风光的不要错过nixon的tutor（001/003/005等单数tutorial），除了全部人都要参加的3个ft外，nixon会组织无数个爬山活动（记bonus。lecture好像不计attendance但会随机刷新quiz，lecture无聊且不怎么相关。之前说这门课a range很多，靓龟，但是被大学打击了a range人数大大减少，本人去了nixon组织的差不多一半的bonus trip，worksheet比较hea的写了（能copy则copy），本来预计能拿a range 的，最后b+
reviews.translated_content: This class is full of local Hong Kong students, so it’s a good chance to get to know them, but I recommend joining only if you speak Cantonese. The workload is light, consisting of just three field trip worksheets and a 3-minute video made by a group of 12. The field trips are mandatory and conducted mostly in Cantonese. This year’s locations were Devil’s Peak, Cape D’Aguilar, the University of Chicago Hong Kong Campus, and Yim Tin Tsai. You need to buy a map from the government for about HKD 470 to complete the worksheets, which is probably the biggest part of the workload. If you like hiking and enjoying nature, don’t miss Nixon’s tutorials (001/003/005 and other odd-numbered sections). In addition to the three mandatory field trips for everyone, Nixon organises countless bonus hiking trips (for extra credit). Lecture attendance doesn’t seem to be counted, but random quizzes pop up; the lectures are boring and not very relevant. It was said that this course had many A-range grades and generous grading, but the university cracked down, greatly reducing the number of A-range grades. I went on about half of the bonus trips organised by Nixon, wrote the worksheets in a relaxed way (copying where possible), and originally expected an A-range grade, but finally got a B+.

reviews.content: 靓grad wl小 有意思 大家快冲！
reviews.translated_content: Good grades, low workload, and interesting content. Everyone, go for it!

course_info.title: The Rule of Law in Modern China
course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: 1.grade：law院课，law院内网给出的grade distribution显示，最常见的得分大概是B+左右，往年从未有A+（不适合冲四刷分的大佬），得到A（也就是真正能得到的最高分）的比例大概是5-6%。 2.内容：适合对法律，历史，政治感兴趣的同学上。主要讲了中国大陆近代与现代的法治史，也有涉及香港台湾。老师讲课略有枯燥，但是内容本身有意义，有助于帮助人真正了解中国近些年的发展。对非law院学生难度适中，如果对这个话题感兴趣，可以选。 3.测试形式：主要是Group Project与3000字 Essay。GP需要找好队友，因为是按组给分，队友拉垮很要命。Essay话题很多，建议早点选好，从学期开始就准备起来，多搜集资料，批判性整合分析。 4.题外话：workload中偏略高（对文科生而言）。lecture可以不听，tutorial认真参加，Essay早点准备，找到窍门，就能水出一个过得去的grade。
reviews.translated_content: 1. Grades: This is a Law Faculty course. The grade distribution shown on the Law Faculty intranet indicates that the most common score is around B+. There has never been an A+ in previous years (not suitable for experts aiming for a GPA above 4.0 or boosting grades). The proportion of students getting an A (which is effectively the highest achievable grade) is about 5–6%. 2. Content: Suitable for students interested in law, history, and politics. It mainly covers the history of the rule of law in modern and contemporary mainland China, also touching on Hong Kong and Taiwan. The lectures are slightly dry, but the content itself is meaningful and helps people truly understand China’s recent development. The difficulty is moderate for non-Law students; if you are interested in this topic, you can choose it. 3. Assessment format: Mainly a Group Project and a 3,000-word Essay. For the GP, you need to find good teammates because grading is by group, and useless teammates can be fatal. There are many essay topics; it is recommended to choose early and start preparing from the beginning of the semester, gathering more materials for critical integration and analysis. 4. Side note: The workload is medium-to-high (for humanities students). You can skip lectures, attend tutorials seriously, prepare for the essay early, and find the tricks, and you can coast to a passable grade.

reviews.translated_content: Jean Lee is originally from the Faculty of Law and was tutoring this course for the first year. She started by saying that previous generous grading belonged to the past and had nothing to do with her. The tutor is very guiding; in the first class, she got to know each student’s growth and educational background, and subsequently asked questions based on that understanding. Although the tutor is nice, I find the tutorials really exhausting because they require long speeches, demanding high English proficiency and careful reading. The tutor genuinely awards participation marks based on contributions. As a student with a Gaokao background, the tutor liked calling on me to speak and was often satisfied with my answers, so my participation marks were probably decent. During our presentation, the tutor found faults in our work and kept us on stage looking for them for a long time. Also, the tutor is quite rigid, requiring strict adherence to instructions for essays. My essay outline was rather divergent, so she directly said it was off-topic. I had to rewrite it and submit it directly, which felt like a gamble. I was quite anxious before the grades came out due to various issues at the end of the term, but getting an A- felt acceptable, especially since the tutor is from the Faculty of Law. I did not experience the generous grading others mentioned, but getting an A- from a Law faculty member is satisfying enough for me.

reviews.content: Saw that there aren't any reviews of the course for the past 2 years, so decided to provide a comprehensive review here. Took this course in semester 2, 2024-2025. Lectures are usually a must, as Professor Hun may take attendance at the end of the lecture with a poll about a subjective topic. Most of these polls happen before the mid-term, though this can be subjected to change. Tutorials are rather "chur", as speaking is not enough; if you speak out your point, Professor Hun may ask for clarification or question you about the point you just made. Naturally, you may feel embarrassed if you can't explain at all. However, Professor Hun herself is "chill"; very relaxed and easygoing, and she's very knowledgeable about the topic in the CC. Critical review paper is quite difficult, because what you are critically reviewing is actually one of the required readings in this CC. These readings are written by highly knowledgeable professors on corruption, while you, a rookie in the academic field of studying corruption (you've barely learnt one month worth of knowledge), have to critically review the reading. After vigorously studying and putting hard work on the paper, I got a C+ in the paper. Not great, but I know that others have received Ds and even Fs, so it's good enough. In the group project, you should be split into 4 or 5 people; grouping is based on tutorials, so if your friend's in this course too, and you want him to be your groupmate, tell him/her to register the same tutorial as yourself. Hence, the number of people in your group really depends on the number of people in your tutorial. Workload for group projects can be medium, but I chose the beaten path and did around 25-30% of the work in a group of 5 (this was completely voluntary). Hence, it was quite chur for me (not as chur as 9044/Dunhuang), but you could work less if you don't aim very high. In the end, my final grade was A-, so it's pretty good. Note that this semester still does not include a field trip to the ICAC due to ongoing maintenance works, but it can be expected that the trip could happen next year. Instead, a lecture hosted by an ICAC official from their Community Relations dept was done instead. Pretty boring (though the lectures in the entire semester can be very boring unless you actively take notes, and I believe the professor knows about this since it's a niche topic). If you are interested or at least do not dislike the topic of corruption and anticorruption, I think you'll be okay. You really have to read the readings (required + suggested) before each tutorial (or use AI to give you the gist of the readings first) to express your point unless you're already knowledgeable in the topic. Also, taking notes is quite important because Professor Hun won't send the lecture PPT out throughout the entire semester, so if you want to review them for tutorial or use it for group projects, taking notes is necessary. I would not suggest this CC if you don't like grade ambiguity (more effort =/= higher grade) or is just completely disinterested on the field of social sciences (if you're just a science guy with little to no interest to the topic, best to avoid). You may find problems like not understanding what was taught (which is understandable, I barely understood much until the midterm), getting a lower-than-expected grade despite your best efforts, or finding the topic less interesting than you expected. All in all, the course itself is slightly demanding and quite stressful, but it's a good course in CCCH. Highly encouraged to register if you believe that you can handle what I said above and have understood what will happen during the course.

reviews.translated_content: First, the grade: A. Assessment breakdown: one video presentation + one individual review (around 800 words?) + tutorial participation and mini presentations + a small attendance component. Overall, the workload is light; skimming the weekly readings is enough to contribute in tutorials. I think showing your face in tutorials might help with other components, but it’s best to focus your comments on the key points the lecturer raised in class and appropriately reference what she said in the large lectures. None of the assignments or presentations receive feedback or returned marks, so the grading feels a bit like a black box, but it is fair. The lecturer’s classes and course planning are both interesting; I think this is a course worth taking.

reviews.content: 真心好龟课，理学院的我最后拿了A+真的感动得哭了😭。教授和tutor人都很nice，上课和tutorial只要出席即可平时成绩满分。上课内容很多还是蛮有趣的，但因为不用考而且跟essay关系不大也基本忘了，不过学完确实对丝路和佛教有了更深的认识。 最关心的：Workload不大，要做的只有以下四个 一个5分钟填完的midterm quiz（会给一些slides去背，但比高中历史简单多了，题目不刁钻，好好背就能拿高分。） 一个field trip report（比写旅游博客稍微学术一些就好，去的是慈山寺，里面很不一样，比如用water offering替代上香。听说自己预约要提前至少两个月）。 一个group project，有三个主题选，两个做ppt的正常prez一个是历史人物表演。我们组选了表演的，workload出奇的小而且效果尤其好（因为看见崔老师一直在笑感觉她挺喜欢的）。当然也是因为遇上了很棒的组友，有人借了汉服有人表演功底极佳。 一个3000词的essay（会在刚开学就给topics，可以用一整个学期慢慢写。ddl是在复习周刚开始的时候，期末可能有点累，但这样就完全不会影响复习周。如果比较早写完还能发给老师和tutor改。会给几十个topics来选，一般都能找到自己喜欢的。比如我一个理科生写的是禅学主题的，写到后面甚至有点想出家哈哈哈哈。） 总而言之这门课真心可以选，好龟评价也持续了几年了，值得信赖啊！
reviews.translated_content: Truly a GPA-friendly course. As a Science Faculty student, I was moved to tears when I finally got an A+ 😭. The professor and tutor are both very nice. You just need to attend lectures and tutorials to get full marks for participation. The lecture content is quite interesting, but since there’s no exam and it’s not very relevant to the essay, I’ve mostly forgotten it. However, I did gain a deeper understanding of the Silk Road and Buddhism after taking the course. Most importantly: The workload is not heavy. You only need to do the following four things: 1. A 5-minute midterm quiz (slides are provided for memorisation, but it’s much easier than high school history; the questions aren’t tricky, so you can get a high score if you memorise well). 2. A field trip report (just needs to be slightly more academic than a travel blog. We went to Tsz Shan Monastery, which is quite different, e.g., using water offerings instead of incense. I heard you need to book at least two months in advance if you go on your own). 3. A group project with three theme options: two involve normal PowerPoint presentations, and one is a historical role-play. Our group chose the role-play. The workload was surprisingly small, and the effect was especially good (because I saw Professor Chui smiling throughout, I felt she liked it). Of course, this was also because we had great teammates; someone borrowed Hanfu costumes, and someone had excellent acting skills. 4. A 3,000-word essay (topics are given at the start of the semester, so you can write it slowly over the whole term. The deadline is at the beginning of Reading Week, so it might be tiring during finals, but it won’t interfere with your revision week. If you finish early, you can send it to the teacher and tutor for feedback. Dozens of topics are provided, so you can usually find one you like. For example, as a science student, I wrote about Zen Buddhism, and by the end, I even felt like becoming a monk hahaha). All in all, this course is highly recommended. Its reputation for generous grading has lasted for several years, so it’s trustworthy!

reviews.content:

1. 感谢小组成员，gp一定要找积极的组员，我们是一开始建群的时候自己组队的，比tutorial上组队的感觉要更凝聚一些，完成gp的时候大家非常积极配合，分工明确，所以每个人分到的部分都不多。再次感恩！
2. 对自己essay非常满意，和tutor邮件确认后知道是A-，有一些格式和AI上的小错漏所以内容从A掉到A-，也算是很好的提醒和提高。
3. 课上其实不听也行，因为感觉用英文听佛教传承这些生词很多有点费劲，感兴趣可以课后钻研一下。lecture随机掉落bonus chance，对我这种每节lec都去的人非常友好
4. Tutorial一定要去。很大程度上影响你的atten+bonus point，且tutor人很好可以随时和她普通话/粤语/Eng讨论问题或者consult ur essay
5. field trip很好玩吧平时不会静下心去看展，对喜欢历史的人很友好，我们去的是唐朝的展，关于佛教起源与exchange这一块唐朝还是很重要的一个交融与传承的朝代，拍拍照回去搓个ppt在tutorial上pre就好了，会发传单于是没记什么东西。
6. 最后是大家最关心的quiz环节，field trip前后的时间教授就会上传quiz专属ppt全背下来是可以稳85+的，这个quiz相当于期中但只占10%，很简单，文科生友好。
综上所述，倾情推荐，教授和tutor都是好人！可以课间或者预约consultation（都可以说普通话）
reviews.translated_content: Highly recommended. I got an A, and the workload was light aside from a 3,000-word essay. 1. Thanks to my group members. For the group project, make sure to find active members. We formed our own group at the beginning via chat, which felt more cohesive than grouping up during tutorials. Everyone cooperated actively with clear division of labour during the GP, so each person had a small share. Grateful again! 2. I was very satisfied with my essay. After confirming with the tutor via email, I learned it was an A-. Some minor formatting and AI-related errors caused the content grade to drop from an A to an A-, which served as a good reminder and area for improvement. 3. You don't really need to listen in class, as listening to Buddhist heritage terms in English feels a bit strenuous due to the unfamiliar vocabulary; if interested, you can study it after class. Bonus opportunities appear randomly in lectures, which is very friendly for someone like me who attends every lecture. 4. You must attend tutorials. They largely affect your attendance and bonus points, and the tutor is very nice; you can discuss problems or consult on your essay with her in Mandarin, Cantonese, or English anytime. 5. The field trip was fun. Usually, I wouldn't calm down to visit exhibitions, but it's friendly for history lovers. We went to a Tang Dynasty exhibition. The Tang Dynasty is an important period for integration and inheritance regarding the origins of Buddhism and exchange. Just take photos, go back, make a PPT, and present it in the tutorial. Handouts were provided, so I didn't take many notes. 6. Finally, the quiz segment everyone cares about most: the professor uploads a quiz-specific PPT around the time of the field trip. If you memorise it all, you can securely score 85+. This quiz is like a midterm but only worth 10%; it's very simple and friendly for humanities students. In summary, highly recommended. Both the professor and tutor are good people! You can talk to them between classes or book consultations (Mandarin is fine).

reviews.content: 网课改了assessment，3000字的essay，gp和tutorial，quiz和lecture，每节tutorial每人都要做一个两三分钟的小presentation，要自己做一个五页作业的ppt，topic每周四五出，可以多选一，ddl是下周周一下午，reading不少，小部分能找到中文版。quiz会划范围，认真背就没什么问题。essay字数上限是3000，建议早点开始写，可以和prof或者tutor讨论essay的规划，但写完之后prof和tutor不会给修改，也不会提出任何意见。gp是五到八人的（一个组的gp展示总时间取决于全组人数，人均三分钟），可以选presentation也可以选play，我们组选的presentation，组员都很努力，最后完成得还可以，但我们组不算特别出彩。lecture一开始听完全听不懂，专有名词太多了，但是听到后面还可以，有些话题还比较有意思。全部的课和作业会在revision week之前全部结束，不会影响别的科目复习。总体来说wl不算小，🐢也还可以，A range，和努力成正比吧（我是理学院的，这种essay也是第一次写😂）。一开始听这门课会感觉有些不太适应（会感觉听不懂，reading多，每周都有作业），但希望选这门课的同学可以坚持下去，努力会有回报哒！
reviews.translated_content: The online class changed the assessment: a 3,000-word essay, a group project, tutorials, quizzes, and lectures. In every tutorial, each person has to give a two- to three-minute mini-presentation and make a five-slide PowerPoint for their assignment. Topics are released every Thursday or Friday, with multiple choices available. The deadline is the following Monday afternoon. There is quite a lot of reading, though a small portion can be found in Chinese. The quiz scope is outlined, so if you memorise it carefully, there shouldn’t be any problems. The word limit for the essay is 3,000 words; I suggest starting early. You can discuss the essay plan with the professor or tutor, but after you finish writing, neither the professor nor the tutor will provide edits or any feedback. The group project involves five to eight people (the total presentation time for a group depends on the number of members, with three minutes per person). You can choose between a presentation or a play; our group chose a presentation. The members worked hard, and we completed it reasonably well, though our group wasn’t particularly outstanding. At first, I couldn’t understand the lectures at all because there were too many technical terms, but it got better later on, and some topics were quite interesting. All classes and assignments finish before Reading Week, so it won’t affect revision for other subjects. Overall, the workload isn’t small, but the grading is okay (A range), and it’s proportional to your effort (I’m from the Science Faculty, and this was my first time writing this kind of essay 😂). At first, taking this course feels a bit uncomfortable (you might feel like you don’t understand, there’s a lot of reading, and weekly assignments), but I hope those who choose this course will stick with it. Your efforts will pay off!

reviews.content: Lectures可以skip，睇notes就夠；tutorial要講多啲嘢

reviews.content: 第一个评论！ 总体来说感觉wl特别小，只要每次上课都去，每节课都参加讨论，然后最后几个人一起出一张海报（或者一个视频）就可以了。本来以为自己每一个都很认真做了，然后还没有偷懒做海报而是做了视频会好龟，最后也不过是个B+，超失望。 课程的内容的确让人有点收获，认真听的话能引发不少思考，但本身作为一门CC课不可能非常深入... 总体是不会劝退的一门课，内地生很少，算半个宝藏吧。
reviews.translated_content: First review! Overall, the workload feels very light. As long as you attend every class, participate in discussions each session, and then collaborate with a few others on one poster (or video) at the end, you’ll be fine. I thought I had done everything seriously, and instead of slacking off with a poster, I made a video expecting a good grade, but in the end, I only got a B+. Super disappointed. The course content does offer some gains; if you listen carefully, it can spark quite a bit of thought, but as a Common Core course, it can’t go very deep... Overall, it’s not a course to avoid. There are few students from Mainland China, so it’s somewhat of a hidden gem.

reviews.content: wl乍一看挺大的，但是只要对中国政治有一定理解就完全可以不看一点reading张口就来。每节lecture最后有个3道选择题的小quiz,上课前把课件看完就可以全做出来。tutorial一定要找好队友一起去上，期末考试是组队画海报或者做视频，所以队友最好有一个人要会画画或者剪视频。我随机的组里3个free rider只留我一个人把视频做了，不知道教授是不是心疼我给了个A-
reviews.translated_content: At first glance, the workload seems heavy, but if you have some understanding of Chinese politics, you can answer everything off the top of your head without doing any reading. At the end of each lecture, there’s a short quiz with three multiple-choice questions; if you finish reading the slides before class, you can get them all right. For tutorials, make sure to find good teammates to attend with. The final exam is a team project to create a poster or a video, so ideally, one teammate should know how to draw or edit video. In my randomly assigned group, three free riders left me to make the video alone. I don’t know if the professor felt sorry for me, but I got an A-.

reviews.content: 嗯…就是说，几乎每周tutorial都要两人一组pre，有那么一两次pre还需要你提前看影片并且做剪裁和比较，tutor严厉，wl比想象中大不少，然后每次上课的时候lecture notes翻一下就可以，上课无聊，quiz挺难的，每节课三道题而且记分，最后需要做一个pre和poster。当时6人小组遇到好几个freerider，难受，虽然最后Arange
reviews.translated_content: Well… basically, almost every tutorial requires a pair presentation. Once or twice, you also need to watch videos in advance and edit/compare them. The tutor is strict, and the workload is significantly heavier than expected. During lectures, you can just flip through the lecture notes; the classes are boring. The quizzes are quite hard—three graded questions per class. In the end, you need to do a presentation and a poster. My six-person group had several free riders, which was frustrating, although I ended up with an A-range grade.

reviews.content: workload很小，lecture也可以不听，但tutorial一定要参加。觉得没学到什么东西吧（可能因为我不感兴趣）就logbook, group pre。总之推荐想水课的同学吧，还不知道最后得分是啥
reviews.translated_content: The workload is very light. You can skip lectures, but you must attend tutorials. I feel like I didn’t learn much (maybe because I wasn’t interested). There were just a logbook and a group presentation. In short, I recommend this to students looking for an easy course. I don’t know what the final grade will be yet.

reviews.content: 总体而言，教授口音迷幻，tutor虾仁猪心，课堂逻辑混乱，还很看组员。 每堂课最后会要求写一个200字左右的logbook，占最后总分的30％（如果我没记错的话）。简单来说就是防止大家翘lecture，然并卵还是很多人不来上课。logbook要求体现出critical thinking，但是问题就在tutor和prof十分口是心非，在tuto上指出该怎么做之后，我反正就算这么做了也没拿到a，加上大概只有两份logbook会被给分，对自己总分最后的评估不确定因素还挺大的。没有考试，有一个group presentation，主题是解读一个China story，可以从field trip干了什么出发。我和我小组一开始偏题被评价最多拿c.... 但是最后的gp没有讲ft又回到题目上了（刺激）。总之这门课就是想拿好龟也不知道怎么拿，想好好学也不知道怎么学。希望有更好选择的别选这个课吧。
reviews.translated_content: Overall, the professor’s accent is disorienting, the tutor is deliberately frustrating, the class logic is chaotic, and your grade depends heavily on your groupmates. At the end of every lecture, we are required to write a logbook entry of about 200 words, which accounts for 30% of the final grade (if I remember correctly). In short, it is meant to stop people from skipping lectures, but it doesn’t really work—many students still don’t show up. The logbook is supposed to demonstrate critical thinking, but the problem is that the tutor and professor are very inconsistent. Even after the tutor explained what to do in the tutorial, I followed those instructions and still didn’t get an A. On top of that, only about two logbook entries are actually graded, so there is a lot of uncertainty in how this affects your final total. There is no exam; instead, there is a group presentation where you interpret a ‘China story’, which can start from what you did on the field trip. My group initially went off-topic and was told we could get at most a C... but in the end, our group presentation didn’t mention the field trip and stayed on topic (what a thrill). In short, with this course, even if you want a good grade, you don’t know how to get one, and even if you want to learn properly, you don’t know how to go about it. If you have better options, avoid this course.

reviews.content: 组队很重要，我tm摊上了三个啥比我真服了
reviews.translated_content: Teaming up is crucial. I damn well got stuck with three idiots, I’m speechless.

reviews.content: 微电影的proj蛮重要的，能拉很多分，非常适合喜欢剪vlog剪小视频/爱演戏的同学，好像是占40%。tutorial每节课都一定一定要发言，而且越多越好，不然没分（10%），有一次pre在tutorial上，占20%. lec的出勤占10%，一般是通过moodle上的quiz来考勤。学期中去了一次大澳拍照，20%的分拍拍照直接拿满。没有exam.
reviews.translated_content: The microfilm project is quite important and can boost your grade significantly. It is very suitable for students who enjoy editing vlogs or short videos, or who love acting. It seems to account for 40%. In tutorials, you must speak up in every class, and the more you participate, the better; otherwise, you will get no marks (10%). There was one presentation during a tutorial, accounting for 20%. Lecture attendance accounts for 10%, usually checked via quizzes on Moodle. During the semester, we went to Tai O once to take photos, and you can easily get full marks for that 20% just by taking photos. There is no exam.

reviews.content: workload不大，lecture上的东西基本用不到，但还是能学到不少有关历史和建筑的文化的。tutorial上会有小组的presentation，平时发言也比较多。课堂上会让做视频介绍香港历史。还有一次field trip，还是挺好玩的，去了解下历史然后转转。因为这学期情况特殊，结束的早没有期末考试。给分蛮不错的 A-，教授人非常好 上课也很认真幽默。（友情提醒，Lavina的tuto慎选，个人感觉有时会强迫发言的。
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy. The material covered in lectures is barely useful, but you can still learn a lot about the culture of history and architecture. There are group presentations in tutorials, and frequent participation is expected. In class, we were asked to make videos introducing Hong Kong’s history. There was also one field trip, which was quite fun—a chance to learn some history and look around. Because of the special circumstances that semester, the course ended early and there was no final exam. The grading was quite good (A-). The professor is very nice, and his classes are serious yet humorous. (Friendly reminder: choose Lavina’s tutorial section with caution; I personally felt she sometimes forced students to speak.)

reviews.content: Good
reviews.translated_content: Good

reviews.content: VERY GOOD ARCHI CC COURSE, LIGHT WORKLOAD AND REALLY NICE GRADE
reviews.translated_content: VERY GOOD ARCHI CC COURSE, LIGHT WORKLOAD AND REALLY NICE GRADE

reviews.content: 这门课是关于文化遗产的，Workload主要是写篇photoessay，两人演讲，小组拍摄视频，阅读的话老师几乎不提，但我找了一些来略读。这门课找组友很重要，不是说组友要多么厉害，关键是要负责。photeessay是自己写，所以分数还不错，两人演讲的搭档也很好，所以分数也ok，小组拍摄视频遇到了不太负责的队友，直接崩塌。不过，这门课本身是很有意思的，有filed trip去大澳，也有kahoot游戏，教授思路很广泛。最后分数B range，还能接受。
reviews.translated_content: This course is about cultural heritage. The workload mainly consists of writing a photo essay, a pair presentation, and a group video shoot. The instructor barely mentions readings, but I found some to skim. Finding good groupmates is important—not necessarily because they need to be super capable, but because they need to be responsible. I wrote the photo essay myself, so the grade was decent. My partner for the pair presentation was also good, so that grade was okay too. But for the group video, I ended up with irresponsible teammates, and it collapsed. Still, the course itself is quite interesting, with field trips to Tai O and Kahoot games. The professor has broad perspectives. I got a B-range grade in the end, which is acceptable.

reviews.content: 龟没有想象中好，wl小，lecture无聊，教授喜欢自嗨很尴尬。视频要做的好玩一点比较容易拿分。
reviews.translated_content: The grade wasn’t as good as I imagined. The workload is small, but the lectures are boring, and the professor’s self-indulgent style is awkward. It’s easier to get points if you make your video interesting.

reviews.content: 非常好，很喜欢prof和tutor，人很好，给分也合理。最后A-
reviews.translated_content: Very good. I really liked the professor and tutor; they were very nice, and the grading was reasonable. I got an A- in the end.

reviews.content: wl挺大的，每周都有任务，各种类型任务都有，能很好的锻炼心智，今天刚交完最后一个3k+字的gp report，希望好🐢😭😭😭
reviews.translated_content: The workload is quite heavy, with tasks every week covering various types. It really exercises your mind. I just submitted the last group project report (over 3,000 words) today. I hope for a good grade 😭😭😭

reviews.content: 有点丰年种地的感觉，工作量很大但是投入程度和收获基本正相关。老师上课前非常老实说了工作量大但是如果你好好做的话绝对能拿高分，所以我累死累活做了，也成功拿了A+✌ Tutor Eugenia人非常好非常帅
reviews.translated_content: It feels a bit like farming in a bumper harvest year: the workload is heavy, but your level of effort and your gains are basically directly proportional. Before class, the teacher honestly stated that the workload is heavy, but if you put in the effort, you can definitely get a high grade. So I worked myself to death and successfully got an A+ ✌. Tutor Eugenia is very nice and very handsome.

reviews.content: Nice course. Workload is not that huge
reviews.translated_content: Nice course. Workload is not that huge

reviews.content: 内地教授和香港tutor特别好！作业内容挺有趣的，做起来不会觉得wl很大，给分好，拿了A
reviews.translated_content: The mainland professor and the HK tutor were both excellent! The assignment content was quite interesting, and the workload didn’t feel heavy. Grading was generous, and I got an A.

reviews.content: 很好玩，给文化遗产用google map 3D街景做VR stories，写一篇期中反思essay，一个group report，一个online gallery。老师很好，wl多大多小取决于你对设计的投入，全组A+ yyds
reviews.translated_content: It was very fun. We used Google Map 3D Street View to create VR stories about cultural heritage. Assessments included a mid-term reflection essay, a group report, and an online gallery. The instructor is great. The workload depends on how much effort your group puts into the design. Our whole group got A+—absolute legends.

reviews.content: wl大但好grade. 上课内容可以完全不听，但是互动答题要做（算participation），tutor干货很多，网站，vr会带领我们一步步做。每周有一个reflection，2个vr，一个小组report，和制作一个网站，一个gp. 虽然看起来麻烦，但是小组6人组队的话 好好做还是很简单的。这门课真的非常有趣，我认识的都是a-打底。 tutor是一个很温暖的人，他是我在hku遇到的唯一一个记住所有学生名字的老师，而且回邮件很快，人很细心温柔。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is heavy, but the grading is favourable. You can completely ignore the lecture content, but you must do the interactive quizzes (they count towards participation). The tutor provides a lot of substantive content; we were guided step-by-step through websites and VR. There is one reflection, two VR tasks, one group report, and the creation of a website and a group project each week. Although it looks troublesome, if you form a group of six and work properly, it is quite easy. This course is really very interesting; everyone I know got at least an A-. The tutor is a very warm person; he is the only teacher I have met at HKU who remembers all the students' names, replies to emails quickly, and is very careful and gentle.

reviews.content: ppt内容特别多，最后根本看不完，exam考的很主观，无法知道自己具体考试情况或者说如何提升，不是很推荐
reviews.translated_content: The PowerPoint slides have too much content; it's impossible to finish them all. The exam is very subjective, making it hard to know how you performed or how to improve. Not highly recommended.

reviews.content: Professor is very interesting, though I only went to 3 lectures, lol. Tutor David is very good as well, I went to all tutorials. I find him very open-minded person. You will have 2 group projects, so choose your teammates carefully. Gladly, my teammates were TOP! Workload is essentially nonexistent. You will have to visit a museum though(still, not really required). I just read and memorized all presentations before the final(like 6-8 hours per day), and got A+ in the end. Please take this course if you like history and culture(don't take otherwise, you will likely find it hard to memorize the stuff), but do not underestimate the course, thinking you will get an easy A-range. In the end, I regret not going to lectures, the professor is very interesting.

reviews.content: 好龟水课，教授是物理学系的澳大利亚人，人很好，只是专业水平不高，纯凭教授的个人兴趣，lecture很无聊，可以不去，但考试需要背slides，建议提前开始，其他assessment认真做就好，最后A

reviews.content: lecture很无聊就去过一两节，中途有个开卷的midterm，选择加简答，占比很小。tutorial必须去 会记发言participation，可以提前准备但是很灵活，对i人不太友好。wl就是最后一个gp的pre和individual的poster，挺轻松的。我midterm考到A+ tutorial每节课就说了一次话，poster感觉做得不错，pre一般般 最后A
reviews.translated_content: The lectures were boring, so I only attended one or two sessions. There was an open-book midterm in the middle with multiple-choice and short-answer questions, but it carried very little weight. Attendance at tutorials is mandatory, and participation in speaking is recorded. You can prepare in advance, but it is very flexible, which isn’t very friendly for introverts. The workload consists of a final group presentation and an individual poster, which is quite relaxed. I got an A+ on the midterm, spoke once in each tutorial session, felt I did well on the poster, and the presentation was just average. I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: 真正的0wl，好grade，不知道是不是因为新开的课，课可以全skip，最爽的一节课
reviews.translated_content: Truly zero workload, good grades. I don’t know if it’s because it’s a newly launched course, but you can skip every class. It’s the most relaxing course ever.

reviews.content: 教授的英文有時聽著很難受，感覺一直在組織語言，很久才憋出一個句子，整體上課氛圍感覺很chill，可能是這個原因導致感覺沒有什麼人聽課（還蠻心疼教授的）。midterm只考了mean，group presentation 感覺有點小炸，感覺隊友都準備比較隨意，自認為poster做得蠻好的，tutorial 爭取每次節都發言，讓tutor留下記憶點，有時感覺自己說離題了，最後A。
reviews.translated_content: The professor’s English is sometimes painful to listen to; it feels like he is constantly organizing his thoughts and takes a long time to squeeze out a sentence. The overall class atmosphere feels quite chill, which might be why it feels like not many people are listening (I actually feel quite sorry for the professor). The midterm only tested means. Our group presentation felt like it bombed a bit; I felt my teammates prepared rather casually, although I thought my poster was quite good. I tried to speak in every tutorial to leave an impression on the tutor. Sometimes I felt I went off-topic. In the end, I got an A.

reviews.content: 完全推薦的一門cc，lecture不記出缺席基本不用去，有一個midterm但本人甚麼都沒讀只考了40幾分...還有一個poster跟group presentation但要做的事情都不多。tutorail佔25%但本人基本上從沒發言過，最後拿B+覺得超出預期很多因為感覺整個學期就這樣被我水過去了
reviews.translated_content: A Common Core course I fully recommend. Attendance isn’t taken in lectures, so you basically don’t need to go. There’s one midterm, but I didn’t study at all and still scored in the 40s... There’s also a poster and a group presentation, but the workload is light. Tutorials count for 25%, but I basically never spoke up. I ended up with a B+, which was way above my expectations because I felt like I just coasted through the whole semester.

reviews.content: lecture 比较无聊，今年新加了midterm quiz，没有怎么准备，wl 不大
reviews.translated_content: Lectures are quite boring. A midterm quiz was newly added this year. I didn’t prepare much. The workload isn’t heavy.

reviews.content: lecture无趣可skip中途有guest来讲课这节课得来因为有essay写加additional points 新课没啥workload 但是组队难建议还是别来了…
reviews.translated_content: The lectures are boring and can be skipped. There was a guest lecturer midway through the term; attending that session was worthwhile because it came with an essay and additional points. As a new course, the workload isn’t heavy, but forming groups is difficult, so I’d suggest avoiding it…

course_info.title: Probing the Local in Chinese Culture and Society

reviews.content: i'm not ready for presentation, but i'm ready for therapy
reviews.translated_content: i'm not ready for presentation, but i'm ready for therapy

reviews.content: 文院白老头（不知道为什么现在只记得他中文名了）勤勤恳恳一学期喜提B+。。。课上讲的完全没用，啥也学不到（个人感觉）半个学期的课都用来pre。小组作业占比挺大的，而且不知道为什么其他组都那么卷。。。总之别来。还有目前上面显示的成绩是ab五五开，但是样本量只有两个人，其中一个是我。所以之后优化可以把样本量也显示出来。
reviews.translated_content: The white-haired old guy from the Faculty of Arts (for some reason I only remember his Chinese name now) worked diligently all semester, and I ended up with a B+... What was covered in class was completely useless; I felt like I didn’t learn anything. Half the semester was spent on presentations. The group project carries a large weight, and for some reason other groups were so intensely competitive... In short, avoid this course. Also, the grades currently shown are split 50/50 between A and B, but the sample size is only two people, one of whom is me. So for future improvements, the sample size should also be displayed.

reviews.content: 課程太新教授第一次教cc不太懂 我的建議是：別來
reviews.translated_content: The course is too new, and the professor is teaching Common Core for the first time and doesn’t quite understand it. My advice: don’t come.

reviews.content:
新课感觉老师给分挺宽松的，基本上全勤，作业量不少，主要是pre太卷了。如果对小组讨论比较感兴趣可以上。
wl的话：
1000字 research proposal（individual
一个ppt＋presentation（group
一个海报（group
reflective writing（individual
reviews.translated_content: It’s a new course, and the instructor seems to grade quite generously. Basically, full attendance is expected, and the assignment load is significant. The main issue is that the presentations are fiercely competitive. You can take it if you’re interested in group discussions. Workload breakdown: 1000-word research proposal (individual), one PowerPoint + presentation (group), one poster (group), reflective writing (individual).

reviews.content: 20% proposal+35%group presentation+15%poster+30%reflective writing，没有考试，课挺好的！虽然lecture完全没用hhh。主要是但是要选中topic，topic要是和中国文化有关系且最好是和自己本身专业相关的，btw教授是linguistic相关学科的所以可以在你的topic中试图结合一下相关元素～最后全组拿了A
reviews.translated_content: 20% proposal + 35% group presentation + 15% poster + 30% reflective writing. No exam. The course is quite good! Although the lectures are completely useless haha. The key is to choose a topic related to Chinese culture, ideally connected to your own major. By the way, the professor is from a linguistics-related discipline, so try to incorporate relevant elements into your topic. Our whole group got an A in the end.

reviews.content: 還沒出🐢，但必須評一下，這門課基本上學不到任何東西，教授（中文學院外國老師，反正只有他一個）在首幾節課會講自己的research經驗（例如研究的時候發現茅廁殺得），反正GP內容和「課」的東西完全無關係！！！也不要指望你會學到什麼東西 GP純自學唄 Tutorial不算attendance內容也是學不到東西的 反正就是很無聊的一門課 GP比重很高（Research proposal, presentation, individual reflective essay) 要找好的組友（本人的組友非常無敵卷，卷王本王），基本上90%的課都用來做小組匯報了，lecture的attendance也是不算分的（不知道take的目的在什麼）反正要是你想體驗大學生活 講師講得一塌糊塗GP純自救掙扎求存 的學習模式的話 讀這門課就沒錯了😀後續來了，A了，但也非常不推薦這門課！！！
reviews.translated_content: Grades haven’t been released yet, but I must review this course. You basically learn nothing from it. The professor (a foreign teacher in the School of Chinese; he’s the only one) talks about his own research experiences in the first few classes (for example, discovering latrine killings during his research). Anyway, the group project content has absolutely no relation to the “course” material!!! Don’t expect to learn anything; the group project is purely self-taught. Tutorials don’t count for attendance, and you don’t learn anything there either. It’s just a very boring course. The group project carries a high weight (research proposal, presentation, individual reflective essay). You need to find good group members (my group members were extremely competitive, the kings of competition themselves). Basically, 90% of the class time was spent on group presentations. Lecture attendance doesn’t count for marks either (I don’t know the point of taking attendance). Anyway, if you want to experience a university life where the lecturer teaches terribly, the group project is a struggle for survival through self-help, then this is the right course for you 😀. Update: I got an A, but I still highly recommend avoiding this course!!!

reviews.content: prof和tutor忍都非常非常好，有问题一定会给解决。不过workload大，组员很重要，不然就像我一样一个人做80%的任务。。最后应该是和tutor刷脸熟混了个A
reviews.translated_content: The professor and tutor are both extremely helpful; they will definitely resolve any issues you have. However, the workload is heavy, and having good group members is crucial. Otherwise, you’ll end up like me, doing 80% of the tasks alone. In the end, I probably scraped together an A by building rapport with the tutor.

reviews.content: 上课挺无聊的，但是要记attendance。wl算偏大，要做两次pre。tut要轮流讨论，讨论压力不大
reviews.translated_content: The lectures are quite boring, but attendance is recorded. The workload is on the heavier side, and you need to do two presentations. In tutorials, we take turns leading discussions, but the pressure isn’t high.

reviews.content: 逆天课程设置 懒得喷。lecture内容完全没用并且几乎不作考核相关 后半部分lec全部被占用做小组pre 合着后半ppt就给你扔那自己爱看不看呗。。。能想出这个课程结构家里得请高人了
reviews.translated_content: The course structure is absurd. I can’t be bothered to rant. The lecture content was completely useless and barely relevant to the assessments. The second half of the lectures was entirely taken up by group presentations, so the rest of the slides were just dumped there for you to look at or ignore as you pleased... Whoever came up with this course structure must have consulted some ‘expert’.

reviews.content: Don’t choose this!!! Can’t learn anything and group project will make you laan grade
reviews.translated_content: Don’t choose this!!! You can’t learn anything, and the group project will lead to harsh grading.

reviews.content: RUN. FUCKING. RUN. 首先disclaimer alison的lecture内容确实是女神级别的属于cc中的一股清流听着不枯燥题材也有意思（本来都准备好写好评了），但是绝对绝对绝对不值得用一个烂🐢换。本人IB film HL高中做过无数film analysis/comp study，tutorial发言踊跃平时quiz 100%，依旧没扛住期末拿B的暴击，并且期末group project手搓20小时剪辑吃了个B+。Tutor Danny人是蛮好的，平时把你捧得越高成绩给的就越是烂到你想吃翔。至今不知道这个B到底是从哪来的但众所周知sem grade出来之后想改比移山还难，发了邮件也只是被用一句" this course is competitive“敷衍，maybe there really is an invisible hand behind all this所以 DONT risk it😭
reviews.translated_content: RUN. FUCKING. RUN. First, a disclaimer: Alison’s lecture content is indeed goddess-level, a breath of fresh air among Common Core courses—neither boring nor uninteresting in topic (I was originally prepared to write a positive review). However, it is absolutely, absolutely not worth trading for harsh grading. I took IB Film HL in high school and have done countless film analyses and comparative studies. I participated actively in tutorials and scored 100% on regular quizzes, yet I still couldn’t withstand the blow of getting a B in the final exam. Additionally, I spent 20 hours manually editing for the final group project and only received a B+. The tutor Danny is quite nice, but the higher he praises you during the semester, the worse the grades he assigns—so bad you’d want to eat sh*t. I still don’t know where this B came from, but as everyone knows, changing a semester grade after it’s released is harder than moving mountains. Sending an email only resulted in being brushed off with the phrase “this course is competitive.” Maybe there really is an invisible hand behind all this, so DON’T risk it 😭

reviews.content: 第一年开的新课，总体来说挺好的，用电影来分析中国女性在不同时期的历史地位和形象这个点真的很吸引我。Lecturer表达清晰，上课能看电影片段，tutor人好，tutorial讨论挺激烈的。wl不算太大，从第三节课开始，每节课课上要写一个150字的问答题，tutorial需要积极发言参与（tutor会记发言情况），最后是一个GP，要产出10-15分钟的视频＋essay（就是你的视频文字稿）。但要做好🐢不是太好的准备，我们组最后的Video Essay被老师夸是“今年最好的作品之一”，还是只有A-。所以，可能更适合抱着看电影、涨知识的目的来学，不太适合刷龟。
reviews.translated_content: This is a new course in its first year. Overall, it’s quite good. Using films to analyse the historical status and image of Chinese women across different periods really appealed to me. The lecturer expresses ideas clearly, we watch film clips in class, the tutor is nice, and tutorial discussions are quite lively. The workload isn’t too heavy. From the third class onwards, you need to write a 150-word short-answer response in each class, and you must participate actively in tutorials (the tutor records participation). The final assessment is a group project that requires producing a 10–15-minute video plus an essay (which is essentially the script for your video). However, be prepared that the grading may not be very generous. Our group’s video essay was praised by the instructor as “one of the best works this year,” yet we still only received an A-. So this course is probably better suited for those who want to watch films and gain knowledge, rather than for boosting your GPA.

reviews.content: wl小，每节课要写in-class essay（交了就有分），tutorial要take attendance+发言（占30%的总成绩），期末要完成video essay（小组作业）。这门课我非常喜欢，prof上课很有意思，助教也很包容。每节课都能看有意思的电影。但最后烂龟！（给分不友好！！！）
reviews.translated_content: Low workload. You need to write an in-class essay for each lecture (you get marks just for submitting it). Tutorials require attendance and participation (accounting for 30% of the total grade). At the end of the term, you need to complete a video essay (group assignment). I really liked this course; the professor’s classes are interesting, and the teaching assistant is very accommodating. We watched interesting films in every class. But the grading was poor! (Not generous at all!!!)

reviews.content: 给分还行，平时workload极小，超级chill。分数构成包括课堂exercise，tutorial发言和40%的final project。前两项都是做了就满分，而且tutorial也不是每周都有，应该是每2～3周才有一次。最后的final project我们组做得比较认真，其实这个video essay不需要太多的剪辑技巧和方法，我们组剪辑得就挺粗糙的，更重要的是内容要分析得合理。课堂内容很有趣，教授风趣幽默，英语口音听得很舒服，而且lecture就是看看电影，做些简单的分析。tutor也是人特别热情特别好。最后轻松拿了A-，还是十分推荐的！
reviews.translated_content: The grading is decent, the regular workload is extremely small, and it’s super chill. The grade composition includes class exercises, tutorial participation, and a final project worth 40%. The first two components give full marks just for completion, and tutorials aren’t held every week—probably once every 2–3 weeks. Our group took the final project seriously. Actually, this video essay doesn’t require advanced editing skills or techniques; our editing was quite rough, but what matters more is having reasonable content analysis. The class content is interesting, the professor is witty and humorous, and her English accent is pleasant to listen to. Lectures basically involve watching movies and doing some simple analysis. The tutor is also very enthusiastic and nice. In the end, I easily got an A-. Highly recommended!

reviews.content: wl量不大，但是期末给分很奇怪，硬是没给A range。argue🈚️用。
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t large, but the final grading was strange—they simply didn’t award any A-range grades. Arguing was useless.

reviews.content: Lecture内容很深刻有趣，每周有一个in class exercise，wl不大；tutor应该只有一位，耐心幽默，tutorial靠发言次数和质量打分，标准不明；final要做一个group project，wl较大，过程有趣， 但给grade一般，overall B+。课程内容值得上，如果需要cc拉grade不推荐enroll，可以旁听。
reviews.translated_content: Lecture content is profound and interesting. There is one in-class exercise per week, and the workload is light. There seems to be only one tutor, who is patient and humorous. Tutorials are graded based on the frequency and quality of participation, but the criteria are unclear. The final requires a group project, which has a heavier workload. The process was interesting, but the grading was average, resulting in an overall B+. The course content is worth attending, but if you need a Common Core course to boost your GPA, I don’t recommend enrolling; you can audit it instead.

reviews.content: 好🐢！巨好🐢！超级好🐢！助教人很好
reviews.translated_content: Generous grading! Extremely generous grading! Super generous grading! The teaching assistants are very nice.

reviews.content: lecture tutorial都几有意思，wl不大，group project组员重要，本人被大佬带最后也才a-
reviews.translated_content: Both lectures and tutorials are quite interesting, and the workload isn't heavy. Group members are important for the group project. I was carried by a very strong student, but still only got an A- in the end.

reviews.content: Workload不是很大 A range
reviews.translated_content: The workload is not heavy. A-range grade.

reviews.content: 是目前读的四门CC中最喜欢的一门！wl不大，每周课堂150字左右的reflection（好像写了就有满分）+ tutorial讨论 + Video essay （group project）。课程设置很有趣，lecturer和tutor人都很nice很平易近人，gp最后给分A-，final grade A-。推荐喜欢中国电影和女性议题的友友reg！！
reviews.translated_content: This is my favourite among the four Common Core courses I’m taking! reviews.translated_content: The lectures are lightweight, but the grading is generous and the workload is small. The tutor, Stella, is particularly excellent. Overall, I got an A.

reviews.content: B+，有每周作业但是教授到了我们交了第七份才给反馈，我看着一堆已经B range的blog要心梗了，然后group project的话是pre前一天要交ppt，所以有一半组会早其他组一整个星期交，还只有3星期做，而且因为tut进度不同导致有些tut班很快就班内组队抢pre时间了，进度慢的班还没准备好组队时间就全被抢了，还有gp和essay没有出过分，但是essay可以直接给教授先整篇看再交和可以延迟交是不错的。
reviews.translated_content: B+. There are weekly assignments, but the professor only gave feedback after we had submitted the seventh one. I was having a heart attack looking at a pile of blogs already in the B range. For the group project, the PPT had to be submitted the day before the presentation, so half the groups had to submit a full week earlier than others. We only had three weeks to work on it. Also, because tutorial progress varied, some tutorial classes formed groups and booked presentation slots very quickly, while slower-paced classes found all the slots taken before they were ready to form groups. Grades for the group project and essay haven’t been released yet, but it’s nice that you can send the full essay to the professor for review before submission and that late submissions are allowed.

reviews.content: B+. 真的很很很无敌水。不去lec都可以因为they are truly useless。no matter how hard you work, B range. 超级简单的B。要A的快跑，you won’t get it here.
reviews.translated_content: B+. It’s incredibly lightweight. You can skip lectures because they are truly useless. No matter how hard you work, you’ll get a grade in the B range. It’s a super easy B. If you’re aiming for an A, stay away—you won’t get it here.

reviews.content: 一门新闻学的CC，单论课程内容很有趣，可以充分锻炼学生解析新闻的能力，个人认为无论读什么专业，阅读新闻都是很重要的。首先，prof和tutor人都特别好！prof的所有作业，essay都专门说过在ddl之后交也OK，甚至不需要晚交的理由，只要说一声交作业的具体时间就行，外面有什么活动prof也会赠送免费的门票～这门课的wl相对大一些，每周作业要写一篇100-300词的小论文（一共10次），tutorial每两周一个循环：第一周布置任务，第二周自己/小组pre，内容和形式广泛，涉及画PPT，制作海报，写稿子等等。期中是一篇1000词essay，期末有一个小gp。如果对自己gpa要求比较高且文科功底不太行的话慎选。本人在这门课投入了很多时间但最后🐢不是很理想，但仍然从这门课里收获了很多经验和知识，如果重新选我还是会enroll～
reviews.translated_content: A journalism-themed Common Core course. The course content itself is interesting and thoroughly trains students’ ability to analyse news. I personally believe that reading news is important regardless of your major. First, the professor and tutor are both very nice! For all of the professor’s assignments and essays, submitting after the deadline is OK; you don’t even need a reason for late submission, just let them know when you will submit. The professor also gives away free tickets to external events~ The workload for this course is relatively heavy. Weekly assignments require writing a 100–300-word short essay (10 in total). Tutorials follow a two-week cycle: tasks are assigned in the first week, and you deliver an individual or group presentation in the second week. The content and format are diverse, involving PowerPoint slides, posters, scripts, etc. The midterm is a 1000-word essay, and the final includes a small group project. If you have high GPA expectations but weak humanities foundations, choose with caution. I invested a lot of time in this course, but my grade wasn’t ideal. Nevertheless, I gained a lot of experience and knowledge. If I could choose again, I would still enrol.

reviews.content: 没怎么去过lecture，教授也很松弛，不过tutorial每节都会去并且发言，最后group presentation找到靠谱的队友就基本没问题了。每周要写个短篇新闻分析（这个我大部分都是A- range的），不过结合essay+gp presentation最后成绩是A。
reviews.translated_content: I rarely attended lectures. The professor is quite relaxed. However, I went to every tutorial and participated. As long as you find reliable teammates for the group presentation, there’s basically no problem. You need to write a short news analysis each week (most of mine were in the A- range). Combining the essay and the group presentation, my final grade was an A.

reviews.content: 每周有200字新闻分析一共十篇，直到学期末第九篇ddl结束才放第一篇的评分和评价导致根本来不及跟着教授评价改进。WL在CC里感觉偏大，🐢也一般，唯一的好处可能是不记attendance。如果对新闻学不感兴趣就快跑。
reviews.translated_content: There are ten 200-word news analyses due weekly. The grades and feedback for the first piece were only released after the deadline for the ninth piece at the end of the semester, making it impossible to improve based on the professor's comments. The workload feels on the heavier side for a Common Core course, and the grading is just average. The only benefit might be that attendance is not recorded. If you are not interested in journalism, stay away.

reviews.content: 换了新的老师，每周要写webblog但老师的反馈特别晚，来不及改进，但最后essay时间给得很足
reviews.translated_content: There’s a new instructor. We have to write a web blog every week, but the instructor’s feedback comes very late, so there’s no time to improve. However, plenty of time is given for the final essay.

reviews.content: wl太大了，比较下来性价比不高，时间投入巨大。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is too heavy. Compared to other options, the cost-performance ratio is low, requiring a huge time investment.

reviews.content: wl 大 老师是重度拖延症 不会给feedback 给龟一般
reviews.translated_content: Heavy workload. The instructor is a severe procrastinator, gives no feedback, and the grading is average.

Tutorials are quite fun—we wrote the Heart Sutra and made lotus lanterns. If you’re interested in Buddhism, consider taking this course.

course_info.requirement: You may add up to two fully online Common Core (CC) courses. And your enrollment must comply with the requirements of CC and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: The course in itself was... weird. You have to do these dumbass assignement which actually get interesting if you really think about it. wl is very low. The prof is very nice, very humourous but I hated the tutor Krisitna honestly. She was not interested in tutoring and overall a bit boring.
reviews.translated_content: The course in itself was... weird. You have to do these dumbass assignement which actually get interesting if you really think about it. wl is very low. The prof is very nice, very humourous but I hated the tutor Krisitna honestly. She was not interested in tutoring and overall a bit boring.

reviews.content: 感觉课程无聊，assignment判分很迷。而且tutorial老师不负责，好几次都没来，严重拖延小组任务。不建议任何理科生和想保好龟的人来。
reviews.translated_content: The course feels boring, and the assignment grading is very confusing. Also, the tutorial teacher is irresponsible; they didn’t show up several times, which seriously delayed our group tasks. I don’t recommend this to any science students or anyone who wants to secure a good grade.

reviews.content: 超绝烂龟课，课是听不懂的，tutor是着急下班的，小组作业组员是一言堂的，最后做出来就是一坨大的，essay的feedback还蛮仔细的老师有用心，总体来说wl不大但是龟也不高
reviews.translated_content: An absolutely terrible course with harsh grading. I couldn’t understand the lectures, the tutor was always rushing to leave, and the group project was dominated by one opinion. The final product was a complete mess. The essay feedback was quite detailed and the teacher put in effort. Overall, the workload isn’t heavy, but the grades aren’t high either.

reviews.content: 垃圾课 太特么垃圾了，说是网课wl多的要死，给分无理由低，必须打考勤。很多莫名其妙assignment。教授和tutor一点都不负责
good course, small workload, TA Kristina asks open-ended questions and engages the class very well. A grade.
reviews.translated_content: good course, small workload, TA Kristina asks open-ended questions and engages the class very well. A grade.

reviews.content: 比较水，成绩一般，但是课很水也不是很需要effort 。适合不想付出的人
reviews.translated_content: It’s quite lightweight. My grade was average, but the course is very easy and doesn’t require much effort. It suits people who don’t want to put in effort.

reviews.content: 中规中矩，但是给分一般。Tutor人不错，组队很重要，wl较大，小组作业非常麻烦，需要实地考察和ppt+video的形式，上课内容比较水。
reviews.translated_content: It’s average, but the grading is just so-so. The tutor is nice. Forming the right group is important. The workload is heavy, and the group project is very troublesome, requiring fieldwork and a presentation plus video. The lecture content is quite lightweight.

reviews.content: 非常好的课程，使我的grade旋转升高。wl巨小，上课挂机也能拿高分，essay给分也不错，身边朋友都是A range
reviews.translated_content: An excellent course that boosted my grade significantly. The workload is tiny; you can zone out during lectures and still get a high score. The essay grading is also decent—my friends all got A-range grades.

reviews.content: 超绝烂🐢课 谁上谁知道 完全莫名其妙的烂🐢
reviews.translated_content: A super terrible grading disaster. Anyone who takes it will know. Completely inexplicably harsh grading.

reviews.content: 超好🐢 workload小 上网课就挂着 给分也很好 总之就是非常好的一节课
reviews.translated_content: Super generous grading, light workload. For the online classes, you can just leave it running in the background. The grading is also very good. In short, it’s an excellent course.

reviews.content: 网课+wl小+gp只有两个人，绝对是性价比很高的cc。三个小时写的essay47/50还是挺好🐢的。就是千万记得tutorial开麦发言啊……不要像我一样都快final了才发现tutorial participation占15%😭
reviews.translated_content: Online class + low workload + group project with only two people; definitely a high value-for-money Common Core course. Getting 47/50 on an essay written in three hours shows the grading is quite favourable. Just remember to unmute and speak in tutorials... Don’t be like me, realizing only near finals that tutorial participation accounts for 15% 😭

reviews.content: 好🐢，基本上workload就是一个group presentation和一个Term Paper，平时的tutorial要积极发言才记入平时分
reviews.translated_content: Generous grading. Basically, the workload consists of one group presentation and one term paper. You need to participate actively in tutorials for it to count toward your continuous assessment score.

reviews.content: 每节tut发言1-2次，essay47/50，pre好像扣2分，最后A
reviews.translated_content: Speak up 1–2 times in each tutorial. Essay score: 47/50. Presentation seemed to lose 2 points. Final grade: A.

reviews.content:
很好的tutor! 非常nice
每堂tutorial积极发言
加上努力做好grp project
和认真写essay
最后A+
reviews.translated_content: Great tutor! Very nice. I participated actively in every tutorial, worked hard on the group project, and wrote my essay carefully. In the end, I got an A+.

reviews.content: 网课，比较轻松，WL超级小，essay 45/50, gp:30/30， tip是GP可以选择第一组做，给分可能会好一点，最后A
reviews.translated_content: It’s an online course, relatively relaxed, with a very small workload. I scored 45/50 on the essay and 30/30 on the group project. Tip: You can choose to be in the first group for the group project, as grading might be more generous. I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: A+, highly recommended
reviews.translated_content: A+, highly recommended

reviews.content: 超绝好🐢课。只是对课堂发言的要求较高
reviews.translated_content: An extremely GPA-friendly course. It just has high requirements for class participation.

reviews.content: curve严重，essay莫名翻车，没有a range ，无语
reviews.translated_content: Severe curving. My essay unexpectedly went poorly. No A-range grades. Speechless.

reviews.content: 老师很认真 要积极发言参与，essay选题可以和tutor沟通，好龟
reviews.translated_content: The instructor is very conscientious. You need to participate actively by speaking up. You can discuss your essay topic with the tutor. Generous grading.

reviews.content: curve感觉有点严，tut好好发言，pre和essay都表现不错，最后才B+
reviews.translated_content: The grading curve feels a bit strict. I participated well in tutorials, and performed well in both the presentation and essay, but still only got a B+.
