reviews.content: 很烂很烂的课，不知道为什么之前的评价那么好 prof确实不错，但是tutorial没有一节课有一个清晰的主体，基本就是随机分组讨论然后结束的时候pre，pre的内容也不知所云，比如让你讨论一支笔怎么globalization。TA全程没有任何有价值的输出，问她问题她会反过来指责你问的晚or非常敷衍地agree然后转头在打分的时候背刺你。pre的要求全程没有提供过，也不给任何形式的指导，TA全程的参与就是记录下我们组员的名字和pre的主题，但是pre完之后又会说按要求你们需要balabala，这个你们没有做到哦/甚至当场和有一组说我不喜欢你们的pre但是别担心我不会给你们F的。课程确实很水只需要看recording就行了，但tut完全如同坐牢。
reviews.translated_content: A very, very bad course. I don’t know why previous reviews were so positive. The professor is indeed good, but not a single tutorial had a clear theme. It was basically random group discussions followed by presentations at the end, and the presentation content was incomprehensible—for example, discussing how a pen relates to globalisation. The TA provided no valuable input throughout. When asked questions, she would either accuse you of asking too late or perfunctorily agree, only to stab you in the back when grading. Presentation requirements were never provided, nor was any guidance given. The TA’s only participation throughout was recording our group members’ names and presentation topics. Yet after the presentations, she would say, ‘According to the requirements, you needed to do blah blah, which you didn’t,’ or even tell one group on the spot, ‘I don’t like your presentation, but don’t worry, I won’t give you an F.’ The course is indeed lightweight and only requires watching recordings, but the tutorials felt like being trapped in prison.

reviews.content: workload中等，老师和tutor人都很好，中间的quiz能上网找到答案。给分蛮好的，课刚开始的时候tutor甚至说他们之前因为给太多A而被学校要求严一点。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is moderate. The lecturer and tutor are both very nice, and you can find answers to the mid-term quiz online. Grading is quite generous; at the start of the course, the tutor even mentioned that they had previously been asked by the university to be stricter because they gave too many As.

reviews.content: 说实话对tutorial很失望 很多人的essay得低分没有feedback 没出分就受不了来评价了 如果什么都不想学混一个🐢应该还行吧； 在pre 的时候有点震惊了哈哈
reviews.translated_content: To be honest, I’m very disappointed with the tutorials. Many people got low scores on their essays without feedback. I couldn’t stand waiting for the grades to come out, so I’m reviewing early. If you don’t want to learn anything and just want to coast to a pass, it should be fine. I was a bit shocked during the presentation, haha.

reviews.content: 课程挺好的 小组作业占比太大了 组员全是随机分的 刚好全是ai哥 两个quiz拿满分 essay分数也还行 上课积极回答问题 最后还是喜提b 这种线上课还是别开了 我怕忍不住去把这种组员🔪了
reviews.translated_content: The course is quite good, but the group assignment accounts for too much. Group members are assigned randomly, and I happened to get a group full of 'AI bros'. I got full marks in the two quizzes, and my essay score was okay. I answered questions actively in class, but I still ended up with a B. This kind of online course should not be offered. I am afraid I will not be able to resist stabbing these kinds of teammates.

reviews.content: joosee paul我要把你的课都上光。。
reviews.translated_content: Joosee Paul, I’m going to take all your courses...

reviews.content: 给分很好 wl很小 教授讲得也很清晰易懂
reviews.translated_content: Grading is generous, the workload is light, and the professor explains things clearly and understandably.

reviews.content: wl很小，prof和tutor都很好，每週的reading和recoding我都没怎么仔细看，第一次essay 14.75/15，两次quiz一次8/10一次满分，第二次没好好写不知道多少分，最后A。group presentation 很重要，要有深度一些。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is very light. The professor and tutor are both great. I didn’t read the weekly readings and recordings very carefully. My first essay got 14.75/15; for the two quizzes, I got 8/10 on one and full marks on the other. I didn’t do well on the second essay, so I’m not sure of the score, but I ended up with an A. The group presentation is very important and needs to have some depth.

reviews.content: wl很小，给分还行吧，但是感觉也没评论说的那么好。如果想要拿A或者A+ pre和essay还是要多做一些相关research再准备的；tutorial最好多说一点话。tutor选的香港tutor感觉不是很好…essay给分不算宽松而且总是要求多一些academic context，不知道另一个tutor会不会好点。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is small, and grading is okay, but I don’t feel it’s as good as the reviews say. If you want an A or A+, you still need to do more related research and preparation for the presentation and essay; it’s best to speak up more in tutorials. I felt the Hong Kong-based tutor wasn’t very good… Essay grading isn’t particularly lenient and always requires more academic context. I wonder if the other tutor would be better.

reviews.content: 线上课，两个quiz 两个essay 一个gp，wl感觉不大，professor和tutor人都很好，非常supportive，好课
reviews.translated_content: It’s an online course with two quizzes, two essays, and one group project. The workload doesn’t feel heavy, and both the professor and tutor are very nice and supportive. A good course.

reviews.content: 感觉确实没怎么努力，任务不多，内容还可以，最后a-
reviews.translated_content: I feel like I didn’t put in much effort. There weren’t many tasks, the content was okay, and I ended up with an A-.

reviews.content:
workload：作业＋group project剪片。
gp是足足12人的超级大组，务必找好groupmate（我那组只有5个人干活，我在组群里@他们都不理我）。值得注意的是，分组是按照一定规则随机分的，具体点就是让各个不同院的人尽可能地平均分配到每一组。所以如果你是理科生就找文科朋友一起去读，反之亦然。
其次，课基本可以不上，只要prof抽问的时候你能答上来点东西就行。
然后那份作业建议涉及比较深入和复杂的概念，同组的朋友写的比较简单，导致直接比我低了一个sub grade。grade还行，被人freeride＋从没剪过片最后还是A了。
reviews.translated_content: Workload: assignments + editing videos for the group project. The group project is in a huge group of 12 people, so make sure you find good groupmates (only five people in my group actually did the work; I tagged them in the group chat and they ignored me). Note that groups are assigned randomly according to certain rules, specifically to distribute students from different faculties as evenly as possible across groups. So if you’re a science student, team up with an arts friend to take the course, and vice versa. Secondly, you can basically skip classes; you just need to be able to answer something when the professor calls on you. For the assignment, I recommend covering relatively in-depth and complex concepts. My groupmate wrote something simpler and ended up one grade step lower than me. Grading is okay; despite being freerided and having never edited a video before, I still got an A.

reviews.content: Cancer course, cancer workload, need to participate in mandatory elderly visit and follow-up, 2 video project. Not recommended if your LS is not too good. (P.S. don’t expect reasonable workload for this course)

reviews.translated_content: Not that relaxed. There was an individual 10-minute presentation to design a health policy in HK, plus a group 10-minute presentation to analyze a country's health policy, and a site visit. I didn't expect to get a B+, as the professor has high standards for the work.

reviews.content: very good course, although you have to go do an elderly visit, the elderly are very nice and the experience is enjoyable. reviews.content: wl不大，grade挺好，本来觉得group pre应该会很低分，但是最后都有a，建议zoom每节课都在chat那里发言一下。个人pre可以用ai，prof说不看plagiarism（但个人感觉没什么用），用心剪还有加一些bgm和clips，不要光念ppt，grade出来就不会特别烂（at least我本人是这样）。
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn't heavy, and the grading is quite good. I originally thought my group presentation would get a low score, but we all ended up with an A. course_info.title: Hong Kong Cinema through a Global Lens
course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: 2021 -2022 sem 1上的課  課程主要是分析香港電影與全球化的關聯，其中涉及到很多全球化的概念，比如cultural hybridisation, orientalism等等，適合文科人，喜歡寫文章分析的人  - assessment主要是兩個video test （60%），video test 是課堂上限時間寫一篇電影分析，會給考試範圍，但是分析哪個片段是到考試的時候才給的。這個課喜歡學生提出自己的critical thinking,並且要有邏輯的解釋  - 還有一個group presentation （30%）, 隨機抽一部電影present, 我運氣好，tutorial組隊上遇到大佬，是local,很有想法，被carry了！所以其實未必要和朋友約好一起組隊，tutorial可以認識到不少有趣的人  -tutorial participation (10%)tutorial可以多講講話  讀Readings對video test很有用，如果沒時間也不用每篇都讀 第一個video test B ，最後A range 挺驚喜的。
reviews.translated_content: I took this course in Sem 1. It mainly analyses the connection between Hong Kong cinema and globalisation, covering many globalisation concepts such as cultural hybridisation and orientalism. It suits humanities students and those who enjoy writing analytical essays. Assessment consists mainly of two video tests (60%). A video test is a timed in-class film analysis; the scope is given beforehand, but the specific clip to analyse is only revealed during the test. The course values students’ critical thinking and logical explanation. There is also a group presentation (30%), where a film is randomly assigned for presentation. I was lucky to meet a very strong student in my tutorial group—a local Hong Kong student with great ideas—who carried the group! So you don’t necessarily need to team up with friends; you can meet many interesting people in tutorials. Tutorial participation accounts for 10%; speak up more in tutorials. Reading the assigned readings is very helpful for the video tests; if you’re short on time, you don’t need to read every single one. I got a B on the first video test and an A-range grade overall, which was quite a pleasant surprise.

reviews.content: workload挺大，grade还可以，如果是文院有一定基础可以拿A range。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is quite heavy, but the grading is decent. If you’re from the Faculty of Arts and have some background, you can get an A-range grade.

reviews.content: 不好拿分 助教也说不清楚高分的要求是什么
reviews.translated_content: It's hard to get good grades. The teaching assistant also couldn't clearly explain what was required for a high score.

reviews.content: tutor给分，很坑，要摸清楚tutor的评分标准...
reviews.translated_content: The tutor’s marking is a real pitfall; you need to figure out the tutor’s grading criteria...

reviews.content: 是clit department开的课，dr fiona真的人美心善，lecture内容都干货很多但不会无聊。tutor是dr leiya，话很多的老师，人也挺好的。主要是两个小测一个group project，后者记得找好队友，如果你有电影分析的经验会很加分，但没有也不要紧，主要是show original thinking。还会有一些免费活动可以参加和做bonus assignment。给分fair，学得很认真所以最后A+了。
reviews.translated_content: This course is offered by the CLIT department. Dr Fiona is truly beautiful and kind-hearted; the lecture content is packed with substantive material but never boring. The tutor is Dr Leiya, a very talkative teacher who is also quite nice. Assessment consists mainly of two quizzes and one group project. For the latter, remember to find good teammates; if you have experience in film analysis, it will be a big plus, but it’s not a dealbreaker—the main thing is to show original thinking. There are also some free activities you can participate in and bonus assignments. Grading is fair; I studied very diligently and ended up with an A+.

reviews.content:
非常好一门香港电影鉴赏课 看了好多喜欢的港片（也有没看过的也有不喜欢的）内容稍微有点发散 可能要针对全球化和老师讲的主旨去理解不能完全自己天马行空
wl不大！只有一个present和两个随堂essay前者是小组自选电影进行分析 后面是老师给video clip进行鉴赏 随堂的essay要求没有那么严格字数要求只要内容言之有物观点新颖就可以拿靓龟
*划重点：学期初和中间会有一些电影相关的活动包括讲座或者去电影院 感觉非常有意思可以看到到了现在的那一年香港电影的发展方向和趋势 也可以和年轻电影人沟通 写reflection paper还会有bonus
Tutor也非常负责任 虽然时间原因基本上每节tutorial都是prez但是也能发散聊很多问题 喜欢电影的（尤其港片）可冲 每周看电影真的很享受 最后靓龟😎
reviews.translated_content: An excellent course on Hong Kong cinema appreciation. We watched many Hong Kong films I liked (as well as some I hadn’t seen before and some I didn’t like). The content is slightly divergent; you may need to interpret it in light of globalisation and the lecturer’s main themes rather than letting your imagination run wild entirely. Workload is not heavy! There is only one presentation and two in-class essays. The former involves choosing a film in your group for analysis; the latter requires critiquing video clips provided by the lecturer. The in-class essays are not strictly marked; as long as the content is substantive and the viewpoints are novel, you can get a good grade. *Key point: There are some film-related activities at the beginning and middle of the semester, including lectures or trips to the cinema. I found them very interesting; you can see the development direction and trends of Hong Kong cinema up to that year, and you can also communicate with young filmmakers. Writing the reflection paper even comes with bonus marks. The tutor is also very responsible. Although, due to time constraints, almost every tutorial session was a presentation, we could still discuss many issues broadly. If you like films (especially Hong Kong cinema), go for it. Watching a film every week was truly enjoyable. Got a good grade in the end 😎

reviews.content:
很喜欢的一门cc课，整门课围绕香港电影对不同电影主题展开讨论，中间会穿插一些对于电影技巧的介绍和赏析，个人觉得还是很有收获的，能够学到很多并应用于现实观影中。
就prof和tutor而言，prof非常supportive，从课堂内容中能够感觉到还是很用心的，tutor也还不错，能够补充一些对于电影的具体见解。
就wl而言，我认为是比较丰俭由人的，如果认真学冲高分的话wl还是挺大的，需要进行2个video tests，1个gp（包含pre, essay和broadcast），幸运的是video test开卷，但仍然需要进行充分的准备。每周会要看一部电影，当然不看也可以，但无论lecture,tutorial还是video test都与要求看的电影有关，如果不想耗费很多精力的话可能需要三思。我属于准备比较充分、耗费了很多精力的类型，最终拿了A。总而言之，这是一分耕耘一分收获的课。
reviews.translated_content: I really liked this Common Core course. The entire course revolves around discussing different film themes through Hong Kong cinema, interspersed with introductions to and appreciation of film techniques. I personally found it very rewarding, learning a lot that I could apply to real-life movie watching. Regarding the professor and tutor, the professor is very supportive, and you can tell from the class content that she puts in a lot of effort. The tutor is also quite good, providing specific insights into the films. As for workload, I think it’s flexible. If you study seriously aiming for a high grade, the workload is quite heavy. There are two video tests and one group project (including a presentation, essay, and broadcast). Fortunately, the video tests are open-book, but you still need to prepare thoroughly. You’re expected to watch one movie per week; of course, you don’t have to, but the lectures, tutorials, and video tests are all related to the required films, so you might want to think twice if you don’t want to spend too much energy. I prepared thoroughly and spent a lot of effort, eventually getting an A. All in all, this is a course where you get out what you put in.

reviews.content: 同上是一個喜歡自嗨的韓國教授，lecture和tutorial頗無聊，lecture拿了notes後可以隨便走，tutor人還不錯，兩次quiz都給了A-，然後我們group present隨隨便便準備的但是tutor好像還挺喜歡？overall A-，個人感覺workload不大，喜歡吹水的文科同學只要把文本分析那一套用在quiz上分數應該都不錯👌🏻
reviews.translated_content: As above, there’s a Korean professor who likes to show off. The lectures and tutorials are quite boring. You can just leave after grabbing the lecture notes. The tutor is quite nice; I got an A- on both quizzes. Then our group presentation was prepared casually, but the tutor seemed to like it? Overall A-. Personally, I feel the workload isn’t heavy. reviews.instructor: Mr. Siufung Law, Dr. Fiona Law, Dr. Alvin Wong
reviews.content: 读reading的wl巨大，每周2-3篇20几30多页，常常书的照片PDF(捂脸哭)。topic还是有趣的，就是PPT全是字，不提前读reading几乎听不懂，教授念PPT，贼无聊痛苦……几乎都是local，没见到有内地生课友。作业是设计hk culture tour，设计leaflet和presentation、photo album或video，各组都很creative惊艳到我! writing test记住笔记关键词和reading的term和definition能写，时间比较紧，第一篇B+最后grade A-还可。非常LGBTQ friendly的一门课。
reviews.translated_content: The workload for readings was huge: 2–3 articles per week, each 20–30+ pages, often just photos of book pages in PDF format (facepalm cry). The topics were interesting, but the PPTs were full of text. If you don’t read the materials in advance, you can hardly understand anything. The professor just reads off the PPTs, which is extremely boring and painful... The class consisted almost entirely of local Hong Kong students; I didn’t see any classmates from Mainland China. The assignment was to design a Hong Kong culture tour, including a leaflet, presentation, photo album, or video. Every group was creative and impressed me! For the writing test, if you remember key terms from your notes and the definitions from the readings, you can write something. Time was quite tight. I got a B+ on the first piece and ended with an A-, which was acceptable. This is a very LGBTQ-friendly course.

reviews.content:
块陶 workload巨大 一份midterm writing 一份final writing 限时两小时 final writing前必须看course material（有电影，有文章）tutorial有学生带领讨论 最后的project是要设计香港的特色旅游景点 然后拍影片或者设计zine 学期末会忙死你 不要选 后悔一生
最後B+
reviews.translated_content: Huge workload. One midterm writing assignment and one final writing assignment, both with a two-hour time limit. Do not choose this; you'll regret it for life. Finally got a B+.

reviews.content: Good grade!
reviews.translated_content: Good grade!

reviews.content: assessment主要有看一个纪录短片写一个600字的分析，一个2500的final essay，每周看完课程视频回答一个reflection question（回答字数小于200，一共十次），tutorial上会有一个一分钟的presentation，一个gp（role- playing，抽签决定组友和扮演的角色）。最后一节tutorial上prof和tutor会跟你讨论final essay，之后有问题也可以单独和tutor约时间讨论，tutor人很好，会帮忙解决很多essay中的问题也会给出很有价值的建议。🐢还不错，和努力成正比。
reviews.translated_content: The assessments mainly included watching a documentary short film and writing a 600-word analysis, a 2,500-word final essay, and answering a reflection question each week after watching the course videos (under 200 words per response, ten times in total). There was also a one-minute presentation in the tutorial and a group project (role-playing, with teammates and roles assigned by drawing lots). In the last tutorial, the professor and tutor would discuss your final essay with you, and you could also schedule separate meetings with the tutor if you had further questions. The tutor was very helpful, assisting with many issues in the essay and providing valuable advice. The grading was decent and proportional to the effort put in.

reviews.content: 好龟课 wl小到爆炸 平时lecture可以划水 每周200词reflection question answer 应该是交了就有分 期末一篇2500词的case study 有20几个题目可以选 自己根据题目选择case 期中一篇600词的纪录片影评 然后有一个角色扮演 一个1分钟presentation➕debate 都很容易准备
reviews.translated_content: A course where good grades are attainable. The workload is incredibly light. You can coast through the regular lectures. There is a weekly 200-word reflection question answer; you likely get marks just for submitting it. The final is a 2,500-word case study with over 20 topics to choose from, allowing you to select your own case. The midterm is a 600-word documentary review. There is also a role-play activity and a 1-minute presentation plus debate, all of which are easy to prepare for.

reviews.content: workload不算大，选之前是看很多人说简单才选的，但我烂龟了，认认真真写的essay得的分很低，总之就是得分特别玄学，如果对自己的文字功底非常自信的同学可以选着试试

reviews.content: 课程确实能让人以更多元的视角审视inequality，inequity和poverty，但是我也是人生第一次拿五十多分essay。不说了，pf
reviews.translated_content: The course really does allow you to examine inequality, inequity, and poverty from more diverse perspectives, but it was also the first time in my life I scored in the 50s on an essay. Enough said; I took it pass/fail.

reviews.content: WL很大，差不多每個星期都有assignment，最後還要拍片，給分一般
reviews.translated_content: The workload is heavy; there are assignments almost every week, and you have to make a video at the end. Grading is average.

reviews.content: 给分不错 课程的projects略有一些繁琐 不过整体难度不是特别大
reviews.translated_content: The grading is decent. The course projects are a bit tedious, but the overall difficulty isn’t particularly high.

reviews.content: 明明prof说第一个作业（挑战10HKD在hk生活一天）可以成功也可以失败，写明失败原因就好。我认认真真尝试了10HKD吃一天饭饿的受不了最后选择放弃+认真在assignment里反思失败原因，最后tutor打分50，跟我说觉得我挑战失败了写不出好essay。学期末的最重要的拍片作业居然是学生互相评分，给龟也不高。血泪教训，避雷。
reviews.translated_content: The professor clearly stated that the first assignment (the challenge to live on HK$10 in Hong Kong for a day) could result in either success or failure, as long as you explained the reasons for failure. I seriously attempted to eat for a whole day on HK$10, but couldn’t handle the hunger and eventually gave up. I then carefully reflected on the reasons for my failure in the assignment. However, the tutor gave me only 50 marks, saying they felt I had failed the challenge and therefore couldn’t write a good essay. The most important video assignment at the end of the semester was actually graded by peer assessment, and the grading was not generous. A painful lesson—avoid this course.

course_info.title: Sports Culture under Global Capitalism
course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: 你永远可以相信Marco的给分/友善/幽默/佛系 上过的课里他不一定是讲的最好的，但一定是给分最好/对学生印象最深的人 是喜欢课上课下都热情跟你互动的人 爱来自🐍院 最后A+
reviews.translated_content: You can always trust Marco’s grading, friendliness, humour, and laid-back attitude. Among all the courses I’ve taken, he may not be the best lecturer, but he is definitely the most generous grader and the one who leaves the deepest impression on students. He is someone who enthusiastically interacts with you both in and out of class. Love from the Faculty of Science. I got an A+ in the end.

reviews.content: 对于喜欢体育➕有一定社科背景的同学是超级无敌好龟课，wl还算小，一个个人pre两个quiz，期末一个gp一个个人report，quiz会稍微有点难度必须认真看reading➕听他上课（但听说满分的也挺多的）。Prof是意大利人Marco，专业是人类学，超级无敌热情社牛的老师，课间会随机找人聊天提问，上课对互动要求高要积极参与他的提问和互动（可能对社恐略有些不友好），如果能课上或者课后给他留下一些印象（比如跟他讨论一些问题或者单纯聊会儿天）感觉对龟有积极影响。Tutor是Holy，人也超级无敌好，特别温柔有耐心的Tutor，可以多找她聊聊，提问都会耐心解答，给龟也很好。我唯一一门拿了A+的课，必须强推！！！
reviews.translated_content: For students who like sports and have some social science background, this is an absolutely fantastic course for getting good grades. The workload is quite light: one individual presentation, two quizzes, and at the end, one group project and one individual report. The quizzes are slightly difficult, so you must read carefully and listen to his lectures (but I heard many people got full marks). The professor is Marco, an Italian anthropologist. He is an incredibly enthusiastic and outgoing teacher who randomly chats with and questions students during breaks. The class requires high levels of interaction and active participation in his questions and discussions (which might be slightly unfriendly to those uncomfortable with social participation). If you can leave an impression on him during or after class (such as discussing some issues or just chatting for a while), it seems to have a positive impact on your grade. The tutor is Holy, who is also incredibly nice, a very gentle and patient tutor. You can chat with her more; she answers questions patiently and her grading is also generous. This is the only course where I got an A+. Must strongly recommend!!!

reviews.content: 去年开的新课吧我记得 总体来说wl挺小的 gp是去观察运动写个关于运动的phenomenon
reviews.translated_content: I remember it was a new course launched last year. Overall, the workload is quite small. The group project involves observing sports and writing about a sports phenomenon.

reviews.content: workload:1. 上课和tutorial的participation，特别是tutorial每周都要读essay和参与讨论，对于在人文社科方面不太感兴趣的同学来说可能比较痛苦😖2. tutorial上有一个presentation，要solo10-15分钟，本人一紧张直接快进成八分半了⏩3. 期中和期末都有1100字以上的大essay，期末有fieldwork还要做小组presentation；总的来说，Marco比较风趣幽默，对学生很有耐心，期中essay出分之后专门约了Marco，他给出了很真诚的建议， tutor也很给力，愿意和学生讨论问题，但课堂内容趣味性一般，只要你认真听课、讨论（很重要❗️会有impression因素）、做作业，最后成绩就不会差，本人期中essay只有B➕,但平时participation +期末pre+report下来有A
reviews.translated_content: Workload: 1. Participation in lectures and tutorials, especially tutorials where you have to read essays and participate in discussions every week. This might be quite painful for students not very interested in humanities and social sciences 😖. 2. There is a presentation in the tutorial, requiring a solo 10–15 minutes. I got nervous and sped through it in eight and a half minutes ⏩. 3. Both midterm and final have major essays of over 1100 words; the final includes fieldwork and a group presentation. Overall, Marco is quite humorous and patient with students. After the midterm essay grades were released, I specifically booked a meeting with Marco, and he gave very sincere advice. The tutor was also very supportive and willing to discuss questions with students. However, the lecture content was only moderately interesting. As long as you listen carefully in class, participate in discussions (very important ❗️ as it affects impression marks), and complete assignments, your final grade won’t be bad. My midterm essay was only B+, but with regular participation + final presentation + report, I got an A.

reviews.content:
神中神 lecture一節沒上 tutorial就上了四五節
Paper瞎寫個1600字數+一份ppt就A了
reviews.translated_content: Legendary. Didn’t attend a single lecture, only attended four or five tutorials. Wrote a random 1,600-word paper plus a PPT and got an A.

reviews.content:
Marco è una brava persona italiana.
Love his course!
reviews.translated_content: Marco è una brava persona italiana. Love his course!

reviews.content: 完美的cc课，wl真的不大，期中一个千字essay自由选题，中间tutorial有一个10分钟的pre（非常好弄，我甚至直接超级超时了），期末是一个5-7人的group project，全组一起交一个10-15分钟的pre然后每个人再交一个千字report就可以。marco是世界上最好的意大利人，你永远可以相信marco，除了他谁还那么溺爱学生。讲课特别特别有意思但就是互动性强，他满屋子随机找人互动所以如果你是社恐那就要慎重一点，对e人就很友好了，我个人认为和他频繁互动是有助于提升他对你的好感度和打分的，总而言之如果喜欢体育（无论是自己喜欢play sports还是纯粹看体育）无脑冲就对了，我永远喜欢marco montagner。另外这学期两个tutor（su jie和he yinjia）人都很好，是两个大陆人所以下课有什么不懂的要求或者安排之类的直接普通话问就ok，两个tutor都很可爱，请无脑随便选。
reviews.translated_content: A perfect Common Core course. The workload is really not heavy. The midterm is a 1000-word essay with a free choice of topic. In the middle, there is a 10-minute presentation in the tutorial (very easy to handle; I even went significantly over time). The final is a group project of 5–7 people, where the whole group submits one 10–15 minute presentation, and each individual submits a 1000-word report. Marco is the best Italian in the world. You can always trust Marco; who else spoils students so much? His lectures are extremely interesting but highly interactive. He randomly picks people around the room to interact, so if you are very uncomfortable with social participation, you should be cautious. It is very friendly to outgoing people. I personally believe that frequent interaction with him helps improve his favorability towards you and your grading. In short, if you like sports (whether you enjoy playing sports or just watching them), just go for it without hesitation. I will always love Marco Montagner. Additionally, the two tutors this semester (Su Jie and He Yinjia) are both very nice. They are from Mainland China, so if you have any questions or requests about arrangements after class, you can just ask them in Mandarin. Both tutors are lovely. Please feel free to choose either section without worry.

reviews.content: lecture不太需要上，但是professor是很有趣的人。学的东西和体育没什么关系，我是本着sports related来的但是讲的都是很复杂的社会学理论。tutorial 跟一群读法男一个class，特别杠，根本插不上嘴。
reviews.translated_content: You don’t really need to attend lectures, but the professor is an interesting person. What we learned had little to do with sports. I enrolled expecting sports-related content, but the course covered complex sociological theories. In tutorials, I was in a class with a group of male law students who were extremely argumentative, making it impossible for me to get a word in.

reviews.content: 一学期上了两门Marco的课，觉得sports发挥得好多了哈哈哈！本soci生就这样薅着家院的cc上来上去……好玩好玩
reviews.translated_content: I took two of Marco’s courses in one semester and felt the sports one was much better, haha! As a sociology student, I just kept taking Common Core courses offered by my own department...

reviews.content: Very nice grading, loved the lectures.
reviews.translated_content: Very nice grading, loved the lectures.

reviews.content: 课真的很好，非常educational，完全改变对非洲看法。不过给龟太差了，还遇到坑爹组友，烂龟到家了。essay是B，group project是C+，最后B-
reviews.translated_content: The course itself is really good and very educational; it completely changed my view of Africa. However, the grading was terrible. I also encountered unreliable teammates, so the grading was harsh all around. I got a B for the essay and a C+ for the group project, resulting in a final grade of B-.

reviews.content: 好gui wl小
reviews.translated_content: Good grade, low workload.

reviews.content: 课是真的好，龟是真的烂 原来对非洲基本上没什么了解，通过这门课学了很多非洲相关的东西，比如语言、音乐、商业什么的。教授是linguistic的，所以有挺多非洲语言的内容，还是挺有意思的，而且也不考难的内容，我们那次好像都没有考试，只有poster，pre和essay。还有guest speaking，总之是挺好玩的。
reviews.translated_content: The course itself is really good, but the grading is truly harsh. I didn’t know much about Africa before, but I learned a lot through this course, such as language, music, and business. The professor specialises in linguistics, so there’s quite a bit of content on African languages, which is quite interesting. It doesn’t test difficult material; it seems we didn’t even have an exam that time, only a poster, a presentation, and an essay. There were guest speakers too, so overall it was quite fun.

reviews.instructor: Fung, Lai Kin Sammy; Benson Lam (导师)
reviews.content: 课程内容： 主要将企业社会合作体系中的一些理论（CSR 综述、CSR 社会合作、CSR 政府管理、CSR 项目实施等）、社会现象（绿色债券、社会创新、社会效益评估等）以及一些相关的公司、时事学习，还包括一次 field trip（课程后期，很可惜因为疫情在线上上课错过了这次机会）。导论课主要针对于指定的一篇 Reading 来进行话题讨论，大部分时间都是大家畅所欲言。  课程任务： Tutorial 出勤率考评（10%）；2 个小组任务（20% + 30%）和一个个人论文（40%）。Tutorial 上课前老师点名不可迟到；第一个小组任务关于评述 CSR 的好处和弊端，第二个小组任务要选择一个特定的企业，为其提出 CSR 项目计划（一个 PPT 演讲和一个报告类型的 CSR 草案）。最后一个个人论文是选择任意一个跟 CSR 相关的主题进行内容调研，产险一些观点或者综述话题的全面性。没有课程考试，但小组项目做起来会比较辛苦，建议提早规划千万不可以赶 due！  课程老师和 Reading： 老师人很好不论讲师还是导师。上课内容推进可能有些快，CSR 这个概念对非商科学生不是很友好，容易跟不上上课进度（但老师会不断尝试刺激你的记忆，或者用案例来诠释也是挺好的）。有很多 Reading  提供，如果读得比较勤快学到知识，可以用来充实小组项目或者个人论文的论据。  课程总评： 一门有着很强社会联系性和社会学问的课程，需要一些时间来消化并且运用所学的理论知识。课堂氛围很好，有很多体验小组项目合作的机会。保证会有收获，打开眼界的一门课！适合喜欢理解社会运作规律、擅长发掘思考相关社会现象并建立联系的同学的一门CC，但对于新手来讲，也是一门尝鲜课。
reviews.translated_content: Course content: Mainly covers theories in corporate social cooperation systems (CSR overview, CSR social cooperation, CSR government management, CSR project implementation, etc.), social phenomena (green bonds, social innovation, social impact assessment, etc.), and related companies and current affairs. It also includes one field trip (late in the course; unfortunately, I missed this opportunity because classes moved online due to the pandemic). Introductory classes mainly discuss topics based on a designated reading, with most of the time spent on open discussion.  Course tasks: Tutorial attendance assessment (10%); two group tasks (20% + 30%) and one individual essay (40%). The instructor takes attendance before tutorials and lateness is not allowed. The first group task involves evaluating the pros and cons of CSR. The second requires choosing a specific company and proposing a CSR project plan (a PowerPoint presentation and a report-style CSR draft). The final individual essay involves researching any CSR-related topic to produce arguments or a comprehensive review. There is no course exam, but the group projects are quite demanding. Plan early and absolutely do not rush the deadlines!  Instructors and readings: Both the lecturer and tutor are very nice people. The pace of content delivery might be somewhat fast. The concept of CSR is not very friendly to non-business students, making it easy to fall behind (but the instructor constantly tries to stimulate your memory or uses cases to explain concepts, which is helpful). Many readings are provided; if you read diligently, you can use the knowledge to enrich the arguments in your group projects or individual essay.  Overall evaluation: A course with strong social relevance and sociological depth. It takes time to digest and apply the theoretical knowledge learned. The classroom atmosphere is great, with many opportunities to experience group project collaboration. You are guaranteed to gain something and broaden your horizons! This Common Core course suits students who enjoy understanding how society operates, are good at discovering and thinking about related social phenomena, and making connections. However, for beginners, it is also a taster course.

reviews.content: 这是一个能学到东西的 cc，但 final 真的很难，速成失败，背背背好多东西。选择题全是那种一个对两个对三个对全对那种，蒙不了一点，简答题会考到上百页 lecture slides 或tut 里涉及过的内容（tut 的 ppt 是不公开的），但并没有想象中好答，因为要默写许多知识点，且复习的面广，没有 pp 参考，要么记忆力超群要么功夫在平时。tut 一周一次，ta 人美心善又温柔，以小组为单位回答问题，但其实略 chur 因为总会有人一次性回答一堆东西，把你准备好的抢走 hhhh  所以要多多思考好好读 reading 做准备。lecture 内容其实很好的，作为 cc 能学到很多，但 lecture 在 14 点这个尴尬时间上课，看着 ppt 一大片字，比较考验意志力 dddd。overall，B range，但课挺好的
reviews.translated_content: This is a Common Core course where you can actually learn something, but the final is really difficult. Last-minute cramming fails; there’s a lot to memorise. The multiple-choice questions are all of the ‘one correct, two correct, three correct, or all correct’ type, so you can’t guess at all. Short-answer questions cover content from over a hundred pages of lecture slides or tutorials (tutorial PPTs are not public), but they aren’t as easy to answer as you might think because you need to recall many knowledge points from memory, and the scope of revision is broad. With no past papers for reference, you either have an exceptional memory or you put in the effort consistently throughout the semester. Tutorials are once a week; the TA is kind, gentle, and nice. You answer questions in groups, but it’s actually a bit demanding because someone will always answer a bunch of things at once, snatching away the points you had prepared for hhhh. So you need to think more, read the readings carefully, and prepare. The lecture content is actually very good; as a Common Core course, you can learn a lot, but lectures are at the awkward time of 2 pm. Looking at slides full of text really tests your willpower, if you know what I mean. Overall, I got a B-range grade, but the course is quite good.

reviews.content: 知识点挺有意思的课。lecture不记attendance，且教授有点催眠所以没怎么去过。tutorial记attendance并且需要在课前读reading，课上举手回答问题（可以当场使用AI。有意思的reading我就会好好看自己回答，没意思的就不看，课上用AI乱答）tutor会记录回答情况（但是总会说你回答得很好！人真的很好）。我是每节课至少回答一次。tutorial的ppt不会直接给我们，但在考试范围内，所以每张都要拍照（我虽然知道这点但还是会走神忘记，不过下课的时候可以马上请tutor再放出来给我拍）。gp占35%，做得很累，是一个小组一起写essay，整组只有两人在干活很痛苦。最后有个和教授的小组meeting，积极回答教授问题可以体现出在小组的贡献（因为有些人根本不知道小组essay写了什么）。gp我觉得尽力了但肉眼可见还是很烂。final不简单，还挺坑的，需要认真看每页ppt。从早背到晚三天速成是可行的，根据文科生的直觉背诵一些。个人觉得final做得还不错。最后拿了A。
reviews.translated_content: An interesting course with engaging content. Attendance is not taken in lectures, and since the professor is a bit hypnotic, I rarely went. Attendance is taken in tutorials, and you need to do the readings beforehand and raise your hand to answer questions in class (you can use AI on the spot. If the reading is interesting, I read it carefully and answered myself; if not, I didn’t read it and just used AI to give random answers in class). The tutor records your responses (but always says you answered very well! Really nice person). I made sure to answer at least once in every tutorial. The tutorial slides are not given to us directly, but they are within the exam scope, so you need to take photos of every slide (even though I knew this, I would sometimes zone out and forget, but I could ask the tutor to display them again for me to photograph right after class). The group project accounts for 35%. It was exhausting; it involved writing an essay as a group, and it was painful because only two people in the whole group were doing the work. There was a final group meeting with the professor, where answering his questions actively could demonstrate your contribution to the group (since some people had no idea what was written in the group essay). I felt I tried my best for the group project, but it was visibly poor. The final exam is not simple and is quite tricky; you need to study every slide carefully. Cramming from morning to night for three days is feasible, relying on a humanities student’s intuition to memorise key points. I personally felt I did quite well on the final. I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: 虽然教授的课有一些催眠，但是tutor Melody真的超级超级好，melody酱人美心善，好爱好爱好爱她
reviews.translated_content: Although the professor’s lectures are a bit sleep-inducing, tutor Melody is truly, truly wonderful. Melody-chan is beautiful and kind-hearted. Love, love, love her.

reviews.content:
ccgl9019
内容：Lecture的内容有good和service trade，资本流动，投资 ，移民，劳动力，全球不平等。每一个板块的内容大概有六七十页PPT，其中trade和financial部分内容比较丰富。tutorial讲经济全球化术语，集装箱化，Fair trade组织，经济全球化下的旅游业，洗钱，避税天堂，特许经营与麦当劳，人口流动中的外包与移民，金融危机下的韩国与马来西亚。每个tutorial前会给三四篇材料进行阅读，每篇材料的长度如果仔细阅读需要20~30分钟，如果借助AI阅读会加速很多。
形式：Lecture不计attendance,教授的声音比较小，不如自己看PPT。tutorial记attendance，每次的形式就是先介绍主题，然后提出问题进行小组讨论，然后发言。tutorial的分数与发言有关，每节课大概5~6个问题。没有ass。有group project，需要写一篇report，选题很自由，但范围不建议太大，拟好之后做好outline他们会检查，课后也会点评每个组的选题，也可以结束之后找prof问清楚他的意见，email也OK，prof会给很详细的建议。最后进行类似于答辩的meeting，提前准备可能会被问到的问题很重要，一旦回答不上来或者被发现很大的漏洞，分数就不理想了。最后就是两个小时的final，选择题是多选题，内容是lecture和tutorial，大多是一些判断，一定要对这门课中的知识点的英文说法熟悉，简答题类似于政治题，涉及lecture和tutorial，只要对lecture和territorial的每个主题下的每个知识点有大致了解，能够讲出每个点有哪些分支，基本就没有问题。
作用：大致了解经济全球化的相关内容，是ccgl中经济学含量较高的一个，其中涉及许多经济学概念。Tutorial是对这些具体概念和知识的运用，通过一些实际的例子来分析运用这些知识。这门课认真去学，能学到非常多的东西。
其他：因为这门课的专有名词比较多，上来我去用中文思维去理解，但考试的时候是全英文的，就比较痛苦，建议平常就尽量用英文思维去学习，记住英文说法。对于group project，在写report的时候，如果能够自己多阅读一些材料，多自己进行一些筛选，少借助AI会更好。这门课的内容非常多，需要不定期的进行复习。
reviews.translated_content: CCGL9019 Content: Lecture topics include trade in goods and services, capital flows, investment, migration, labor, and global inequality. Each section has about 60–70 slides of PPT, with the trade and finance sections being particularly rich in content. Tutorials cover terminology of economic globalization, containerization, Fair Trade organizations, tourism under economic globalization, money laundering, tax havens, franchising and McDonald's, outsourcing and migration in population flows, and South Korea and Malaysia during financial crises. Before each tutorial, three or four reading materials are provided. Each material takes 20–30 minutes to read carefully, but using AI to read can speed this up significantly. Format: Attendance is not taken for lectures. The professor’s voice is rather quiet, so it is better to just read the PPTs yourself. Attendance is taken for tutorials. Each session follows this format: introduce the topic, pose questions for group discussion, and then present. Tutorial grades are related to participation, with about 5–6 questions per class. There are no individual assignments. There is a group project requiring a report. The topic selection is very free, but the scope should not be too broad. After drafting an outline, the instructors will check it. They also comment on each group’s topic after class, and you can email the professor for detailed advice. Finally, there is a meeting similar to a defense/viva. It is important to prepare for potential questions in advance; if you cannot answer or if major loopholes are found, the grade will not be ideal. Lastly, there is a two-hour final exam. The multiple-choice questions are multiple-response items covering lectures and tutorials, mostly true/false judgments. You must be familiar with the English terminology for the concepts in this course. The short-answer questions are similar to political science questions, covering lectures and tutorials. As long as you have a general understanding of each branch under every topic in the lectures and tutorials, you should be fine. Purpose: To gain a general understanding of economic globalization. This is one of the CCGL courses with a higher economics content, involving many economic concepts. Tutorials apply these specific concepts and knowledge through practical examples. If you study this course seriously, you can learn a great deal. Other: Because this course has many specialized terms, I initially tried to understand them using Chinese thinking, but since the exam is entirely in English, it was quite painful. I suggest trying to think in English during your studies and memorizing the English terms. For the group project, when writing the report, it is better to read and filter more materials yourself rather than relying heavily on AI. This course has a lot of content and requires irregular review.

reviews.content: 对有政治经济底子的小伙伴非常友好，workload很小，一个term essay一个final而已，中间可以完全不用上。final注意看past paper，题目几乎一样；essay…我乱写的，A+，被tutor拿去给下一届当范文了，所以你们可能读着我的essay（笑）
reviews.translated_content: Very friendly for those with a background in political economy. The workload is small: just one term essay and one final. You can completely skip attending in between. For the final, make sure to look at past papers; the questions are almost identical. As for the essay... I just wrote whatever, and got an A+. My tutor even used it as a model essay for the next cohort, so you might be reading my essay (lol).

reviews.content: Essay花了3小时写 没听过课 最后拿了A 学过econ1220的同学会觉得很简单 非常推荐
reviews.translated_content: I spent three hours writing the essay. I did not attend lectures and ended up with an A. Students who have taken ECON1220 will find it very easy. Highly recommended.

reviews.content: 超赞！评分维度单一，老师牛逼，课程有趣，好好写文章就A Range
reviews.translated_content: Absolutely amazing! The grading criteria are straightforward, the instructor is brilliant, and the course is interesting. If you write your essays well, you can get an A-range grade.

reviews.content: 這個學期只有5課，考試essay只需要做一個（也可以兩個都做然後算比較高分的那個），tutorial甚至不用attendance。Proposal comment不像其他留言説得mean，很encouraging，Essay feedback也詳細。考試把Ppt背了就好了。最後A+,推薦
reviews.translated_content: There were only five classes this semester. For the exam, you only need to write one essay (or you can write two and have the higher-scoring one counted). You don’t even need to attend tutorials. The proposal comments weren’t as mean as other reviews suggested; they were quite encouraging, and the essay feedback was detailed. For the exam, just memorise the PowerPoint slides. I ended up with an A+. Recommended.

reviews.content: 整个学期基本上没有什么作业，但如果你不自学到了期末就会爆炸。整门课只有一个1500的essay和一个final。 不建议不建议不建议高中理科生学习，很多基本概念都不了解。建议学过ECON1210和1220的朋友上。Richard上课是很风趣但是基本在吹水，全靠看lecture note和reading。
reviews.translated_content: There is basically no coursework throughout the semester, but if you don’t teach yourself, you’ll crash and burn by the finals. The whole course has only one 1500-word essay and a final exam. I do not recommend, do not recommend, do not recommend this for high school science students, as they won’t understand many basic concepts. I suggest friends who have taken ECON1210 and 1220 take this course. Richard is humorous in class, but he mostly rambles. It relies entirely on reading the lecture notes and assigned readings.

reviews.content: workload还可以，有学到东西，最重要的是没有group project，essay慢慢写就好了
reviews.translated_content: The workload is acceptable, and I learned something. Most importantly, there is no group project; you can just take your time writing the essay.

reviews.content: 非常烂龟
reviews.translated_content: Very harsh grading.

reviews.content: workload不大 如果学过ECON1220其实压力不会太大
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy. If you’ve taken ECON1220, the pressure won’t be too great.

reviews.content: 需要自学的东西挺多的，wl还行，主要是final需要熟悉几个课上讲过的典型事例
reviews.translated_content: There’s quite a lot of self-study involved. The workload is acceptable. The main thing is that for the final, you need to be familiar with several typical case studies covered in class.

reviews.content: 为Richard Wong选的一门课 Reading超多assessment少但是essay占比很大 建议学过Econ1220和对写essay比较有信心的同学上
reviews.translated_content: I took this course for Richard Wong. There is a huge amount of reading. Assessments are few, but essays carry a large weight. Recommended for students who have taken ECON1220 and are confident in essay writing.

reviews.translated_content: The lectures are quite interesting but a bit superficial. There is a lot of reading. Tutorials involve group presentations; if you don’t attend the discussion when others are presenting, you can write a reflection to count as attendance. Finally, there is a group project requiring a long report, plus a final exam. Overall, the workload isn’t huge, but the grading is poor. I got a B range. Choose with caution.

reviews.content: 上一个小时课看一个小时视频啦，教授讲得还蛮有意思，就是有的时候有划水的嫌疑。个人觉得龟一般，没有特别好。大一刚上来tutorial讨论全是大佬，一句话都插不上，所以和我一样口语不够流利胆子不够大就完蛋了，只能写essay逆天改命。wl还行
reviews.translated_content: An hour of class means an hour of watching videos. The professor’s lectures are quite interesting, though there are times when he seems to be slacking off. I feel the grading is just average, nothing special. As a first-year student, I found that the tutorial discussions were dominated by very strong students, so I couldn’t get a word in. If your spoken English isn’t fluent enough and you’re not bold enough, you’re done for; you can only rely on essays to turn your grade around. The workload is acceptable.

reviews.content: wl少，給分不錯，看隊友，samuel很nice
reviews.translated_content: Low workload, decent grading. It depends on your teammates. Samuel is very nice.

reviews.content: 挺烂的龟，摸不着头脑，身边的人也是这龟

reviews.content: 其实感觉workload不怎么大，除了最后的research要写比较多，平时就只有一个presentation，最后一节课会有一个essay test，还会提前划重点。对政治经济这方面积累比较多的话tutorial发言随便讲讲就可以，也不需要提前准备或者读reading啥的... Samuel Wong是真的好随性，听他的课很有意思哈哈哈。tutor也很有意思。不过下年好像两个Samuel都不教这门课了。
reviews.translated_content: Actually, the workload doesn't feel very heavy. Apart from the final research paper, which requires quite a bit of writing, there's only one presentation during the term. reviews.content: 第一次在cc达到A-，给分不错。我完全没修过经济相关的课，两个essay我一篇B（400字）一篇A+（800字），感觉是字数差距，因为是tutor批感觉你努力了分就高。takehome test当final很舒服，还延长了due，时间比较充足。gp靠队友带飞，给了很长时间做，拖到最后也来得及。上课内容其实挺无关紧要的，也不用去背什么东西，要用到直接翻ppt就行，基本就是去记个attendance然后做自己的事就好。
reviews.translated_content: First time achieving an A- in a Common Core course; the grading was generous. I had never taken any economics-related courses before. For the two essays, I got a B on one (400 words) and an A+ on the other (800 words). It seems the difference came down to word count. Since the tutor marked them, it felt that if you showed effort, you got a higher grade. The take-home test served as the final, which was quite comfortable, and the deadline was even extended, so there was plenty of time. For the group project, my teammates carried me; we were given a long time to work on it, so even leaving it until the last minute was fine. The lecture content was actually quite insignificant; there was no need to memorize anything. You could just refer to the slides whenever needed. Basically, you just needed to show up for attendance and then do your own thing.

reviews.content: wl大到要吐血，assignment每份写了一千多字都是9.5/10，final写了差不多五千，final有一周时间每天一直写才能写完，但group project有点崩最后出分没想象的好只有A-。整体来说grade还是不错的，而且真的感觉到自己学到很多东西，但感觉还是有点卷的，要拿高分group project得做好
reviews.translated_content: The workload is huge enough to make you spit blood. Each assignment was over 1,000 words and scored 9.5/10. The final essay was nearly 5,000 words; I had to write continuously every day for a week to finish it. But the group project fell apart a bit, so the final grade wasn’t as good as I imagined—only an A-. Overall, the grading is still decent, and I really feel I learned a lot, but it feels quite competitive; you need to do well on the group project to get a high grade.

reviews.content: 对于没有系统学过金融知识的人，尤其非商院高考生，跑断腿也要跑！一上来就上难度，不管零基础的人死活，理解极其费劲，wl极大。呕心沥血最后B-，组员也是类似的情况，全员B range
reviews.translated_content: For those who haven’t systematically studied finance, especially non-Business School students with a Gaokao background, you should run away! It jumps straight into high difficulty, disregarding complete beginners, and is extremely hard to understand. The workload is huge. After pouring my heart out, I got a B-. My group members were in a similar situation, with everyone getting grades in the B range.

reviews.content: 课程：完全没经济金融的知识初听会有点懵，但教授挺会讲的，多听几节慢慢就能明白，他甚至能把量化的部分深入浅出，挺不错的。不过还是要自己下课去查点资料理解一些概念。谢教授讲课有趣的，尤其是他不讲正经知识的时候（误），金融秘史人世沧桑香港发展青春往事你都可以听到一耳。当然for exam purpose课不去，自学，也没什么问题。wl: 还可以，含期末考试三次作业，还有一个gp. 作业看着题多，但大多课上讲过，且如果能找到source的话会非常非常有用。给分：我本人有A+，据身边同学说给分也不错，应该是拉了curve。两次assignment 倒是拿高分都不容易，因为跟高中语文阅读题一样，踩点得分，踩不到就没（再次说明source重要性），还是得多写一些点。
reviews.translated_content: Course: If you have no background in economics or finance, you might feel confused at first, but the professor explains well. After attending a few lectures, you’ll gradually understand. He even breaks down quantitative parts in an accessible way, which is quite good. Still, you need to look up some materials after class to understand certain concepts. Professor Tse’s lectures are interesting, especially when he goes off-topic (just kidding)—you can hear anecdotes about financial secret histories, worldly vicissitudes, Hong Kong’s development, and youthful memories. Of course, for exam purposes, skipping classes and self-studying is also fine. Workload: Manageable. There are three assignments including the final exam, and one group project. The assignments look like they have many questions, but most were covered in class, and finding sources is extremely helpful. Grading: I got an A+. According to classmates, the grading is also quite good, likely due to a grading curve. It isn’t easy to get high marks on the two assignments because, like Chinese reading comprehension in high school, you score points only if you hit the marking criteria; if you miss them, you get nothing (which again shows the importance of sources). You still need to write more points.

reviews.content: emmm有点迷 不知道为啥烂🐢
reviews.translated_content: Hmm, a bit confusing. Not sure why the grading was poor.

reviews.content: wl绝对是偏大的cc，只能说有兴趣并且愿意花功夫的话，算得上一门fair的cc，wl包含了两篇paper总共十页a4纸吧，take home final(题量很多写得吐血)，一个group project要产出一个视频(想要做好还是靠组友)，总体比较难对于非商科同学不友好，但是好好学的话a range还是挺多的
reviews.translated_content: The workload is definitely on the high side for a Common Core course. I can only say that if you're interested and willing to put in the effort, it's a fair CC. The workload includes two papers totaling about ten A4 pages, a take-home final (with so many questions it made me bleed), and a group project requiring a video (doing it well really depends on your teammates). Overall, it's quite difficult and not friendly to non-business students, but if you study properly, there are quite a few A-range grades.

reviews.content: 老师是个大佬，课很硬核 给分一般
reviews.translated_content: The instructor is an expert. The course is rigorous and highly technical. Grading is average.

reviews.content: 比想象中好🐢太多，基本上没去过lecture都是看ppt自学。essay和小组作业都是自己认真搞得，最后的分数还挺满意。take home exam有点难，但好好学根据ppt写的最后还是成功拿到了A。
reviews.translated_content: Much easier to get a good grade than I expected. I basically never attended lectures and self-studied using the slides. I worked seriously on the essay and group assignment, and I was quite satisfied with the final score. The take-home exam was a bit difficult, but by studying properly and writing based on the slides, I successfully got an A.

reviews.content: 作业满分，gp几乎满分，上课积极参与讨论发言结果得了B+。向prof询问后得知final paper分数也好，但是attendance几乎为0，总分排在32名，所以得B+。没啥technical的东西，对经济感兴趣的朋友即使不是FBE student也能学好，如果有insights则预定满分。但是值得注意的是每次lecture&tutorial都要签到，所以一定不要迟到&注意签到表，不要像我一样努力一学期最后喜提B+。btw总分咬得挺紧的所以比较卷。
reviews.translated_content: I got full marks for assignments and nearly full marks for the group project. I participated actively in discussions during lectures, yet ended up with a B+. After asking the professor, I learned that my final paper score was also good, but my attendance was almost zero, and I ranked 32nd overall, hence the B+. There isn’t much technical content; friends interested in economics can do well even if they’re not FBE students, and if you have insights, a full mark is practically guaranteed. However, note that sign-in is required for every lecture and tutorial, so definitely don’t be late and keep an eye on the sign-in sheet. Don’t be like me, working hard all semester only to somehow get a B+. By the way, the total scores are very close, so it’s quite competitive.

reviews.content: 没听过课，assignment 1 rank3, 其他不知道，最后A
reviews.translated_content: I didn't attend any classes. I ranked 3rd on Assignment 1, don't know about the rest. Final grade: A.

reviews.content: 吹爆這門課，e人➕對創業有興趣的超級推薦。Lecture有點無聊但是Tutorial超級好玩，Tutor Benson的課堂互動性強➕全是硬核乾貨，又有趣又能學到東西。計分20% participation➕40% individual essay➕40% grp project Workload不算大建議和朋友一起讀然後reg同一個tut。最後grade A
reviews.translated_content: I cannot recommend this course highly enough. It comes super recommended for extroverts and those interested in entrepreneurship. Lectures are a bit boring, but tutorials are super fun. Tutor Benson’s classes are highly interactive and packed with rigorous, substantive content—both interesting and educational. Grading breakdown: 20% participation, 40% individual essay, 40% group project. The workload isn’t heavy. I suggest taking it with friends and registering for the same tutorial. I finished with an A.

reviews.content: 课程内容极水，学的基本上都是common sense，哪怕没听过一秒钟的课，都可以完成作业和assessment。组队太重要了！！！本人的individual essay拿了相当于A的分数，后因为group project最后只有B，后来发现同组两个香港groupmate取关了我ins：）几乎没有wl但烂龟的课，选的人祝你good luck
reviews.translated_content: The course content is extremely lightweight; you basically learn common sense. Even if you hadn’t attended a single second of class, you could still complete the assignments and assessments. Teamwork is crucial!!! My individual essay scored the equivalent of an A, but because of the group project I only got a B in the end. Later I discovered that two Hong Kong groupmates unfollowed me on Instagram :) A course with almost no workload but harsh grading—good luck to those who choose it.

reviews.content: wl小到离谱，gp真的看运气，individual分很高最后也没a
reviews.translated_content: The workload is ridiculously small. The group project really depends on luck; my individual score was high, but I still didn’t get an A.

reviews.content: 组队非常重要，tutor挺无语的个人偏好太重，教授完全不管事，全是tutor说了算。遇到烂组友，gp爆雷，individual paper很用心花了特别多时间做最后只有B+
reviews.translated_content: Team formation is crucial. The tutor was speechless-inducing due to strong personal biases, and the professor was completely hands-off, leaving everything to the tutor. I encountered bad group members, and the group project was a disaster. I put a lot of effort and time into the individual paper, but only got a B+ in the end.

reviews.content: 其实有兴趣了解创业和喜欢创业的同学可以选这门课，教授有特别丰富的行业经验，而且也是北大光华和港大合办EMBA的教授，上课会将他学生的创业故事，虽然ppt做的一般好看，留心听课的话，会学到特别多有意思的东西
reviews.translated_content: Students who are interested in learning about entrepreneurship and enjoy the subject can take this course. The professor has extensive industry experience and is also a professor in the joint EMBA programme between Peking University’s Guanghua School of Management and HKU. He shares his students’ entrepreneurial stories in class. Although the PowerPoint slides are just average in design, if you pay attention in lectures, you will learn many interesting things.

reviews.content: WL中等｜两个大Project：个人采访记录Essay+组队Pitch Deck Pre｜有Tutorial｜Group Pre记得提前组队｜纸质版Attendance｜挺有意思和干货的一门课
reviews.translated_content: Workload: Medium | Two major projects: an individual interview-record essay and a group pitch deck presentation | Has tutorials | Remember to form your group early for the group presentation | Paper-based attendance | An interesting course with substantive content.

reviews.content: wl小且好龟！不社恐的可选，每次tut都即兴发言，最终report认真写了，平时完全没给时间，A
reviews.translated_content: Low workload and generous grading! If you’re not uncomfortable with social participation, take it. Every tutorial requires impromptu speaking. I didn’t spend any time on it during the semester but wrote the final report seriously, and got an A.

reviews.content: 我真的吹爆这门课，教授和tutor！虽然因为疫情原因，不得不变成纯网课，但教授和tutor真的超级认真负责，课后有问题也会认真回答。workload不算大，但如果恢复面授应该会有field trip，可能会多占用一部分时间。总体来说，这肯定不是门能完全让你走向创业之路的课，但确实会让你对创业者有更多的了解及理解。
reviews.translated_content: I cannot recommend this course, the professor, and the tutor highly enough. Although we had to switch to fully online classes due to the pandemic, the professor and tutor were extremely serious and responsible, and answered questions diligently after class. The workload isn’t heavy, but if face-to-face teaching resumes there would likely be field trips, which might take up more time. Overall, this certainly isn’t a course that will set you on an entrepreneurial path, but it will give you greater insight and understanding of entrepreneurs.

Overall, it is a good course but you need to be willing to do reading and good at writing essays.

search_summary.title: Weapons of Mass Destruction: Science, Proliferation and Terrorism

course_info.title: Weapons of Mass Destruction: Science, Proliferation and Terrorism

reviews.content: 受疫情影响，只在第一周面授课，剩余课时发了一本讲义装订成的booklet。网课阶段Lemke经常落课、拖堂，好在内容比变成单人，始终没有透较简单，自学也没问题。上网课使评分方式变化较大，取消了final，essay由二人合作露各项assessment的加权，而且发布新评分方式、poster和essay主题都非常拖延。grade很烂，全组都没有在A range的同胞。慎选\掀桌  补充：workload较小...网课阶段对CC大概都是突击吧，只是写essay做poster会有reference的质量和不小的数量要求
reviews.translated_content: Due to the pandemic, we only had face-to-face classes in the first week; the remaining sessions were replaced by a booklet compiled from lecture notes. During the online phase, Lemke often missed classes and ran overtime. Fortunately, the content wasn’t too difficult since it essentially became self-study, which was manageable. Online learning led to significant changes in assessment: the final was cancelled, and the essay became a two-person collaboration, with various assessment weightings adjusted. Moreover, the new grading scheme, poster, and essay topics were released very late. The grades were poor; no one in our entire group got an A-range grade. Choose with caution / table flip. Addendum: The workload is relatively light... For Common Core courses during the online phase, it was mostly cramming. However, the essay and poster did have requirements for both the quality and a considerable quantity of references.

reviews.content: soso
reviews.translated_content: soso

reviews.content: 得分A- Workload：夹杂在toturial中有两至三次quiz，一篇双人合作essay，小组poster制作和prez，final。 课程讲授的内容还是比较有意思，包括核武器、生化武器、核条约和一些其他的大规模杀伤性武器。教授的口语很好，但是语速奇快，可能不太容易跟上。Quiz只有几道选择题，基本回顾下课件就能解决。Essay和poster感觉难度也不大，取决于组友；所谓的prez其实相当自由，所有组把poster贴在教室里像展览一样，只要在教授逛到你的poster时向他解释几句就行。Final就比较烦，纯背诵式，基本上就是课件里句子的完形填空。最后得分不理想可能是因为当时没掌握final的要点所以没怎么去背... 总之算是比较有意义的一门CC。
reviews.translated_content: Grade received: A-. Workload: Two to three quizzes mixed into tutorials, one two-person collaborative essay, a group poster production and presentation, and a final exam. The course content is quite interesting, covering nuclear weapons, biological and chemical weapons, nuclear treaties, and other weapons of mass destruction. The professor speaks English well, but his speed is unusually fast, so it might be hard to keep up. The quizzes have only a few multiple-choice questions, which can basically be solved by reviewing the lecture slides. The essay and poster don’t seem difficult; it depends on your group mates. The so-called presentation is actually quite free-form: all groups stick their posters in the classroom like an exhibition, and you just need to explain a few sentences to the professor when he visits your poster. The final exam is more troublesome; it’s purely rote memorisation, basically fill-in-the-blanks using sentences from the slides. My final grade wasn’t ideal, possibly because I didn’t grasp the key points for the final at the time and didn’t memorise much... All in all, it’s a fairly meaningful Common Core course.

If you put effort into the poster, getting an A-range grade is no problem. My friend revised seriously for the final and got an A+, but since I’m bad at rote memorisation for humanities subjects, I only got an A-.

search_summary.title: Globalization and Architecture

course_info.title: Globalization and Architecture

reviews.content: 来自理院，no archi basis。个人觉得比较有意思的一门课，讲如何从建筑特征设计看全球化趋势，除了建筑本身的知识还涉及到一些social science，history，econ的内容。workload不算特别多：会有3个field trip去艺术馆，码头，购物中心之类的地方，每去一次都要写一篇short response。每一次课后会有一个小quiz也是现写一篇short response。有一个midterm是写一篇论文（因为网课变成写一整天了，原本也是现写允许带小抄）。有两个project，一个individual可以自由研究一个建筑；一个组队，prof给你topic。reading是一本1厘米多厚的一本小书。虽然最后只有B+（可能是group project没抱到大腿。。），也没感觉自己学到啥，但还是挺推荐的。（毕竟其它评论都是a range hhh）
reviews.translated_content: From the Faculty of Science, with no architecture background. I personally found this course quite interesting. It discusses how to view globalization trends through architectural design features. Besides architecture itself, it covers some social science, history, and economics. The workload isn’t too heavy: there are three field trips to places like art galleries, piers, and shopping malls, and you have to write a short response after each visit. After every lecture, there’s a small quiz that also involves writing a short response on the spot. There’s a midterm essay (because of online classes, it became a full-day take-home exam; originally it was also written on the spot but allowed a permitted reference sheet). There are two projects: one individual where you can freely research a building, and one group project where the professor gives you the topic. The reading is a small book over 1 cm thick. Although I only got a B+ in the end (maybe because I didn’t team up with strong partners for the group project…) and didn’t feel like I learned much, I still recommend it. (After all, other reviews are all A-range, haha.)

reviews.content: workload不大，field trip有点意思，专业性太强了，对于不了解建筑的同学不太友好
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy, and the field trip is somewhat interesting. However, it’s highly specialized, which isn’t very friendly to students who don’t have a background in architecture.

reviews.content: 总体来说workload很小，老师是新加坡口音一开始有点听不清，后来习惯了就好了。GP组队非常重要，建议提前找靠谱的同学组好。midterm五选二写essay，没有final考试。Tutor人都挺好的。
reviews.translated_content: Overall, the workload is very light. The lecturer has a Singaporean accent, which was a bit hard to understand at first, but I got used to it. Forming your group project team is very important; I recommend finding reliable classmates to form a group in advance. For the midterm, you choose two out of five topics to write essays on. There is no final exam. The tutors are all nice.

reviews.content: grade好
reviews.translated_content: Good grade.

reviews.content: 蛮有意思的一个课 wl主要是读reading和final project 教授和tutor人都很好 tutorial积极一点分不错
reviews.translated_content: A quite interesting course. The workload mainly consists of readings and a final project. The professor and tutor are both very nice. If you participate actively in tutorials, you can get good marks.

reviews.content: lecture没意思，project还比较有趣，essay考试很水
reviews.translated_content: The lectures were boring, but the project was quite interesting. The essay exam was lightweight.

reviews.content: Koon人nice，field trip绝了特别好玩，建院的同学可以去建筑公司转转（看看未来的自己），建议建院大一都来选这门课，一门cc比大一上的两门专业课都干货。整体偏建筑理论，社科背景的同学也非常推荐这门课！PS建院可能会压分
reviews.translated_content: Koon is nice, and the field trip was amazing and really fun. Architecture students can visit architecture firms (to see their future selves). I recommend that all first-year Architecture students take this Common Core course; it has more substantive content than the two major courses I took in my first year. It leans toward architectural theory, so I also highly recommend it for students with a social sciences background! P.S. The Faculty of Architecture might grade harshly.

reviews.content: group project随机分配topic和组友，还蛮看运气的
reviews.translated_content: Topics and teammates for the group project are assigned randomly, so it depends quite a bit on luck.

reviews.content: 没有想象当中好龟…感觉自己挺认真的但还是b range
reviews.translated_content: The grading wasn’t as generous as I had imagined... I felt I was quite diligent, but I still ended up in the B range.

reviews.content: 课程并不涉及对建筑本身的技术讨论，更像是从社会学角度对人与空间关系的反思 Koon上課干货多多 reading非常有意思（虽然有一些没有很好读）  Workload在CC中偏中上，fieldtrip好玩。龟好，A range
reviews.translated_content: The course does not involve technical discussions of architecture itself; it is more like a sociological reflection on the relationship between people and space. Koon provides lots of substantive content in class, and the readings are very interesting (although some are not easy to read). The workload is on the higher side for a Common Core course, and the field trip was fun. The grading is generous, resulting in an A-range grade.

course_info.title: Challenges of Global Governance: Past and Present

reviews.content: 非politics同学不建议选，本人politics，essay只有B+，tutor是Adrian
reviews.translated_content: Not recommended for non-Politics students. I’m a Politics major, and I only got a B+ on the essay. My tutor was Adrian.

reviews.content: 不感兴趣慎选，真的催眠
reviews.translated_content: If you’re not interested, choose with caution; it’s truly hypnotic.

reviews.content: 主题：讲国际政治方面的（比如某个国家的外交政策，不同国家之间的关系等等），建议对这方面感兴趣的同学可以试试；如果一点都不感冒的话，上起来可能会觉得内容比较枯燥。  Workload：个人感觉不是特别大，但是essay占比较高（期中一篇1500words左右的essay，期末一篇2000words左右的essay）；lecture和tutorial各有10%的participation：lecture主要是pop quiz和attendance，tutorial主要是大家围绕tutor提出的问题进行讨论。由于这学期都在上网课，pop quiz就取消了，所以我个人感觉这20%就比之前要好拿一点...?不过这门课最重要的是没有prez和gp（对我这种自闭星人很友好）！！  Prof & Tutor：Dr. Chow英文超好！！而且上课风格挺风趣的，lecture上经常会放很多小视频（比如崔娃脱口秀的cut）来引入话题，总之不会很干巴巴！这个学期的tutor只有Jessica，因为上网课所以对她没有太多了解，个人感觉给分挺fair的，不会特别chur（可能只是我的片面看法，仅供大家参考）。最后得分A
reviews.translated_content: Topic: Covers international politics (e.g., a country’s foreign policy, relations between different countries, etc.). I recommend it for students interested in this area; if you’re not interested at all, you might find the content quite dry. Workload: Personally, I didn’t feel it was too heavy, but essays carry a high weight (one ~1500-word essay at mid-term, one ~2000-word essay at finals). Lecture and tutorial each account for 10% participation: lectures mainly involve pop quizzes and attendance, while tutorials focus on discussions around questions raised by the tutor. Since classes were online this semester, pop quizzes were cancelled, so I personally felt that this 20% was easier to secure than before...? However, the most important thing about this course is that there are no presentations or group projects (very friendly for introverts like me)!! Prof & Tutor: Dr. Chow’s English is excellent!! His teaching style is quite humorous, and he often plays short video clips (such as cuts from Trevor Noah’s stand-up) to introduce topics, so it’s never dry. This semester’s only tutor was Jessica. Due to online classes, I didn’t get to know her well, but I felt her grading was quite fair and not particularly strict (this may just be my partial view, for reference only). Final grade: A.

reviews.content: Ok course, if you have a very good knowledge of international history, international relations and politics. The course mainly relies on three major theories: constructivism, realism, liberalism and all topics are analyzed through these three theories. Take this course only if you are good at writing essays and/or like writing essays. The assignment essay and the final exam essay are not very long (1,500 - 2,000 words) so if you are used to that it shouldn't be an issue for you. The lecturer is very nice and open and you can ask him about any topic. The T.A. was also very friendly and was good at conveying knowledge.

reviews.translated_content: The course is quite interesting, mainly because the prof has great charisma, teaches vividly, speaks good English with little accent. Low workload: just one essay each for midterms and finals, plus regular tutorials, and that’s it. But personally I feel the grading wasn’t great; I scored over 80 on the midterm essay and got a B. After thinking it over, I took it on a pass/fail basis. Overall the course experience was quite good and I learned something; it’s suitable as an introduction to IR. If you’re not too concerned about grades or are already quite strong, you might consider it.

reviews.content: 对于对政治历史感兴趣的同学来说 算是不错的课了 内容大致关于各种不同的人道主义援助 有八个类别 讲到很多例子 每次tut要准备读一下reading 然后发言 习惯了还好 然后会分一个国家给你 你可以代表这个国家在一个人道主义危机冲突中选择立场和解决办法 期中大概写一篇文章分析自己的立场和建议 期末有一个大家讨论然后做出一个memo的gp  最后有个考试 大概给几天写篇essay  总的来说workload中等偏上 但是给分还行 gl如果没得选 选不上那些好课 又对政治还感兴趣 是个不错的选择
reviews.translated_content: For students interested in political history, this is a decent course. The content roughly covers various types of humanitarian aid, divided into eight categories, with many examples discussed. Each tutorial requires preparing by doing some reading and then speaking up; it’s fine once you get used to it. Then you are assigned a country, and you can represent that country in a humanitarian crisis conflict, choosing a stance and solutions. The midterm is roughly an essay analysing your stance and recommendations. For the final, there is a group project where everyone discusses and produces a memo, followed by an exam where you are given a few days to write an essay. Overall, the workload is medium-to-high, but the grading is okay. Good luck! If you have no choice, can’t get into those popular courses, and are interested in politics, this is a good option.

reviews.content: Larry是哈佛大学的博士毕业生，上课很认真。课程内容顾名思义，讲的是人类文明的发展史。这门课号称是communication intensive course，所以tutorial participation很重要，占了不少分，tutor会记录你的发言次数，不过个人觉得讨论话题很方便就能差得上话，不用提前做准备。另一大assessment就是每节课的quiz，6道单选题，内容来自课堂和reading，好好准备不难拿高分，但想每次都那高分甚至满分，我觉得有难度。最后一大assessment是group prez，和组友之间无需很多互动，每人分管同一个贫困国家的某一政府部门，从部门自身出发为脱贫提意见，我觉得不难。wl小，我在写这条comment的时候还没拿到grade，所以不知道给分如何。。。
reviews.translated_content: Larry is a PhD graduate from Harvard University and takes his teaching very seriously. As the name suggests, the course content covers the history of human civilization. This course is billed as a communication-intensive course, so tutorial participation is very important and accounts for a significant portion of the grade. The tutor will record how many times you speak, but personally I found it quite easy to join in on the discussion topics without needing to prepare in advance. Another major assessment is the quiz every class: 6 multiple-choice questions based on the lecture and readings. It’s not hard to get a high score if you prepare well, but I think it’s difficult to get a high score or even full marks every time. The final major assessment is a group presentation. There isn’t much need for interaction among group members; each person is responsible for a specific government department in the same impoverished country, proposing poverty-alleviation measures from that department’s perspective. I found it not difficult. The workload is small. I haven’t received my grade yet while writing this comment, so I don’t know how the grading is...

reviews.content:
wl其实还行，正常用功拿到A+。因为这次summer semester只有84个人参加，所以成绩按说会蛮卷的，好在有75%左右的summer visiting student所以又不卷了。99%的mainland visiting student的英语水平不支持ta们在tutorial上发言，整个tutorial完全是hkuer的主场，凡是举手都可以发言，甚至无所谓你说得多烂都会计入评分，所以uu们summer大胆冲！

然后评价一下好龟强度，占比30%的quiz一共错六道，curve后得分100%。占比30%的tutorial每节课差不多是十多次发言，是我们十二人tutroial中发言最多的人，得分100%。占比40%的pre应该烂了，教师评分48/60，真的很严，所有主观判断的打分项我都是tier2，好在别人估计也烂，所以我算烂中优。这个课正常学期上还有奇怪的bonus，类似写adjustment porposal以及在forum和prof互动，但summer没有，搞得我很紧张，最后龟也还好。

接下来是吐槽，前面哪个大佬说看看书+正常上课就可以让quiz全部满分？请回答一下这个鬼题：五选一，世界人口排名前十的国家中、哪个没有世界人口排名前十的城市？你看看这个是人能做出的题吗？不仅你得知道分开问题的20个国家/城市，还得知道它们的一一对应关系，xswl我觉得Larry在出新题上真的花样繁多，而且每个人题目不定，难度也不定，我觉得这个课就没人能抽到我这个题，所以quiz得分还得看命。

反正如果能拿到quiz往年题确实做起来会顺手很多，能要到近两年题目的人估计能全部押中原题。所以如果你读过中文版《人类简史》，并且对社会学感兴趣，还是支持大家选Larry的cc！
reviews.translated_content: The workload is actually okay; with normal effort, you can get an A+. Because only 84 students enrolled in this summer semester, the grading was expected to be highly competitive. Fortunately, about 75% were summer visiting students, so it wasn’t that competitive after all. The English proficiency of 99% of the Mainland visiting students didn’t support them speaking up in tutorials, so the tutorials were entirely dominated by HKU students. Anyone who raised their hand could speak, and it didn’t matter how poorly you spoke; it would still count toward your grade. So, everyone, go for it boldly in the summer!  Then, let’s evaluate the grading generosity. For the quiz, which accounts for 30%, I got only six questions wrong, and after curving, my score was 100%. For the tutorial component, also worth 30%, I spoke more than ten times per session and was the most active speaker in our twelve-person tutorial, scoring 100%. The presentation, worth 40%, probably went poorly; the instructor gave me 48/60. He is really strict with grading. I received Tier 2 on all subjectively graded items, but since others likely did poorly too, I was among the better of the poor performers. In a regular semester, this course has strange bonus tasks, such as writing an adjustment proposal and interacting with the professor on the forum, but there were none in the summer, which made me very nervous. In the end, the grade was still okay.  Now for the complaints. Which expert earlier claimed that just reading the book and attending class normally would guarantee full marks on the quiz? Please answer this absurd question: Multiple choice (one out of five). Among the top ten countries by world population, which one does not have a city in the top ten by world population? Is this a question a human can even answer? Not only do you need to know the 20 separate countries/cities, but you also need to know their one-to-one correspondence. LOL. I think Larry really comes up with diverse new questions. Moreover, each person gets different questions of varying difficulty. I feel like no one else in this course drew the same question as I did, so quiz scores depend on luck.  Anyway, if you can get past papers for the quizzes, it will be much easier to handle them. Those who can obtain questions from the last two years can probably guess all the original questions correctly. So if you have read the Chinese version of Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind and are interested in sociology, I still support everyone taking Larry’s Common Core course!

reviews.content: Heavy workloads…Readings are important for the quizzes.
reviews.translated_content: Heavy workloads…Readings are important for the quizzes.

reviews.content: Interesting course, which really makes you rationally-optimistic. The whole course is centered around almost one book - Rational Optimist by Matt Ridley. Sometimes you have to be absurdly active during the tutorials, as they literally count each your word. The workload is pretty high, given that there are quizzes on lectures every week. Highly recommend this course, but be ready for the workload

reviews.content: 被好龟评论一波带走。。自己的确有认真看lecture，认真读reading，但是结果不尽人意。 学的内容让我感觉这课像是个分享ideas的workshop(也就是水)，但是学的时候以为挺稳的也就没选择drop。 plus，presen得分高低和分配到的国家以及自己选的ministry很有关系（得分高的多是津巴布韦的economy minister），毕竟有些国家可以说的点很有局限性，我就没听说过身边人做housing ministry有好结果的！！
reviews.translated_content: I was swept away by the reviews saying it’s easy to get a good grade... I did watch the lectures and read the readings seriously, but the result was unsatisfactory. The content made me feel like this course was more of an idea-sharing workshop (i.e., lightweight), but I thought I was safe while taking it, so I didn’t drop it. Plus, your presentation score depends heavily on the country assigned to you and the ministry you choose (those who scored highly were mostly the economic ministers of Zimbabwe). After all, some countries have very limited points to discuss. I’ve never heard of anyone doing well with the housing ministry!!

reviews.content: summer上的，intensive mode，任务量很重，读两本书，隔一天一次quiz，同学更卷，给分相当严格，tutorial发言都是抢答，有时抢不到，这门课适合口语能力强的同学
reviews.translated_content: I took this in summer mode (intensive). The task load is very heavy: you have to read two books and there’s a quiz every other day. The cohort is highly competitive, and grading is quite strict. Tutorial participation is first-come-first-served; sometimes you can’t even get a chance to speak. This course suits students with strong oral communication skills.

reviews.content: 明明很chur，summer sem上得要死人了，最后一周半一天至少10个小时都在查资料改ppt，不知道从哪里传出来说这个课好龟的
reviews.translated_content: It’s actually very demanding; taking it in the summer semester was exhausting. In the last week and a half, I spent at least 10 hours a day researching and editing PowerPoint slides. I don’t know where the rumour started that this course has generous grading.

reviews.content: 拿好grade挺容易，但想拿A+非常難。放了很多心思在assignment和tutorial上面最終還是得A-。lecture内容有時會有點悶，不懂打瞌睡多少次了。wl 還不錯，不會太重，只要細心地完成assignment(group presentation)就ok。 這門課是communication intensive course 所以grading會注重在presentation skills和tutorial participation。鼓勵大家拿這堂cc，尤其在暑假時侯。可是要注意這cc很hot，會很快爆滿。
reviews.translated_content: It is quite easy to get a good grade, but very difficult to get an A+. I put a lot of effort into the assignments and tutorials but still only got an A-. The lecture content can be a bit boring; I lost count of how many times I dozed off. The workload is acceptable and not too heavy; it is fine as long as you complete the assignment (group presentation) carefully. This is a communication-intensive course, so grading focuses on presentation skills and tutorial participation. I encourage everyone to take this Common Core course, especially in the summer. However, note that this Common Core course is very popular and fills up quickly.

reviews.content: 好🐢是個傳說，為了拉開分數和grade，導致相差一點點分數就會差很多grade
reviews.translated_content: Generous grading is a myth. To spread out the scores and grades, even a small difference in marks results in a large difference in grades.
