course_info.title: Europe without Borders?

reviews.content:
上课不让看电子产品，但是老师有点吹水。reading material特别好，pavel的tutorial讲得特别好，还是学到了很多有意思的关于现当代欧洲政治和历史的知识。最后的大作业是模联，有些混乱，但是还是比较有体验感的。
这门课选课的国际生也比较多，前几周大家上课都比较活跃的时候确实是感受到了一下hku diversity的好处，就是prof讲到哪个国家，问有没有来自这个国家的人，基本上都有（俄罗斯小哥好几个，以色列小哥，巴勒斯坦裔移民，波兰人，意大利人英国人德国人法国人），还有很多一看就是特别喜欢欧洲现代战争史，像是history society的local小哥，感觉大家上课的时候还是很活人，所以暂且忍了一下Auer有时候开始疯狂吹水hh。
这门课好像不给A+，dz因为reading response分数不是特别高，最后A-。
reviews.translated_content: Electronic devices are not allowed in class, but the professor tends to ramble a bit. The reading materials are excellent, and Pavel’s tutorials are taught very well. I learned a lot of interesting knowledge about contemporary European politics and history. The final major assignment was a Model United Nations simulation. It was a bit chaotic, but still provided a good experiential learning opportunity. This course has a relatively high number of international students. During the first few weeks when everyone was more active in class, I truly experienced the benefits of HKU’s diversity: whenever the professor mentioned a country and asked if anyone was from there, there was usually someone (several Russian guys, an Israeli guy, a Palestinian immigrant, Poles, Italians, Brits, Germans, French people). There were also many local students who clearly loved modern European military history, like members of the History Society. I felt that the students were quite engaged and alive in class, so I tolerated Auer occasionally going off on long rants haha. It seems this course does not give A+ grades. Because my reading response scores were not particularly high, I ended up with an A-.

reviews.content: 超级好龟！Pierce我滴超人！！！lecture基本没怎么听，全靠每周reading和tutorial理解当周的话题。Pierce真的人超好超级耐心！选他的tutorial的话需要多发言（会记录活跃度），然后期末simulation多多活跃就没什么大问题！我的两篇essay写得一般般不过参与讨论和最后的模拟都比较活跃最后a
reviews.translated_content: Extremely generous grading! Pierce is my hero!!! I barely listened in lectures and relied entirely on the weekly readings and tutorials to understand the topics. Pierce is genuinely a wonderful and super patient person! If you choose his tutorial, you need to speak up more (participation is recorded), and if you are active in the final simulation, there shouldn’t be any major issues. My two essays were just average, but I was quite active in discussions and the final simulation, so I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: 来到HKU的第一个A+！这门课今年由Pavel当tutor后实际上是会给A+的！Lecture和所有Coursework都没有关系，而且lecture都比较吹水，但如果想了解多一些有关欧洲历史还是蛮有趣的。Tutorial部分才是真正学东西的，从欧洲民族矛盾，到欧洲的核心文化，到底什么促成了欧洲人这个身份，都非常有趣。至于workload真的轻得不能再行，tutorial上的讨论（去之前只需要看一篇很短的文章，并且就算没看也能吹水）+2篇300字的reading response（一篇A+ 一篇A）再到最后一份4页的Policy paper （实际上是4个人一起写，也就是说一人一页），最后是模拟欧盟紧急峰会，讨论应否加速审理乌克兰的入盟申请，尽管程序上有所混乱，但是也真的模拟到了政治在现实中的乱象，以及政治就是一门谈判妥协的艺术。可惜不知道为什么25-26取消了，如果后来的学弟学妹看到了，又刚好看到了这门课再次举办，真的非常建议选择。
reviews.translated_content: My first A+ at HKU! This year, with Pavel as the tutor, the course actually does give A+ grades! Lectures have no relation to any coursework, and the lectures tend to ramble a bit, but they are quite interesting if you want to learn more about European history. The tutorial part is where you really learn. From ethnic conflicts in Europe to the core culture of Europe and what constitutes European identity, everything is very interesting. As for the workload, it could not be lighter: discussions in tutorials (you only need to read one very short article beforehand, and even if you haven’t read it, you can still chat), two 300-word reading responses (one got an A+, one got an A), and finally a 4-page policy paper (actually written by a group of four, meaning one page per person). The last component was a simulated EU emergency summit discussing whether to accelerate the review of Ukraine’s accession application. Although the procedure was somewhat chaotic, it truly simulated the chaos of politics in reality and showed that politics is the art of negotiation and compromise. Unfortunately, I do not know why it was cancelled for the 2025–26 academic year. If junior students see this and happen to see this course offered again in the future, I highly recommend choosing it.

reviews.content:
劝退，grade不好，上tutorial巨大压力，而且participation mark非常主观，只要你一开始跟tutor心中的答案有差别的话，就算后来表现好也没有用；policy paper workload 还好，但如果碰着不好的teammates就非常辛苦；整个course给grade很迷，就算你在大部分assessment 都是a range，最后也没能拿a range 的grade，我真服了
professor则是从头到尾都没见过他回复email
上课不让用电子设备，巨无聊
英语不好的快逃
唯一的优点是reading material很有趣
reviews.translated_content: Avoid this course. The grades are poor, and there is immense pressure in tutorials. The participation mark is very subjective; if your initial answers differ from what the tutor has in mind, performing well later does not help. The policy paper workload is manageable, but it becomes very tough if you get bad teammates. The overall grading is confusing; even if you achieved A-range results in most assessments, you still did not get an A-range final grade. I am really frustrated. The professor never replied to emails from start to finish. Electronic devices are not allowed in class, which makes it extremely boring. If your English is not good, run away. The only advantage is that the reading materials are interesting.

reviews.content: Workload基本为零，整个学期两篇300词的reading response，一个小组作业和一个debate。课程主要讲欧盟的各种精巧设计背后蕴含的政治理念和历史因素，干货很多。Dr.Auer是斯洛伐克人，自己的人生经历就可以充当非常鲜活的讲课材料。最后的gp可能看上去会有点棘手但评分时的要求和这个project所占的权重应该也没有特别高。reading response和小组作业的书面部分好好写的话A range难度应该不大。但要注意这门课的syllabus是明确写了不给A+的，想要A+的朋友可以绕道。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is basically zero: two 300-word reading responses, one group project, and one debate over the whole semester. The course mainly covers the political ideas and historical factors behind the EU’s sophisticated designs, with lots of substantive content. Dr. Auer is from Slovakia, and his personal life experiences serve as very vivid teaching material. The final group project might look a bit tricky, but the grading criteria and the weight of this project aren’t particularly high. If you write the reading responses and the written part of the group project well, getting an A-range grade shouldn’t be too hard. But note that the syllabus explicitly states no A+ grades are given, so if you’re aiming for an A+, you might want to avoid this course.

reviews.content: 良心好grade课！pierce你是我的神！两篇短essay平均分只有B，但是每节tutorial有积极发言，simulation我们组也只发言了一次。本来以为最多只有b+没想到和其他组友最后都拿了A！除了每周要读reading以外wl不大，而且讲欧洲历史政治相关的议题也确实讲得很有趣！强推！
reviews.translated_content: A conscientious course with favourable grading! Pierce, you are my god! The average for the two short essays was only a B, and although we spoke actively in every tutorial, our group only spoke once during the simulation. I thought I’d get at most a B+, but unexpectedly, my groupmates and I all got As! Apart from the weekly readings, the workload isn’t heavy, and the topics on European history and politics are taught in a really interesting way! Highly recommended!

reviews.content: 这个课如果不是对欧洲历史文化政治特别感兴趣➕口语不是特别好就劝退了，平时的reading也非常demanding，最大压力就是上tutorial真不知道讲啥，lecture也是巨无聊必睡，如果对欧洲有兴趣可以多看看新闻和书就没必要上这个课了❌
reviews.translated_content: Unless you are particularly interested in European history, culture, and politics, and your spoken English is decent, I’d advise staying away from this course. The regular reading load is very demanding. The biggest pressure comes from tutorials, where I really didn’t know what to discuss. The lectures were also extremely boring and guaranteed to put you to sleep. If you’re interested in Europe, you might as well read more news and books; there’s no need to take this course ❌.

reviews.content: 超级好课推荐！！！wl非常flexible，想学习知识可以学到很多，只是单纯想上水课可以把wl调整为0。本人是lecture什么都没听，每周100页reading也从来不看，tutorial积极发言，essay临时看个文章抱佛脚，自己很喜欢simulation所以参与积极。龟极好无比！轻松A
reviews.translated_content: Super good course, highly recommended!!! The workload is very flexible. If you want to learn, you can gain a lot of knowledge; if you just want an easy ride, you can adjust the workload to zero. Personally, I didn't listen to anything in lectures and never read the 100 pages of weekly readings. I participated actively in tutorials, crammed an article right before the essay deadline, and engaged actively because I really enjoyed the simulation. The grading was incredibly generous! An easy A.

reviews.content: 课程包含了欧洲历史，思想，政治等，required reading每周都有但是都不是很长，每周的tutorial需要讨论reading的内容，wl算正常，有participation，debate，两篇短essay一篇长essay，上下来还是可以学到很多内容的，并且很有意思，认真学，认真读各种required和further readings成绩应该不错的。
reviews.translated_content: The course covers European history, thought, politics, etc. There is required reading every week, but it's not very long. Weekly tutorials require discussing the reading content. The workload is normal. There is participation, debate, two short essays, and one long essay. You can still learn a lot from it, and it's quite interesting. If you study seriously and read various required and further readings, your grade should be decent.

reviews.content: 上课老师自己讲 内容不会打在PPT上  workload小 一学期就3个作业和一个debate 给龟应该可以 一整个学期啥都没听懂混了一个b+ 坐我前面的大佬摞A了好像
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer just talks; the content isn't on the slides. The workload is light—just three assignments and one debate for the whole semester. The grading should be okay. I didn't understand anything all semester and still managed a B+, while the very strong student sitting in front of me seemed to get an A.

reviews.content: 上了一半我實在覺得離譜。 。 。 首先wl大，期中做20min+（實際上所有環節完成要40min+）的reading pre，一篇1500的essay，一篇900的report，final還要做video，為了video還需要做很多調查採訪。 我認為身為cc這個wl相當不合理，不光不適合yr1-2的學生，已經遠超了一些理科advanced專業課一學期的wl。 其次，老師的講課方式相對片面，可能有本身是社科人+vegan視角的原因，課堂基本在輸出老師的看法，而且並不新穎，至於觀點碰撞和討論可以說就是沒有；不光跳過 了menti裡很多值得討論的發言，老師對不少問題的觀點也有局限性，例如大熊貓保護。 這門課確實拋出了很多inspiring的問題，但它本可以做得更好的，上到現在啥都沒學到，挺失望的。 說得難聽一點就是在情緒輸出。
reviews.translated_content: After attending half the course, I truly feel it is absurd... First, the workload is heavy: a 20+ minute reading presentation in the midterm (actually 40+ minutes to complete all parts), a 1500-word essay, a 900-word report, and a video for the final, which requires a lot of survey and interview work. I think this workload is quite unreasonable for a Common Core course. It is not only unsuitable for Year 1–2 students but far exceeds the workload of some advanced science major courses for a whole semester. Secondly, the professor's teaching style is relatively one-sided. Possibly due to her background as a social science major and a vegan perspective, the class basically outputs the teacher's views, which are not novel. As for viewpoint collision and discussion, there is practically none. She not only skipped many worth-discussing comments in Mentimeter, but her views on many questions also have limitations, such as giant panda conservation. This course did raise many inspiring questions, but it could have been done better. Up to now, I haven't learned anything and am quite disappointed. To put it bluntly, it is just emotional venting.

reviews.content: 我是思維方式偏文科的理科生 （生物/生命科學綜合類專業），對社會科學以及對生命的哲學探討有興趣，所以整個CCGL類裡獨選這門課。作為從初中就一直深思動物跟人類的關係/差別/平等權益等問題的人，這門課講了許多入門的切入點，但也不乏更全面地概括了之前我未曾想過的層面，比如老師問我們「有沒有發現，人類日常生活語言中，常常用動物來侮辱或是貶低別人，比如駡別人如豬如夠之類？」。學生們會被引導去思考為何我們已經把這些事情看地理所當然。又例如「為何人開車撞死某隻寵物時，是向其主人賠償及承擔法律責任而非判定為【過失殺人】？若是撞死為未成年孩童，肯定會需要其父母監護人出面釐清法律問題，為何動物未享有跟人一樣的法律地位？」。  這些問題隨便一列舉，很快會發現，生命不是平等的，又或者說，「生命平等」是個美好的主義，但是幾乎不可能實現，即使一個人吃全素不用皮毛等等也難免觸犯傷害動物的原則，會陷入自我的道德探討及問責中。可能因為這個課的主題我本就十分有興趣，所以學地很享受，雖然我本期待著比它所呈現的更深度更激烈的思辨 （偏哲學/法律/生命平等權益的部分是很後面才介紹的，故而沒法花很多時間，前面大部分把主力放在引導學生覺察自己跟動物的關係上了）。
reviews.translated_content: I am a science student (majoring in Biology/Life Sciences) with a humanities-oriented mindset. I am interested in social sciences and philosophical discussions about life, so I chose this course exclusively from the entire CCGL category. As someone who has been deeply contemplating the relationship/differences/equal rights between animals and humans since middle school, this course provided many introductory entry points, but also comprehensively covered aspects I had not previously considered. For example, the teacher asked us, “Have you noticed that in everyday human language, we often use animals to insult or belittle others, such as calling someone a pig or a dog?” Students are guided to think about why we take these things for granted. Another example is, “Why is it that when a person hits and kills a pet with a car, they compensate the owner and bear legal liability rather than being charged with [manslaughter]? If a minor child were killed, the parents or guardians would definitely need to step in to clarify legal issues; why do animals not enjoy the same legal status as humans?” Listing these questions quickly reveals that life is not equal, or rather, “equality of life” is a beautiful ideal but almost impossible to achieve. Even if a person is vegan and does not use fur, etc., they inevitably violate the principle of not harming animals, leading to self-moral exploration and accountability. Perhaps because I was already very interested in the theme of this course, I enjoyed learning it very much, although I originally expected deeper and more intense speculation (the parts leaning towards philosophy/law/equal rights for life were introduced quite late, so not much time could be spent on them; most of the earlier part focused on guiding students to become aware of their relationship with animals).

reviews.content: boring as fxxk and pointless
reviews.translated_content: Boring as fxxk and pointless

reviews.content: 內容我很喜歡，討論了不少動物在人類社會上的用途和遭遇，不過說真的，reading report 還有reflective essay 真的好難，我的分好低，幸虧之後的video making 另我有b+
reviews.translated_content: I really liked the content. We discussed the uses and experiences of animals in human society quite a bit. But honestly, the reading report and reflective essay were really difficult, and my marks were very low. Fortunately, the subsequent video-making assignment lifted me to a B+.

reviews.content: 内容：内容真的是挺好的，关于如何去看待人和动物的关系，我们对待动物的一些方式算不算虐待，又是不是过度地怜悯，站在动物的角度考虑事情是否就能考虑到了动物的感受，人和动物是否应该平等，怎样的平等又算作平等，利用其他动物是一种自然合理的行为还是一种虐待行为。 给分：不过给分挺严格的，不过本来我就打算所有的非理科cc都是B+的，文科社科对我来说太费脑子了。。。作业也挺多的（我们组的题目自己chur了自己。。。），分组真的很重要。这门课挺不容易报的，我报了六次才报上，但是内地生却出奇的少，我那个学期好像只有我一个大陆学生。。。
reviews.translated_content: Content: The content is really good, covering how to view human–animal relationships, whether certain ways we treat animals count as abuse or excessive pity, whether considering things from animals’ perspectives truly captures their feelings, whether humans and animals should be equal and what equality means, and whether using other animals is natural and reasonable or abusive. Grading: However, grading is quite strict. But I already expected all non-science Common Core courses to yield B+; humanities and social sciences are too mentally taxing for me... There’s also quite a lot of assignments (our group pushed ourselves hard on the topic...), and grouping is really important. This course is quite hard to enrol in; I tried six times before getting in, but there were surprisingly few students from Mainland China—it seemed like I was the only mainland student that semester...

reviews.content: 课程内容是好的，guest talk也是好的，唯一让我郁闷了整个学期的就是tutor Sophia，问建议时给出的回答不清晰，根据tutor指示减去某些部分的作业被说缺少那个部分🙄准备presentation时完全按照tutor建议去除了做问卷的计划，结束present后tutor表示最好做个问卷，给出的问卷问题exactly就是我们当时拟定的问题。哦还有遇到了freerider，总之这门课真的上得我一肚子火，workload大龟不好，想受气的请便。
reviews.translated_content: The course content is good, and the guest talks are good too. The only thing that depressed me throughout the semester was the tutor, Sophia. Her advice was unclear when I asked for suggestions, and work I omitted based on her instructions was later criticised as missing that part 🙄. When preparing the presentation, I removed the survey plan entirely according to her advice, but after the presentation, she said it would have been better to include a survey, and the survey questions she suggested were exactly the ones we had drafted at the time. Oh, and I also encountered a free rider. In short, this course really made me furious. The workload is heavy and the grading is poor. If you want to suffer, go ahead.

reviews.content: 补充一下关于freerider的问题，原本课程详情写得清清楚楚有peer review section，Sophia为了图方便在我们present完以后直接告诉所有人既然没有收到举报，她assume每个组都合作得很愉快，所以peer review section就不弄了，除非两天内举报并且让他通知所有组员有人不满意group project的分工。我当场傻眼。
reviews.translated_content: To add to the issue of free riders: the course description clearly stated there would be a peer review section. However, for convenience, Sophia told everyone after our presentations that since she hadn’t received any complaints, she assumed every group had collaborated happily, so she wouldn’t conduct the peer review. Unless someone reported within two days and asked her to notify all group members that they were dissatisfied with the division of labor in the group project. I was dumbfounded.

reviews.content: Interesting course, hv heart to do essay and project than grade will be ok
reviews.translated_content: Interesting course, hv heart to do essay and project than grade will be ok

reviews.content: 我不理解，为什么我什么都做了，quiz也做了，gp也做了，slides也交了，reflection paper也交了，为什么是个D？不是说好🐢吗？为什么是个D
reviews.translated_content: I don’t understand. Why did I get a D when I did everything—completed the quizzes, the group project, submitted the slides, and handed in the reflection paper? Wasn’t it supposed to have generous grading? Why a D?

reviews.content: Very nice prof and tutors. I think if you are passionate about the topic of suicide and mental well being in general, this course is for you. Relatively easy to achieve the A range if you put in some work in my PERSONAL opinion. Have fun!
reviews.translated_content: Very nice prof and tutors. I think if you are passionate about the topic of suicide and mental well being in general, this course is for you. Relatively easy to achieve the A range if you put in some work in my PERSONAL opinion. Have fun!

reviews.content: 社工的课，跟原来预期差距还挺大的，本来以为更偏向研究自杀者心理之类的。wl挺小的，给龟一般。喜欢社工的可冲
reviews.translated_content: It’s a social work course, quite different from my original expectations; I thought it would focus more on the psychology of people who attempt suicide. The workload is quite light, but the grading is average. If you like social work, go for it.

reviews.content: 很喜欢的一门课 从心理学 社会学等方面讲了一些预防自杀的知识 内地生很少 wl小 主要是quiz+一个gp的proposal&prez+一篇reflection quiz主要内容是lecture讲的东西和一小部分reading 基本看看PPT都能找到 gp就是要设计一个预防自杀的项目 认识的local朋友也很nice 大概选这门课的都是内心温柔善良的人吧
reviews.translated_content: A course I really liked. It covers knowledge on suicide prevention from psychological and sociological perspectives. There are very few students from Mainland China. The workload is light. Assessments are mainly quizzes, a group project proposal and presentation, and a reflection paper. The quiz content is mostly from the lectures and a small part from the readings; you can basically find the answers just by looking at the PowerPoint slides. The group project involves designing a suicide prevention programme. The local friends I met were also very nice. Perhaps those who choose this course are all gentle and kind-hearted people.

reviews.content: 好老师好课感兴趣可以上，所有tutor都很温柔，讲的东西也很有意义，但是龟就一般，我上的挺认真的也没缺课tutorial也挺活跃的但是最后B，可能是第一次写reflection paper不知道老师到底想看什么样的paper吧，然后group presentation也有一点草率，和local没有沟通好，同tutorial的其他组都准备的特别特别好可能相比之下我们就逊色了一点。
reviews.translated_content: Good teacher, good course—if you’re interested, you can take it. All the tutors are very gentle, and the material is meaningful. However, the grading is just average. I attended diligently, didn’t miss any classes, and was quite active in tutorials, but I still got a B in the end. Maybe it was because it was my first time writing a reflection paper and I wasn’t sure what the instructor was looking for. Also, our group presentation was a bit sloppy; we didn’t communicate well with the local students. Other groups in the same tutorial prepared exceptionally well, so we probably looked inferior by comparison.

reviews.content: 和上课之前想象的内容不太一样，主要是讲社工和social innovation的。好在workload很小，就一个proposal一篇essay。
reviews.translated_content: The content was different from what I imagined before class; it mainly focused on social work and social innovation. Fortunately, the workload was very light, with just one proposal and one essay.

reviews.content: 感觉自己没怎么认真上，结果最后给了A+。wl不大，group project也不会特别严格。Quiz基本上把资料看完就可以做出，最后的essay也很好写。但是因为是关于心理健康和自杀问题的课，一些内容和案例真的听得很难受，太容易共情的可以选择性听课。
reviews.translated_content: I didn’t pay much attention in class, but I still got an A+ in the end. The workload isn’t heavy, and the group project isn’t particularly strict. You can basically answer the quiz questions just by reading through the materials, and the final essay is easy to write. However, since this course covers mental health and suicide, some of the content and case studies were really distressing to hear. If you’re highly empathetic, you might want to choose whether to attend selectively.

reviews.content: not recommended, the project feedback given by the tutor is unclear and useless
reviews.translated_content: not recommended, the project feedback given by the tutor is unclear and useless

reviews.content: 被我水过的一门课 基本没去上过课 tuto应该需要积极参与一下容易拿好龟但我没有 workload挺小 印象中是做一个poster写一篇essay 几乎没学的课拿了B也算还行吧
reviews.translated_content: This is a course I coasted through. I basically didn’t attend classes. You probably need to participate actively in tutorials to get a good grade, but I didn’t. The workload was quite small. From what I remember, there was a poster and an essay. I got a B in a course where I hardly studied, which is acceptable.

search_summary.title: Responding to the Challenges of Aging Societies

course_info.title: Responding to the Challenges of Aging Societies

reviews.content: 这门课是一门需要认真对待的课。wl不大，但有一门期中考试（感觉大家分差有点大，有90多分的也有很低分的，均分65），一篇essay，一个小组合作的report或prez。给龟比较公平，但是不会压分。教授和tutor都很nice。建议对ageing感兴趣的学生可以尝试一下这门课。最后A range。
reviews.translated_content: This is a course that needs to be taken seriously. The workload isn’t heavy, but there is one midterm (I feel the score spread was quite large, with some above 90 and some very low; the average was 65), one essay, and a group report or presentation. Grading is fairly fair and not harsh. The professor and tutor are both nice. Students interested in ageing might want to try this course. I got an A-range grade in the end.

reviews.content: 好龟，讲香港的老龄化，lecture纯读ppt，自己看看得了。tutorial要记录考勤，需要积极回答问题。最终考核包括一次小考（前7个ppt好好看 做了份例题仔细点有90+），一个小组作业（要提前联系好采访的老人），和一个essay。总体wl中规中矩，认真去tutorial就没啥问题。a range，叫我ding神
reviews.translated_content: Generous grading. It covers aging in Hong Kong. The lectures are just reading off the slides, so you might as well study them yourself. Tutorials take attendance, and you need to answer questions actively. The final assessment includes a quiz (study the first 7 sets of slides carefully; if you do the sample questions carefully, you can get 90+), a group project (you need to contact the elderly interviewees in advance), and an essay. Overall, the workload is average. If you attend tutorials seriously, there won’t be any problems. I got an A-range grade; call me Ding Shen.

reviews.content: 大家好，我是zhuang神，ccgl9054我只需略释小计直接a＋拿下，楼下ding神只能说还得再练练
reviews.translated_content: Hello everyone, I am Zhuang Shen. For CCGL9054, I only needed to use a little trick to secure an A+ directly. Ding Shen below can only say he needs more practice.

reviews.content: nice
reviews.translated_content: nice

reviews.content: Lecture比较无聊，上课几乎没怎么听。wl很小，平时没有作业只有tutorial的reading。term test前临时学了概念，最后将近80，刚刚过mean。没怎么花心思在这门课上但最后也有A-，很惊喜。如果上课认真听再背好ppt的话应该会更好龟。
reviews.translated_content: The lectures are quite boring, and I barely listened in class. The workload is very light; there are no regular assignments, only tutorial readings. I crammed the concepts before the term test and scored nearly 80, just above the mean. I didn’t put much effort into this course but still got an A-, which was a pleasant surprise. If I had listened carefully in class and memorised the slides, I probably would have gotten an even better grade.

reviews.content: lecture 有点无聊。期中考试考前需要复习一下notes，考的内容基本上是lecture和tutorial讲的东西，不难，最后A。
reviews.translated_content: The lectures are a bit boring. You need to review the notes before the midterm. The exam content is basically what was covered in lectures and tutorials, so it’s not difficult. I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: lecture有点无聊，tutorial有趣，给分fair。有个term test需要认真准备，不单单是考背诵，还要理解内容，考试会给情景题考concept。
reviews.translated_content: The lectures are a bit boring, but the tutorials are interesting, and the grading is fair. There is one term test that requires serious preparation; it’s not just about rote memorisation, you also need to understand the content. The exam includes scenario-based questions testing concepts.

reviews.content: Interesting tutorials but boring lecture. The project required a video instead of presentation, so it might be difficult for those who don't know IT.
reviews.translated_content: Interesting tutorials but boring lecture. The project required a video instead of presentation, so it might be difficult for those who don't know IT.

reviews.content: 这门课cc需要稍微认真对待，因为有mid-term 然后prez和essay 也得认真写 注意interviewee的选择 尽量选符合aging要求的写 就会好龟 prez我们选的是做游戏卡牌 难度非常大 但是我们还是做出来了 最后A+
reviews.translated_content: This Common Core course requires a bit of serious attention because there is a midterm, and you need to write the presentation and essay carefully. Pay attention to your choice of interviewee; try to choose someone who fits the aging society criteria, and you will get a good grade. For our presentation, we chose to create a card game. It was very difficult, but we managed to pull it off. In the end, I got an A+.

reviews.content: 挺良心的一门课，workload不大，可能因为是新课所以给分也不错，老师人也很好，最终得分A，内容是关于种族屠杀的，从很多不同的角度看这个问题，很有趣 50%的project，最多三人一起做，也可以自己做，形式很自由，基本上想怎么做都可以，就是有字数限制，20%的分是plan，感觉基本都有A range，但是对citation要求很严格 20%的weekly response，在一张小纸片上写，每次满分3分，大部分人会拿到2分，个人感觉想拿3分主要是看想法是不是比较独特 30%是课上的participation，这个我其实也不太知道是怎么评的，大概就是多说话多刷存在感吧，Reading其实挺难读也挺多的，而且每次都有，但是不读好像一般问题也不大，想办法在课上说话就好
reviews.translated_content: It’s a fairly conscientious course. The workload isn’t heavy, and perhaps because it was a new course, the grading was also quite good. The teacher is very nice. I ended up with an A. The content is about genocide, examining the issue from many different angles, which is quite interesting. The project is worth 50%; you can work in a group of up to three people or do it individually. The format is very flexible—you can basically do whatever you want, though there is a word limit. The proposal is worth 20%, and I feel most people get an A-range grade for it, but the citation requirements are very strict. Weekly responses are worth 20%; you write them on a small piece of paper, with a maximum of 3 marks each time. Most people get 2 marks. Personally, I feel that to get 3 marks, your ideas need to be somewhat unique. Participation in class is worth 30%. I’m not really sure how this is assessed; it’s probably just about speaking up more and making your presence felt. The readings are actually quite difficult and plentiful, and there are readings every time, but it doesn’t seem to be a big problem if you don’t read them. Just figure out a way to speak in class.

reviews.content: 总体来说professor口语迷幻，备课不认真；讲课时语无伦次，毫无逻辑性，思想混乱。 所以别上 千万别上 。 理科生快跑 跑断腿也要跑
reviews.translated_content: Overall, the professor’s spoken English was confusing, and lesson preparation seemed careless. The lectures were incoherent, lacked logic, and showed confused thinking. So don’t take this course—definitely avoid it. Science students, run away; run as fast as you can.

reviews.content: 这学期算是选了个比较感兴趣的cc了，课程主要是讲历史上比较有名的大屠杀案例，上课的方式基本就是讨论不同case然后穿插一些理论和辩论。平时每周的作业是课前的一个小quiz大概3道题（占30%），我最后两次test各错一道，其他全部满分；每节课后需要看后面一天tutorial的reading material，tutorial课上的发言占总成绩的30%，助教很严格会要求学生多多发言然后也会一直观察每个学生的专注程度来打分，我平均每节助教课都会发言1-2次。剩下40%可以自己选择是做group project还是写logbook。我选择了后者因为怕freerider，每节课后写一个300左右的课程总结和reflection。wl不算大这门课，没有期中没有期末很爽，但是一定要认真听课，上课没有zoom回放没有ppt提供，纯靠自己的笔记复习quiz和写logbook，最后B+。
reviews.translated_content: This semester I chose a Common Core course that I'm quite interested in. The course mainly covers famous historical genocide cases. The teaching method basically involves discussing different cases interspersed with some theory and debate. The weekly assignment is a short pre-class quiz of about three questions (worth 30%). I got one question wrong in each of the last two tests and full marks for all others. After each class, you need to read the material for the next day's tutorial. Participation in tutorials accounts for 30% of the total grade. The teaching assistant is strict, requires students to speak up frequently, and constantly observes each student's level of focus to assign marks. I spoke up 1-2 times on average in each TA session. For the remaining 40%, you can choose between doing a group project or writing a logbook. I chose the latter because I was afraid of free riders, writing a course summary and reflection of about 300 words after each class. The workload isn't heavy for this course. No midterm, no final exam, which is great. But you must listen carefully in class. There are no Zoom recordings or PPTs provided; you rely entirely on your own notes to revise for quizzes and write the logbook. I got a B+ in the end.

reviews.content: 总体体验不是特别好，课程被分成了theory-case-theory三个部分，但是讲theory的部分和讲case的部分都没讲太明白（可能讨论最多的就是联合国现在关于genocide的定义了）。关于case：在基本事实、时间线不清晰的情况下讲细节。关于theory：譬如最后反思the politics of memory的部分，本以为会介绍比较多大屠杀相关的理论思考，但是只是看了一堆memorial（提到阿伦特、鲍曼的部分也完全没讲清楚）。tutor Penny一直让人感觉有些严格，会根据发言打勾记分，这种被observed，tutorial大家争相发言拿分的感觉真的很累。最后给分却意料之中（老师说we're willing to give out A+）又出乎意料（大约是全程没拿过成绩，最后的project又没有参考，只能和groupmate闷头做）地很好（A+）。另外一个minor feeling：感觉Dr sacks 全程sounds like非常有礼貌且caring但又常常让人觉得他礼貌得太熟练有点冷漠......评分：30%participation，20%quiz（lecture上提到的内容，lecture后两天内任意时间完成，历时30min，个人加起来大概错了四五题的样子），50%group project（tutorial内组队）
reviews.translated_content: The overall experience wasn’t particularly good. The course was divided into three parts: theory–case–theory. However, neither the theory nor the case sections were explained very clearly (perhaps the most discussed topic was the current UN definition of genocide). Regarding the cases: details were discussed without a clear grasp of basic facts or timelines. Regarding the theory: for example, in the final reflection on “the politics of memory,” I expected more theoretical discussion related to the Holocaust, but we just looked at a bunch of memorials (and the parts mentioning Arendt and Bauman were not explained clearly at all). Tutor Penny always seemed somewhat strict; she would tick and score based on participation. This feeling of being observed, with everyone in the tutorial competing to speak for points, was really exhausting. In the end, the grading was surprisingly good (A+)—expected because the teacher said “we’re willing to give out A+,” yet unexpected because we never received graded feedback during the term and had no reference for the final project, so we just had to work on it blindly with our group mates. Another minor feeling: Dr Sacks sounded very polite and caring throughout, but his politeness often felt so practiced that it came across as somewhat cold... Grading breakdown: 30% participation, 20% quiz (content mentioned in lectures, to be completed within two days after the lecture, lasting 30 minutes; I personally got about four or five questions wrong in total), 50% group project (teams formed within tutorials).

reviews.content: 课程不难，给分挺好，我做的是logbook，基本上就是课后的总结，最难的地方就是lecture notes除了reading week之前的都不给，而且不可以拍照，但只要边上边把内容打在电脑里，然后把它们总结一下放在logbook便好，基本上不用什么反思，就考你有没有上課（笑），tutorial起初有种严格的感觉，但只要说过一两次就行，最后A。
reviews.translated_content: The course isn't difficult, and the grading is quite good. I did the logbook, which is basically a summary after class. The hardest part is that lecture notes are not provided except for those before Reading Week, and you aren't allowed to take photos. But if you type up the content on your computer during class and then summarize it in the logbook, it's fine. Basically, no deep reflection is needed; it just tests whether you attended class (lol). The tutorial felt strict at first, but you only need to speak up once or twice. I got an A in the end.

reviews.content: 好grade水課！quiz全部用AI做 tutorial summarize reading只發言了一次 grp好好做了最後A
reviews.translated_content: A GPA-friendly, easy course! I used AI for all the quizzes, spoke up only once in tutorials to summarise readings, worked properly on the group project, and ended up with an A.

reviews.content: Tutorial的氛围很不好，有种被逼迫发言的感觉。课程安排在本人（文院）看来只能说一般般，毕竟只是cc，而且Sacks在历史系的风评很emmm… 平均每次导修发言1-2次，gp也好好做了，最后拿了B+，说实话有点失望。不过也无所谓了，不值得和ccgl这种糟粕较劲。
reviews.translated_content: The tutorial atmosphere was quite bad; I felt pressured to speak up. As a Faculty of Arts student, I found the course arrangement just average—after all, it’s only a Common Core course—and Sacks’ reputation in the History Department is, well, emmm… I spoke up 1–2 times per tutorial on average and put solid effort into the group project, but only ended up with a B+. Honestly, I’m a bit disappointed. But it doesn’t matter; it’s not worth fighting over trash like this CCGL course.

reviews.content: 同学大多是世界各地的，大家都是对自己经常migrate的经历有所好奇，才选这门课的吧。  教授很喜欢上课互动，可惜只上了第一堂课就一直online了。以往是当堂互动（可能要写写画画什么的交上去），online了之后就要在每次听完lecture video（对，他的ppt没几个字）做一点moodle的小quiz。无限次的，取最高分，基本相当于take attendance。  听说往年在课上要记笔记的，而且教授不让用电子产品来记，就一定要纸笔。online这一年也很乖巧的记了笔记，因为他说video link会在两周内关掉。但其实到最后他也没关掉hhhh教授人其实非常nice   Tutorial很简单的在moodle chat room，打打字，也不需要开视频。有参与发言就好。   Workload不大，平时看一点reading，看完reading写一篇感想，然后tutorial上就会根据reading讨论一下。跟之前上过的文革比，这个reading真的算很少的了。可能就是几篇新闻稿。教授很喜欢结合时事，所以看的东西也都蛮新的。有的时候也可能不是reading，是电影什么的。  整体workload也不大，midterm一个interview稿 500字（大概吧 记不清了），去年应该是site visit的，今年当然是不行了，所以换成interview。Final一个editorial 900-1000字，是关于一个讲过的topic，可以自己选。   最后教授给分很好哈哈，本人也很帅很nice，可惜后来录视频都不露脸。加拿大人，疫情初期举例讲过加拿大的一个研究，大意是“排斥黄种人并不会降低一个人感染非典的几率”，印象深刻。冲这个也要推荐这门课。
reviews.translated_content: Most classmates are from around the world. Everyone probably chose this course because they were curious about their own experiences with migration. The professor likes in-class interaction, but unfortunately, we only had the first class in person before everything went online. Previously, there were in-class activities (possibly involving writing or drawing to submit), but once it went online, we had to complete small Moodle quizzes after watching each lecture video (yes, his PPTs have very few words). Unlimited attempts, highest score counted—it was basically taking attendance. I heard that in previous years, you had to take notes in class, and the professor didn’t allow electronic devices, so you had to use pen and paper. During this online year, I dutifully took notes because he said the video links would be removed within two weeks. But in the end, he never removed them haha. The professor is actually very nice. Tutorials were simple, conducted in the Moodle chat room; you just needed to type, no video required, as long as you participated. The workload isn’t heavy. You read a bit, write a reflection after reading, and then discuss the readings in the tutorial. Compared to the Cultural Revolution course I took before, the reading load here is really light—maybe just a few news articles. The professor likes to connect with current events, so the materials are quite up-to-date. Sometimes it’s not readings but films or something similar. Overall, the workload isn’t large. The midterm was a 500-word interview script (roughly, I can’t remember clearly). Last year it was supposed to be a site visit, but of course that wasn’t possible this year, so it was replaced by an interview. The final was a 900–1000 word editorial on a covered topic, which you could choose yourself. In the end, the professor graded generously haha. He’s also handsome and nice, but unfortunately, he didn’t show his face in later videos. He’s Canadian. Early in the pandemic, he cited a Canadian study along the lines of “excluding people of East Asian descent does not reduce one’s risk of contracting SARS,” which left a deep impression. I’d recommend this course for that alone.

course_info.title: Villages and Global Futures
course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content:
wl并不是很大（其实也不小），但是所有人都给我RUN！！！！
先是最大的雷：field trip x2。对你没看错，有两个field trip，一个在reading week一个在其中一堂课上。reading week的那个field trip用了一整天。早上8点从沙田出发（要自己去沙田哦）先坐船坐一个钟，然后直接带我们爬山（路上全是牛粪😅），几乎一整天都在走，然后再坐船回来。另一个在一堂课上，Winnie你是算准了这节课在7点下课我们后面没有课所以直接把我们拖到快8点半才解散是吧，去附近的一个叫薄扶林村的地方做实地考察，这个field trip和前面那个比起来不知道好了多少。。。
essay方面给出了几乎为零的指导，而且tutor自己都不记得自己说过什么（本来说的topic想写“A”然后问可不可以tutorial说了yes结果essay后面又给我打回来说不能写“A”？？我请问呢）。而且就跟前面的评论一样，tutor一直在说innovative idea，拜托90%课上的学生都是urban growup students我们能想象出什么。。。能想象出一个village life已经很难了你还要我们怎么innovative。
group project挺看组员（在此表白一下我三个组员，大家都做work而且两位local同学超给力带飞但gp最后也只有b不知道tutor到底在评些什么），而且一直在问practicability和innovative point在哪里（拜托如果我真的能给你个两全的方案你下一秒就是拿来当你自己的thesis吧🙄）
lecture感觉没有attendance？错啦！每节课课后都有in class exercise，而且很多都是有worksheet的那种，所以别想跑。必须要呆在那里待到下课做完inclass exercise才能走哈哈！而且，lecture特别的无聊哦！内容上来说没有任何用处的那种，然后讲师大部分时间是Winnie which讲的稍微有趣一点（风格上），其他另外两位讲师讲的屎一样。
所以，快跑！！！！！！！！！！！！
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t huge (actually, it’s not small either), but everyone should RUN!! First, the biggest red flag: two field trips. Yes, you read that right, two field trips—one during Reading Week and one during a regular class. The Reading Week trip took the whole day. We had to get to Sha Tin on our own, depart at 8 am, take a one-hour boat ride, and then go straight into hiking (the path was covered in cow dung 😅). We spent almost the entire day walking, then took the boat back. The other trip was during a class slot. Winnie, you must have calculated that this class ends at 7 pm and we had no classes after, so you kept us until nearly 8:30 pm, right? We went to a nearby place called Pok Fu Lam Village for fieldwork. Compared to the first one, this trip was much better... Regarding the essay, there was almost zero guidance, and the tutor didn’t even remember what she had said (she originally said topic “A” was fine, I asked in the tutorial and got a yes, but then she rejected it in the essay feedback saying we couldn’t write about “A”?? Excuse me?). Also, as mentioned in previous reviews, the tutor keeps asking for “innovative ideas.” Come on, 90% of the students are urban kids; what can we imagine? It’s hard enough to imagine village life, and yet you want us to be innovative. The group project depends heavily on your teammates (shout-out to my three teammates, who all did the work, and the two local students were super helpful and carried the group, but we still only got a B—I don’t know what the tutor was grading). She also keeps asking where the practicability and innovation are (come on, if I could really give you a perfect solution, you’d just use it as your own thesis next second 🙄). It seems like there’s no attendance for lectures? Wrong! There are in-class exercises after every lecture, many with worksheets, so don’t think you can skip. You have to stay until the end of class and finish the in-class exercises before you can leave, haha! Also, the lectures are extremely boring! The content is completely useless. Most of the time, Winnie is the lecturer, and her style is slightly more interesting, but the other two lecturers teach like crap. So, run away!!!!!!!

reviews.content: 这条评论是针对cchu9058 Nature in the City。但是检索不到这门课。所以无奈只能po在这里（sorry！） 我是暑假的时候online上的这门课，体验一般。感觉教授人不错，给分fair吧，但完全没教什么东西（我以为会涉及一些建筑学的知识，但是完全没有），lecture感觉有点水；tutorial十分十分水，都在breakout room自行讨论，啥都没学到。
reviews.translated_content: This review is for CCHU9058 Nature in the City. However, I couldn’t find this course in the system, so I had no choice but to post it here (sorry!). I took this course online during the summer, and the experience was average. The professor seems nice, and the grading is fair, but I didn’t learn anything substantial (I expected some architecture-related knowledge, but there was none). The lectures felt a bit lightweight; the tutorials were extremely lightweight, consisting mostly of self-discussion in breakout rooms, and I learned nothing.

reviews.content: 是本人很喜歡很喜歡的課（因為專業和興趣）但客觀來說普普通通，如果你不喜觀鄉村講保育這課甚至有一點點無聊。fieldtrip給了很好的opportunity遊覽，但其實學不了甚麼。grp project真的要笑死，就一節tutorial跟tutor brainstorm，第二次經要mock present，而且tutor不會給評語，只會說好（但其實看得出不好）。assignment可以說是跟lectures無關的。雖然最後出分A，但純粹因爲自己喜歡和熟悉這個課題，對其他人不太友善。
reviews.translated_content: This is a course I really, really like (because of my major and interests), but objectively speaking, it’s just average. If you’re not interested in village conservation, this course is even a bit boring. The field trip provided a good opportunity for sightseeing, but you don’t actually learn much. The group project is laughable: we brainstormed with the tutor in just one tutorial session, and the second time we had to do a mock presentation. The tutor doesn’t give feedback, only says “good” (but you can tell it’s not good). The assignment can be said to be unrelated to the lectures. Although I got an A in the end, it was purely because I like and am familiar with the topic; it’s not very friendly to others.

reviews.content: 课个人感觉挺无聊的，每节课有课内作业，课不用咋听，gp一直强调innovation, 花了大量时间搞创新性。一个村民日记，要画画，一个filed trip。wl小，最后A range。
reviews.translated_content: I personally found the course quite boring. There are in-class assignments every session. You don’t really need to listen in class. The group project constantly emphasises innovation, so I spent a huge amount of time trying to be innovative. There was a villager’s diary assignment that required drawing, and a field trip. The workload is light, and I ended up with an A-range grade.

reviews.content: 有趣的課程，如果您不懶惰，則成績不錯，有趣的講座
reviews.translated_content: An interesting course. If you are not lazy, you can get good grades. The lectures are interesting.

reviews.content: 上课很无聊，project用心做了也没有很高分，最后b+
reviews.translated_content: The lectures were very boring. I put a lot of effort into the project but didn’t get a very high score; I ended up with a B+.

reviews.content: workload小，但给分严格，essayB, grp project B-，最后B+；instructor非常非常期待 deep reflection和innovative idea, 如果不能自信脱颖而出，慎选，local多，几十个组里面有几个实力相当强大，很容易显得其他人平庸。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is light, but the grading is strict. I got a B for the essay, a B- for the group project, and a B+ overall. The instructor expects deep reflection and innovative ideas very strongly. If you can't confidently stand out, choose with caution. There are many local Hong Kong students, and among the dozens of groups, a few are extremely strong, which easily makes others look mediocre.

reviews.content: 一门Social Science内容的课程，就课程内容来说，可以了解很多的专业知识。workload小，一个group presentation和一个individual essay, 能得到什么样的成绩主要取决于所写所想的东西是否有让教授认可的创新性和实际意义。
reviews.translated_content: This is a Social Science course. In terms of content, you can gain a lot of professional knowledge. The workload is light, consisting of one group presentation and one individual essay. The grade you get mainly depends on whether what you write and think demonstrates innovation and practical significance that the professor recognises.

reviews.content: 上课蛮无聊的，不过上课的最后会有in-class exercise。最后的grp project 很强调innovation，但是标准很迷。
reviews.translated_content: Classes are quite boring, but there are in-class exercises at the end. The final group project emphasizes innovation, but the criteria are very confusing.

reviews.content: 头也不回的跑吧。有两个field trip还特别累 都记attendance 然后group proj也是给分特别烂 上课特别无聊 别选别选别选
reviews.translated_content: Just run away without looking back. There are two field trips that are especially tiring, and attendance is recorded for both. The group project grading is also terrible. The lectures are extremely boring. Don’t choose it, don’t choose it, don’t choose it.

course_info.title: Water in a Changing World

reviews.content: Low workload. Two mid-term quizzes (one during lecture, one at home). One group project. Lectures are optional. Topic is applicable in real/daily life (reduce water consumption). Overall recommend.
reviews.translated_content: Low workload. Two midterm quizzes (one during lecture, one at home). One group project. Lectures are optional. The topic is applicable to real/daily life (e.g., reducing water consumption). Overall recommended.

reviews.content: 给分好玄学，pre讲得烂的组给高分，讲得好的组没给高分，考试要背东西，不然就拿不了A
reviews.translated_content: The grading is opaque and unpredictable. Groups with poor presentations got high marks, while groups with good presentations didn’t. The exam requires memorisation, otherwise you won’t get an A.

reviews.content: 還行，不過要高分就重workload，gp嚴格
reviews.translated_content: It’s acceptable, but if you want a high score, the workload is heavy and the group project grading is strict.

reviews.content: 挺chill的一门课，lecture内容比较无聊 ，prof对平时的assessment比较摆烂，交了就几乎满分，gp给分相对严格，给grade只能说中规中矩吧，不烂grade但也没有感觉特别好grade
reviews.translated_content: It’s a fairly chill course. The lecture content is quite boring. The professor is quite slack with regular assessments; you get nearly full marks just for submitting them. The group project grading is relatively strict. As for the overall grade, it’s just average—not a bad grade, but nothing particularly generous either.

reviews.content: wl挺小的 professor来自非洲 讲这个课题有更深的感触 gp要好好做 他非常看重是否有创新以及是否用心做了gp 我可能是因为individual essay写的一般吧 最后A- 同组law院的厉害同学是A+
reviews.translated_content: The workload is quite small. The professor is from Africa and has deeper feelings about this topic. You need to do the group project well; he places great emphasis on whether it is innovative and whether you put effort into it. Maybe because my individual essay was average, I ended up with an A-, while a brilliant classmate from the Law Faculty in my group got an A+.

reviews.content: lec讲了很多但没高阶知识，tut前总有点小任务(包括ppt)可能要发言，给分一般
reviews.translated_content: The lecture covers a lot but lacks advanced knowledge. Before tutorials, there are always small tasks (including PPTs) and you may need to speak. Grading is average.

reviews.content: 看的出来教授挺摆烂的，wl 不算大，但是小东西很多，需要认真一些做。最后 A range
reviews.translated_content: You can tell the professor is somewhat slacking off. The workload isn’t heavy, but there are many small tasks that require careful attention. I ended up with an A-range grade.

reviews.content: 挺水的课 ppt就是满满的字挺无聊的 没学到什么东西 但是wl很小 最后B
reviews.translated_content: A rather lightweight course. The PPTs are just walls of text and quite boring. I didn’t learn much, but the workload is small. I ended up with a B.

reviews.content: 好课，wl很小，一篇短essay，一个gp pre，2个quiz（很简单），教授人还不错的
reviews.translated_content: Good course, very low workload. One short essay, one group project presentation, and 2 quizzes (very simple). The professor is quite nice too.

reviews.content: 给的资料内容较杂且乱，内容不算多，收获一般。教授很多asm和quiz都还没给分，也不知道成绩如何，给grade很迷。wl小，最后B range。
reviews.translated_content: The provided materials are quite scattered and messy. The content isn’t extensive, and the takeaways are average. The professor hasn’t graded many assignments and quizzes yet, so I don’t know how the results look; the grading is confusing. The workload is small. I ended up with a B-range grade.

search_summary.title: Digital Humanitarianism: Can You Save the World with Your Computer?

course_info.title: Digital Humanitarianism: Can You Save the World with Your Computer?

reviews.content: 首先课程内容非常没意思，学下来一学期收获不到什么东西。workload还巨大，每次上课前看两小时的recording，认真看PP T准备十个课堂quiz，还有各种无聊的assignment，非常占时间，最后还要拍video……最后🐢A-，感觉不如之前评价的好🐢，关键是收获不到任何东西，最后教授发的邮件还把我的一个assignment算错了，发邮件解释半天教授才勉为其难给我算进去还说我需要感到抱歉因为浪费了自己跟家人相处的时间。总之，run，非常不推荐。
reviews.translated_content: First, the course content is very uninteresting; you don’t gain much from it after a whole semester. The workload is huge: you have to watch two hours of recordings before each class, carefully go through the PowerPoint slides to prepare for ten in-class quizzes, complete various boring assignments that take up a lot of time, and finally shoot a video... I ended up with an A-, which feels worse than the good grades mentioned in previous reviews. The key issue is that I didn’t learn anything. To make matters worse, the professor miscalculated one of my assignments. After I emailed to explain at length, he reluctantly included it but said I should feel sorry for wasting my own time and time with my family. In short, run away; I definitely do not recommend this course.

reviews.content:
很高wl 每节课都有quiz 内容是提前看的lecture视频和reading随机出
gp给分很迷 最后video做得艺术视频 给分很主观
总结是超高wl烂龟课
reviews.translated_content: Very high workload. There is a quiz in every lesson, with questions randomly drawn from the pre-watched lecture videos and readings. Grading for the group project is confusing; my group made an artistic video for the final submission, and the grading felt very subjective. In summary: extremely high workload and harsh grading.

reviews.content: Very boring course; useless content; rigid assessment framework
reviews.translated_content: Very boring course; useless content; rigid assessment framework

reviews.content: 每节课都要做quiz，而且很容易就只对几个，分很低。wl很大，有poster，video，花的时间很久但是感觉学不到什么
reviews.translated_content: There is a quiz every class, and it’s easy to get only a few questions right, so the marks are low. The workload is heavy, with a poster and a video. It takes a long time, but I feel like I haven’t learned much.

reviews.content: 5个assignment，其中两个group work。每节课都有quiz（占10%），workload一个顶两个CC，不是疯了千万不要选，除非你对人道主义有非常大的热衷。
reviews.translated_content: There are 5 assignments, two of which are group work. Every class has a quiz (worth 10%). The workload is equivalent to two Common Core courses combined. Do not take this unless you are crazy or have a huge passion for humanitarianism.

reviews.content: wl巨大 不好🐢 没有好的组员就完蛋 跑！！
reviews.translated_content: Huge workload. Poor grading. If you don’t have good groupmates, you’re doomed. Get out while you can!

reviews.content: 没有什么用的课，wl超大，每节课都不知道在讲啥还要写quiz（需要课前读几个reading或者video才能回答出来），虽然给分还行（一般），但真的不建议。Tutorial会让你做奇奇怪怪的讨论和debate
reviews.translated_content: A useless course with a huge workload. You don’t know what is being taught in each class, yet you still have to do quizzes (which require reading several articles or watching videos beforehand to answer). Although the grading is okay (average), I really don’t recommend it. Tutorials involve strange discussions and debates.

reviews.content: 好🐢a range。发了report大部分人都在a range。作业只是单纯的耗时但是非常简单，比如说mapping，只要做够3hr就可以了，写一篇essay有时候可能都不止3hr。而且还有image transfer还是啥的，非常简单，十分钟搞定。而且tutor非常非常非常好人，不需要上课，只需要看一下ppt写一下quiz就好。真的快来吧很好，而且内容超级无敌简单！
reviews.translated_content: Generous grading; an A-range grade. Most people got an A-range grade on the report. The assignments are simply time-consuming but very easy. For example, mapping only requires 3 hours of work; writing an essay might take more than 3 hours. There was also something like image transfer, which was very easy and done in ten minutes. Also, the tutor is extremely nice. You don’t need to attend class; just look at the slides and do the quizzes. Really, come and take it; it’s great, and the content is super simple!

reviews.content: wl大，基本每节课课前都要看slides和reading做quiz，大大小小gp也很烦人！给分一言难尽，总之run！
reviews.translated_content: Heavy workload. Basically, before every class you have to watch slides and readings and do quizzes. The various group projects are also annoying! The grading is hard to describe—in short, run!

reviews.content: 内容基本上是教授介绍一些人道主义手段并且实操少部分，课程还蛮有意思，画地图，做AI图片，拍视频，需要好队友！需要好队友！需要好队友！只要有几个比较能干有主意的好伙伴可以上的很舒服！笔者运气很好随机找到了一个会剪辑视频外国女生组队，最后应为final project的视频拿到了好龟。
reviews.translated_content: The content basically involves the professor introducing some humanitarian methods with a small amount of hands-on practice. The course is quite interesting: we drew maps, created AI images, and filmed videos. You need good teammates! You need good teammates! You need good teammates! As long as you have a few capable and idea-driven partners, you can have a comfortable experience. I was lucky enough to randomly find a foreign female teammate who could edit videos, and I ended up with a good grade thanks to the final project video.

course_info.title: How to Make (Sense of) Money

reviews.content: 体验非常好，罕见的没有gp的ccgl。老师每节课都快乐得像个婚礼司仪，tutor人也很好，无论我发言讲了多蠢的话都会微笑点头。没有任何社科基础最后也拿了A range 我自己感觉到的一些刷分小技巧： 每节课后的online quiz要仔细看ppt，一般都会有原文 期中有一个500字的hk money museum，期末有一个1.5k字的role play letter，都是比较生活化的小作文。老师貌似更喜欢你选一个很具体的话题，再结合某几节课的内容深入讨论。从多个角度展示一个比较大的论题容易被老师评价讲得不够深 prez最好不要只是总结复述reading的内容，要结合一些你自己的想法。
reviews.translated_content: Great experience. It’s rare for a CCGL course to have no group project. The lecturer is as cheerful as a wedding emcee in every class, and the tutor is very nice too, smiling and nodding no matter how silly my comments were. I had no background in social sciences but still got an A-range grade. Some tips I found for boosting your grade: read the slides carefully for the online quiz after each class, as the answers are usually quoted directly. For the mid-term, there’s a 500-word piece on the HK Money Museum, and for the final, a 1,500-word role-play letter; both are relatively casual, everyday-style essays. The teacher seems to prefer that you choose a very specific topic and discuss it in depth by connecting it to content from several lectures. Presenting a broad argument from multiple angles tends to be criticised by the teacher as lacking depth. For the presentation, it’s best not to just summarise or repeat the readings; you should incorporate some of your own ideas.

reviews.content: 从社会学角度分析钱的存在和与钱有关的现象。 教授很有意思，每一节课都讲得很有激情，课程内容也设计得逻辑比较清楚，但是个人感觉lecture不会讲很多深入细节的东西，节奏有一点点慢（可以水）。 因为是线上课所以每节课后quiz都是看着ppt做，很容易。期中的report有创意的分就很好；期末的essay要好好写，结合课上讲过的理论；tutorial中间有个pre，那周要提前好好读reading，做好分析。总体来说龟还可以。
reviews.translated_content: It analyzes the existence of money and money-related phenomena from a sociological perspective. The professor is interesting and lectures with passion. The course content is logically structured, but personally, I feel the lectures don’t go into much deep detail, and the pace is a bit slow (you can coast). Since it was an online course, the post-lecture quizzes were easy to do by just looking at the slides. For the midterm report, creativity scores well. For the final essay, write carefully and integrate the theories discussed in class. There was a presentation during the tutorials; for that week, read the assigned readings in advance and prepare your analysis. Overall, the grading is decent.

course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: 好龟，每节课都有quiz，但是可以Google(不知道线下可不可以)，tuto楼上已经说了就不赘述~ gp是四选一，每项都非常有意思，无需音乐基础但本身喜欢听歌的人会很爱，也很简单，不用上课就会做： 1. 用动画或视频的形式设计这门课的visual learning tool 2. 选择一个主题，设计一份musical boxed set并用brochure的形式展现出来，包括名称&track list(5-6张专辑 貌似单曲也可以)&为什么选择这些曲目 3. 与课程相关的podcast(好像是要讲一整季，但没有说一季多少集) 4. 设计一份巡演计划，包括时间&地点&音乐人&当然还有如此选择的原因，需要着重强调cultures和location的关系 (貌似大多数人会选2和4，最后需要各自提交视频或brochure等文件，不过prez的时候也可以用ppt的形式来pre) 或许和课比较新的原因有关，tutor在介绍gp requirements的时候讲得很不清楚，要多问问。 不做gp也可以，有alternative：每星期提交与本星期lecture相关的logbook(10-15 sentences)，感觉很少有人选这个
reviews.translated_content: Generous grading. There’s a quiz every class, but you can Google the answers (not sure if this applies to in-person sessions). As mentioned above, I won’t repeat the tutorial details. The group project offers four options, all very interesting. No musical background is needed, but people who enjoy listening to music will love it. It’s also simple enough to complete even if you don’t attend class: 1. Design a visual learning tool for the course using animation or video. 2. Choose a theme and design a musical boxed set, presented as a brochure, including the name, track list (5–6 albums, apparently singles are allowed too), and reasons for selecting these tracks. 3. Create a podcast related to the course (seems like a full season is required, but the number of episodes wasn’t specified). 4. Design a tour plan, including dates, locations, musicians, and reasons for these choices, with emphasis on the relationship between cultures and location. (Most people seem to choose options 2 and 4. Finally, you need to submit files such as videos or brochures, but you can use PowerPoint for the presentation.) Perhaps because the course is relatively new, the tutor explained the group project requirements very unclearly, so ask plenty of questions. You can opt out of the group project; there is an alternative: submit a weekly logbook (10–15 sentences) related to that week’s lecture. Few people seem to choose this option.

reviews.content:
如果你对政史哲感兴趣（bushi）、对贝多芬、瓦格纳、性手枪、涅槃、鲍勃马利、Kino、春之祭、国家主义、法西斯、乌合之众、后朋摇滚等topic感兴趣或者想要拓展自己音乐视野的，这门课绝对是你的菜。reading很多，虽然教授硬性要求只是每周一篇文章10页，为了更好理解lecture内容还是建议有时间起码所有的reading都过一遍。教授不会在历史背景上花很多时间，更主要的是侧重不同时期社会现象以及主线，会有很多影音分享。tutor Mohammed很幽默，可以跟他单独约讨论自己的作业如何改进。小组项目和个人logbook是二选一。本人是logbook选手，感觉除了基本每周要写一个追求质量的300字周记外基本无压力。logbook选手一个优势是最后Quiz过后这门课就不需要再花时间了，但其实感觉小组项目也很有趣，只是final前一个月会比较忙。
拿A不难，wl基本只在reading。
reviews.translated_content: If you’re interested in politics, history, and philosophy (just kidding), or if you’re interested in topics like Beethoven, Wagner, the Sex Pistols, Nirvana, Bob Marley, Kino, The Rite of Spring, nationalism, fascism, The Crowd, post-punk rock, etc., or if you want to broaden your musical horizons, this course is definitely for you. There is a lot of reading. Although the professor’s硬性 requirement is only one 10-page article per week, to better understand the lecture content, I recommend going through all the readings if you have time. The professor doesn’t spend much time on historical background, focusing more on social phenomena and main themes across different periods, with lots of audio-visual sharing. The tutor, Mohammed, is very humorous, and you can book individual sessions with him to discuss how to improve your assignments. You can choose between a group project and a personal logbook. I chose the logbook option and felt there was basically no pressure other than writing a quality 300-word weekly entry. One advantage of the logbook option is that after the final quiz, you don’t need to spend any more time on the course. However, the group project also seems interesting, though it would be busier in the month before the final. Getting an A isn’t difficult; the workload is mainly just the reading.

reviews.content: 好🐢cc,但感觉不太火，特地多写一点打破信息差。课程内容主要讲音乐发展与政治历史背景的联系，内容还是比较有意思的，上课会放很多音乐听，本人高考生所以英语没有那么好，上课有的时候会跟不上，需要私下再去复习以应对quiz（不过后来基本上是上半节课讲下半节课做quiz，就只能直接上了）整体来讲wl不大，期中150字左右的文章+期末的gp，本身做完心里也没底，但最后A-，感恩🙏🏻
reviews.translated_content: A Common Core course with generous grading, but it doesn’t seem very popular, so I’m writing more to bridge the information gap. The content mainly explores the connection between musical development and political-historical backgrounds, which is quite interesting. We listen to a lot of music in class. As a student with a Gaokao background, my English isn’t that strong, so I sometimes struggled to keep up and had to review privately for quizzes (though later on, it was basically lecture in the first half and quiz in the second, so you just had to attend). Overall, the workload isn’t heavy: a ~150-word essay for the midterm and a group project for the final. I wasn’t confident after finishing them, but I ended up with an A-. Grateful 🙏🏻

reviews.content: 无敌烂龟课！转线下之后quiz考点ppt基本都没有！wl也很大，tutorial发言机会很少所以抢到飞起，很可能写了几百字发言稿但是因为抢不到发言而白费！快跑快跑

reviews.content: 成绩由小组的作业，展示以及个人的essay组成。小组的project就是构思一个social enterprise，一步步把它的产品，盈利模式想出来。最后的business pitch很好玩，有专业的投资人过来提问。要是之后想建立social enterprise，或开个公司，这门课可以提供有用的知识。 grade不算好把~很努力地在tutorial当中发言，写论文，做小组project，还是B range。要是想拿高分，估计要有经济等学科基础。

reviews.content: gp遇到的组员都很好，tutor很热心，每周写完essay都会有feedback，给分很高，但total 90以上也只有a
reviews.translated_content: The group members I met were all great, and the tutor was very helpful. We received feedback every week after submitting our essays, and the grading was high. However, even with a total above 90, you only get an A.

reviews.content: wl臃肿得莫名其妙，主题更多是泛泛而谈，缺乏深度。整体低于预期，不推荐。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is bloated for no clear reason. The themes are mostly discussed in general terms, lacking depth. Overall, it fell short of expectations. Not recommended.

reviews.content: 如各位评论区所见，新课，教授出身nb，愣是把一个cc整成一个专业课的架势。在和tutor反馈，他们再反馈给prof之后，成功将reading降至一周一篇十来页的required的reading。每周200字的essay是有题目要求，题目不是每周固定发放的，而是他一早写好的，你得根据你那周看的reading看看能答上他给的什么问题。有field trip，由于我的tutor victory挺摆的（个人看法），field trip也很不幸的脖子受伤没带我们去，然后我们组自己走，也不知道走了些什么，要写reflection，根据给的框架写就可以了。Group project感谢大佬们带飞，真的是大佬带飞才有的成绩，建议pre之前consult一下prof，因为我们组consult完被prof推翻重新做了一个，不过算有个好grade了。
reviews.translated_content: As seen in the comments section, this was a new course. The professor has an impressive background and managed to turn a Common Core course into something resembling a major-specific course. After providing feedback to the tutors, who then relayed it to the professor, we successfully reduced the required reading to one article of about ten pages per week. The weekly 200-word essays had specific prompts. The topics weren’t released weekly; instead, he had written them in advance, and you had to see which of his questions you could answer based on that week’s reading. There was a field trip. Since my tutor Victory was quite slack (in my personal opinion), and unfortunately I injured my neck and couldn’t lead us on the trip, our group went on our own. We weren’t sure what we were supposed to observe, but we had to write a reflection following the provided framework. For the group project, thanks to the strong students carrying the group—really, only because they carried us did we achieve that result. I suggest consulting the professor before the presentation. Our group consulted him, and he overturned our work, forcing us to redo it, but we ended up with a good grade.

reviews.content:
wl大 有gp 有final essay 还有每周200字essay 还有字数巨多的required reading
、成绩不知道 我现在有点痛苦
reviews.translated_content: Heavy workload. There’s a group project, a final essay, weekly 200-word essays, and required readings with a huge word count. I don’t know my grade yet; I’m suffering a bit right now.

reviews.content: 课程内容就是讲很多古代的城市规划，古罗马，古中国啥的，讲建筑和城市规划的一些东西，又能扯到人文，政府管理，历史的很多方面，ppt也是密密麻麻的，rfinal essay，eading和每周essay也是关于这些。但是gp和field trip的reflection更偏向香港，大湾区这些东西，就挺跳脱的。
reviews.translated_content: The course content covers many ancient urban planning topics, such as ancient Rome and ancient China, discussing architecture and urban planning. It also touches on humanities, government management, history, and many other aspects. The PPTs are densely packed. The final assessment is an essay, and the readings and weekly essays are also on these topics. However, the group project and field trip reflections lean more towards Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area, which feels quite disjointed.

reviews.content: workload很大，不同tutor给的分相差也大，每周几百字的writing还有接近100页的reading，一门cc跟专业课差不多
reviews.translated_content: The workload is heavy. Different tutors’ grading varies widely. There are weekly writing assignments of a few hundred words plus nearly 100 pages of reading. This Common Core course feels almost like a major course.

reviews.content: You need to write an essay every week until it's time to do the project. I was lucky to have gotten groupmates from the architecture and urban studies faculty. The project might seem very confusing and vague at first but that's because the professor will literally allow to do just about anything. Haotian Man is a good tutor.

The project might seem very confusing and vague at first but that's because the professor will literally allow to do just about anything. Haotian Man is a good tutor.

reviews.content: WL was quite average. The professor was very approachable, helpful, and friendly. My tutor, Haotian, was a godsend. He was an amazing assistance to our group project. And it is incredibly important that everyone in your group participate and somehow proactively cooperate. Course content is also very interesting and engaging, but the presentations were a bit too long and packed.
reviews.translated_content: WL was quite average. The professor was very approachable, helpful, and friendly. My tutor, Haotian, was a godsend. He was an amazing assistance to our group project. And it is incredibly important that everyone in your group participate and somehow proactively cooperate. Course content is also very interesting and engaging, but the presentations were a bit too long and packed.

reviews.content: When I took CCGL9070, the workload was quite a lot, especially with weekly short essays and required readings, though I heard it’s been reduced since then. I was the group leader in a large team — it could get a bit chaotic, but I really enjoyed the experience. My groupmates were amazing to work with, which made everything much easier and more fun. The topics were broad and interesting, and it was quite easy to earn bonus points. The tutors were kind and supportive, and the final essay wasn’t too difficult if you’d been keeping up with the short essays. The professor was very passionate about the course and invited selected groups, including ours, to present at the Common Core Festival. I ended up getting an A+.

course_info.title: Fashion, Politics and the Global City

reviews.content: wl很小，tutor人很好，老师讲的也不错，2个inclass quiz一个short essay，有点划水最后A，好龟
reviews.translated_content: The workload is very light, the tutor is very nice, and the lecturer teaches well. There are two in-class quizzes and one short essay. I coasted a bit and still got an A. Generous grading.

reviews.content: wl小，兩個quiz只要去tutorial就會有溫習材料。short essay 沒多花心機但 四十分有三十多。很喜歡tutor，人很好很照顧學生並鼓勵教導學生。
reviews.translated_content: Small workload. For the two quizzes, you’ll get revision materials as long as you attend the tutorials. I didn’t put much effort into the short essay, but I got over 30 out of 40. I really like the tutor; they are very nice, look after students, and encourage and guide them.

reviews.content:
wl小，一个group project的fashion show，十几个人摊下来就比较轻松，老师给show的分也很宽松。还有一篇800-900字的essay，认真写就好龟（我的分37/40），有社科基础的话轻轻松松搞定。
老师讲课还行，不过有很多专业词汇，且不会显示在ppt上，也不会解释；对于没有社科基础的同学不太友好。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is light. There’s one group project—a fashion show—which is relatively relaxed when shared among a dozen people. The teacher’s grading for the show is also very generous. There’s also an 800–900-word essay; if you write it seriously, you’ll get a good grade (I scored 37/40). It’s easy to handle if you have a background in social sciences. The lecturer is okay, but there are many technical terms that don’t appear on the slides and aren’t explained, which isn’t very friendly for students without a social-science background.

reviews.content: 是一节很容易困的课 但是课上会有很多的时尚政治文化的例子 tutorial定final project的主题之后就是讨论 quiz前会有复习 wl就是tutorial一个小pre 一个800essay 两个quiz 一个final fashion show+pre 总的来说算轻松
reviews.translated_content: It’s a class that makes you sleepy easily, but there are many examples of fashion, politics, and culture during lectures. After determining the final project topic in the tutorial, it’s mostly discussion. There is a review session before the quiz. The workload consists of a short presentation in the tutorial, one 800-word essay, two quizzes, and a final fashion show plus presentation. Overall, it’s quite relaxed.

reviews.content: 课程有趣，但是quiz感觉很难 会丢很多分
reviews.translated_content: The course is interesting, but the quizzes feel difficult and you can lose a lot of marks.

reviews.content: 真的一般般 很看选题 但是topic是随机分配的 队友也是 总的来说轻松但不好gui
reviews.translated_content: Honestly, it was just average. It really depends on the topic, but topics are assigned randomly, and so are teammates. Overall, it’s relaxed but not GPA-friendly.

reviews.content: Lecturer上课非常用心，每节课内容都紧随时事。Workload不算小，一篇essay，一个期末gp，两次quiz，quiz很难，非常认真复习但是还是不尽人意，essay和gp给分都挺fair
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer puts a lot of effort into classes, with content closely following current affairs in every session. The workload isn’t small: one essay, one final group project, and two quizzes. The quizzes are very difficult; I revised very seriously but the results were still unsatisfactory. The grading for the essay and group project is quite fair.

reviews.content: 老师讲得不算差但给分玄，gp看队友，🐢很难办，最后莫名其妙吃了个B-。看成绩图大家能看出问题，让我再选一次包避雷了。
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer wasn’t bad, but the grading was unpredictable. Your group project grade depends on your teammates, making it hard to secure a good grade; I inexplicably ended up with a B-. Looking at the grade distribution chart reveals the problem. If I could choose again, I would definitely avoid this course.

reviews.content: 莫名其妙b-了 明明gp给分还行 wl是两个课堂quiz（20%）+essay+gp gp是按tut分 遇到不负责任队友你基本玩完 最好和朋友一起报
reviews.translated_content: I inexplicably got a B-. The group project grading was actually okay. The workload consists of two in-class quizzes (20%), an essay, and a group project. The group project grade is based on tutorial performance. If you encounter irresponsible teammates, you are basically done for. It is best to enrol with friends.

reviews.content: 课堂内容很有意思，老师讲得很好，如果没有12个人一组的fashion show group work会更好。总之各种assignment和quiz的分看着很高最后莫名其妙没有A，过来一看原来大家都是。推测要全部assignment都至少high 80%或者90才能A吧。不是一定要A的可以跟朋友选。
reviews.translated_content: The class content is very interesting and the instructor teaches well. It would be even better if there weren’t a fashion show group project with 12 people per group. In short, although the marks for various assignments and quizzes look high, I inexplicably didn’t get an A in the end. When I checked, it turned out that everyone else was in the same boat. I suspect you need to score at least in the high 80s or 90s on every assignment to get an A. If getting an A isn’t essential for you, you can take this course with friends.

reviews.content: 虽然最后A了，但感觉这课怎么说呢，就是project大部分都是自己做的，而且也得到了很高的评价，结果最后还是只有A。然后反而是一个project什么事没干的free rider拿了A，另一个做数据分析的朋友拿了B。给分给的很奇怪，虽然对我自己影响不大就是了，但觉得还是要反馈下
reviews.translated_content: Although I ended up with an A, I have mixed feelings about this course. Most of the project work was done by myself and received high praise, yet I still only got an A. Meanwhile, a free rider who did nothing on the project also got an A, while a friend who handled data analysis got a B. The grading logic is strange. It didn’t affect me much personally, but I felt I should provide feedback.

reviews.content: 快润快润！给分真的玄乎 最后视频做得很认真花了大量时间 还是B。。。。
reviews.translated_content: Get out while you can! The grading is really unpredictable. I put a lot of time and serious effort into the final video, but still got a B...

reviews.content: 强推！今年新开的cc课，wl超级小。因为有课前作业所以lecture基本只上1h，不过lecture完全不去听也没问题，Tutorial讲Tableau等一些数据可视化，蛮有趣。Final的时候一个300字的reflection journal和一个video的GP，最后A+
reviews.translated_content: Highly recommended! This is a new Common Core course launched this year, with a very light workload. Because there are pre-class assignments, lectures basically last only one hour. However, it’s fine even if you don’t attend lectures at all. Tutorials cover Tableau and other data visualization tools, which are quite interesting. The final assessment consists of a 300-word reflection journal and a video group project. I got an A+.

reviews.content: 像ccst的一门ccgl！lecture可以完全不听，tutorial跟着guide做就行，每周作业作图部分和tutorial的内容基本一致，只是要写一些description，作图+文字可能有些耗时。gp遇到很棒的队友，最后A range！（tutor选zu jinyan小姐姐，人超nice！
reviews.translated_content: A CCGL course that feels like a CCST one! You can completely skip the lectures; just follow the guide in the tutorials. The weekly assignment’s graphing part is basically the same as the tutorial content, though you need to write some descriptions. Graphing plus writing can be time-consuming. I had great teammates for the group project and ended up with an A-range grade! (For the tutor, choose Ms. Zu Jinyan; she’s super nice!)

reviews.content: 给分不好，老师对gp作业的反馈说分不错，最后出来gp给了C，overallB，笑面虎教授
reviews.translated_content: Grading is poor. The professor gave positive feedback on the group project, saying the marks were good, but in the end the group project received a C and the overall grade was a B. An all-smiles-but-ruthless professor.

reviews.content: 课程内容简单，wl小，最后就一个视频的project比较烦。最后B+，龟一般
reviews.translated_content: The course content is simple and the workload is small. The only annoying part was a video project at the end. I got a B+; the grading was average.

reviews.content: 课程很有趣，我认为我自己付出许多，tutorial的作业也完成的很好，但是不知道为什么grade不高，不过是个B+
reviews.translated_content: The course is interesting. I feel that I put in a lot of effort and completed the tutorial assignments well, but for some reason, the grade wasn’t high—it was a B+.

reviews.content: 明明很认真的做了，不知道为什么最后烂龟了
reviews.translated_content: I worked really hard, but for some reason, I ended up with a poor grade.

reviews.content: wl几乎为零，遇到了很好的队友合作，gp做的还不错最后a
reviews.translated_content: The workload was almost zero. I had great teammates, our group project went well, and I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: wl小，给分好，每周上个tutorial（签个到之后也不用听直接跟着instruction做就行），lecture上不上无所谓。grp project也难度不大，基本感觉用心点做就A+。
reviews.translated_content: Low workload, generous grading. You have a tutorial every week (just sign in, then you don’t need to listen; just follow the instructions). It doesn’t matter whether you attend the lectures. The group project isn’t difficult either; if you put in some effort, you’ll basically get an A+.

reviews.content:
不要因爲是新課就不選啊kkk，這課完全是我的愛（？？？
首先本人就讀建院，但這個cc比起主修課還要更全面，個人成長的空間也更大
自己研發一種新物料真是一個很有趣很新的體驗（asm4) ，asm1-3也會促成看生活上對不同物料的改變
總之就是，很好的一課，大愛tutors們和Susanne
reviews.translated_content: Don't avoid this course just because it's new, haha. This course is totally my love (???). First of all, I'm in the Faculty of Architecture, but this Common Core course is even more comprehensive than my major courses, with greater room for personal growth. Developing a new material yourself is a really interesting and novel experience (ASM4), and ASMs 1–3 also encourage you to look at how different materials change in daily life. In short, it's a great course. Big love to the tutors and Susanne.

reviews.content: filed trip+debate+期末兩分鐘的個人pre+四份作業(包括一份800essay)。適合建院的學生選，作業需要畫圖，field trip也需要畫圖，畫畫不好的慎選。四個tutor都挺好的，回復速度快，lecture不計attendance可以不去，而且幾乎沒有group work
reviews.translated_content: Includes a field trip, debate, a two-minute individual presentation at the end, and four assignments (including one 800-word essay). Suitable for students from the Faculty of Architecture, as the assignments and field trip require drawing. If you’re not good at drawing, choose with caution. All four tutors are quite nice and respond quickly. Attendance is not counted for lectures, so you can skip them, and there is almost no group work.

reviews.content: 对ib学生非常友好的一门口，wk load不大，基本就是那些ib练的：discussion and essays，老师和tutors都很supportive
reviews.translated_content: A very IB-friendly Common Core course. The workload isn’t heavy; it’s basically the same skills practiced in IB: discussions and essays. Both the professor and tutors are very supportive.

reviews.content: High workload course but creative assessment criteria and not boring even for non archi student. The professor and tutors are all nice and know their topics well but the guest speakers are kind of bad and rude especially when they give feedback to students in the 2 min presentations.
reviews.translated_content: High workload course but creative assessment criteria and not boring even for non archi student. The professor and tutors are all nice and know their topics well but the guest speakers are kind of bad and rude especially when they give feedback to students in the 2 min presentations.

reviews.content: 本人建筑base，看了先前的人的高评价闭眼选了此课，总的来说wl小，作业形式也比较多样，但其实感觉并没有从这门课学到什么，个人对课程的评价体系感到模糊，且这个学期由于台风导致课程进度常被耽误导致总体的体验感并不是那么好。另外说说感觉这门课的大多数学生也是建院base，如果对于画图、创意、材料等感兴趣还是可以来，最后B（其实感觉有点烂🐢。。）
reviews.translated_content: I’m from an Architecture background. Seeing the high ratings from previous students, I chose this course without hesitation. Overall, the workload is light, and the assignment formats are diverse. However, I feel I didn’t actually learn much from this course. I find the grading criteria vague. Also, typhoons this semester frequently disrupted the schedule, so the overall experience wasn’t that great. Additionally, most students in this course seem to be from the Faculty of Architecture. If you’re interested in drawing, creativity, and materials, you can still take it. I got a B (actually, I feel the grading was a bit harsh..).

reviews.content: overall人上人。作业按时交就可以拿b以上。field trip很有意思，但是要自己手绘A3大海报以及地质图之类的，如果画画不好慎选。
reviews.translated_content: Overall, it's for the elite. Submit assignments on time and you can get a B or above. The field trip is interesting, but you have to hand-draw large A3 posters and geological maps, etc. If you're not good at drawing, choose with caution.
