search_summary.title: Education as Solution?: Debating Education round the Globe
search_summary.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

course_info.title: Education as Solution?: Debating Education round the Globe
course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: 今年新开的一门CC～ 是我上个Sem超爱的CC的lecturer和tutor的二搭。课程主要围绕世界各地教育议题展开，例如性教育，hidden curriculum，decolonization education 和本地的一些教育议题等等。考核方式为每周课堂上150字的reflective essay + tutorial participation （需要积极发言哦）+ 小组creative project。因为是喜欢的老师+议题，所以这个学期格外努力 （特别是小组作业..）,最后喜提A+～
reviews.translated_content: A new Common Core course this year~ It features a reunion of the lecturer and tutor from the CC I loved last semester. The course mainly revolves around educational issues around the world, such as sex education, hidden curriculum, decolonization of education, and some local educational topics. Assessment consists of weekly 150-word reflective essays in class + tutorial participation (you need to speak up actively) + a group creative project. Because I liked the teachers and the topics, I worked especially hard this semester (especially on the group assignment..) and somehow ended up with an A+~

reviews.content: 要卷发言，卷gp，非常非常非常卷让人上的压力很大
reviews.translated_content: You have to compete fiercely in class participation and on the group project. It is extremely intense and creates a lot of pressure.

reviews.content: 这门课非常不适合政治谱系中立或偏保守的学生，比如说我，因为这门课充斥着西方白左虚伪的普世价值。教授对DEI的推崇，对女权主义的理解以及将两蒋时期的台湾视为国民党殖民地的做法令我尤为不解，烦恼甚至生理性厌恶。更加糟糕的是，这门课要求tutorial上积极发言，对于本就不认同该课程政治立场的同学来说，我不知道这些同学能在课上说什么，毕竟克制反驳的冲动就已经耗尽了大部分精力。最后，该课程的期末项目是小组作业，如果碰不到志同道合的组员或者碰到性格较mean的同学会很难过。
reviews.translated_content: This course is highly unsuitable for students who are politically neutral or conservative, such as myself, because it is saturated with what I see as the hypocritical universal values of the Western liberal left. I particularly struggled to understand, and even felt physically repulsed by, the professor’s advocacy for DEI, their understanding of feminism, and their treatment of Taiwan during the Chiang Kai-shek era as a Kuomintang colony. Worse still, the course requires active participation in tutorials. For students who do not agree with the course’s political stance, I don’t know what they could possibly say in class, since suppressing the urge to refute arguments already exhausts most of their energy. Finally, the final project is a group assignment; it can be very distressing if you don’t get like-minded teammates or encounter peers who are rather mean.

reviews.content: 很轻松，好🐢，平时随便写一下上课的quiz就行，那个不计分，开放式的，tut上发言也很随意，想到什么说什么，而且tutor英文也一般，所以我自己带点口音也毫无压力，gp遇到两个靠谱队友，很好
reviews.translated_content: Very relaxed, easy to get a good grade. You can just casually write the in-class quizzes, which don't count towards the grade and are open-ended. Participation in tutorials is also very casual; you can say whatever comes to mind. Plus, the tutor’s English is just average, so I felt no pressure even with my own accent. I met two reliable teammates for the group project, which was great.

reviews.content: 教授和tutor都很负责，但小组作业发挥空间大，小组作业成绩基本取决于队友怎么样，而且lecture必去（要当堂写东西，作为点名）
reviews.translated_content: The professor and tutor are both very responsible, but the group project allows for a wide range of performance, so your grade basically depends on your teammates. Also, attendance at lectures is mandatory (you have to write something in class, which serves as the attendance check).

course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: 莫名其妙b-了（inclass quiz 80％和85％），wl不算大但wl比这个少的太多了，然后内容也蛮闷的……
reviews.translated_content: I inexplicably got a B- (in-class quizzes were 80% and 85%). The workload isn’t huge, but there are plenty of courses with much less workload, and the content is quite boring...

reviews.content: 老师上课真的很很很很催眠 不过内容本身是有意思的 就是拿一些小例子来讲一些理论在生活中的应用 几乎没有计算 虽然有两个考试但是都不是太难 essay是reflective所以就还好 gp有靠谱的组员明确分工跟着他的那个guidance做就可以
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer is really, really, really, really hypnotic in class, but the content itself is interesting. It uses small examples to explain the application of theories in everyday life. There is almost no calculation. Although there are two exams, neither is too difficult. The essay is reflective, so it’s okay. For the group project, if you have reliable teammates who clearly divide the labour and follow the guidance, you’ll be fine.

reviews.content: 不否认课程内容是有意思的，前半段讲的game theory比如如何solve games但点到为止，不涉及任何计算，后半段讲的behavioural的内容以及各种bias，wl一般，期中期末各一次quiz，一个1000words essay一个gp，但lecturer和tutor都有点水，对课不是很上心，lecturer讲课水平实属非常一般且英文不太好，给龟算还行但也没有说特别好
reviews.translated_content: I won’t deny that the course content is interesting. The first half covers game theory, such as how to solve games, but only scratches the surface without involving any calculations. The second half covers behavioural content and various biases. The workload is average. There is one quiz each for the midterm and final, one 1000-word essay, and one group project. However, both the lecturer and tutor are somewhat superficial and not very engaged with the course. The lecturer’s teaching ability is truly mediocre, and his English isn’t very good. Grading is acceptable, though not particularly excellent.

course_info.title: Leadership and Influence in a Dynamic World
course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: prof很好，课堂氛围很轻松，🈚️attendance，wl小，只有course journal+group project+reading journal，课堂有点像TED演讲，最后给龟也还行
reviews.translated_content: The professor is great, the class atmosphere is relaxed, there is no attendance requirement, and the workload is small. Assessments consist only of a course journal, a group project, and a reading journal. Classes are a bit like TED Talks, and the grading at the end is decent.

reviews.content: Workload很合理，每节课都像ted talk，不过课程内容比较松散，主要是教授回答一些人的问题、唠嗑，要写的一个journal需要你看一本教授给的书单里的书，这个书建议尽早开始读，给journal留足时间，一般都要写得挺长的，要让自己的反思和思考尽量深刻、有理有据。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is reasonable. Every lecture feels like a TED Talk, but the course content is quite loose; it’s mainly the professor answering some students’ questions and chatting. There is one journal assignment that requires you to read a book from the professor’s reading list. I suggest starting to read early and leaving enough time for the journal, as it generally needs to be quite long. You should make your reflections and thinking as profound and well-reasoned as possible.

reviews.content: 跟另一个david 的business ethics 风格很类似，都是上课以聊天为主的cc. 虽说不学硬核的东西，但是认真听的话收获肯定不少。对于真的对这个topic 有兴趣的或者还不确定要选什么的year 1 都会是不错的体验。wl 整体感觉下来，只要能较为自律的主动的去完全隐性的deadline, wl 绝对不大。
reviews.translated_content: The style is very similar to David’s Business Ethics course; both are Common Core courses where classes are mainly discussions. Although you won’t learn rigorous technical content, you’ll definitely gain a lot if you listen carefully. It’s a good experience for Year 1 students who are genuinely interested in this topic or haven’t decided what to choose yet. Overall, the workload isn’t heavy as long as you’re self-disciplined enough to proactively meet the entirely implicit deadlines.

reviews.content: 老师讲的超级有意思！上课上得很开心，付出就有回报的课
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer is super interesting! I really enjoyed the classes. It’s a course where effort pays off.

reviews.content: A+ 上課多發言 多多刷存在感 深刻反思課題內容 課前稍微看一下reading 內容不多 journal 不要用AI寫 自己認真寫一下 字數不多但是看得出有個人反思就可以很高分 小組作業不要做視頻 還要剪視頻很煩的 做個高質量的infographic 也可以高分 整體非常推薦 是整個學期最讓我喜歡的課 可以體驗一下成年人的思辨氛圍 課堂氛圍也很輕鬆有趣 推薦推薦
reviews.translated_content: A+. Speak up more in class and increase your presence. Reflect deeply on the course content. Skim the readings before class; there isn’t much content. Don’t use AI to write your journal entries; write them seriously yourself. The word count isn’t high, but showing personal reflection can earn a very high score. For the group assignment, don’t make a video; editing videos is annoying. Making a high-quality infographic can also get a high score. Highly recommended overall. It was my favourite course of the entire semester. You can experience an adult-level critical thinking atmosphere, and the class vibe is relaxed and fun. Recommended, recommended.

reviews.content: Excellent course, every class felt like it was relevant to your life. 10/10，decently easy to get an A as well. Most people get similar grades since the course doesn't demand much. I got an A-
reviews.translated_content: Excellent course, every class felt like it was relevant to your life. 10/10，decently easy to get an A as well. Most people get similar grades since the course doesn't demand much. I got an A-

reviews.content: 老师很好很幽默，有两次guesttalk 有机会接触一些大佬（可能商院同学会比较感兴趣）wl不是很小… 一个book reflection，一个gp，还有course journal（七八个题简答即可）还有一个小组辩论hhh attendance看上课发言和tutorial发言 需要e一点
reviews.translated_content: The instructor is great and humorous. There were two guest talks, offering a chance to interact with some industry experts (Business School students might find this more interesting). The workload isn’t exactly light… There’s one book reflection, one group project, and a course journal (just short answers to seven or eight questions), plus a group debate hahaha. Attendance is based on participation in lectures and tutorials, so you need to be a bit extroverted.

reviews.content: The course is excellent. I highly recommend it!! The tutor is the best ever
reviews.translated_content: The course is excellent. I highly recommend it!! The tutor is the best ever

reviews.content: I loved this course actually, very inspirational and chill, perfect for when you wanna do something outside of studying very hard subjects, the workload was fine and the professor and tutor were both amazing and interesting. i didn't end up getting the best grade but this course was super fun!
reviews.translated_content: I loved this course actually, very inspirational and chill, perfect for when you wanna do something outside of studying very hard subjects, the workload was fine and the professor and tutor were both amazing and interesting. i didn't end up getting the best grade but this course was super fun!

reviews.content: 作业压力较小，要交的作业只有一篇学习日志，其中包含一些课上要求反思的问题、对于讲座的思考和读书笔记；没有期末考试
reviews.translated_content: The assignment pressure is relatively low. You only need to submit one learning journal, which includes some reflection questions required in class, thoughts on the lectures, and reading notes. There is no final exam.

reviews.content: The best cc ever!! low wl. No attendance for lectures but I'd still go cuz the topics are really interesting to me eg myths, economy, geography, humanity... . Usually the first half of the lecturer will be taught by lecturer/ TA and the second half by outside guests. There're 2 gp which require you to take photos and type a caption, as simple as you post an instagram post. The MOST IMPORTANT factor for your grade is your 1500 word final report, an open topic ethnographic report (as long as your topic is somehow related to water). Basically you gather your interview results, insight, and some photos taken during your research process. No worries for conducting interviews bc the tutorials will equip you with all the skills you need for the final report including interview, photography, and report brainstorming. There're quite a few optional field trips for you to practise skills learnt in tutorials, or even to start your final report interviews so you don't have to spend extra time on interviewing at somewhere else. The lecturer and 2 TAs are super nice and i can feel their deep passion towards water -- if I remembered correctly in one lecturer they mentioned that 3 of them would go to scuba diiving tgt + they're super supportive that they're always more than willing to listen to your questions related to your essay/ sharing insights regarding the lectures/ even chatting. I miss the days when i was still taking this course!! I got an A for the course but it could definitely be higher if we did better in our gp
reviews.translated_content: The best Common Core course ever!! Low workload. Attendance isn’t required for lectures, but I’d still go because the topics are really interesting to me, e.g., myths, economy, geography, humanity... Usually, the first half of the lecture is taught by the lecturer/TA and the second half by outside guests. There are 2 group projects which require you to take photos and type a caption, as simple as posting on Instagram. The MOST IMPORTANT factor for your grade is your 1500-word final report, an open-topic ethnographic report (as long as your topic is somehow related to water). Basically, you gather your interview results, insights, and some photos taken during your research process. No worries about conducting interviews because the tutorials will equip you with all the skills you need for the final report, including interviewing, photography, and report brainstorming. There are quite a few optional field trips for you to practise skills learnt in tutorials, or even to start your final report interviews so you don’t have to spend extra time on interviewing somewhere else. The lecturer and 2 TAs are super nice, and I can feel their deep passion towards water -- if I remembered correctly, in one lecture they mentioned that the three of them would go scuba diving together + they're super supportive; they're always more than willing to listen to your questions related to your essay, share insights regarding the lectures, or even just chat. I miss the days when I was still taking this course!! I got an A for the course, but it could definitely have been higher if we had done better in our group project.

reviews.translated_content: I can only say that Jessica is a very nice person. If you want to change your tutorial time, even if that slot is full, just ask her and she will help coordinate it. As a Year 1 student, I’m not sure if the workload counts as heavy, but the grading is indeed average. There are no assignments outside of class, but you need to complete some tasks during class. There is one field trip during Reading Week, one group project (with PPT + presentation), and one essay. I only got a B in the end. Hmm.

reviews.content: 很水的課！兩位外國教授和tutors 都挺友善，一個學期只有4次tutorial，平時有隨機lecture discussion 要交上moodle 但不算attendance, assessment 只有一份gp 和一個poster + 800字 individual assignment。給分fair 沒有特別好, 最後A-。想chill 的推薦！
reviews.translated_content: A very lightweight course! The two foreign professors and tutors are quite friendly. There are only four tutorials in the semester. There are random lecture discussions to submit on Moodle, but they don’t count toward attendance. Assessment consists of only one group project and a poster plus an 800-word individual assignment. Grading is fair, nothing special; I got an A- in the end. Recommended if you want to chill!

reviews.content: 别选，稀烂的结构，模糊的标准，随机的讲师，最重要的两个assessment由三节tutorial指导，讲座给的内容原封引用在写在作业里被判定为写的是错的。Moodle上教授的名字和教室号码页是错的，还得当面澄清。答疑可以用无证据的观点来反驳你的证据本身。
reviews.translated_content: Don’t choose this course. The structure is terrible, the criteria are vague, and the instructors are random. The two most important assessments were guided by only three tutorials, and content quoted verbatim from the lectures was marked wrong in the assignments. The professor’s name and room number page on Moodle were incorrect and had to be clarified in person. In Q&A sessions, they would use unsubstantiated opinions to refute your evidence itself.

reviews.content: 教的内容比较有趣，网课也相对轻松，每节课会有一两个小的activity，只要在moodle上写了东西就有分，所以每堂课都要听。workload不大，前面有些法新社提供的elearning只要刷完就可以了，最后的大assessment个人觉得总体不难，但是需要一定的运气。。。要求是要找到一个社交媒体上你觉得真实性存疑或可能存在误导的的推文/视频等，然后去进行fact check。于是是否能找到一个好的素材就很重要了。。因为很多大新闻的fact check都已经有专业的新闻机构在做了，一些过于细枝末节的推文可能又很难找到fact check的途径，所以说找一个合适的可行的fact check素材是最关键的，这一步搞定了剩下就非常轻松。按照他刚开学给的百分制和等级的换算表dz只能A-，但最后拿了A
reviews.translated_content: The content is quite interesting, and the online course is relatively relaxed. There are one or two small activities in each class; you get marks as long as you post something on Moodle, so you need to listen to every lecture. The workload isn’t heavy. At the beginning, there are some e-learning modules provided by AFP that you just need to complete. I found the final major assessment generally not difficult, but it requires a bit of luck... The requirement is to find a tweet, video, or other social media content whose authenticity you doubt or which may be misleading, and then fact-check it. So finding good material is crucial... Because many major news items have already been fact-checked by professional news agencies, while some overly trivial tweets might be hard to find fact-checking sources for. Therefore, finding suitable and feasible fact-checking material is the most critical step; once that’s done, the rest is very easy. According to the percentage-to-grade conversion table he gave at the start of the semester, I could only get an A-, but I ended up with an A.

reviews.content: 并没有网传的那么好grade，每次lecture从头听到尾，没缺勤，并且经常发言刷存在，但由于发言的人也很多，prof可能下一秒就忘了你叫啥了，unless像课上一位姐一样每节课疯狂不停的发言。每周都要做一个小组pre。这门课很看队友，后期队友摆烂，根本不负责semifreerider。podcast更是一个人carry，结果B+。并没有感觉付出和努力很对等。因为最后的podcast是一个不设限的qualitative作业，个人认为打分很主观，belike这个主题，你podcast选择的方式喜不喜欢，很玄学。
reviews.translated_content: It’s not as good for grades as online rumours suggest. I listened carefully from start to finish in every lecture, had perfect attendance, and frequently spoke up to make my presence known. However, since many others also participated, the professor probably forgot your name by the next second—unless you’re like one female student in class who kept talking non-stop every session. Every week requires a small-group presentation. This course heavily depends on your teammates; later on, my teammates slacked off and were essentially free riders. I ended up carrying the podcast project alone, yet only got a B+. I didn’t feel that my effort and input were fairly rewarded. Because the final podcast is an open-ended qualitative assignment, I personally find the grading very subjective—it feels like whether the professor likes your chosen approach to the topic is somewhat opaque and unpredictable.

reviews.content: Carol绝世好老师啊。很有社会关怀，课程内容丰富，材料新。非常乐于帮助同学。最大的project是一个podcast。想好龟请一定多和prof交流，很重要
reviews.translated_content: Carol is an absolutely wonderful teacher. She has strong social concern, the course content is rich, and the materials are current. She is very willing to help students. The biggest project is a podcast. If you want a good grade, please communicate with the professor as much as possible; it’s very important.

reviews.content: I saw comments saying dont take this course if youre not a feminist; in my opinion, you shouldnt take this even if you are one. The course is very surface level... and only tells you everything you already know. I also dont understand why a large unnecessary chunk of time in tutorials and lectures was about how men feel.... it this course was advertised as talking about sexism, I understand. But as a girl, I did not feel any "power". The instructors and tutors did their best im sure, but the course itself is very cowardly, it does not challenge much or talk about illusion of choice or actual modern problems... infact, i felt like a lot of it was outdated and not feminist enough. If you are a feminist or just someone wanting to be truly free from the patriarchy, this is not for you.

reviews.content: 是一门讲feminism的课，有两个教授两个tutor。workload的话，第一是从教授给的书单里选一本书，写一篇book review，800-1000词，rw之后交。第二是tutorial上会随机分组，每组有不同的reading，读完之后要在tutorial上做presentation。第三是在tutorial上自己组队，选一个话题，然后做interview video。按理来说这个video应该是会在lecture上放给大家看的，但这学期由于某些缘故少了半个月课，于是就变成了网上提交。第四的话是要读一些reading然后根据给定问题写一篇essay，1000-1200词，revision week期间交。lecture的话从不同的方面讲了feminism。课上有时候会做一些小活动，就是教授提一些问题然后学生把自己的回答交上去，会有bonus mark，所以lecture还是要去上的哈哈。tutorial的话两周一次，除去做presentation，还会有一些讨论，并且会留一些时间给group mate之间讨论怎么做interview。 给龟的话，对于本理科生来说，我觉得还不错。并且有一次在课上听一个已经毕业的学姐跟我们说这门课在她上学那会儿就已经给龟很不错了
reviews.translated_content: This is a course on feminism, with two professors and two tutors. Regarding workload: first, choose a book from the professor’s reading list and write an 800–1000-word book review, due after Reading Week. Second, you’ll be randomly grouped in tutorials; each group has different readings, and after reading them, you must give a presentation in the tutorial. Third, form your own group in the tutorial, choose a topic, and make an interview video. In theory, this video was supposed to be shown to everyone in the lecture, but because we lost half a month of classes this semester for certain reasons, it became an online submission instead. Fourth, read some materials and write an essay based on given questions, 1000–1200 words, due during revision week. The lectures covered feminism from different perspectives. Sometimes there are small activities in class where the professor asks questions and students submit their answers for bonus marks, so you should still attend lectures, haha. Tutorials are held every two weeks. Besides presentations, there are discussions, and some time is left for groupmates to discuss how to do the interview. As for grading, as a science student, I think it’s quite good. Also, once in class I heard a senior alumna tell us that the grading for this course was already quite generous back when she was a student.

reviews.content: 课程十分有趣，特别喜欢tutorial的老师，tutorial 就是在小组讨论，很能启发思维
reviews.translated_content: The course is very interesting. I especially liked the tutorial instructor. Tutorials involve group discussions, which are very thought-provoking.

reviews.content: 先叠个buff 我对所有合理存在的少数群体都尊重认可 以下只是主观观点只针对个人。 我觉得Brenda是不配在hku有教职的 从课堂内容/教学质量/性格上看她都是我上过课最差的老师：1）Moodle设置混乱 没有syllabus 所有东西都扔在Moodle里 无序杂糅；2）教学质量堪忧 很多上课内容重复 完全从个人角度出发，广度深度不够，学不到任何东西；3）迟到早退+水时间 抛去看电影/guest lecture（她请了好多好多嘉宾 虽然这些嘉宾的分享都还行）/她迟到/quiz和pre 一学期她讲课的时间很短 根本没法系统性授课；4）考核内容抽象 无考核反馈 一些问题和内容不是太过肤浅让人无话可说就是模糊 包括quiz的题目也十分离谱 而且无论是individual还是gp她毫无反馈 透明度极低 根本无法知道她的标准 5）从她课堂里的言论来看她很mean 极端看重自己的性别身份 对自己的课堂内容十分自信。 庆幸tutor Meg人还算OK gp的组员也不太划水都在做事 最后B+ 但当我有种吃了F的难受感
reviews.translated_content: First, a disclaimer: I respect and acknowledge all reasonably existing minority groups. The following is just my subjective view and targets only this individual. I think Brenda does not deserve a teaching position at HKU. In terms of course content, teaching quality, and personality, she is the worst instructor I have ever had: 1) The Moodle setup is chaotic, with no syllabus; everything is dumped into Moodle in a disordered mess. 2) The teaching quality is worrying; much of the class content is repetitive, entirely from her personal perspective, lacking breadth and depth, so you learn nothing. 3) She arrives late, leaves early, and fills time. Aside from watching movies, guest lectures (she invited many guests, and although their shares were okay), her lateness, quizzes, and presentations, she lectured for very little time during the semester, making systematic teaching impossible. 4) The assessment criteria are bizarre, with no feedback on assessments. Some questions and content are either too superficial, leaving nothing to say, or vague; the quiz questions were particularly ridiculous. Moreover, she gave no feedback on either individual work or the group project, with extremely low transparency, so it was impossible to know her standards. 5) From her remarks in class, she seems very mean, places extreme importance on her gender identity, and is overly confident in her course content. Fortunately, the tutor Meg was reasonably OK, and my group project teammates didn’t slack off and did their work. I finally got a B+, but it felt as unpleasant as if I had received an F.

reviews.content: Overall, one of the best courses I have attended in my life. The professor is very interesting and makes the lectures really interactive. If you enjoy critical thinking and philosophy, it is a very easy course to get A range in. I think you should also go to visit the professor more often during his office hours and build rapport, which can push your grades up. In the end I got an A+ although I barely did any readings and just grinded for the 2 essays I had to write. I would reccomend following his sample essay and the video he uploads on how to structure an essay, this should push up your grade.

reviews.content: 课很有趣，喜欢社科的人应该会很喜欢，professor和tutor人都很nice！ lecture和tuto都是引导思考、讨论为主，课上讨论的时长可能比讲课还多。讨论的话题很广泛，包括安乐死、基因编辑、prostitution, abortion等等。workload不算小，主要就是midterm final各一篇两千字essay和一个tuto上的个人8分钟present，每节课大概有一到三篇reading（不过不读完也没啥关系）。给分fair，我A-，essay写得好的话龟应该还不错
reviews.translated_content: The course is interesting; people who like social sciences should enjoy it. The professor and tutors are all very nice! Lectures and tutorials focus mainly on guiding thinking and discussion; class discussion time might even exceed lecturing time. Topics are broad, including euthanasia, gene editing, prostitution, abortion, etc. The workload isn’t small: mainly a 2,000-word essay each for the midterm and final, plus an individual 8-minute presentation in tutorial. Each class has about one to three readings (but it’s fine if you don’t finish them all). Grading is fair; I got an A-. If you write your essays well, the grade should be pretty good.

reviews.content:
I'll ask you two questions:
i) Do you value your sanity?
ii) Do you value your GPA?

If the answer is yes to any of those, even a tiny bit, I'll tell you this: STEER CLEAR OF THIS COURSE, EVEN IF YOU ARE FORCED TO TAKE A CC IN THE SUMMER. Seriously, the amount of workload this course has made me question between the difference between this and an actual humanities course. There are 3 readings per week, 57-70 pages each in the worst case, or 1 reading per week with the same number of pages at the very least. All of these are written in such abstract language, that at least me, as an engineering student, had to sit down for 8 hours per reading to decipher all the points, and even then, I don't understand a lot of the parts fully. Granted, the profs and tutors are very responsive, but that's the only good part about this course. Then, you're expected to actively participate in the tutorials, which means reading AND understanding the readings, and making framing your questions in terms of the readings to contribute to the class, and if you don't, you get poor marks. As for your essay, you're expected to interview some minority groups at the very least in order to back up your claims. Let's not even talk about the finals, which expects you to read ALL the readings up until then, and will ask very, very specific things from the readings which unless you're a memory god, you'll never be able to fully answer correctly.

Unless you really, REALLY care about social divisions and an interesting lecturer, you'll be greeted with a semester full of stress, misery and frustration taking this course. I would go as far as to argue it's better to take an additional semester to finish your CCs rather than putting this hunk of stressful GPA sink onto your course list.
reviews.translated_content: I'll ask you two questions: i) Do you value your sanity? ii) Do you value your GPA? If the answer is yes to any of those, even a tiny bit, I'll tell you this: STEER CLEAR OF THIS COURSE, EVEN IF YOU ARE FORCED TO TAKE A CC IN THE SUMMER. Seriously, the amount of workload this course has made me question between the difference between this and an actual humanities course. There are 3 readings per week, 57-70 pages each in the worst case, or 1 reading per week with the same number of pages at the very least. All of these are written in such abstract language, that at least me, as an engineering student, had to sit down for 8 hours per reading to decipher all the points, and even then, I don't understand a lot of the parts fully. Granted, the profs and tutors are very responsive, but that's the only good part about this course. Then, you're expected to actively participate in the tutorials, which means reading AND understanding the readings, and making framing your questions in terms of the readings to contribute to the class, and if you don't, you get poor marks. As for your essay, you're expected to interview some minority groups at the very least in order to back up your claims. Let's not even talk about the finals, which expects you to read ALL the readings up until then, and will ask very, very specific things from the readings which unless you're a memory god, you'll never be able to fully answer correctly. Unless you really, REALLY care about social divisions and an interesting lecturer, you'll be greeted with a semester full of stress, misery and frustration taking this course. I would go as far as to argue it's better to take an additional semester to finish your CCs rather than putting this hunk of stressful GPA sink onto your course list.

reviews.translated_content: My eternal favourite course... The prof teaches with great passion and is super interesting, and really teaches you deep insights you didn’t know before. The workload is indeed heavy, with a group project, an essay, and a final exam. But if you really enjoy field trips and care deeply about social division, you’ll find it super interesting and appreciate that the essay requires a field trip. I will always support my idol Emery... If you’re hesitating whether to enrol in 9011, don’t hesitate—go audit the class. Idol, can you offer more courses? I want to take your class again. Anna and Ashley, dear tutors, can you lead more tutorials? I want to be your student again.

reviews.content: 看到大家都說wl 大 但是我真的不覺得 我Reading都沒有看除了自己要present的那個看了（其實不看也可以）wl大概是group 2人present 某一topic (第一堂就要搶了有點傻眼 老師先前並沒有給任何指引 是亂組隊的 結果就是碰到了醫學生freeride心情極其不好！freerider行衰運！不過我覺得Tutorial老師不太尊重人 Present的時候都沒有認真聽在玩筆 一副不耐煩的樣子就算我英文不太好老師應該要尊重學生吧）+2500字文（interview minority+先前要做個簡單的大綱+final test（可以打開ppt 上網查都行 有點難 不過時間好多 有人做了15分鐘就走了 我坐到了一個小時後但是成績也是一般）不過professor 教書很有趣 （聽完全堂都不會困！很欣賞這個professor 不是照PPT讀 上堂有互動但不會強迫人答問題） 自己也比較喜歡社會學 可以從不同角度思考 就是派分不透明 到現在都沒有收到小分和評語 。。。我也B range
reviews.translated_content: Everyone says the workload is heavy, but I really didn’t feel it was. I didn’t even read the assigned readings, except for the one I had to present on (though you could probably skip that too). The workload mainly consisted of a group presentation with two people on a chosen topic (you had to grab a topic in the first class, which was a bit shocking; the professor gave no prior guidance, so groups were formed randomly. As a result, I ended up with a medical student who was a free rider, which made me extremely unhappy! Bad luck with free riders!). However, I felt the tutorial instructor was disrespectful. During my presentation, he wasn’t listening carefully and was playing with his pen, looking impatient. Even if my English isn’t great, the instructor should still respect students.) There was also a 2,500-word essay (interviewing a minority group + preparing a simple outline beforehand) + a final test (open-book: you could use PPT slides and search online. It was somewhat difficult, but there was plenty of time. Some people finished in 15 minutes and left; I stayed for an hour, but my grade was just average). That said, the professor’s teaching was interesting (I wasn’t sleepy at all during the entire lecture! I really appreciate this professor; he doesn’t just read off the PPT. There is interaction in class, but he doesn’t force students to answer questions). I also enjoy sociology as it allows thinking from different perspectives. The only issue is that grading is opaque. I still haven’t received breakdowns or comments... I ended up with a B-range grade.

reviews.content: 要踩这个课，主要的问题不是给分差和workload大，而是根本学不到什么，而且各位看到这条的同学请一定记住我的这句话：凡是课程由三个不同意义的单词以A，B and C的形式命名的，都是烂课。比如Body，Beauty and Fashion（但是三个有内在很深联系的词组成的课名就还很靠谱，比如CCCH9009），原因很简单，就是因为任何一个词都可以开一门课，结果一门课给你讲三个词，除了水就没别的解释了，而且课水的前提下，为了保持CC课程学习的workload大致稳定，就会加大workload，这就是很多其他同学抱怨的根本原因 其他的问题： 1）你以为是时尚行业的社会学研究，结果是gender studies，不是我不喜欢gender studies，而是我选这门课不是要学gender studies 2）essay quiz有两个，虽然现在看来已经没什么可怕的了，但是作为我大学遇到的第一个essay quiz，当时是把我chur到了，新生慎选，没考过essay quiz的慎选 3）tutor的话Alexandra Ridgway很棒，其他的也不了解 4）一定要记得做每周一个的journal question，不然期末会很难过 5）给分很一般，因为你能拿高分的只有tuto，presentation和midterm assignment（占40%左右），两个essay quiz和journal都是很难把握的
reviews.translated_content: If you’re considering this course, the main issue isn’t poor grading or heavy workload, but that you basically learn nothing. And to everyone reading this, please remember my words: any course named with three distinct concepts in an “A, B and C” format is a bad course. For example, Body, Beauty and Fashion (whereas courses with three deeply interconnected concepts in the title, like CCCH9009, are quite reliable). The reason is simple: each concept could easily constitute its own course, so covering three in one class leaves no explanation other than that it’s superficial. And given that superficiality, to keep the Common Core workload roughly consistent, they increase the actual workload, which is the root cause of many other students’ complaints. Other issues: 1) You might expect sociological research on the fashion industry, but it turns out to be gender studies. It’s not that I dislike gender studies, but I didn’t choose this course to study gender studies. 2) There are two essay quizzes. Although they don’t seem scary now, as my first-ever essay quiz in university, it really exhausted me at the time. Freshmen should choose with caution; those who haven’t taken an essay quiz before should also choose with caution. 3) As for tutors, Alexandra Ridgway is great; I don’t know about the others. 4) Be sure to complete the weekly journal question, otherwise you’ll struggle at the end of the term. 5) Grading is just average, because the only components where you can reliably score high are tutorials, presentation, and the midterm assignment (worth around 40%); the two essay quizzes and journals are very hard to gauge.

reviews.content: 听上去美妆小课堂，实际性别研究。话题有趣，例如有一个用barbie讲现代女性的审美标准。reading好好看很有含金量，两篇reflective journal量不大，但是是很有效率的输出，很有意义的assessment。gp也很不局限形式，我们组就做了个vogue杂志，队友可以的。但上课有些泛泛，只是列举现象，没有结合reading给人启发的那种感觉，缺少了一些更深层次的思考。
reviews.translated_content: It sounds like a beauty and makeup mini-class, but it’s actually gender studies. The topics are interesting—for example, using Barbie to discuss modern aesthetic standards for women. The readings are worth reading and have substantial value. The two reflective journals aren’t heavy in volume, but they require efficient output, making them a meaningful assessment. The group project format is also very flexible; our group created a Vogue magazine, and my teammates were capable. However, the lectures were somewhat superficial, merely listing phenomena without providing the kind of inspiration that connects with the readings, lacking some deeper thinking.

reviews.content: 很喜欢的一门课，社会学讨论女性男性body image等相关问题，workload有点大，有16-20页的reflection journal，还有essay，quiz

reviews.translated_content: Attendance is not counted, but there are tutorials. Tutorials are quite demanding, with two presentations. Lecture content is not difficult, but requires critical thinking; personally, I feel it has some connection to gender studies. Both professors are very nice and lecture well.

reviews.translated_content: A-. The course difficulty is reasonable and not too bizarre. However, there are detailed differences between the professor’s in-class PowerPoint slides and those on Moodle. The assignment load is acceptable (one individual presentation, one group presentation, and one 1,000-word essay), and you need to integrate knowledge learned in class. I found it quite easy. I arrived more than ten minutes late on the exam night, lol. The tutorial instructor recommends choosing the professor’s section; I attended tutorials from both instructors. The professor’s tutorial involves a collaborative presentation by two or three people rather than an individual one, so the difficulty is lower.

reviews.content: 我是Local，以前唸Geo感覺非常有趣和簡單，學到一些有關文化遺產的東西，Final有腦子便懂，Tutorial和Prof人很好，要多多問他們問題，他們便會對你有印象，Wl可，一篇essay+Tutorial presentation + Gp + Final，Gp建議選材新穎一點，我們有人選蛇羹被Prof心心眼，本人A-，好🐢
reviews.translated_content: I am a local student. I studied Geography before and found it very interesting and easy. I learned some things about cultural heritage. The final is easy if you use your brain. The tutor and professor are very nice; ask them more questions so they remember you. Workload is acceptable: one essay + tutorial presentation + group project + final. For the group project, I suggest choosing a novel topic; someone in our group chose snake soup and the professor loved it. I got an A-. Generous grading.

reviews.content: Steve是特别好的人，final还会发巧克力。Tutor Cheryle也特别nice，温柔美丽。。。整体wl不大，gp选好队友挺重要的。好龟，lecture半个学期没去，final看了ppt，essay好好写了，最后a-
reviews.translated_content: Steve is a really nice person; he even hands out chocolates at the final. Tutor Cheryle is also very nice, gentle and beautiful... The overall workload isn’t heavy, but choosing good teammates for the group project is quite important. Grading is generous: I skipped half the semester’s lectures, reviewed the slides before the final, and wrote the essay properly, ending up with an A-.

reviews.content: workload不是很大，事儿比较少。gp essay给分到还可以，但是不知道为什么最后出成绩是A-
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t very heavy, and there are few tasks. The group project essay grading is decent, but for some reason my final grade came out as an A-.

reviews.content: 很水，wl很小，lecture不记考勤也没必要听（除了最后三次）。给分很好。
reviews.translated_content: It’s a very lightweight course with a small workload. Attendance isn’t taken in lectures, and there’s no need to attend (except for the last three sessions). Grading is generous.

reviews.content: The professor is nice and patient in guidance. Willing to do office visit if you emailed him. The topics are not burdening. Still even with A-, this is a great course! Recommended for anyone
reviews.translated_content: The professor is nice and patient in guidance. Willing to do office visit if you emailed him. The topics are not burdening. Still even with A-, this is a great course! Recommended for anyone

reviews.content: 不建议跟风选择，大一选的，但自觉Palmer这门课上的很水很一般（至少离我觉得的人类学很远），全程顺直白男讲自己的家庭故事
reviews.translated_content: I do not recommend following the crowd to choose this course. I took it in my first year, but I feel Palmer’s classes were very lightweight and mediocre (at least far from what I consider anthropology). It was just a straight white male talking about his own family stories throughout.

reviews.content: 对宗教感兴趣的话内容是值得推荐的。wl适中，龟不错，需要写的paper篇幅都比较小，不会对写essay有高门槛。推荐。
reviews.translated_content: If you are interested in religion, the content is worth recommending. The workload is moderate, the grading is good, and the required papers are relatively short, so there is no high barrier to writing essays. Recommended.

reviews.content: 对灵性宗教感兴趣的话，很推荐！教授准备的内容都很有启发性，lecture挺有意思的，但是如果不去也没关系哈哈。wl不大，而且作业难度不大，tutorial上有group pre，tutorial平时要轮流发言，但是不会按质量记分，去就记attendance。Hua Ye内地tutor很好！推荐！再就是field trip reflective essay，reflective video，都很容易。平时需要选2个field trip，必须去，挺有意思的！🐢挺好A。
reviews.translated_content: If you’re interested in spiritual religion, this is highly recommended! The content prepared by the professor is very inspiring, and the lectures are quite interesting, but it’s okay if you don’t attend, haha. The workload isn’t heavy, and the assignments aren’t difficult. There’s a group presentation in the tutorial, and you need to take turns speaking during tutorials, but marks aren’t awarded for quality; attendance is recorded just for showing up. Hua Ye, the mainland tutor, is great! Recommended! Also, the field trip reflective essay and reflective video are both very easy. You need to choose two field trips, which are mandatory and quite interesting! The grading is quite good; an A is attainable 🐢.

reviews.content: 好龟 wl极小 内容insightful 组织了去各种宗教场所的fieldtrip很开阔眼界 对这个话题感兴趣的同学放心冲！
reviews.translated_content: Generous grading, extremely low workload. The content is insightful. The field trips to various religious sites were very eye-opening. If you are interested in this topic, go for it with confidence!

reviews.content: wl不大 教授很可爱 经常说中文 和秀恩爱
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy. The professor is very cute, often speaks Chinese, and shows off their relationship.

reviews.content: 个人感觉是很清流的一门cc，在节奏极快的学期中间每周上tutorial讨论点哲学问题，上lec看点philo方面的知识感觉还是挺治愈的，不错的哲学启蒙也不需要很多的基础知识。wl不大而且讨论的问题与每个人都息息相关，field trip也很有趣见证了一些失传的仪式。唯一的问题是tutor给分好像有点不稳定，我几次assessment都在a-但是同组有c的。个人觉得好好写essay，lec随缘去就行。总体来说推荐。
reviews.translated_content: Personally, I feel this is a refreshing Common Core course. In the middle of a fast-paced semester, attending weekly tutorials to discuss philosophical questions and watching lectures to gain some philosophical knowledge felt quite healing. It’s a good introduction to philosophy that doesn’t require much prior knowledge. The workload isn’t heavy, and the discussion topics are relevant to everyone. The field trip was also interesting, allowing us to witness some lost rituals. The only issue is that the tutor’s grading seems a bit unstable; several of my assessments were A-, but a teammate in the same group got a C. Personally, I think if you write your essays well, you can just attend lectures casually. Overall, recommended.

reviews.content: 不知道是不是这个学期field trip被取消的原因 这门课给我一种空谈玄学的感觉 如果你对religion本身没有兴趣的话可能永远也写不出教授想看到的essay 感觉半个学期也没学出个所以然 最后干脆选了pf图个清静
reviews.translated_content: I’m not sure if it was because field trips were cancelled this semester, but this course felt like empty metaphysical talk. If you aren’t interested in religion itself, you might never write the kind of essay the professor wants to see. I felt like I hadn’t learned much concrete substance even after half a semester, so I eventually chose to take it on a pass/fail basis just for peace of mind.

reviews.content: 很有意思的哲学启蒙课。教授的经历也很有趣，时常上课的时候给我们提一嘴。中文说的很好，第一节课说着说着蹦出一句“意识形态”惊呆众人。给分也很不错，但因为本菜鸡实在是哲学宗教小白... 社院文院大佬应该轻松Arange
reviews.translated_content: A very interesting introductory philosophy course. The professor's background is also interesting, and he often mentions it in class. He speaks Chinese very well; in the first lecture, he suddenly dropped the term 'ideology', stunning everyone. The grading is also quite good, but since I am really a beginner in philosophy and religion... strong students from the Faculty of Social Sciences or Faculty of Arts should easily get an A-range grade.

reviews.content: 讲宗教的，很有趣！！！3个filed trip，assessment基本就是reflective essay，可以不用很学术，写出自己的想法就能好🐢啦！depth还不错，是真的会好好分析ideology伤的一些东西，入股不亏！
reviews.translated_content: It covers religion and is very interesting!!! There are three field trips, and the assessments are basically reflective essays. You don’t need to be overly academic; just write down your own thoughts and you can get a good grade! The depth is quite good; it really analyses ideological issues properly. You won’t regret taking it!

reviews.content:
这学期wl很大啊 - Tutorial and field trip participation - 15% 
- weekly quizzes on readings - 25%
- field notes taking - 5%
- field trip reflective essay - 15% 
- final reflective video - 20% 
- weekly journal 20% 神了，第一周本来没有journal的，第二周又增加了。wl增加了我可能会drop掉，不知道好不好🐢，不过Palmer人真的很有意思呀
reviews.translated_content: The workload this semester is huge: Tutorial and field trip participation - 15%; Weekly quizzes on readings - 25%; Field notes - 5%; Field trip reflective essay - 15%; Final reflective video - 20%; Weekly journal - 20%. It’s crazy; there was no journal in the first week, but it was added in the second week. With the increased workload, I might drop the course. I’m not sure if the grading is generous 🐢, but Palmer is really an interesting person.

reviews.content: 强烈推荐这门课，顺利到手A。 虽然课程内容略有点十八禁，上lecture看AV，guest lecture请性玩具店老板，tutorial就直接问你能否接受兽交，但是这有什么呢，好grade才是一切啊。内容其实如果你脸皮够厚，听一听还是有意思的。 课程要求是30% individual essay（2000-2500 words），30% group project（tutorial内分组，每组五个人，每人写五百字左右，还需要上台做creative presentation），30% tutorial presentation（四个人一组，时常共计45-60mins，但很多人会present一个多小时），10% lecture participation。 不需要看很多reading也没有考试，把ppt和essay做好就很高分。当时的Tutor是Sky，一个很负责性格很好的人，讲课也很有意思，多去问他问题可以增加印象分，建议积极提问。
reviews.translated_content: Highly recommend this course; I smoothly secured an A. Although the course content is slightly NSFW—we watched adult videos in lectures, invited a sex toy shop owner as a guest lecturer, and tutorials directly asked if you could accept bestiality—but so what? Good grades are everything. The content is actually interesting if you have thick skin and just listen. Course requirements: 30% individual essay ([REDACTED_PHONE] words), 30% group project (groups formed within tutorials, five people per group, each writing about 500 words and doing a creative presentation on stage), 30% tutorial presentation (groups of four, total duration 45–60 minutes, but many present for over an hour), and 10% lecture participation. You don’t need to do much reading and there are no exams. If you prepare the PPTs and essays well, you’ll get a high score. The tutor at the time was Sky, a very responsible and nice person who also taught interestingly. Asking him more questions can boost your impression score, so I recommend participating actively.

course_info.title: Art and Ideas: East and West

reviews.content: 就两个字：快逃
reviews.translated_content: Just two words: stay away.

reviews.content:
主线为西方艺术史，从古希腊罗马讲到现代艺术，上半学期先讲了一点偏理论/方法论的形式六要素，然后讲古典时期：古希腊罗马雕塑湿壁画，中世纪壁画，文艺复兴油画（米开朗基罗，拉斐尔，达芬奇，扬范艾克），浅浅提了一下巴洛克，之后新古典主义（雅克路易大卫）。下半学期讲现代：浪漫主义（德拉克洛瓦），现实主义（库尔贝），日本主义（马奈），印象派（雷诺阿），后印象派（梵高，高更），抽象表现主义（波洛克），立体主义（毕加索），最后浅浅提了一下德国表现主义、达达主义和当代艺术。辅线为中国、日本艺术史，中国画家讲了顾恺之，徐熙，文同，李公麟，苏轼，石涛，是真的很跳脱；日本那边主要讲了日本禅宗艺术、浮世绘对西方近代绘画的影响。可以看出来基本上是一个艺术家几部作品代表一个时代/流派，很简略很精炼了。对画的理解更多在于分析形式要素、理解其在艺术史上的地位和代表性，与其它画作的区别联系，以及看到中日艺术对西方的影响这些层面，并不会特别深究一幅画的历史背景和各种细节品读。换句话说这课“背多分”是有的，不过还是比较建议对以上列举的内容有兴趣做多了解的朋友来上吧。
Dr Hammers讲课有股美式幽默，也很负责，不过这是她最后一学期授课了，不知道这课以后会换哪个老师上。
reviews.translated_content: The main thread is Western art history, from ancient Greece and Rome to modern art. In the first half of the semester, we covered some theoretical/methodological elements of form, then the Classical period: ancient Greek and Roman sculpture, wet-fresco murals, medieval murals, Renaissance oil painting (Michelangelo, Raphael, da Vinci, Jan van Eyck), with a brief mention of Baroque, followed by Neoclassicism (Jacques-Louis David). The second half covered Modern art: Romanticism (Delacroix), Realism (Courbet), Japonisme (Manet), Impressionism (Renoir), Post-Impressionism (Van Gogh, Gauguin), Abstract Expressionism (Pollock), Cubism (Picasso), and finally a brief mention of German Expressionism, Dadaism, and contemporary art. The secondary thread is Chinese and Japanese art history. Chinese painters covered include Gu Kaizhi, Xu Xi, Wen Tong, Li Gonglin, Su Shi, and Shitao, which is quite eclectic; for Japan, the focus was mainly on Zen art and the influence of ukiyo-e on modern Western painting. You can see that basically a few works by each artist represent an era or school, so it’s very concise and refined. Understanding paintings focuses more on analysing formal elements, understanding their status and representativeness in art history, their connections and distinctions from other works, and seeing the influence of Chinese and Japanese art on the West, rather than delving deeply into the historical background and detailed appreciation of individual paintings. In other words, there is some ‘memorisation for marks’, but it’s still recommended for friends who are interested in the above-mentioned content and want to learn more. Dr Hammers has a style of American humour and is very responsible, but this was her last semester teaching, so it’s unclear which teacher will take over the course in the future.

reviews.content: 喜欢艺术的人会很喜欢的课。如果你对艺术史有兴趣的话切勿错过～就是从这门课上学到了很多艺术流派和知识。一共两个test两个writing assignment，我觉得work load不大，reading也很有意思，页数也不多（很多都是画）。Professor 真的超好！最后A+。但是前提是，一定要真的对这方面的知识感兴趣。
reviews.translated_content: People who like art will really enjoy this course. If you’re interested in art history, don’t miss it~ I learned a lot about art movements and knowledge from this course. There were two tests and two writing assignments in total. I felt the workload wasn’t heavy, the readings were interesting, and they weren’t long (many were just images of paintings). The professor is super nice! I got an A+ in the end. But the prerequisite is that you must genuinely be interested in this area of knowledge.

reviews.content: 超级有趣！从雕塑、文艺复兴到Zen painting都有讲，很inspiring。考试要背pieces的作者和年代挺辛苦的，不过最后给分还不错。
reviews.translated_content: Super interesting! It covers everything from sculpture and the Renaissance to Zen painting, which is very inspiring. Memorising the authors and dates of the pieces for the exam is quite tough, but the final grading was decent.

reviews.content: 对各种画不感兴趣的 分不清流派的 记不住知识点的 RUN！！！
reviews.translated_content: If you’re not interested in various paintings, can’t distinguish between art movements, or can’t remember key points, get out while you can!

reviews.content: wl很小 但如果对艺术不感兴趣 课堂内容就会变得很无聊 老师ppt上没有文字 需要好好听好好做笔记 第一篇paper拿了B test1也是B 最后pf了 可能因为写作能力太差了 tutor总说我有些地方表述不清…对于全国卷英语水平来说 分析一幅画 还是有一定难度 如果擅长写作 擅长背记 热爱艺术就选它！
reviews.translated_content: The workload is small, but if you’re not interested in art, the class content becomes very boring. The teacher’s slides have no text, so you need to listen carefully and take good notes. I got a B on the first paper and a B on Test 1, so I eventually took it on a pass/fail basis. Maybe my writing skills are too poor; the tutor always said my expression was unclear in some places. For someone with a Gaokao-level English background, analyzing a painting is still somewhat challenging. If you’re good at writing, good at memorizing, and love art, go for it!

reviews.content: 对艺术入门生也很好～整体课程难度不高 教授超级可爱
reviews.translated_content: It's also great for beginners in art~ The overall course difficulty is not high, and the professor is super cute.

reviews.content: tutor还蛮严格的 课程很有趣 考试前复习wl较大 其他还行
reviews.translated_content: The tutor is quite strict. The course is interesting. The workload for revision before the exam is heavy, but otherwise it’s fine.

reviews.content: 挺好的课 workload不大
reviews.translated_content: A good course with a light workload.

reviews.content: 唯一难点就是两次quiz之前先写后背各种画儿的名称时代艺术家重要意义。。。写作能力和耐力好会更容易，但暂时是全国卷英语水平也不用害怕，慢慢就上道了（比如我自己 当时以为最多得B哈
reviews.translated_content: The only difficulty is memorising the names, eras, artists, and significance of various paintings before the two quizzes. Good writing skills and endurance make it easier, but don’t be afraid even if your English is only at the national Gaokao level for now; you’ll get the hang of it gradually (for example, I thought I’d get at most a B at the time, haha).

reviews.content: chur 要看180页数 两周一次2hr的10人精致tuto 但是好龟 老师也很好
reviews.translated_content: Demanding: you have to read 180 pages and attend biweekly 2-hour tutorials with only 10 people. But it’s easy to get a good grade, and the teacher is also very nice.

reviews.content: 膜一下A range大佬 但我得分只有B  反正就是 不要选  lecturer都很好 但tutor真的 声音总是颤抖的 让我非常难受 重点是tuto上嘲笑我的发言？ 然后要读一本非常无聊的小说 仿佛是在讲某个少数民族历史 上课随机分组答题 考一些细节 真的记不住 可能是我分到的组友都不太好？大家都不太会 然后随机的分组里面 再合作做一个思维导图 peerevaluation 根本没有criteria可言 唉 不说了 tuto分组的prez也让我非常气 全是free rider 甚至有人剽窃我的创意？全靠我和一个大三semilocal carry  Essay也 是argumentative 给分也不好
reviews.translated_content: Hats off to the A-range experts, but I only got a B. Anyway, do not choose this course. The lecturers are all good, but the tutor really... their voice always trembles, which makes me very uncomfortable. The main issue is that they mocked my comments in the tutorial? Then we had to read a very boring novel that seemed to be about the history of an ethnic minority. In class, we were randomly grouped to answer questions testing details that are really hard to remember. Maybe the group mates I got were not very good? No one really knew the answers. Then, within these random groups, we had to collaborate on a mind map. There were no clear criteria for peer evaluation at all. Sigh, let’s not talk about it. The presentation from the tutorial group also made me very angry; it was full of free riders, and someone even plagiarized my ideas? It was entirely carried by me and a strong third-year semi-local student. The essay was argumentative, and the grading was not good either.

reviews.content: 课程设置非常成熟，靓龟
reviews.translated_content: The course structure is very mature. Generous grading.

reviews.content: 内容覆盖太广了，医学到哲学到艺术等等，虽然都不难但是需要很多讨论。小组作业很多，要是组友不好的话会超级难受。tutorial要发言计分，不过给分挺好的。组友太拉跨所以P了
reviews.translated_content: The content coverage is too broad, ranging from medicine to philosophy to art. Although none of it is difficult, it requires a lot of discussion. There are many group projects; if your teammates are bad, it will be super painful. Tutorials require speaking for participation marks, but the grading is quite good. My teammates were too unreliable, so I took it pass/fail.

reviews.content: wl小 好gra 了解一些哲学和心理学的东西
reviews.translated_content: Light workload, good grading, and you get to understand some philosophy and psychology.

reviews.content: 有很多小作業&pre，比較雜亂，但總體來說wl不大
reviews.translated_content: There are many small assignments and presentations, which can feel a bit disorganized, but overall the workload is not heavy.

reviews.content: 感觉讲的很杂且有点乱，需要小组用artwork展现topic
reviews.translated_content: It feels like the content is quite scattered and a bit messy. Groups need to use artwork to present their topic.

reviews.content: 不同寻常的一个学期，上网课进行的cc，lecture并不算非常有趣，workload比较大，每周的tutorial都要做分享读readings，要读一本书1-12章节做两次小组活动，另外有小组报告需要发挥想象力根据题目进行艺术创作(例如摄影，画画等)并进行小组报告，最后还要交一篇个人的论文。wl大，但tutor人挺好，给的龟也不错，A-
reviews.translated_content: It was an unusual semester with this Common Core course conducted online. The lectures weren’t very interesting, and the workload was heavy. Every week in tutorials, we had to share our reading. We had to read chapters 1–12 of a book and complete two group activities. There was also a group report that required creativity and artistic creation based on the topic (such as photography or drawing), followed by a group presentation. Finally, we had to submit an individual essay. The workload was heavy, but the tutor was nice, and the grading was good. I got an A-.

reviews.content: 还可以，教授是医学院的老师
reviews.translated_content: It’s alright; the professor is from the Faculty of Medicine.

reviews.content: 对理科生超级友好。assessment是attendance和期中期末两次test，都不太难。课水，lecturer十分敷衍，没有reading，几乎没有workload。给分好。
reviews.translated_content: Very friendly to science students. Assessment consists of attendance and two tests (midterm and final), neither of which is too difficult. The course is lightweight, the lecturer is quite perfunctory, there are no readings, and the workload is almost non-existent. Grading is generous.

reviews.content: 课巨水，lec炒鸡无聊，不过tutor感觉很睿智人也好ww几乎无wl，grade不错，只是test的时候提前一两天背很少的内容，gp随便做一下就A了。占分主要是两个test，考的跟上课内容没多少关系主要看个人逻辑严密程度吧，逻辑好反应快的人学起来真的很轻松，反之可能有点点困难。
reviews.translated_content: The course is very lightweight, lectures are super boring, but the tutor seems wise and nice ww. Almost no workload, grades are good. Just memorise a small amount of content a day or two before the tests, and you can get an A with minimal effort on the group project. The grading is mainly based on two tests, which don’t relate much to class content and depend mostly on personal logical rigor. People with good logic and quick reactions find it really easy, while others might find it a bit difficult.

reviews.content: wl小 内容有意思 不难 但是给我上了很有意义的一堂人生课 那就是别人说好龟不等于我能好龟 认真学了 B 没啥好说的了
reviews.translated_content: Low workload, interesting content, not difficult. But it taught me a very meaningful life lesson: just because others say it’s easy to get a good grade doesn’t mean I will get a good grade. I studied seriously and got a B. Nothing more to say.

reviews.content: mid和final都挺難的..很認真看notes也還是有點寫不完  lecture超無聊tutorial也不是很有用。最後B（早知道pf了
reviews.translated_content: Both the midterm and final were quite difficult... Even reading the notes carefully, I still couldn’t finish writing everything. The lectures were super boring, and the tutorials weren’t very useful either. I ended up with a B (I should have taken it pass/fail).

reviews.content: 适合文科生学，上课挺有意思的，wl不大。但grp pre由tutor打分，比较主观玄学且grp pre占30%，被不符合tutor预期的grp pre拉到了A-
reviews.translated_content: Suitable for humanities students. Classes are quite interesting, and the workload isn’t heavy. However, the group presentation is graded by the tutor, which is rather subjective and unpredictable. Since the group presentation accounts for 30%, my grade was pulled down to an A- by a presentation that didn’t meet the tutor’s expectations.

reviews.content: 垃圾一點也不好 速逃不好不好不好
reviews.translated_content: Garbage. Not good at all. Run away. Bad, bad, bad.

reviews.content: 是一门超适合理科生的hu 无敌水 讲的是一些很basic的逻辑之类的 想学到真东西的就绕路吧～总共workload就只有一个midterm，一个final，一个presentation以及attendance，没有任何essay以及reading，presentation的主题都是给定好的不用自己想（爱了）。考试都很简单，考前好好看看ppt记下概念就完事了。整个学期我几乎没有花时间在这个cc上，记attendance的turorial都翘了好几节然后拿了A+，所以说给分真的没谁了！同组的伙伴也都是A range 想水一门cc并且拿好龟的就选它！
reviews.translated_content: This is a humanities elective that is extremely suitable for science students. It’s incredibly lightweight, covering only very basic logic and similar topics. If you want to learn something substantial, look elsewhere. The total workload consists of just one midterm, one final, one presentation, and attendance; there are no essays or readings, and the presentation topics are pre-assigned so you don’t have to come up with them yourself (love that). The exams are very easy; just review the slides carefully and memorise the concepts before the test and you’re done. I barely spent any time on this Common Core course all semester, skipped several tutorials where attendance was taken, and still got an A+. So the grading is truly unmatched! My group mates were also in the A range. If you want an easy Common Core course and a good grade, choose this one!

reviews.content: wl很小，给分也很好，但在转成网课之后教授就没有再出现过，只是tutor post一些ppt上来，没有再学到过任何东西。但overall, 只有一个midterm，final,prez 很不错
reviews.translated_content: The workload is light, and the grading is generous. However, after switching to online classes, the professor never appeared again; the tutor just posted some PowerPoint slides, and I didn’t learn anything new. reviews.content: 并不是传说中那么好🐢。。。本来抱着对建筑感兴趣的想法选的这门课，并且听说好🐢，但实际上跟建筑关系不太大，反而是教你怎么鉴赏图片。lecture作用不大，甚至可以不听不来。。但是有inclass writing的时候还得来。tutorial作用比较大，而且会经常Q到发表看法。 wl一般，有4个inclass writing（一般为20分钟），一个16张照片的photobooth，再用这16张照片做一个视频（3min），最后有一个大的inclass writing（一个半小时），写对4张照片的评价。最后还有一个750字的essay。 最后B+ archi玄学hucc没跑了😩
reviews.translated_content: It wasn't as easy to get a good grade as rumored... I chose this course because I was interested in architecture and heard it was GPA-friendly, but it actually had little to do with architecture; instead, it taught you how to appreciate images. The lectures weren't very useful; you could even skip them. However, you had to attend when there was in-class writing. The tutorials were more useful, and the instructor often called on students to share their views. The workload was average: there were four in-class writings (usually 20 minutes each), a photobooth assignment with 16 photos, a video made using those 16 photos (3 minutes), a final major in-class writing (one and a half hours) evaluating four photos, and finally a 750-word essay. I ended up with a B+. The grading for Architecture Common Core courses is opaque and unpredictable, as expected 😩

reviews.content: 得分B+ Workload：大概每周有一次短essay，200词左右；一次field trip（额好像不算严格field trip?是自己去然后写观感）；一至两次in-class writing；一篇中篇essay，750词左右；没有final但是有final in-class writing。（抱歉很多细节记不太清了，因为是隔了一年来写评论） 刚入学时因为还没打定想选的专业，所以是以按照家里人建议接触下建筑的心态选的这门课（虽然最后的专业完全没有和建筑相关就是了）。Lecture教得不错，教授的口音很好听，讲的内容也比较有意思，但是也许氛围稍嫌平淡所以对本人经常催眠... Tutorial很重要，每节基本都是discussion，对于新生是个很好的锻炼口语的机会。Workload现在看来作为cc有蛮大...而且essay比重巨大，写作苦手可以选择规避。 最后的龟并不好，不过本人写作能力实在差劲所以也没有什么可抱怨的... 而且鉴于最后的专业是计算机工程相关，学到的艺术和建筑内容用不上也就很快忘掉了... 对于崩院新生确实不是个很好的选择吧。不过平心而论，之前仅接触过应试英语的我在上这门课的过程中写作和口语都得到了很好的锻炼，对之后大学生活各个层面都有帮助。总的来说对和我相似的新生并不推荐毕竟烂龟还是不值得，但是写essay很好的人不妨一试。
reviews.translated_content: Grade: B+. Workload: roughly one short essay per week, around 200 words; one field trip (well, maybe not strictly a field trip? It was going on your own and writing up your impressions); one or two in-class writings; one medium-length essay, around 750 words; no final exam, but there was a final in-class writing. (Sorry, I don't remember many details clearly, as I'm writing this review a year later.) When I first enrolled, since I hadn't decided on my major yet, I took this course with the mindset of exploring architecture as suggested by my family (although my eventual major had nothing to do with architecture). The lectures were taught well; the professor's accent was pleasant, and the content was quite interesting, but perhaps the atmosphere was a bit flat, so it often put me to sleep... Tutorials are important; each session is basically discussion, which is a good opportunity for freshmen to practise speaking. Looking back, the workload is quite significant for a Common Core course... Moreover, essays carry huge weight; those who struggle with writing may want to avoid it. The final grade wasn't great, but my writing ability is really poor, so I have little to complain about... Also, given that my final major is related to computer engineering, the art and architecture content I learned was useless to me and quickly forgotten... For freshmen from the Faculty of Engineering, it's indeed not a very good choice. However, to be fair, having previously only been exposed to exam-oriented English, my writing and speaking skills were well exercised during this course, which helped in various aspects of my university life thereafter. Overall, I don't recommend it to freshmen similar to me, after all, harsh grading isn't worth it, but those who are good at writing essays might give it a try.

reviews.content: 教授的口音不错～实际授课内容也许会与你期望的相差有点大，不局限于建筑，但我自认为我学到了不少东西，是理想的“通识教育”了。workload我自认比较大而且种类繁多，从essay到storyboard到video…遇到好的tutor龟会比较好，最后A-。
reviews.translated_content: The professor has a nice accent. The actual teaching content might differ somewhat from your expectations; it’s not limited to architecture, but I feel I learned quite a lot. It’s an ideal “general education” course. I found the workload rather heavy and varied, ranging from essays to storyboards to videos. If you get a good tutor, the grading tends to be favourable. I got an A-.

reviews.content: 烂烂烂
reviews.translated_content: Bad, bad, bad.

reviews.content: 教授英文很好，跟建筑比较有关，但写essay太差PF了
reviews.translated_content: The professor’s English is very good. The course is quite related to architecture, but I wrote my essay so poorly that I took it on a pass/fail basis.

reviews.content: most of the ppl got B+ a quite leng grade course but need to attend all lecture and tutorials
reviews.translated_content: Most people got a B+. It’s a course with favourable grading, but you need to attend all lectures and tutorials.

reviews.content: 课非常有意思，sony讲课真的优美流畅赏心悦目，讲了很多不上这门课很少有机会接触的故事(除非是建院出身) wl个人觉得还是非常小的，每周250字小essay，最后750字中essay，再加上定期的那么几次提前会知道该怎么写inclass writing。 好龟秘诀就是，一定要选taoyiqi的tuto session！！tutor里给分最好的！别的tutor打分好像人均b，甚至c，taoyiqi保你上a哈哈哈
reviews.translated_content: The course is very interesting. Sony’s lectures are truly elegant, fluent, and pleasing to watch. He shares many stories that you rarely get to hear unless you are from the Faculty of Architecture. reviews.content: 与自己上课前想象的非常不同。原以为是一个介绍电影建筑如何建造、cg的运用、实物搭建等等的cc，实际上完全不同，是将不同种类电影分开来讲lecture的cc。lecture可以看出eunice很用心挑选了film clip但是观感并不好，讲得多看得少，感觉很泛泛，没有深入了解。同时，lecture大多选择了老电影或者是不太popular的电影，让人觉得没有太多共鸣。reading很多哲学内容，非常深，但是tutorial并不能讲清楚author到底想说什么，感觉一头雾水。wl较大，作业是写在一个blog上面的，让人觉得比较有趣的是field trip report，reading response很头痛。
reviews.translated_content: It was very different from what I had imagined before taking the class. I originally thought it would be a Common Core course introducing how architectural structures in films are built, the use of CG, physical construction, etc., but it was completely different. It was a Common Core course where lectures were organised by discussing different types of films separately. You could tell that Eunice put a lot of effort into selecting film clips, but the viewing experience wasn’t great; there was more talking than watching, so it felt quite superficial without deep exploration. Also, the lectures mostly featured old or less popular films, which made it hard to relate. There was a lot of reading, much of it philosophical and very deep, but the tutorials didn’t clarify what the authors actually meant, leaving me confused. The workload was heavy. Assignments were posted on a blog; the field trip report was interesting, but the reading responses were a headache.

reviews.content: 没那么好龟 最后认真做了只拿了B 课程内容太抽象了

reviews.content: 教授人很nice，每节tutorial是讲解reading。期中期末两个作业分别需要独自一次field trip，期末需要独自完成一个2min的video，workload有点大。平时workload小。兴趣比较重要吧～

reviews.instructor: Prof. William Wong; TA: Rachel Heung
reviews.content: I chose this course because I found it interesting but the group project ended up making me want to pull my hair out. You work a lot with your group and the group project makes up most of your grade. Try to join this CC with friends because you have no guarantee you will like your tutorial classmates. The lectures were alright. Some guest lecturers were boring but others were deeply touching. That being said, I stopped attending lectures after a few weeks because they didn't take attendance. The tutorials were quite fun. They were mostly group projects and discussions. The TA was great at engaging with students and prompting them for more information. She is very sweet. However, note that she grades low. Do not panic if you keep getting major deductions. She's just like that. I got a 10/15 on my reflective journal and mediocre scores for the group projects but got an A- in the end. Try to consult her on your assessments before submitting just to make sure it fulfills her standards. It's hard to know what she wants sometimes. Also, as mentioned in other reviews, she is a bit biased towards students who participate a lot. So in tutorials, speak as much as you can to make her like you. This is not a leng course by any means. It seems that a lot of students get B range, so if you pick this course, make sure you're ok with the possibility of that. I regret taking this course because I was so stressed about the group project and I was worried that I would get B range because of my scores. Because of that, it is hard for me to recommend. But if you are truly interested in this course and don't have a GPA requirement, then sure, why not.

reviews.translated_content: Don't take this Common Core course. The TA is very shallow and biased.

reviews.translated_content: The workload is moderate—not big, but not small either. However, I think the grading is quite poor; I got a B-.

reviews.content: tutor人特别好，课程内容有趣，讨论氛围极好，对话题有兴趣的同学应该会感到很吸引人，给分虽然没有预期好但是学习过程很愉快
reviews.translated_content: The tutor is very nice, the course content is interesting, and the discussion atmosphere is excellent. Students who are interested in the topics will likely find it very appealing. Although the grading was not as good as I expected, the learning process was very enjoyable.

reviews.content: 这个ta完全乱来的，言之无物，非常有偏见，一定要组好队去这个cc，不然你就分到一些陌生的女local们，啥都不干事就我来干。会说粤语比较好，groupmate基本都是local。内容还算有趣，老师会告诉你课的安排，想去就去没attendance。除非你对这个很有兴趣
reviews.translated_content: This TA is completely all over the place, speaks without substance, and is very biased. You must form a good team for this Common Core course; otherwise, you’ll be grouped with some local Hong Kong female students you don’t know who do nothing while you do all the work. It helps if you speak Cantonese, as groupmates are mostly locals. The content is fairly interesting. The teacher outlines the course schedule; attendance is optional, so go if you want to. Only take it if you are genuinely interested in the topic.

reviews.content: 内容有意思 但不一定好grade哦
reviews.translated_content: The content is interesting, but it’s not necessarily easy to get a good grade.

reviews.content: 課程的設置挺有意思的，涉及性別定型、LGBT以至於性工作者等議題，要求我們看的電影《喜宴》也很精彩。我是2020年sem2上的這門課，因為那時候突然改成了online mode, 所以group project被取消，只要求寫4篇800字-1000字的reflective journal,每篇佔總成績20%，workload非常小。但是因為今年workload小，所以大家的grade好像普遍比較低。我的journal每次收到的評論都很好，但是最後出來的grade並沒有想象中好。
reviews.translated_content: The course design is quite interesting, covering topics such as gender stereotypes, LGBT issues, and even sex workers. The required film, The Wedding Banquet, is also excellent. I took this course in Sem 2 of 2020. Because it suddenly switched to online mode, the group project was cancelled. We were only required to write four reflective journals of 800–1000 words each, with each journal worth 20% of the total grade, so the workload was very light. However, because the workload was light that year, everyone’s grades seem to have been generally lower. Although the feedback on my journals was always very good, the final grade I received was not as good as I had expected.

reviews.content: 感觉group pro很重要 基本上就看你group pro做的怎样
reviews.translated_content: I feel the group project is very important; basically, it all depends on how well your group project is done.

reviews.content: 課的内容還是比較有趣的，有種打開新世界的大門的感覺。Lecture有介紹性工作者，性疾病（STI），跟sexuality有關的女性電影，LGBTQ，還有一節課請來了一位Transgender教授。每節課可能都會有不同的教授講課，教課的風格也不一，有時候會比較枯燥（上到六點半結束的時候人已經少了一半），有時候會偏向于快樂討論的氣氛。Tutorial上每個人基本上都會發言，另外這個學期只有一位tutor。 這門課要求寫兩篇reflective journal——幾個問題，挑一回答。個人認爲題目還是挺啓發思考的，但是很多題目又是緊密跟Hong Kong聯係在一起，作爲初來HK的人在這樣的問題上會有劣勢，因此供選擇的問題還是挺少的。兩篇journal的分數不會被公開。 還有就是gp，做一個跟sexuality有關的網站。網站製作還是比較簡單的，但是想到好的主題比較難。 最後B+（個人認爲爛龜，大膽發言——與我的付出不成正比！）沒有任何一項assessment分數是公開的，這個分數就給的莫名其妙，讓人摸不着頭腦。不過平心而論，這門課還是學到挺多東西的，可以當作一種獨特的體驗（對於内地生裏想要瞭解更多關於LGBTQ知識的人來説）。
reviews.translated_content: The course content is quite interesting; it feels like opening a door to a new world. Lectures cover sex workers, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), films about female sexuality, LGBTQ issues, and one session even invited a transgender professor. Different professors may teach each class, so teaching styles vary. Sometimes it’s rather dull (by the time class ends at 6:30 pm, half the students are gone), and other times the atmosphere leans toward lively discussion. In tutorials, basically everyone speaks, and this semester there was only one tutor.  The course requires two reflective journals—answer one question from a set. I think the prompts are quite thought-provoking, but many are closely tied to Hong Kong. As someone new to HK, you’re at a disadvantage on these topics, so there aren’t many choices. The marks for the two journals are not released.  Then there’s the group project: create a website related to sexuality. Building the site is relatively simple, but coming up with a good theme is difficult.  I ended up with a B+ (I think the grading was harsh, bold statement—it wasn’t proportional to my effort!). None of the assessment marks are released, so this grade was given inexplicably, leaving people confused. That said, honestly, I did learn quite a lot from this course. It can be seen as a unique experience (especially for students from Mainland China who want to learn more about LGBTQ issues).

reviews.content: 別選 這裏的人卷得很 presentation 就像坐牢 你不會鬥得過那些卷賊
reviews.translated_content: Don’t choose this. The people here are intensely competitive. The presentations feel like a prison sentence. You won’t be able to compete against those hyper-competitive students.

reviews.content: 内容很充实，但是教授是那种学术十分严谨然后要求比较高的那种，虽然上课的人不多，感觉都是写大三大四的大佬，A range有点难。
reviews.translated_content: The content is very substantial, but the professor is the type who is extremely rigorous academically and has high requirements. Although attendance was low, it felt like most students were strong third- or fourth-year students, making A-range grades somewhat difficult.

reviews.content: 教授Cecilia Chu非常博学，布置的reading都很有启发性，TA们也都很热心，回复很快。课程内容方面，涉及到城市历史和规划的方方面面，非常全面详尽，推荐！
reviews.translated_content: Professor Cecilia Chu is very knowledgeable, and the assigned readings are very inspiring. The TAs are also very helpful and reply quickly. In terms of content, the course covers all aspects of urban history and planning, very comprehensively and in detail. Recommended!

reviews.content: 课程设计很好，虽然有时候会有点无聊（linda教授语气语调好催眠），但每个话题还有配的reading细看会觉得很有启发。两个assessment一个是weekly journal记录对每周内容的想法，另一个是小学生作文（（（报这门课初衷是希望以后旅游到新城市可以多些欣赏角度。这个初衷有没有实现还不知道，但它确实帮我欣赏到以前和现在待过的熟悉的城市的各种美（客观+主观）journal和小学生作文写得也挺开心。唯一就是全程从tutor那得到的评价让我以为A range稳了结果最后B+（流汗黄豆）（头顶蓝色光环微笑）对自己很有信心或者没那么看重龟的推荐来读（如果感兴趣）
reviews.translated_content: The course design is good. Although it can be a bit boring at times (Prof. Linda’s tone and intonation are very hypnotic), if you read carefully, each topic and its accompanying readings are quite inspiring. There are two assessments: one is a weekly journal recording your thoughts on the weekly content, and the other is like a primary-school essay (((). My original intention for taking this course was to gain more perspectives for appreciating new cities when travelling in the future. I don’t know yet whether that intention was fulfilled, but it did help me appreciate the various beauties (objective + subjective) of familiar cities where I have lived before and now. I quite enjoyed writing the journal and the primary-school-style essay. The only issue is that the feedback I received from the tutor throughout the course made me think an A-range grade was secure, but I ended up with a B+ (sweat emoji) (blue halo smiley). Recommended for those who are confident in themselves or don’t care too much about grades (if you are interested).

reviews.content: 换prof了 烂grade 两个作业都是在lecture表扬的 最后才B+。。。并且从不出分。。。
reviews.translated_content: They changed professors. The grading is poor. Both assignments were praised in the lecture, yet I only got a B+ in the end... And grades are never released...

reviews.content: Workload 不大
reviews.translated_content: Workload is not heavy.

reviews.content: 很不错
reviews.translated_content: Very good.

reviews.content: 有一点点难度，wl总体不是很大，每周按时写完assignment就还好
reviews.translated_content: It’s slightly difficult. The overall workload isn’t very heavy; it’s manageable if you complete the weekly assignments on time.
