reviews.content: 好课，绝对好课，认识20人，没一个比C高的
reviews.translated_content: Great course, absolutely great. I got to know 20 people, and not one of them ended up with a grade lower than a C.

reviews.content: 没有音乐基础也没关系，workload小，只要每节课认真记笔记quiz没问题，教授超好多找他改concert report就没问题，gp占比50%，改革做网页prez，tutorial内随机分组队友还是很重要的，但好像gp大家差的不会太多，总体非常推荐！
reviews.translated_content: It’s fine even without a music background. The workload is light. As long as you take careful notes in every class, the quizzes are no problem. The professor is super nice; if you ask him to revise your concert report, it’ll be fine. The group project accounts for 50%. For the reform project, we did a web presentation. Random grouping in tutorials means teammates are quite important, but it seems the group project marks didn’t vary much among groups. Overall, highly recommended!

reviews.content: 很后悔没有pf，自认平时认真听课，讨论也要发言，workload觉得较大，每周都有journal，我的journal得分较低，可能不擅长文字分析吧，期末有一个做网页的gp，我觉得我们组gp做挺好没选pf，现在就是非常后悔。课内容主要是古典音乐的再创新之类的。一般有趣，个人觉得给龟不合理。如果写作，分析，不好的建议慎选
reviews.translated_content: I really regret not taking it pass/fail. I considered myself attentive in class and participated in discussions, but I found the workload quite heavy, with a journal due every week. My journal scores were low, perhaps because I’m not good at textual analysis. There was a group project involving website creation at the end. I thought our group did well on the GP, so I didn’t choose pass/fail, and now I deeply regret it. The course content is mainly about reinventing classical music and the like. It’s moderately interesting. Personally, I feel the grading was unreasonable. If your writing and analysis skills are weak, I’d advise choosing with caution.

reviews.content:
写journal写到崩溃跑来给评价劝退各位的，
首先说教学风格的问题，ppt不发没有recording但是在journal里面又要求必须结合课堂例子，本人必须每节课把所有ppt拍下来才行；然后课程设置的问题，八篇journal每篇起码五百字，约等于一篇essay了，实际的wl并不小，且给分非常主观，完全视乎能否符合教授和助教对于课程的见解；加上tutorial必须出席且以发言次数与质量记分，过程很紧促急迫，氛围难受；group project做网页，随机在tutorial里挑选队友，freerider的概率就会大大上升，最好要自带队友入场如果一定要选；但是教授本人还是回复email很快，乐于回答问题。
建议就是，如果不是一定要选就别选，课程内容跟古典乐实际关系不大，都是一些新奇的古典乐例子（4‘33’‘之类的）和环保经济文化性别平等等等的话题，预期接触的经典古典乐频率高（时常提及贝多芬）但没有深入。
reviews.translated_content: I’m writing this review to warn others after breaking down from writing journals. First, regarding the teaching style: slides aren’t distributed and there are no recordings, yet the journals require you to incorporate examples from class, so I had to photograph all the slides in every lecture. Then, regarding the course structure: eight journals, each at least 500 words, which is essentially equivalent to an essay. The actual workload isn’t small, and the grading is highly subjective, depending entirely on whether your views align with those of the professor and TAs. On top of that, tutorial attendance is mandatory, and participation is graded based on the frequency and quality of your contributions. The pace is tight and rushed, creating an uncomfortable atmosphere. The group project involves building a website, and teammates are randomly selected in tutorials, which greatly increases the chance of getting free riders. It’s best to bring your own teammates if you must take this course. However, the professor does reply to emails quickly and is willing to answer questions. My advice is: unless you absolutely have to take it, don’t. The course content isn’t closely related to classical music itself; it mostly covers novel classical music examples (like 4'33'') and topics such as environmental protection, economics, culture, and gender equality. While classic composers like Beethoven are mentioned frequently, there is no in-depth exploration.

reviews.content: 好课，我有几个同学都在这上，分数都挺高的。绝世好课！瞿旎𪐎𣮰
reviews.translated_content: Great course. Several of my classmates took it, and their grades were quite high. An absolutely fantastic course!

reviews.content: 绝世烂课，整个课完全在结构传统音乐，拆的七零八落。体验非常差劲，古典爱好者一定不要上这门课。由于本学期网课所以没有quiz但是每周（几乎）都要写一个report，类似于reflection。老师评分标准浮动巨大，且无意义。最后group project是做网站，workload巨大但是结课早。整个课特别重视critical thinking，但是你认为的critical和老师认为的不一样，导致你所有东西都烂掉。pf了所以不知道龟，但是普遍反应龟巨烂。建议取消这个课。
reviews.translated_content: An absolutely terrible course. The entire class completely deconstructs traditional music, tearing it into pieces. The experience was very poor; classical music lovers must avoid this course. Since it was online this semester, there were no quizzes, but we had to write a report (similar to a reflection) almost every week. The teacher’s grading criteria fluctuated hugely and were meaningless. The final group project was to build a website; the workload was huge, but the course ended early. The course places great emphasis on critical thinking, but what you consider critical differs from what the teacher considers critical, causing everything you do to fall apart. I took it pass/fail, so I don’t know about the grade distribution, but the general consensus is that the grading is extremely harsh. I suggest cancelling this course.

reviews.content: 18-19sem2上的，网课之后好像变了。占比最大的group project是用Google Site做一个网页，tutor在同一个tutorial里帮你随机组队，主题就是这门课的标题，讲述人/组织/活动等在对reinventing classical music这件事情上做了什么。当时是只能选择在hk范围内的，不过可以选择的角度还是很多的。大概率要去采访之类的，去联系相关的人，想拿高分只靠网上的二手信息是不太可能的。然后就是有一篇音乐会感想，去找过lecturer修改但还是不太懂他想要的点。 还有就是随堂测试和tutorial participation，随堂考了六七次吧，说会取最高的五次，考前面一两节课的内容。tutorial就上过三四次，看材料，然后上课再给看一些资料，然后一起讨论，后面几次tutorial都是在和tutor聊project。总体wl不算很大吧（可能做网页会觉得有点累），最后成绩听天由命。最重要的一点，最好对古典音乐感兴趣，不然真的会听不进去lecture，而且上课要记笔记，留给随堂测试复习。笔记对project没什么用，对音乐会感想可能会有一点用。
reviews.translated_content: I took this in Sem 2 of 2018–19; it seems to have changed since moving to online classes. The largest component is a group project where you build a webpage using Google Sites. The tutor randomly assigns groups within the same tutorial. The theme is the course title itself: explaining what a person, organization, or event has done to 'reinvent classical music.' At the time, we could only choose subjects within Hong Kong, but there were still many angles to explore. You’ll likely need to conduct interviews and contact relevant people; it’s unlikely you can get a high score relying solely on second-hand information online. Then there’s a concert reflection paper. I asked the lecturer for feedback but still didn’t quite grasp what he was looking for. There are also in-class quizzes and tutorial participation. We had about six or seven quizzes, with the best five counting; they cover material from the previous one or two lectures. I attended only three or four tutorials, where we reviewed materials, looked at additional resources in class, and discussed them. The later tutorials were mostly spent discussing the project with the tutor. Overall, the workload isn’t too heavy (though building the website might feel a bit tiring), and the final grade is largely up to fate. Most importantly, you’d better be interested in classical music; otherwise, you really won’t be able to focus during the lectures. Also, you need to take notes in class to review for the quizzes. The notes aren’t very useful for the project, but might help a little with the concert reflection.

reviews.content: 良心好课！ 首先workooad很小，期中一篇concert review，期末一个group project,平时有些小quiz,认真听lecture就没问题 把音乐作为艺术现象探讨其与其他艺术门类的联系，从社会意义的角度来看音乐的创作传播和创新 干货多内容有趣  而且好🐢
reviews.translated_content: A genuinely worthwhile course! First, the workload is light: a concert review for the midterm, a group project for the final, and some small quizzes during the term. As long as you listen carefully in lectures, you’ll be fine. It explores music as an artistic phenomenon, examining its connections with other art forms, and looks at the creation, dissemination, and innovation of music from a social perspective. The content is substantive and interesting, plus grading is generous.

reviews.content: 总体来说是很好的课！从头到尾都很有趣也很impressive 围绕classical music讲了很多内容 很有意义 课的内容非常好 教授和tutor人都很好 有quiz但是只要听课了就会做（不需要背书）对attendance的要求基本上是100%  report可以去找教授改 他还因为没及时回复邮件给我延迟了交report的ddl workload不大 就是占比50%的gp评分比较严格 认识的人大多数gp评分都不高 最后B+ 总体来说还是推荐！
reviews.translated_content: Overall, it’s a very good course! It was interesting and impressive from start to finish. It covered a lot of content around classical music and was very meaningful. The course content was excellent, and the professor and tutor were both very nice. There are quizzes, but if you attend class, you can do them (no need to memorize). Attendance requirements are basically 100%. You can ask the professor to review your report; he even extended my report deadline because he didn’t reply to my email in time. The workload isn’t heavy, but the grading for the group project, which accounts for 50%, is quite strict. Most people I know didn’t get high marks for the group project. I finished with a B+. Overall, still recommended!

reviews.content: 本人冲着喜欢古典音乐选的。课内容和想象的完全不一样，出了介绍几个现代音乐家之外，大部分都环绕着所谓的big issues。虽然个人喜欢写essay，但是每周写一篇500字journal还是挺考脑筋的，写到最后有点被掏空的感觉。journal每篇才5分，8篇加起来就是40分。journal的给分很悬，有时认为自己写得还不错的时候就拿个4分; 认为写的一般的时候就4.5分，5分。而且只能写8篇不能多写。journal虽然没有题目但是还很容易离题，本人第一篇就离题拿了3分，后来发邮件问tutor后被加了1分。tutor人很友善，有什么问题能直接发邮件问她。reading不多，几周一篇，tutorial discussion积极回答应该不是问题。个人认为最有问题的是final project，不知道他们到底要什么，队友也特别重要，反正很容易被坑。最后龟为b，全因为final project拿了c。
reviews.translated_content: I enrolled because I like classical music. The course content was completely different from what I imagined; apart from introducing a few modern musicians, it mostly revolved around so-called “big issues.” Although I personally enjoy writing essays, writing a 500-word journal every week was quite mentally taxing, and I felt drained by the end. Each journal was worth only 5 marks, but eight of them added up to 40%. The grading for journals was unpredictable: sometimes I thought I had written well and got 4 marks; other times I thought my work was average and got 4.5 or 5. You could only submit eight journals, no more. Although there were no specific topics, it was easy to go off-topic. I went off-topic in my first journal and got 3 marks, but after emailing the tutor, I received 1 extra mark. The tutor was very friendly, and you could email her directly with any questions. There wasn’t much reading, just one article every few weeks, and actively participating in tutorial discussions shouldn’t be a problem. In my opinion, the biggest issue was the final project. It was unclear what they wanted, and having good teammates was crucial; otherwise, you could easily get screwed. My final grade was a B, entirely because I got a C on the final project.

reviews.content:
Amit口语很流利，这门课他开了因该有将近十年了，课程体系安排的还是比较好的。

我是大一sem1选的这门课，因为之前就对哲学感兴趣，讲的东西也基本有浅浅了解或者听说过，所以没有觉得有什么难度。tutorial的密度也不是很高。建议tutorial能选上午的就选上午的，因为只有tim一个tutor他讲到下午就特别累，可能听课体验感会下降一点。

一、评分构成
1.两次lecture response
2.一个argument analysis
3.一个newsreport（300字之内）
4.一个final essay（1000字之内）
5.一个midterm（都是选择题）（感觉只要上课听一下或者看一下reading就OK，我复习了一个半小时的lecturenote最后25道题错2道，折百分比后14%/15%）
个人觉得作业量特别合适，正好能巩固一下学的东西，还省去了做group project各种分工协调浪费掉的时间精力。

二、涉及内容
1.adp的lecture很水，讲一下课程构成
2.week2 笛卡尔 阅读材料是沉思录的节选。自己看不懂没关系，上课会带着分析。
3. reductionlism/functionlism/physicalism等概念的串讲。amit讲的挺有意思的，不会觉得枯燥。
4.各种AI的话题。
5.freewill
6.personal identity
7. extended mind
reviews.translated_content: Amit speaks very fluently. He has probably been offering this course for nearly ten years, and the curriculum is quite well structured. I took this course in my first semester of Year 1. Since I was already interested in philosophy and had a basic understanding or had heard of most of the topics, I did not find it difficult. The tutorial sessions were not very frequent. I recommend choosing a morning tutorial slot if possible, because Tim, the only tutor, gets particularly tired by the afternoon, which might slightly lower the quality of the learning experience. 1. Grading components: 1) Two lecture responses; 2) One argument analysis; 3) One news report (under 300 words); 4) One final essay (under 1000 words); 5) One midterm (all multiple-choice questions). I felt that just listening in class or doing the readings was enough. I reviewed my lecture notes for one and a half hours, got 2 out of 25 questions wrong, which translated to about 14–15% of the total grade. Personally, I found the workload very appropriate; it helped consolidate what I learned and saved the time and energy wasted on coordinating group projects. 2. Content covered: 1) The lecture during the add/drop period was quite lightweight, mainly outlining the course structure. 2) Week 2: Descartes. The reading was an excerpt from Meditations. It does not matter if you cannot understand it on your own; the professor will guide you through the analysis in class. 3) A connected explanation of concepts such as reductionism, functionalism, and physicalism. Amit’s lectures were interesting and not boring. 4) Various AI-related topics. 5) Free will. 6) Personal identity. 7) Extended mind.

reviews.content: 先聲明，我是思維方式偏文科的理科生 （生物/生命科學綜合類專業），對哲學有興趣；我剛好CCHU9051 跟 CCHU9052 都上過。兩門課都是哲學類的，但是前者注重探討「人為何以及如何有思維？」「人究竟有無自由思維？？」，主意從科學跟哲學的角度去思辨。後者比較探討是「人生中怎樣才幸福？」。就老師講課跟給的材料的深度而言，我覺得91的思辨跟深度遠比92强，個人認為老師還蠻會引導的。51的reading 量不算多 （比52少不少，也比較定時定量不會忽多忽少，通常一週一兩篇，共10＋頁PDF左右的程度）。但是論文還是92好寫很多，個人認為91很挑戰辯論本事，我當初想破頭，寫地蠻抓狂，但是成績不是特別好。我屬於在意學習過程的人，所以分數對我是其次，我覺得51很值得。但若是想輕鬆點拿高分，CCHU9051可能不會特別容易。
reviews.translated_content: First, a disclaimer: I am a science student (biology/life sciences) with a humanities-oriented mindset and an interest in philosophy. I happened to take both CCHU9051 and CCHU9052. Both are philosophy courses, but the former focuses on exploring “Why and how do humans think?” and “Do humans truly have free will?”, approaching these questions through scientific and philosophical reasoning. The latter explores “What makes life happy?”. In terms of the depth of lectures and materials, I feel the critical thinking and depth in 9051 are far stronger than in 9052. Personally, I think the teacher is quite good at guiding us. The reading load for 9051 isn’t heavy (much less than 9052, and fairly consistent rather than fluctuating; usually one or two articles per week, totaling around 10+ pages of PDF). However, the essay for 9052 was much easier to write. I think 9051 really challenges your debating skills; I racked my brain and wrote frantically, but my grade wasn’t particularly good. I care more about the learning process, so grades are secondary to me. I think 9051 is very worthwhile. But if you want to relax and get high marks easily, CCHU9051 might not be particularly easy.

reviews.content: absolutely loved this course! really just broadened my mind (or brain whatever) and now I have started questioning literally everything. The instructor and tutor are very supportive and kind (i glaze the prof). I used to wait the whole lecture just for the after-class discussions. The classes were really interactive and entertaining and I also got good grades. dont take it if you dont consider urself to be a philosophy person. However, if you read or question stuff around you even a little bit, this course is just perfect to gain knowledge from all aspects and may lead to a happy life

reviews.content: Lecturer人非常好，课题也都很有意思，对于想入门哲学的人来说也很实用。assignment比较细碎比较多，但是总体来说并不是很难做（难高分吧，感觉需要一点哲学的灵性）。tutor人不错，但是说话很mean给人很大压力，tutorial也非常耗脑子，需要花比较多时间准备，也需要聆听同学说的话做出回应（同学问的问题tutor会直接丢给其他同学回答，最后才会讲自己的见解）。很适合喜欢思考的人，想摸鱼的别去。我已经对哲学是挺有兴趣的了，自认为也有一些哲学的思维，但是写assignment时辩论属实把我弄不会了，最后还是只有B+。但是想学东西的话是非常建议去的，上lecture也很relax。
reviews.translated_content: The lecturer is very nice, and the topics are all quite interesting. It’s also practical for those who want an introduction to philosophy. The assignments are quite fragmented and numerous, but overall they aren’t very difficult to complete (though getting a high grade is hard; I feel it requires a bit of philosophical intuition). The tutor is nice, but speaks quite meanly, which creates a lot of pressure. The tutorials are also very mentally draining; they require considerable preparation time, and you need to listen to your classmates’ comments and respond (the tutor will often throw questions asked by students back to other students to answer, only sharing their own insights at the end). It’s very suitable for people who enjoy thinking; if you want to coast, don’t take it. I was already quite interested in philosophy and consider myself to have some philosophical thinking, but the argumentation in the assignments really threw me off. In the end, I only got a B+. However, if you want to learn something, I highly recommend taking it. Attending lectures is also quite relaxing.

reviews.content:
这个课程安排挺好的，lecture不强制去，但是感兴趣的人会对其特别感兴趣，lecturer和tutor上这个课上了快十年了，很有经验，而且人也很nice。个人感觉tutorial相比lecture无聊，but tutorial takes attendance and participation，多参与讨论和回答问题才有更高分。这个课要以兴趣为主导，如果对哲学方面，如对人的思维形成、ai有没有思维、以及人生观方面很有兴趣的同学可以选报，课程总体算是瑕不掩瑜。
此外，assignment在cc里面算是很大量的: 2 lecture responses (1 for any one lecture from lec 3-6, the other for any one from lec 7-12), 1 news report, 1 final essay. Good news is no group project, but bad news is there is also a mid-term quiz , which did not provide any notes for us and you need to review yourself.
最后一点，如果是追求grade的同学或许不用考虑这个课程，因为tutor亲自和我们说的是A range no more than 15% of total candidates，所以除非真的很感兴趣且准备真的用功在此，否则在这里想争A range是不太现实的。
reviews.translated_content: The course structure is quite good. Lecture attendance isn’t mandatory, but those who are interested will find it particularly engaging. The lecturer and tutor have been teaching this course for nearly ten years; they’re very experienced and nice. Personally, I found the tutorials more boring than the lectures, but tutorial attendance and participation are taken into account. You’ll get higher marks if you participate more in discussions and answer questions. This course should be driven by interest. Students who are keen on philosophy—such as how human thinking forms, whether AI has consciousness, and perspectives on life—can consider enrolling. Overall, the pros outweigh the cons.  In addition, the assignment load is quite heavy for a Common Core course: two lecture responses (one from Lectures 3–6 and one from Lectures 7–12), one news report, and one final essay. The good news is there’s no group project, but the bad news is there’s also a midterm quiz, for which no notes were provided, so you need to review on your own.  Lastly, if you’re chasing grades, you might want to skip this course. The tutor told us directly that no more than 15% of the total cohort would receive an A-range grade. So unless you’re genuinely interested and prepared to put in real effort, aiming for an A range here isn’t very realistic.

reviews.content: lecture和内容都好有趣，没有gp，没有final exam。tutorial积极发言就好，我本人不是很擅长哲学写作，所以essay，reflection都不是特别好。不过可以当做哲学基础课，老师讲的真的很好，也可以从专业的角度了解哲学学习。个人觉得workload还可以，ddl很灵活（可以选），分散开觉得还好。
reviews.translated_content: The lectures and content are very interesting. There is no group project and no final exam. Just participate actively in tutorials. I’m not very good at philosophical writing, so my essay and reflection weren’t particularly strong. However, it can serve as a foundational philosophy course; the instructor teaches really well and provides a professional perspective on studying philosophy. Personally, I found the workload manageable. The deadlines are flexible (you can choose them), so spreading them out makes it feel okay.

reviews.content: 主题：主要讨论有趣且不晦涩的哲学话题，其中我自己印象最深的是“Do we love for reasons”。因为哲学没有绝对正确的答案，所以不管是写essay还是tutorial discussion的自由度都很高。 Workload：适中，主要是文字输出，没有prez和gp！！！一个学期一共要写5篇400words左右的小essay，期末写一篇1500words左右的essay。Lecture participation就是每节课要以纸笔形式回答一个小问题（结合自己的想法回答，没有标准答案，主要是为下一节lecture做铺垫）；Tutorial participation主要是大家围绕reading的内容进行讨论。 Prof & Tutor：Prof Chan超级nice，在介绍哲学理论的同时会结合一些生活中的例子，所以听起来不会觉得晕或者无聊， 课堂氛围挺轻松欢快的；Tutor建议选Natalie（如果她还教这门课的话），人美心善给分好！最后得分A
reviews.translated_content: Topic: Mainly discusses interesting and accessible philosophical topics. The one that impressed me most was “Do we love for reasons”. Since philosophy has no absolutely correct answers, there is a high degree of freedom in both essay writing and tutorial discussions. Workload: Moderate, mainly involving written output. No presentations and no group projects!!! In one semester, you have to write five short essays of around 400 words each, and one essay of around 1500 words for the final. Lecture participation involves answering a small question in pen and paper in every class (answer based on your own thoughts; there is no standard answer; it mainly sets the stage for the next lecture). Tutorial participation mainly involves everyone discussing the reading content. Prof & Tutor: Prof Chan is super nice. He combines philosophical theories with examples from daily life, so it doesn’t feel dizzying or boring. The classroom atmosphere is quite relaxed and cheerful. For tutors, I recommend choosing Natalie (if she is still teaching this course). She is beautiful, kind-hearted, and grades generously! I got an A in the end.

reviews.content: This is my favourite course among all the CC that I have selected!   Workload  1. Three sentences responding to the lectures  2. Short essays (Around 500 words) (After each lectures)  3. Final essay (Around 1,500 words) (Choose from a range of assigned questions)   Tutorial  Disucssion based on the pre-assigned questions based on the readings

reviews.content: 之前被课程的名字吸引去上的，讲授的内容大抵也和哲学相关。workload挺大的，基本每周都有的tutorial需要提前阅读两篇小长文章，但是收获也很多。不建议yr1选，因为还不太会写essay可能会拿不到好🐢
reviews.translated_content: I was attracted by the course name and enrolled. The content taught is largely related to philosophy. The workload is quite heavy; basically, every tutorial requires reading two short-but-long articles in advance, but I gained a lot. I do not recommend Year 1 students take it, as you may not yet know how to write essays well and might not get a good grade.

reviews.content: 这门课就是与人生有关的哲学问题的讨论，对哲学感兴趣的同学推荐选。Lecture 中能激起辩论的内容还是非常有趣的（比如hedonism），有一些内容听了有一点点boring（比如virtue）。Prof. Chan 和 tutor Natalie都非常友善，去上face to face下课还跟我们聊天讨论。Natalie 和 Zheng还在课程结束后自己组织了自愿的读书会，真的非常用心。但是对于阅读和写作的要求还是很高的，workload我个人感觉适中偏大，给的哲学reading确实没那么容易看，但我觉得也不至于晦涩，如果自认为有很强的思辨能力推荐选。大一一上来就选了这个CC拿了B+我觉得还可以。
reviews.translated_content: This course discusses philosophical questions related to life. I recommend it to students interested in philosophy. The parts of the lecture that spark debate are very interesting (e.g., hedonism), though some content is a bit boring (e.g., virtue). Prof. Chan and tutor Natalie are both very friendly; they even chatted and discussed with us after face-to-face classes. Natalie and Zheng also organized voluntary reading groups after the course ended, which shows they really put their heart into it. However, the requirements for reading and writing are quite high. I feel the workload is moderate to heavy. The assigned philosophical readings aren’t exactly easy, but I don’t think they’re overly obscure either. I recommend this course if you believe you have strong critical thinking skills. I took this Common Core course in my first year and got a B+, which I think is acceptable.

course_info.title: Contested Words, Disputed Symbols
course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: wl挺小的，只需要寫一篇essay 和grp project。但是lecture是真的無聊且聽不懂。不過上完tutorial就會稍微懂一點。prof Sinead人很好，tutor 人也很好。grp project outline Sinead 給分很慷慨，我看好像很多組都是A range。但最終的presentation 我只有B-，最後拉出來最終的🐢就是B+
reviews.translated_content: The workload is quite light; you only need to write one essay and complete a group project. However, the lectures are truly boring and hard to understand. You’ll understand a bit more after attending the tutorials. Prof Sinead is very nice, and the tutor is also very nice. Sinead grades the group project outline generously; it seems many groups got an A-range grade. But I only got a B- for the final presentation, which pulled my final grade down to a B+.

reviews.content: 课程内容有点难，essay和presentation给分都不太好，很难拿高分
reviews.translated_content: The course content is a bit difficult. The grading for the essay and presentation is not very good; it is hard to get high scores.

reviews.content: 每周教授会把他录好的课的音频放在moodle上，自己找时间去听就行了，没有attendance之类的要求。wl很小，有四份500字以内的quiz，难度很低，教授会写明你要完成这份作业需要读的reading，基本上读完reading就能答好。而且我很喜欢的是tutor改的很认真，看她们的评注能感觉到她们批改时的想法和感情，有时甚至像在跟她们对话。占比最大的最后的essay，没有格式要求，字数要求好像是1200，反正wl特别小。但我好想看我最后一篇essay的评语啊，为什么这个不放出来！
reviews.translated_content: Every week, the professor uploads audio recordings of his lectures to Moodle; you can listen whenever you have time. There are no attendance requirements. The workload is very light: there are four quizzes, each under 500 words, and they are very easy. The professor clearly lists the required readings for each assignment, and basically, if you finish the readings, you can answer the questions well. What I really like is that the tutors grade very carefully. Reading their comments, I could sense their thoughts and feelings while marking; sometimes it even felt like I was having a conversation with them. The final essay carries the most weight. There are no formatting requirements, and the word count seems to be around 1,200. Anyway, the workload is extremely small. But I really wish I could see the feedback on my last essay—why isn’t it released!

reviews.content: 老师人很好，workload很小，不用听课，只要quiz和最后一篇小论文写好就行。
reviews.translated_content: The instructor is very nice, the workload is light. You don’t need to attend lectures; just do well on the quizzes and the final short essay.

reviews.content: 每节lecture最后有手写小quiz，考当堂课的内容。tutorial要签到并记发言participation，好好读reading吧。最后期末有一次presentation 和一个term project（essay video podcast据说是啥都可以），可以个人也可以合作。好像没看见太多内地生？wl还好，注意规划时间，我就没有好好规划
reviews.translated_content: There is a short handwritten quiz at the end of each lecture covering that day’s content. Tutorials require attendance and participation marks for speaking, so make sure to do the readings well. For the final assessment, there is one presentation and one term project (reportedly, you can choose between an essay, video, or podcast). You can work individually or in groups. I didn’t seem to see many students from Mainland China? The workload is manageable; just plan your time well—I didn’t plan properly.

reviews.content: 挺有意思的英语文学课，内容围绕与“变形”有关的文学作品，比如吸血鬼德古拉，卡夫卡变形计，奥维德变形计，弗兰肯斯坦等等。workload不大，课前要读一些作品节选但不多，要写两篇essay一篇改写。Jessica和两位tutor都很nice。我最后A-

reviews.content: 是一门技术性比较强的课，在课上要从零开始学习制作3D场景的工具，例如twinmotion和unity3d，但不会特别深入，因为很多上课时间会用来探讨”虚拟“这个概念的历史与发展。
reviews.translated_content: This is a fairly technical course. You start from scratch in class to learn tools for creating 3D scenes, such as Twinmotion and Unity3D, but it doesn’t go into great depth, as much of the class time is spent exploring the history and development of the concept of the 'virtual'.

reviews.content: RUN，summer上的课，wl巨大无比，强烈建议先确认一下自己的电脑配置是否够流畅运行unity，twinmotion，sketchup，并可以流畅剪辑视频和一些小特效（e.g.PR)。是的以上所有软件你都会在这门课里学到且要交作业/用到project里。有以上软件基础的同学可以尝试（不过本人哪怕会3d建模和剪视频都很吃力...)
reviews.translated_content: Get out while you can. This is a summer course with a huge workload. I strongly recommend checking first whether your computer specs are sufficient to run Unity, Twinmotion, and SketchUp smoothly, and to edit videos and add small effects (e.g., in PR) smoothly. Yes, you will learn all the above software in this course and need to submit assignments or use them in projects. Students with prior experience in these software tools can give it a try (though even with skills in 3D modelling and video editing, I found it very strenuous...).

search_summary.title: Nature in the City: Beyond the Concrete Jungle

course_info.title: Nature in the City: Beyond the Concrete Jungle

reviews.content: 课程内容总体来说比较有意思，task和lecture内容基本上没什么关系，有一篇essay（30%），一个group视频（20%）和一张海报（30%），wl不算小但做起来不枯燥，需要体现自己对人与自然关系的思考，需要一定的视频剪辑和海报制作能力。tutorial互动极多，不建议极度社恐参加。field trip的小quiz很简单。这门课我上得非常认真，但是不知道为什么我们全组都烂龟了......都是B和B＋，感觉努力和龟不太成正比，比较玄学，慎选。
reviews.translated_content: The course content is generally quite interesting. The tasks and lecture content are basically unrelated. There is one essay (30%), a group video (20%), and a poster (30%). The workload is not small, but it isn't boring to do. You need to demonstrate your own thinking on the relationship between humans and nature, and you need some video editing and poster-making skills. There is extensive interaction in tutorials, so it is not recommended for those who are very uncomfortable with social participation. The quizzes on the field trip are very easy. I took this course very seriously, but for some reason, our entire group received poor grades... all Bs and B+s. It feels like effort and grades are not proportional; the grading is quite opaque and unpredictable. Choose with caution.

reviews.content: 在summer sem上的课。讲的是人与自然（……？）。要上一个月，一周两节lecture两节tutorial。也就一般般有意思吧，lecturer喜欢搞很多小活动让大家交流（所以严重社恐不建议参加）。有一次field trip，一篇小essay，一个tutorial内组队完成的video，一个poster。最后其实给龟不错。A-
reviews.translated_content: I took this course in the summer semester. It is about humans and nature (...?). It lasts for one month, with two lectures and two tutorials per week. It was just moderately interesting. The lecturer likes to organize many small activities for everyone to interact (so it is not recommended for those who are very uncomfortable with social participation). There was one field trip, one short essay, one video completed in teams during a tutorial, and one poster. In the end, the grading was quite good. A-

reviews.content: 本人的专业跟这门课的内容八竿子打不着选这门是因为喜欢，但是在剪视频、做海报中非常有成就感，并且很感激这门课把我久违沉默的创造力和想象激发了出来，最后做海报时可以拿着手绘草稿跟教授1v1，比较允许自我想法的生长，同时教授也会说make sense to me的话就很好了。dz视频被guest judge评为runner up，手画的海报也在gallery中大受好评，但最后a，不知道a+谁在得
reviews.translated_content: My major has nothing to do with the content of this course; I chose it because I liked it. I felt a great sense of achievement in editing videos and making posters, and I am grateful that this course rekindled my long-dormant creativity and imagination. For the final poster, I could have a one-on-one session with the professor using my hand-drawn drafts. The course allows personal ideas to develop, and it was great when the professor said things like 'that makes sense to me.' My video was rated runner-up by the guest judge, and my hand-drawn poster was well-received in the gallery. However, I ended up with an A, and I don't know who got the A+.

reviews.content: 辛辛苦苦最後就得了個A-也不知道該說甚麼了：）三份作業也有信心有A/ A+的水準 最後就A- ：）
reviews.translated_content: After all that hard work, I only got an A-, so I don’t even know what to say :) I was confident that my three assignments were at an A/A+ standard, but in the end, it was just an A- :)

reviews.content: 相对而言没有很高的课后阅读需求，所有分数来源为：reflective writing(30%), 2-student group video (30%), poster (40%). 课程设计可能会有变化，但基本确定主要追求“有创新性”/“让人眼前一亮”的观点，同学评估不计入分数，在美术方面有要求但这方面分数较少……不过肯定是对教授胃口的给分高。给A的数量比较少，需谨慎选择。
reviews.translated_content: Relatively low demand for after-class reading. All grades come from: reflective writing (30%), 2-student group video (30%), and poster (40%). The course design may change, but it basically focuses on “innovative” or “eye-catching” ideas. Peer assessment doesn’t count towards the grade. There are artistic requirements, but they carry little weight... However, you’ll get higher marks if you cater to the professor’s taste. Few As are given, so choose with caution.

reviews.content: 还没出龟，但据说去年45% A range 55% B range。第一份作文比较简单，后面影片project和手绘海报很吃功底，不然会做得很辛苦，但是给分主要是在内容上。一星期有两次lect两次tut，作业也排得很紧。
reviews.translated_content: Grades haven’t been released yet, but reportedly last year 45% were in the A range and 55% in the B range. The first essay was relatively simple, but the subsequent film project and hand-drawn poster require strong foundational skills; otherwise, they will be tough to complete. However, grading focuses mainly on content. There are two lectures and two tutorials per week, and the assignment schedule is tight.

reviews.content: 马马虎虎，剪视频很累，不会画海报
reviews.translated_content: Just so-so. Editing videos is tiring, and I do not know how to design posters.

reviews.content: i thought i did pretty decent, but the students in the class are way too artsy and i had a hard time managing the high WL assignments along with my summer intern. i got a B+, honestly thought i'd be getting an A- thought. very disapppointing ugh. recommend not to take if u have a lot of work over the summer. but its quite fun if you're free and excited about drawing posters by hand and editing crazy videos
马马虎虎，剪视频很累，不会画海报
reviews.translated_content: So-so. Editing videos was tiring, and I don’t know how to design posters.

reviews.content: It’s a good course and it was enjoyable. However, the workload is high and strong effort is really needed. There was an essay, a video, and a poster for the assignments. foreign market today. The poster must be HAND DRAWN if you want to get a good grade. Moreover, you need to compete and be active every single tutorial and lecture. The tutors are very nice but you have to be proactive. I finally got A range, and I’m satisfied with the result, but for those expecting an easy grade, especially if you have never drawn a proper art piece, beware.

search_summary.title: Making and Appreciating Drama (SCCE)

course_info.title: Making and Appreciating Drama (SCCE)

reviews.content: 课程内容还挺有趣的，两个英国lecturer都很耐心，有很多practical的drama技巧，不过给🐢不是很好，而且workload略大，如果不是非常有兴趣不建议选
reviews.translated_content: The course content is quite interesting, and both British lecturers are very patient. There are many practical drama techniques, but the grading isn’t great and the workload is slightly heavy. Unless you’re very interested, I wouldn’t recommend taking it.

reviews.content: 老师和助教人都很好！每节课会讲一小点内容 大部分时间留给大家排自己的小drama wl还行 总体很有趣
reviews.translated_content: The instructor and teaching assistants are all very nice! Each class covers a small amount of content, leaving most of the time for us to rehearse our own short dramas. The workload is acceptable, and overall it’s quite interesting.

reviews.content: 因为疫情原因只能在网上授课，但没有减少戏剧课的趣味性和互动性。个人认为是全年上过最开心的course。重心在于“演”，而“making drama”涵盖的写剧本、导演、服化等等基本没接触。coursework不算太多，有两篇reflective journal，一篇final essay，和一个letters live的表演。想要轻松愉快的cc就选它。
reviews.translated_content: Due to the pandemic, classes were held online, but this didn’t reduce the fun and interactivity of the drama course. I personally found it the most enjoyable course I took all year. The focus is on ‘performing’, while aspects of ‘making drama’ such as scriptwriting, directing, costumes, and makeup were barely covered. The coursework isn’t too heavy: two reflective journals, one final essay, and a Letters Live performance. Choose this if you want a relaxed and enjoyable Common Core course.

reviews.content: 上过最chur的cc 三小时连堂，写500+500+500+1500的作文，还要每周空时间去排drama，痛并快乐着吧，最后B+。。。
reviews.translated_content: The most demanding Common Core course I’ve taken. Three-hour consecutive classes, essays of 500+500+500+1500 words, and you also have to find free time every week to rehearse drama. It was painful yet enjoyable. Ended up with a B+...

reviews.content: 老师和助教人都很好！基本就是每节课讲一小点东西 一学期排一个小drama 总体比较有趣 wl不算太大
reviews.translated_content: The instructor and teaching assistants are all very nice! Basically, each class covers just a small amount of material, and there is one short drama production over the semester. Overall, it is quite interesting, and the workload is not too heavy.

reviews.content: 啊！为啥你们都说给分不好！我来给想选这门课被ric劝退的同学一剂强心针！我没有任何drama基础，选这门课的时候也还只是yr1不会写essay的状态，上课也不积极发言，就傻坐着，最后final表演的时候我还出错说串词了，我组友用力瞪我我才反应过来，还是她们帮忙圆上故事……就这还有a……没错就这还有a……
reviews.translated_content: Ah! Why does everyone say the grading is bad? Let me give a boost of confidence to students who want to take this course but were discouraged by RIC! I had no background in drama, and when I enrolled I was only in Year 1 and didn't know how to write essays. I wasn't active in class either; I just sat there dumbly. During the final performance, I even made a mistake and mixed up my lines. My group mates glared at me until I realised, and they helped salvage the story... And yet I still got an A... Yes, I still got an A despite all that...

reviews.content: 教授和助教都是英国人，上完一整个学期后我的口音都有点被带偏（no offense, 只是我一直都是美音）：）课程内容顾名思义，有表演练习，也有各个流派的介绍，对于我这个艺术修养不深厚的人来说还蛮开眼界的~ assessment是2篇reflection，1篇essay，一个表演作业，peer evalution占比小，大家得分好像普遍都还不错。每年的表演作业好像都不一样，我们是letters live，就是和组友分不同部分完成同一篇信件朗读。这个我得分还不错，但是本人不太擅长写essay，所以最后只有B+。我的组友没有人拿到A range。
reviews.translated_content: Both the professor and the TAs are British. After a whole semester, my accent shifted a bit (no offense, I’ve always had an American accent) :) As the name suggests, the course includes acting exercises and introductions to various schools of drama. For someone like me without deep artistic cultivation, it was quite eye-opening. Assessment consists of two reflections, one essay, and one performance assignment. Peer evaluation carries little weight, and everyone seems to have scored reasonably well. The performance assignment changes every year; ours was ‘Letters Live’, where group members divided parts of the same letter to read aloud. I did quite well on that, but I’m not good at writing essays, so I ended up with only a B+. None of my groupmates got an A-range grade.

course_info.title: Games: Play, Learning and Society
course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: 能找到一起做游戏的队友才建议读。计划书和 Present 都很麻烦，但实际把游戏做出来才是最难的，就算是 Scratch 也不简单。不管游戏实际成品做得多烂，大家还是要自卖自夸，感觉不好。教育游戏化这个概念本来就没有什么说服力。最大的收获是必读书 Fundamentals of Game Design，虽然懂了这些对 Group Project 一点用都没有。
reviews.translated_content: I’d only recommend taking this if you can find teammates to build a game with. The proposal and presentation are both troublesome, but actually making the game is the hardest part; even Scratch isn’t simple. No matter how bad the final game turns out, you still have to sell it and brag, which feels off. The concept of gamifying education isn’t very convincing. The biggest takeaway was the required book Fundamentals of Game Design, although understanding it was useless for the group project.

reviews.content: 課堂内容蠻有意思但可能會有點悶。教授有時會講得太深，很難理解。Tutor的英文不太好，非常難明白。課業方面算還好，一個group presentation和一篇essay， 但如果想好Grade就不建議拿.
reviews.translated_content: The class content is quite interesting but might be a bit dull at times. The professor sometimes goes too deep, making it hard to understand. The tutor’s English isn’t very good, so it’s very hard to follow. The coursework is manageable: one group presentation and one essay. However, if you want a good grade, I wouldn’t recommend taking this course.

reviews.content: 讲课内容还算有意思，考核以essay为主
reviews.translated_content: The lecture content is reasonably interesting. Assessment is mainly based on essays.

reviews.content: vague content, boring lectures
reviews.translated_content: vague content, boring lectures

reviews.content: 这门课旨在打破对宗教科学传统的分类和认知，对truth, reality, knowledge等进行更全面的阐述分类，挺引发思考的。但涉及到不少哲学方面的概念和内容，因此对于哲学小白（比如我）而言有难度。而且课程设置不系统。 lecture很有意思，教授经常用一些有趣直观的演示来解释问题。tutorial由学生主导，实际相当于每组做两个presentation。要写一篇film review和final essay。每周有20页左右的reading，有些难度很大我看不懂放弃了。 这门课主要是local和国际生，别的内地生我没有遇到。很多有宗教背景，或者对这方面感兴趣。 我也有很用心地学习及完成各项内容。最后A-
reviews.translated_content: This course aims to break down traditional classifications and perceptions of religion and science, providing a more comprehensive elaboration and classification of truth, reality, knowledge, etc. It is quite thought-provoking. However, it involves many philosophical concepts and content, so it is difficult for philosophy beginners (like me). Also, the course structure is not systematic. Lectures are very interesting; the professor often uses fun, intuitive demonstrations to explain problems. Tutorials are student-led, effectively equivalent to each group giving two presentations. You need to write a film review and a final essay. There are about 20 pages of reading per week; some are very difficult, so I gave up on them. The class consists mainly of local and international students; I did not encounter any students from Mainland China. Many have a religious background or are interested in this area. I also studied hard and completed all the tasks. Finally got an A-.

course_info.title: Buddhist Visions in World Cinema
course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: 人生第一节cc，期中考了77.5（A➕水平），最后结果B，最傻逼的cc，傻逼教授，每次上课人都会越来越少。所有的课和tutorial都记attendance，所有课都去了最后participation70%。凭着对佛教和电影的一腔热血去上了这节课，结果直接吃屎。
reviews.translated_content: My first Common Core course ever. I scored 77.5 (A+ level) on the midterm, but the final result was a B. The most ridiculous Common Core course, with a ridiculous professor. Attendance dropped every class. All lectures and tutorials took attendance, yet despite attending every class, my participation score was only 70%. I went into this course with passion for Buddhism and cinema, and the result was a complete disaster.

reviews.content: 最开始是因为听说好龟选的这门，但第一节lecture就被吸引住了，整学期上下来给了我很大的启发。assessment大概分为以下四个：1attendance：每节课/tuto都要去，readings得看（会抽问+记分），2midterm：非essay大神最好选quiz，3final essay：一定要注意格式 否则吃c range。4做poster或拍视频：靠谱队友+审美+切题很重要。另外：因为后来真的有兴趣了，想出比较好的问题，拿到extra credit；essay的角度也很独特+写的比较深入，所以给分不错。最后A+。ps 强烈不建议不擅长essay/对佛学毫无兴趣/不想读reading的同学选。最后，好龟课也可能会烂龟的。烂龟课也可能好龟。强烈建议多考虑兴趣的因素。
reviews.translated_content: I initially chose this course because I heard it offered favourable grading, but I was captivated by the first lecture, and the entire semester was very inspiring. The assessments are roughly divided into four parts: 1. Attendance: You must attend every lecture/tutorial and complete the readings (there will be random questions and marks awarded). 2. Midterm: Unless you’re an essay expert, it’s better to choose the quiz option. 3. Final essay: Pay close attention to formatting, otherwise you’ll get a C-range grade. 4. Poster or video project: Reliable teammates, aesthetics, and relevance to the topic are crucial. Additionally, because I developed a genuine interest later on, I asked good questions and earned extra credit. My essay angle was unique and written in depth, so the grading was generous. I ended up with an A+. PS: I strongly advise against taking this if you are not good at essays, have no interest in Buddhism, or don’t want to do the readings. Finally, a course known for good grades can sometimes result in harsh grading, and a course with a reputation for harsh grading can sometimes yield good grades. I strongly recommend considering your interest level.

reviews.content: 史诗级大烂课。。。tutor非常抽象，prof很好，但是tutor让这个课变得极其恶心
reviews.translated_content: An epic terrible course... The tutor is very bizarre. The prof is good, but the tutor makes this course extremely unpleasant.

reviews.content: 很棒的课，能学到很多东西，重要的是field trip很有趣，去了大屿山的寺院，吃了非常非常好吃的素食午餐，老师很好问问题回答也很细致，推荐
reviews.translated_content: Great course; you can learn a lot. Importantly, the field trip was fun—we visited a monastery on Lantau Island and had a very delicious vegetarian lunch. The instructor is approachable and answers questions in detail. Recommended.

reviews.content: 平心而论这是我上火嘴受益匪浅的课。wl不大reading其实都有趣 不管抽查还是不抽 写essay的时间总会要看 电影都非常有意思 好莱坞大片或者黑白电影 都让我一个初学者对佛学有了更全面的认识 专业知识可能会忘记 但是对生命的启发是一辈子的事 龟A+
reviews.translated_content: To be fair, this is the Common Core course where I benefited the most. The workload isn’t heavy, and the readings are actually interesting. Whether there are spot checks or not, you’ll always need to spend time writing the essay. The movies are very interesting—whether Hollywood blockbusters or black-and-white films—they gave me, as a beginner, a more comprehensive understanding of Buddhism. You might forget the professional knowledge, but the inspiration for life lasts a lifetime. Grade: A+.

reviews.content: 老师很友善，上课较无聊，wl轻松，好龟
reviews.translated_content: The instructor is very friendly. Classes are rather boring, but the workload is light, and it’s easy to get a good grade.

reviews.content: assessment是一篇1200的short essay，一篇2000的final essay和一个gp（可选拍视频或者做poster）。上课内容可能比较无聊，tutorial比较chur，每节课都会被tutor cue好几个问题，prof和tutor的英语不算特别标准，偶尔会有点理解问题，但大部分时间还好。🐢很不错，在short essay C的情况下最后还有A range，对佛教有兴趣有想法的同学可以考虑这门课。
reviews.translated_content: The assessments are one 1,200-word short essay, one 2,000-word final essay, and a group project (you can choose to make a video or a poster). The lecture content might be a bit boring, and the tutorials are quite demanding; the tutor calls on several students to answer questions in every class. The professor’s and tutors’ English isn’t particularly standard, so there are occasional comprehension issues, but it’s fine most of the time. The grading is quite generous; even with a C on the short essay, I still ended up with an A-range grade. Students who are interested in Buddhism and have their own ideas might consider this course.

reviews.content: 绝世好课，每周看一个电影学习佛教知识，期中可以不选考试选写essay。prof超好，除了tutor christina很chur之外没其他毛病
reviews.translated_content: An absolutely fantastic course. Every week we watch a film to learn about Buddhism. For the midterm, you can choose to write an essay instead of taking an exam. The professor is super nice; apart from the tutor Christina being quite demanding, there are no other issues.

reviews.content: 从2021年fall开始换tutor了！以前是好grade课、现在开始不一定。至少我认识的大部分都是b range（包括我）每周都要看一个电影，读reading，花的时间真的很多，而且佛教我觉得很晦涩，至少我看的云里雾里。midterm要选quiz，我选了essay然后烂了。gp做个海报，很简单。final是个大essay，jnan特别注重格式，一定要仔细检查。总的来说，这门课适合会写essay的人上
reviews.translated_content: Starting from Fall 2021, the tutors have changed! It used to be a course where good grades were attainable, but that’s not necessarily the case now. At least most people I know got B-range grades (including me). You have to watch a movie and do the reading every week, which takes a lot of time. Also, I find Buddhism quite obscure; at least I was confused by what I read. For the midterm, you choose between a quiz or an essay; I chose the essay and did poorly. The group project is making a poster, which is simple. The final is a long essay. Jnan pays particular attention to formatting, so make sure to check carefully. Overall, this course suits people who are good at writing essays.

reviews.content: 很好龟的课，平时lecture一堂课没听，一部电影都没看过。就是tutorial tutor Christina会疯狂chur你问你电影的内容，只要tutorial之前看看豆瓣和维基百科就好了。一篇期中essay一篇期末essay 一个poster，只要找个reading好读的电影写essay就能好龟。和我一起读的朋友都拿了A/A+
reviews.translated_content: This is a GPA-friendly course. I didn’t attend a single lecture or watch any films during the semester. However, the tutorial tutor, Christina, will relentlessly grill you on the film content. As long as you check Douban and Wikipedia before the tutorial, you’ll be fine. There is one mid-term essay, one final essay, and one poster. If you choose a film with easy-to-read materials for your essays, you can get a good grade. Friends who took it with me all got A/A+.

reviews.content:
少有的令我感到不爽的课。首先，每节课都要记attendance，tutorial必须读reading，wl看似不多实际上比一节普通的electives都要大，每节课上课前都要交200字essay，这200字就要回答6，7个问题，也不知道能说啥。但是这个给龟很好，到后面essay+video给分成谜，完全主观，criteria就是一个笑话（很容易就莫名其妙的烂了，而且不是很好🐢）

life worth living：这节课实际上解答不了这个问题，随便take一个phil的课都解答的比它好。尤其是对于不太信宗教的同学，几乎每节课上课都学一种宗教，一开始还有热情，但是短时间内浅显了解那么多个宗教令人癫狂，有种什么都学不到，还学了好像很多的感觉。有的guest speaking完全是在服务于信仰他们宗教的学生，没信仰的别去，自找苦吃。第一节课prof讲的巨有意思，留下来不drop，之后就是一场漫长的折磨。
reviews.translated_content: One of the rare courses that made me feel unhappy. First, attendance is taken in every class, and you must do the readings for tutorials. The workload seems small but is actually heavier than a normal elective. Before every class, you have to submit a 200-word essay answering 6–7 questions; it’s hard to know what to write. However, the grading is generous. Later on, the marking for the essay and video became mysterious and completely subjective; the criteria were a joke (it is easy to inexplicably get a poor grade, and it is not easy to get a good grade). Life Worth Living: This class actually fails to answer this question. Any philosophy course would answer it better. Especially for students who are not very religious: almost every class covers a different religion. At first, there was enthusiasm, but superficially learning about so many religions in a short time was maddening. It felt like learning nothing while simultaneously feeling like you learned a lot. Some guest speakers were entirely serving students who share their faith. If you have no faith, don’t go; you are just asking for trouble. The professor’s first lecture was extremely interesting, which is why I stayed and didn’t drop the course. After that, it was a long torture.

reviews.content: 吹爆TA keri呜呜呜太牛了 我目前最好龟的cc了
reviews.translated_content: Cannot recommend TA Keri highly enough—she’s amazing. This is the Common Core course where I’ve gotten the best grade so far.

reviews.content: 在final presentation里tutor会问每一个人的宗教信仰，基督徒的同学都会很高分。 Tutor也会邀请同学在课余时间参与祈祷聚会。
reviews.translated_content: During the final presentation, the tutor asks every student about their religious beliefs. Christian students tend to get high scores. The tutor also invites students to join prayer gatherings in their spare time.

reviews.content: 很chill 但是社恐都要小心了 每堂強制回答一天問題 表示抗拒 但功課都很輕鬆 很容易完成
reviews.translated_content: Very chill, but those who are very uncomfortable with social participation should be careful. Every class requires answering one question. I resisted this, but the coursework is very relaxed and easy to complete.

reviews.content: criteria成谜，但不是不能拿好🐢吧。wl一般，每个lec写小问题，tut要发言讨论，交课前200字小回答。 e人友好，tutor是chen sukai，感觉他上课比我还紧张！小回答可以看分，我大概是我tut上最烂的。  final是video和essay，有趣，标准迷惑。不过根据之前同学给的经验和老师们的指导，要阐述自己的理解和想法就好，我也是这样来的，很享受表达自己的过程吧。 lec有几个略无聊但是很能开拓对各种宗教的理解。。。总体上墙推！！ 老师们都非常非常nice，我最后A。
reviews.translated_content: The grading criteria are a mystery, but it’s not impossible to get a good grade. The workload is average: each lecture requires answering short questions, tutorials involve speaking and discussion, and you need to submit a 200-word short response before class. It is friendly for extroverts. Our tutor was Chen Sukai, who seemed more nervous in class than I was! You can see the marks for the short responses, and I was probably the worst in my tutorial group. The final consisted of a video and an essay; it was interesting, though the criteria were confusing. However, based on advice from seniors and guidance from the teachers, you just need to articulate your own understanding and ideas. That’s what I did, and I quite enjoyed the process of expressing myself. Some lectures were a bit boring but really broadened my understanding of various religions... Overall, I strongly recommend it!! The teachers are all very, very nice. I finished with an A.

reviews.content: workload is really big, many readings and attendance in every lectures and tutorials. Jonathan is really nice so the speaking with him will help you think a lot. But some guest lectures are really boring. I fuck up the video and essay but still got a B.
reviews.translated_content: The workload is really big, with many readings and attendance required for every lecture and tutorial. Jonathan is really nice, so speaking with him helps you think a lot. But some guest lectures are really boring. I messed up the video and essay but still got a B.

reviews.content: 很少人上过的CC。形式主要是每节lecture请一个有宗教信仰的guest speaker来解释这一宗教&他们认为的a life worth living. 可能会觉得有点散，毕竟每节课的speaker都在换（睡过了很多节emmm）。Reading正如每一门cc一样不需要也没办法全读，tutorial个人感觉可能占了很多分。我的tutor Jonathan采取的形式是role play小人打怪什么的... 总体上付出不多，🐢很好拿了A
reviews.translated_content: A Common Core course with low enrolment. The format mainly involves inviting a guest speaker with a religious affiliation to each lecture to explain their religion and their view of 'a life worth living'. It may feel a bit scattered since the speaker changes every class (I slept through many sessions, emmm). As with every Common Core course, you don’t need to—and can’t possibly—read all the assigned readings. I feel the tutorial probably accounts for a large portion of the marks. My tutor, Jonathan, used formats like role-playing characters fighting monsters... Overall, the effort required is not high, and it is easy to get an A.

reviews.content: 绝世好课！Carl和Keri都超级超级nice，上课氛围很轻松愉快，是本大四老狗的精神家园。每节课介绍一个主流宗教或哲学思想，注重体验和意义。tutorial上探讨关于价值、变化、美、爱的话题。prez和final essay都是阐述自己眼中的life worth living，是一个非常好的回顾与反思的机会，不需要高深的知识，而要真诚的体验和思考。最后拿了A。我觉得这门课带给我的思考是我大学生活中最大的收获之一。强烈推荐！
reviews.translated_content: An absolutely amazing course! Carl and Keri are super, super nice. The class atmosphere is relaxed and enjoyable; it was a spiritual sanctuary for me as a burnt-out final-year student. Each class introduces a mainstream religion or philosophical thought, focusing on experience and meaning. Tutorials discuss topics like values, change, beauty, and love. The presentation and final essay both involve explaining your own view of “a life worth living,” which is a great opportunity for review and reflection. It doesn’t require profound knowledge, but sincere experience and thinking. I ended up with an A. I think the reflections this course gave me are one of the biggest gains of my university life. Highly recommended!

reviews.content: 烂grade。。
reviews.translated_content: Poor grading..

reviews.content: 教不同宗教和思想对a life worth living的定义 大多数lecture都有guest speaker workload蛮大  每堂lecture前都要看reading和写问题 lecture后要写反思 还有个indivisual presentation和1500字reflective essay 每堂tutorial都要讨论
reviews.translated_content: It covers how different religions and philosophies define 'a life worth living'. Most lectures have guest speakers. The workload is quite heavy: you must do the readings and write questions before every lecture, write reflections after each lecture, and there is also an individual presentation and a 1500-word reflective essay. Every tutorial involves discussion.

reviews.content: 新课一门，没final，lecture performance要算但是好像给分普遍好，要自己用blog形式更新一个research report，然后还有个grp poster，虽然看上去很繁杂但是完全可以水，最后A
reviews.translated_content: It’s a new course with no final exam. Lecture performance counts, but grading seems generally generous. You need to update a research report in blog format, and there’s also a group poster. Although it looks complicated, you can easily coast through it. I got an A in the end.

reviews.content: 一个linguistics的老师教。 貌似每个学期的评分方式都要换？当初看他还有名额就选了。评分方式倒是很有意思，四个创作40分，5个一分钟测试20分，然后出席分20分，group project20分。不过我感觉老师和tutor根本就不考虑学生会不会被分数影响。一分钟测试没有太多时间去考虑写什么，然后四个创作的评分很大程度很看老师喜不喜欢你的作品，不建议
reviews.translated_content: Taught by a linguistics instructor. It seems the grading scheme changes every semester? I enrolled because there were still spots available. The grading scheme is quite interesting: four creative assignments worth 40%, five one-minute tests worth 20%, attendance worth 20%, and a group project worth 20%. However, I feel the instructor and tutor don’t really consider how the grading affects students. There isn’t much time to think about what to write for the one-minute tests, and the grading of the four creative assignments depends heavily on whether the instructor likes your work. Not recommended.

reviews.content: 这门课的老师是韩国的女老师，有一个男宝宝，她上课的时候给我们看的。评分方式如下：（1）4个小作业，一个作业10%，总共40%，每个作业的满分是10分。 但我每次作业都只能达到7分，上不了8-10这一档，每次都get不到老师到底想要考察什么，觉得还是挺崩溃的，因为感觉也用心，花时间去做了，但是分数没有提高 （2）（7-2）道课上的quiz算分，一分钟作答，总共20%，每个满分4分 这个quiz不难，我一般都是3-4分，3分偏多  （3）小组作业20% 有三个部分，有些繁琐，就是那种一直有事不能放的那种感觉 我个人不喜欢 （4）lecture和tutorial的参与程度 总共20% 我的参与程度不高，所以不知道这块老师给分怎么样  总结一下，就是老师上课听认真的，但我不喜欢上课的内容，所以感觉没有什么意思，然后作业比较杂而细，而且我的评分不好，所以我有点失望 因为课程的作业真的是贯穿一整个学期，但是分数却很一般
reviews.translated_content: The instructor for this course is a Korean female teacher who has a baby boy; she showed him to us during class. The grading breakdown is as follows: (1) Four small assignments, each worth 10%, totaling 40%. Each assignment is marked out of 10. However, I could only reach 7 points on each assignment and never broke into the 8–10 range. I couldn’t figure out what the instructor was actually testing, which was quite frustrating because I felt I put in effort and time, but my scores didn’t improve. (2) In-class quizzes (between 2 and 7 of them) count for 20% in total. You have one minute to answer each, and each is marked out of 4. These quizzes aren’t difficult; I usually scored 3–4, mostly 3s. (3) Group project accounts for 20%. It has three parts and is quite tedious—it feels like there’s always something to do that you can’t let go of. I personally don’t like it. (4) Participation in lectures and tutorials accounts for 20%. My participation wasn’t high, so I don’t know how the instructor grades this part. To sum up, the instructor teaches seriously, but I didn’t enjoy the course content, so it felt uninteresting. The assignments are miscellaneous and detailed, and since my grades weren’t good, I’m a bit disappointed. The coursework really runs through the entire semester, yet the grades are just average.

reviews.content: 内容非常非常水的一门课，涉及一些心理学和语言学常识，assignment很有意思，是画图做gif做海报等等，但如果get不到老师作业要求可能会烂龟。我个人风格可能很对tutor和老师胃口，平时作业都接近满分，gp很认真完成了，reflective essay也是满分，最后没拿到a+，只拿了a的原因可能是平时quiz分太低，quiz只给3分钟回答问题，对我来说有点太仓促了...
reviews.translated_content: The content is extremely lightweight. It covers some common knowledge in psychology and linguistics. The assignments are interesting, involving drawing, making GIFs, creating posters, etc., but if you don't grasp the instructor's requirements, you might get a poor grade. My personal style probably suited the tutor and instructor well; my regular assignments were nearly full marks, I completed the group project very seriously, and my reflective essay also got full marks. The reason I didn't get an A+ and only got an A was likely because my quiz scores were too low. The quizzes only allow 3 minutes to answer questions, which felt a bit too rushed for me...

reviews.content: 有趣但龟不是很好
reviews.translated_content: Interesting, but the grading isn’t very good.

subclasses.instructor: Wong,Yue Chim Richard; Yuen,Wing Han Vera

reviews.content:
Highly recommend this course. As other commenters have mentioned, Professor Wong is a well-known, highly acclaimed academic in HKU. His knowledge about political philosophy and in other areas is deeply vast, able to speak for hours without end. In this semester, he had an optional, 4-hour lecture during reading week (for freshmen, this is a week-long holiday in the middle of the semester, usually midterms would be conducted in this period), and we only managed to enjoy a 10-minute break after 3 hours of nonstop teaching. He was about to continue even further until someone reminded him that it should end soon. Professor Wong is full of passion, vigor, and vitality; despite his old age, his energy radiates throughout the room. His lecture notes are around 20-pages long; he had already cut out some pages after a suggestion given by Dr Yuen. The notes are great reading material, providing brief yet profound introductions on each figure mentioned in the lectures. Overall, excluding minor figures that were only lightly mentioned, 45 people were introduced. Dr Wong skipped the last chapter because he couldn't finish it (it was excluded in the assessment). 

Regarding the grading, I would say that it's okay. I had my doubts about the grading before I enrolled this course, and my concerns were righteous. I received zero feedback and results about my essay even after the overall grade was presented. It should be mentioned that although many previous commenters have mentioned that there are quizzes after class, this has now been untrue (or true, depending if they switch back to the previous examination format) as of 2025. Instead, a final is provided to be finished within 2 hours. Students have to complete 3 essay questions out of 5. Essay questions are easy if you had studied. Overall, I got an A-. I would highly recommend those that want to dip their toes in political philosophy, those wishing to gain some brief understanding about political philosophy, or those that just want an excellent lecturer, certainly a rarity in most universities. I do find it quite amusing that this course is offered by FBE yet has little to do with data analytics or business, more on political theory (under fac of social science) and philosophy (under fac of arts). It's a lovely course, that's all I can say.

reviews.content: 教授是副校长王于渐先生，人文积淀深厚到任何一位哲学名家都能信手拈来侃侃而谈的程度，上课十分有激情和感染力，无限敬佩。然而比较实用主义的同学绝对要避雷这门课，给龟稀碎：平常的quiz都在80左右（算高的），paper给Amy看也得到了很高的评价，但由于实际上paper是Vera改的（这位作为GPA Killer实属名声远扬，著有《Price for Sin》细陈学生各种拿F的罪恶渊薮），最终只拿了B，背后的原因令人暖心🥰
reviews.translated_content: The instructor is Vice-President Professor Richard Wong, whose depth of humanistic knowledge allows him to effortlessly discuss any famous philosopher with passion and infectious energy; I have infinite admiration for him. However, students with a pragmatic mindset should definitely avoid this course, as the grading is terrible: my usual quiz scores were around 80 (which is considered high), and Amy gave my paper a very positive evaluation. But since Vera actually marked the paper (this person is widely known as a GPA killer, famously documenting the various sins that lead students to fail in “Price for Sin”), I only ended up with a B. The reason behind this is heartwarming 🥰

reviews.content: 看到那个piechart了吗？我就是fail的那一个。原因是Paper由于ai问题0分。本人花了前后三四周时间准备paper没有让ai生成任何东西，但是grammarly开着加个逗号什么的就加了。提交完成之后不确定是否要appendix于是去询问是否妥当，Vera一个月后回信，我说明情况并表示如果需要可以立马补appendix没有回应。再半个月后出成绩就是fail，再发邮件交涉半个月无果，觉得自己也挺🍬的直接声明没有用ai就无事发生，但总之确实发生了这么个事，各位就这么一听吧。作为对课程的评价，请习惯英语进行大量书面哲学讨论的同学考虑报课，如果向往一种坐而论道的氛围大可不必，尤其yr1学生，lecture比较基础，tut大家讨论浑水摸鱼成分有点多。有兴趣walkin即可，不要高估这个鬼学校的生活，祝好运🍀
reviews.translated_content: See that pie chart? I am the one who failed. The reason was that my paper received 0 marks due to an AI issue. I spent three to four weeks preparing the paper and did not let AI generate anything, but I had Grammarly on, which added things like commas. After submitting, I was unsure whether I needed an appendix, so I asked if it was appropriate. Vera replied a month later; I explained the situation and said I could add the appendix immediately if needed, but there was no response. Another half-month later, the result was a fail. I emailed to dispute it for another half-month with no result. I feel I am also quite sweet/naive. Declaring that I didn’t use AI would have prevented this, but anyway, this is what happened. Just take it with a grain of salt. As an evaluation of the course: students who are accustomed to extensive written philosophical discussions in English should consider enrolling. If you aspire to a atmosphere of abstract theoretical debate, there is no need, especially for Year 1 students. Lectures are quite basic, and in tutorials, there is a fair amount of coasting and muddling through. If you are interested, just sit in on the class. Do not overestimate life at this damn school. Good luck 🍀

reviews.content: 对于对政治哲学/意识形态方面感兴趣的同学（包括但不限于键政大师和P社玩家）来说是绝世好课，非常详细的讲述了各种政治意识形态的诞生/发展/影响等，教授本身没有什么意识形态倾向，所以说没啥担心。 wl不多不少吧 每周一个chapter大概30·40页的reading，然后一共有四次essay quiz, 200字以内，期末是一篇1500字以内的essay，也比较适合不喜欢花里胡哨作业的同学。 给龟的话还行？ 不过没拿到A稍稍有点不爽就是了orz
reviews.translated_content: For students interested in political philosophy/ideologies (including but not limited to keyboard politicians and Paradox Interactive game players), this is an exceptional course. It provides a very detailed account of the birth, development, and impact of various political ideologies. The professor himself has no ideological bias, so there’s nothing to worry about. The workload is moderate: about 30–40 pages of reading per chapter each week. There are four essay quizzes (under 200 words each), and the final is an essay of under 1,500 words. It’s also suitable for students who dislike flashy assignments. As for grading, it’s okay? Though I’m slightly annoyed that I didn’t get an A orz.

reviews.content: 一开始是对政治经济学很感兴趣所以才选了这门，结果学着学着逐渐失去耐心和兴趣，首先周六早八并且强制attendance就算了，中间还搞各种各样的makeup class，搞得没人能上完所有课并且讲课进度飞起，ppt也是乱七八糟的，基本就是prof讲课的文字版，但无疑prof本身的知识底蕴是毋庸置疑的，只是整个课的风格和结构我不喜欢，整个学期我每节课都是打了卡之后坐在位置上睡觉。tutorial也没啥意思，每次只有一两个人会主动和tutor互动，经常上着上着就陷入没人讲话的僵局。term paper给了半个学期的时间准备，我硬是拖到final最后一周才开始写，最后拿了a-。对政治经济学以及哲学不感兴趣的人不要来，会特别痛苦。本来感兴趣的，学完之后彻底不想接触这方面的东西了。
reviews.translated_content: I initially chose this course because I was very interested in political economy, but gradually lost patience and interest as I studied. First, there were Saturday 8 am classes with mandatory attendance, and then various make-up classes were arranged, making it impossible for anyone to attend all sessions. The lecture pace was flying, and the PPTs were messy—basically just text versions of the professor's lectures. Undoubtedly, the professor's knowledge base is solid, but I didn't like the style and structure of the whole course. I checked in for every class and then slept in my seat. Tutorials weren't interesting either; only one or two people would actively interact with the tutor each time, often leading to awkward silences. We had half a semester to prepare for the term paper, but I dragged it out until the last week of finals to start writing, and finally got an A-. If you're not interested in political economy and philosophy, don't take this course; it will be extremely painful. I was originally interested, but after finishing it, I completely lost the desire to engage with this subject.

reviews.content: 很有趣的课但是龟很烂。。。学得最累分数最烂我请问呢？？但是lecture真的非常非常有趣就是了，如果对政治哲学感兴趣的话强烈推荐
reviews.translated_content: Very interesting course, but the grading is harsh... May I ask why this was the most exhausting course for me yet yielded the worst grade?? That said, the lectures are truly, truly interesting. If you’re interested in political philosophy, I highly recommend it.

reviews.content: 得分：A-。个人认为是好课，好龟课。如果单纯只是为了拿好龟，可以直接不听lecture，等到需要做quiz或者写essay之后再回头去找对应的知识点。quiz难度适中，并且是线下给出好多天完成，可以借助lecture notes，ppt，同学以及wiki帮助。essay建议先参考past paper高分作品，明白这门课essay应该怎么写，之后再选一个自己熟悉的题目尽情地写，并多咨询tutor意见。如果想要学知识，这节课也不错。个人觉得Richard Wong虽然在读ppt，但是他讲的很有激情，而且会穿插自己的感悟。此外，这门政治哲学课覆盖范围很广，涉及多个阶段的思想与思想家，适合对此感兴趣的同学作为引入的课找到自己真正喜欢的方向！
reviews.translated_content: Grade: A-. I personally consider it a good course and a GPA-friendly one. If you’re solely aiming for a good grade, you can skip the lectures and only look up the relevant knowledge points when you need to do quizzes or write essays. The quiz difficulty is moderate, and you have several days to complete it offline, so you can use lecture notes, PPTs, classmates, and Wikipedia for help. For the essay, I suggest referring to high-scoring samples from past papers first to understand how essays should be written for this course. Then choose a topic you’re familiar with, write freely, and consult your tutor frequently. If you want to learn knowledge, this class is also good. I feel that although Richard Wong just reads off the slides, he lectures with passion and intersperses his own insights. Furthermore, this political philosophy course covers a wide range, involving thoughts and thinkers from multiple stages. It’s suitable as an introductory course for interested students to find the direction they truly like!

reviews.content: 没兴趣别来，烂grade了我谢谢你啊vera
reviews.translated_content: Don’t come if you’re not interested. Thanks for the harsh grading, Vera.

reviews.content: 不看lecture notes和课的我拿了b 我英语水平真的不行甚至还拖quiz tutorial还爱睡觉 tutor叫Douglas香港人 好像名字是不戴口罩很帅人很nice选他冲
reviews.translated_content: I got a B even though I didn’t read the lecture notes or attend class. My English is really poor; I even dragged down my quiz and tutorial performance, and I tend to fall asleep in class. The tutor is Douglas, a local Hong Konger. His name seems to be “No Mask”; he’s handsome and very nice. Go for his section.

reviews.content: online lecture 每一課長達三小時。。。結果我在考試前只看了十個lecture（總共應該有13課）。除了lecture還有很長的lecture notes。其實lecture notes都是lecture的内容，但更加詳細。不過只看lecture 内容已經很花時間了。都是一些philosophy的東西，光是分辨清楚和理解已經很花時間。workload 很少，只有150-400字的幾次quizzes（不太難，我幾乎都在lecture notes搜關鍵字應付過去了），還有1500字左右的essay（題目自定，有點麻煩，我是用了以往學生用過的題目了）。不過lecture内容非常豐富，如果有更多時間的話可以學到很多。
reviews.translated_content: Online lectures, each lasting three hours... As a result, I only watched ten lectures before the exam (there should have been 13 in total). Besides the lectures, there are very long lecture notes. The notes basically cover the same content as the lectures but in more detail. However, just going through the lecture content already takes a lot of time. It’s all philosophy stuff, and just distinguishing concepts clearly and understanding them is very time-consuming. The workload is light, with only a few quizzes of 150–400 words (not too difficult; I mostly coped by searching for keywords in the lecture notes), and an essay of around 1500 words (you choose your own topic, which is a bit troublesome; I used a topic that previous students had used). However, the lecture content is very rich, and if you have more time, you can learn a lot.

reviews.content: 亲测纯文纯理的人都不太适合。wl特别大，几乎所有存在的assessment种类都囊括了，把我的整个学期弄得非常黑暗，给分b+，感觉付出和回报不成正比。lecture挺有趣的，其实我对这个topic挺感兴趣。但从体验和结果来看，只能说大家慎重
reviews.translated_content: Personally tested: neither pure humanities nor pure science students are well-suited. The workload is particularly heavy; it covers almost every type of assessment existing, making my entire semester very dark. Grade: B+. I feel the effort and reward were disproportionate. The lectures were quite interesting; actually, I was quite interested in this topic. But judging from the experience and result, I can only say everyone should choose with caution.

reviews.content: 课内容很有意思楼上都提到了就不说了。 陈老师口语中“啊”的有点多（稍微吐槽一下）但是讲课还是可以挺有意思的。 要读很多paper是真的，但是偷懒小技巧来了：不需要全读，读paper主要是为了写作业，作业中会提示你读哪篇paper，就去读那几篇就好。读的时候先看abstract再看intro再看个conclusion，基本上就可以写作业了。如果作业问到细节再去原文定位找一找就好。所以读paper不是一个太耗费时间的工作（当然了，topic很有趣所以读paper也挺享受的，有余力可以多读一读） 网上final是开卷，不知道接下来线下会怎样安排。都是moodle选择题，题目不难（但我也有几个不确定的）。gp我的队友都蛮靠谱的。 最后拿A还不错，付出和回报还是成了正比
reviews.translated_content: The course content is quite interesting, as others have mentioned, so I won’t repeat that. Professor Chen uses the filler word “ah” a bit too often in his speech (just a small complaint), but his lectures are still quite interesting. It is true that you have to read many papers, but here is a lazy hack: you don’t need to read them all. Reading papers is mainly for completing assignments, and the assignments will indicate which papers to read, so just read those. When reading, check the abstract first, then the introduction, and then the conclusion; basically, that is enough to complete the assignment. If the assignment asks for details, go back to the original text to locate them. So reading papers is not too time-consuming (of course, the topics are interesting, so reading papers is quite enjoyable; if you have spare capacity, you can read more). The online final was open-book; I’m not sure how it will be arranged for offline sessions in the future. It consisted of multiple-choice questions on Moodle. The questions were not difficult (though I was uncertain about a few). For the group project, my teammates were quite reliable. I finally got an A, which is not bad; the effort and reward were proportional.

reviews.content: 挺有趣的但不建议
reviews.translated_content: Quite interesting, but not recommended.

reviews.content: wl其实有点点大，有4个固定作业，一个term paper，一个presentation，tutorial也都要上。而且上学期online，prof 陈会把上课视频放在moodle里，需要lecture之前先自己看。🐢很fair！学到了很多很多东西，重点是prof陈 思考问题的方式，很受用！希望学到一些金融或者有关社会问题知识的朋友！推荐！！
reviews.translated_content: The workload is actually a bit heavy. There are four fixed assignments, one term paper, and one presentation, and you must attend tutorials. Moreover, last semester was online; Prof. Chen would post lecture videos on Moodle, so you needed to watch them yourself before class. The grading is very fair! I learned a great deal. The key takeaway is Prof. Chen’s way of thinking about problems, which is very useful. Recommended for friends who want to learn some finance or knowledge related to social issues!!

reviews.content: 努力，最后gp有东西选和tutor请教明白了就没大问题，最后A，有两个asm没满分。最后考试要好好准备，reading 多，总体wl极大
reviews.translated_content: If you put in the effort, clarify any issues by choosing your group project partners wisely and consulting your tutor, there should be no major problems. I ended up with an A, though I did not get full marks on two assignments. You need to prepare well for the final exam. There is a lot of reading, and the overall workload is extremely heavy.

reviews.content: czw满嘴跑火车，上课用的耶鲁的课件。整体来说内容还挺有启发性的，就是很cliche. 那个时候有个索嗨tutor Karen Mai Xiaoting满口good excellent, 给分稀烂。最后B.
reviews.translated_content: Chen Zhiwu talks nonsense in class and uses Yale’s slides. Overall, the content is quite inspiring, just very cliché. At that time, there was a silly tutor, Karen Mai Xiaoting, who kept saying 'good' and 'excellent', but her grading was terrible. I got a B in the end.

reviews.content: 真的好龟！！！
reviews.translated_content: The grading is really generous!!!

reviews.content: 很有意思，好分
reviews.translated_content: Very interesting, and easy to get a good grade.

reviews.content: 虽然workload大，但只要认真做ps，好好复习课上学过的ppt，龟还是不错的
reviews.translated_content: Although the workload is heavy, as long as you complete the problem sets seriously and review the PowerPoint slides taught in class properly, the grade is quite decent.

reviews.content: 陈志武教授教学水平很高，只不过workload很大，经常考试，还有期末论文。压力挺大，但学到东西
reviews.translated_content: Professor Chen Zhiwu teaches at a very high level. However, the workload is heavy, with frequent exams and a final paper. The pressure is quite high, but you do learn something.

course_info.title: Making Movies: Creative Expression on Screen

reviews.content: workload真的很小了，实践性很强，作业全部是自己运用拍摄手法拍摄，与小组follow简易电影制作过程拍摄短电影。主题内容不限，自由性很高，我想象力真是很差了，看了别人的作品才知道可以有这么多有趣的话题。 小组五个人只有我一个内地生。个人认为这门课与非大陆生组队，优点是见识许多很有才华又新奇的想法，缺点是很考验沟通。可能需要衡量一下。 这门课留给我最重要是学会发现以前忽视的风景和声音。
reviews.translated_content: The workload is really light. It’s very practical. All the assignments involve using filming techniques yourself, following a simple film production process with your group to shoot a short film. The theme is open, so there’s a lot of freedom. My imagination is really poor; I only realized how many interesting topics were possible after seeing other people’s work. There were five people in my group, and I was the only student from Mainland China. Personally, I think teaming up with non-Mainland students has the advantage of exposing you to many talented and novel ideas, but the downside is that it really tests your communication skills. You might need to weigh this up. The most important thing this course left me with was learning to discover scenery and sounds I had previously ignored.

reviews.content: 我是ding神，大电影叫the watch。摄影大师欢迎，最后a grade。ez boys
reviews.translated_content: I’m Ding Shen. Our big film project was called 'The Watch'. Shout-out to the cinematography experts. I got an A grade in the end. Easy, boys.

reviews.content: A。due很密集，大作品每周更新进度，所以被迫不至于拖due的情况。（本人有在非专业水平中自认为还不错的拍摄基础）并且在这门课上耗费挺大的精力（比专业课用心），所以每次assessments收到的grade和feedback都还算是fair。prof和tutor都不错，不是什么harsh的人；是真的可以收获满满的；很享受欣赏很有才华的peers的作品并且互相critique（虽然轮到自己的时候有些紧张），能学到很多。唯一遗憾的是公布了分数的70%左右assessments我都拿到了很高的分数，这门课又是给了grade对应分数的分数线的，最后的final project的feedback也是被评定了“very good”的水准，觉得再怎么济明明都可以轻松达到A+的分数线。发邮件问prof只是回了一句总分没有算错，难得这么用心好好学一门课没拿A+也没有解释有些遗憾吧。。。害。但课是好课（衷心建议：如果对艺术有自己的想法，害怕被不认同的话还是慎选创作型的。。。自己的作品都是亲儿子 被给了个B啥的都会很难受的。。除非你不care😂
reviews.translated_content: I got an A. Deadlines were very tight, with weekly progress updates required for the major project, so I was forced not to procrastinate. (I have a filming background that I consider decent for a non-professional.) I invested a lot of effort in this course—more than in my major courses—so the grades and feedback I received for each assessment were fairly reasonable. The professor and tutors are nice people and not harsh markers; you can genuinely gain a lot from the course. I really enjoyed appreciating my talented peers’ work and critiquing each other (though I felt a bit nervous when it was my turn), and I learned a lot. The only regret is that for about 70% of the graded assessments, I received high scores. Since the course publishes the grade boundaries corresponding to each letter grade, and even the final project feedback rated my work as “very good,” I feel I could have easily reached the A+ threshold if anything. When I emailed the professor, they just replied that the total score was calculated correctly. It’s a pity there was no further explanation, given how hard I worked on this course... Oh well. But it is a good course. (Sincere advice: if you have your own artistic ideas and fear they won’t be accepted, choose creative assignments with caution... Your own works are like your children, so getting a B or similar would feel terrible... unless you don’t care 😂)

reviews.content:
Fun and easy course if you already know filmmaking and want to get a grade boost. It gave me a good excuse to spend time making films, and I'm grateful for that. The feedback is detailed and personalized and really helped me improve each project. 

The downside is that the lectures and tutorials are quite lackluster in terms of teaching quality. The spoken explanations are disorganized and somewhat clumsy, and I don't think I would have learned very much had I not already known the merits of the topics being discussed.

reviews.content: 丘静美老师真的是比较文学系电影研究的宝藏老师（是大佬！），是一位非常渊博、智慧、敏锐，并且很鼓励学生的女性。课程相对来说不会讲太多technical的拍摄技巧（不超过介绍各种景别的程度，也不会教怎么用摄影机、怎么打光之类的，但是会介绍怎么画分镜、做拍摄计划之类），更偏向film studies的方法，用电影细读的方法讲音乐、蒙太奇等等。总之是一门鼓励大家拿起摄影机/手机，创造性地、自由地处理任何题材的好课！下课之后找她聊聊她参与过的电影，或是让她帮忙给自己做的电影提些建议，都会有很大的收获~（丘老师的惯常操作：学期快结束peer review的时候给大家一人发一块巧克力hahaha）给分的话我觉得还fair？自己的经验供参考：一些小拍摄任务在B+/A-左右，一个10%的小作业A；45%（还是55%来着）的 group project拿了B++；10% reflective paper拿了A，最后overall grade是A。
reviews.translated_content: Professor Qiu Jingmei is truly a treasure in the Department of Comparative Literature’s film studies programme (she’s an expert!). She is a very knowledgeable, wise, and sharp woman who is highly encouraging to students. The course doesn’t go into too many technical filming skills (it won’t go beyond introducing different shot types, and won’t teach you how to use a camera or set up lighting, but it will introduce storyboarding and shooting plans). It leans more towards film studies methods, using close reading of films to discuss music, montage, and so on. In short, it’s a great course that encourages everyone to pick up a camera or phone and creatively and freely handle any subject! After class, chatting with her about the films she has worked on, or asking for her advice on your own film projects, can be very rewarding. (Professor Qiu’s usual move: handing out a piece of chocolate to each student during peer review near the end of the semester hahaha.) As for grading, I think it’s quite fair? Here’s my experience for reference: some small filming tasks were around B+/A-; a 10% minor assignment got an A; the group project (45% or maybe 55%) got a B++; and the 10% reflective paper got an A, resulting in an overall grade of A.
