course_info.title: The Science of Crime Investigation

reviews.content: 你能看到这条评论，而且你对犯罪和侦查都有兴趣。那么不需要往下看了，赶紧选这门课。 这门课应该是港大近几年来改革程度最大的一门cc了，课程内容十分的活跃且内容十分充实。 1.真正意义上的翻转课堂。每两周一次lecture，形式近乎ccst9003。每次会公开一个游戏内容，小组聚在一起玩游戏，无沉闷课程内容。寓教于乐。所学皆以网课形式教授，时间灵活。 2. 所有案例均为实践案例（名字时间有所更改），超高代入感。现实中的悬疑案件往往比任何电视剧都要精彩。 3.无硬性workload，所有小组学习和讨论全为揭开你们组案件最后的谜底。tutor即为调查员，每周一次机会指示其进行某些项调查，获得结果。你的指示细节极为重要。（我们组就因为先调查证物上的dna而把上面的指纹污染了）。调查结果也是直接从现实警察处获得的拷贝。你能否改写现实将逃脱罪犯绳之以法，或者被其律师找到漏洞为其开脱，开启全新一个世界线的钥匙就在你手。 4.teli为这门课做了个手机ar app你敢信？！拿起你们组的地图，手机扫描，身临其境的进入现场，寻找藏在蛛丝马迹的线索。墙角里掉落的纤维，地毯上格格不入的暗红色花纹，还是死者身上伤口的形状或凶器进入的角度.......快把你的发现交给tutor调查，你所看见的都可能是最后决定性的证据。 5.超多福利，超多诱惑。本人一个学期通过小组作业收获总计$200星巴克券。 更多福利只有想不到。  选课提示： 1.因为这门课所有案件均为实例，所以不能留存任何电子形式文稿，包括证物或者口供的记录，照片或者复印件，只能以实体的一份档案袋传递。这给分析材料带来困难，哪怕小组内有序传递，每个人接触证物时间依然是有限的。所以对信息的收集和分析能力有一定的要求。 2.这门课为四校联办，小组成员可能来自中，科，理工。且私下小组讨论可能也须前往较为方便的学校。（我们组一半以上的人来自理工，所以每周我要跑差不多一次理工meeting）。如不是特别喜欢出门需慎重考虑。 3.小组规模较大，12人左右，难免会有free rider，不过好在硬性规定每周汇报贡献，不太会影响成绩，但是会让人很不爽。 4. 抱大腿！！！尤其是学医和学法的。没有前者尸检报告都看不懂。我反正是被正反六页全是伤口的尸检报告吓着了，前后连个死因也没有，没学医的都不知道死者是怎么受的伤怎么死的。没后者哪怕证据都找全了也会在最后的presentation上被被告律师（professor扮演）碾着打。  本人A+，推荐指数五星。
reviews.translated_content: If you’re seeing this comment and are interested in crime and investigation, you don’t need to read further—just enrol in this course immediately. This course has likely undergone the most significant reform among HKU Common Core courses in recent years. The content is very active and substantial. 1. It’s a flipped classroom in the true sense. Lectures are held once every two weeks, similar in format to CCST9003. Each session reveals a game scenario where groups gather to play, with no dull coursework. It’s edutainment. All learning materials are taught via online courses, offering flexible timing. 2. All cases are based on real-life examples (with names and dates changed), providing a high level of immersion. Real-life suspense cases are often more exciting than any TV drama. 3. There is no mandatory workload; all group study and discussion aims to uncover the final mystery of your group’s case. The tutor acts as an investigator. You have one chance per week to instruct them to conduct specific investigations and obtain results. The details of your instructions are extremely important. (Our group contaminated the fingerprints on evidence by investigating the DNA first). Investigation results are copies obtained directly from real police forces. Whether you can rewrite reality to bring the escaping criminal to justice, or have their lawyer find loopholes to exonerate them, the key to opening a new timeline is in your hands. 4. Can you believe TELI created a mobile AR app for this course?! Pick up your group’s map, scan it with your phone, and immerse yourself in the scene to find clues hidden in the tiniest details. Fibres dropped in a corner, incongruous dark red patterns on the carpet, or the shape of wounds on the deceased and the angle of entry of the weapon... Hand your findings over to the tutor for investigation; what you see could be the decisive evidence. 5. Lots of perks and temptations. In one semester, I earned a total of $200 in Starbucks vouchers through group assignments. There are more benefits than you can imagine. Enrolment tips: 1. Since all cases in this course are real instances, no electronic documents can be retained, including records, photos, or copies of evidence or statements. Only one physical file folder can be passed around. This makes analysing materials difficult; even with orderly circulation within the group, each person’s contact time with the evidence is limited. Therefore, there are certain requirements for information collection and analysis skills. 2. This course is jointly organised by four universities, so group members may come from CUHK, HKUST, and PolyU. Private group discussions may also require travelling to a more convenient university. (More than half of our group members were from PolyU, so I had to run to PolyU for meetings almost once a week). If you don’t particularly like going out, consider carefully. 3. The group size is large, around 12 people, so there are bound to be free riders. Fortunately, there is a strict rule requiring weekly contribution reports, so it doesn’t really affect grades, but it can be very annoying. 4. Rely on strong teammates!!! Especially those studying medicine and law. Without the former, you won’t even understand the autopsy report. I was scared stiff by a six-page autopsy report full of wounds, with no cause of death stated before or after. Those without medical training wouldn’t know how the deceased was injured or how they died. Without the latter, even if you find all the evidence, you’ll be crushed by the defendant’s lawyer (played by the professor) in the final presentation. I got an A+. Five-star recommendation.

reviews.content: 不要只看热评。除非你对法医刑侦这些痴迷到一定程度，都不要来，不要来，不要来，不要来，不要来。 workload巨大，专业性偏强。如果你不想在final期间顶着专业课的due们还搞cc的结课作业，快run！
reviews.translated_content: Don't just look at the top-rated reviews. Unless you are obsessed with forensic science and criminal investigation to a certain extent, do not come, do not come, do not come, do not come, do not come. The workload is huge, and it is quite specialised. If you don't want to handle the due dates for your major courses while also working on the final assignment for this Common Core course during finals period, get out while you can!

reviews.content: 非常难受 final期间几乎一直都在做final report 搞得很多其他课的任务甚至被耽误了 结果付出与回报不成正比 只有B+ 这么大的workload却这么差的给分我真的很难受 做的我心力憔悴累死累活把其他好龟课豁出去了最后收到这样的结果我真的非常非常难受 早知道就选其他又水又好龟的cc了 害 气话虽然这么说 课还是好课的 内容充实干货很多 但是隔周开一次两三个小时的gp小组会议是真的有点顶不住 太累太累了 真的 除非真的对刑侦非常非常感兴趣 别来 别来 快跑 费力不讨好 真的
reviews.translated_content: It was very unpleasant. During the finals period, I was almost constantly working on the final report, which caused me to fall behind on tasks for many other courses. The effort didn’t match the reward; I only got a B+. With such a huge workload but such poor grading, I’m really upset. I exhausted myself and sacrificed other GPA-friendly courses, only to receive this result. I’m extremely, extremely upset. If I had known, I would have chosen other Common Core courses that were easier and offered better grades. Sigh. Although these are angry words, the course itself is good. The content is substantial and genuinely useful. However, having two- or three-hour group project meetings every other week is really a bit much. It’s too tiring, really. Unless you are truly, truly interested in criminal investigation, don’t come. Don’t come. Stay away. It’s not worth the effort. Really.

reviews.content: Wincy说24-25 Sem2是最后一次开这个课了，之后她会开一门新的课。lecture内容不算硬核，有很多额外内容，客座博士的分享还挺有意思的，（可能因为Wincy在cc的办公室担任一些职位？）学生分享cc技巧的部分有点无聊。
reviews.translated_content: Wincy said that 24–25 Sem 2 is the last time this course will be offered; she will open a new course afterwards. The lecture content isn’t particularly rigorous; there is a lot of extra material. The guest PhD shares were quite interesting. (Perhaps because Wincy holds some positions in the Common Core office?) The student-sharing section on Common Core tips was a bit boring.

reviews.content: 一开始选课前犹豫过很久，因为RIC的评论几乎每个都在说work load大，结果还是选了。感谢当时的选择，让它成为了我最喜欢的课。 确实很难很难，reflective portfolio反复被批评，和不配合的同学组队查法医专业术语查到怀疑人生（我还是med院的）。如果不是真心喜欢刑侦建议不要选，但若你对犯罪调查感兴趣，是一个忠实的侦探小说粉，一定要选它。这可能是你人生中唯一一次能接触到这么多专业的犯罪材料并享受破案过程了。
reviews.translated_content: I hesitated for a long time before choosing this course, because almost every review on RIC said the workload was heavy. In the end, I still enrolled. I’m grateful for that choice, as it became my favourite course. It is indeed very, very difficult. My reflective portfolio was criticised repeatedly, and working with uncooperative teammates to look up forensic terminology made me question my life choices (and I’m from the Faculty of Medicine). If you don’t genuinely like criminal investigation, I suggest you don’t take it. But if you are interested in crime investigation and are a loyal fan of detective novels, you must take it. This might be the only time in your life when you get to access so many professional crime materials and enjoy the process of solving cases.

reviews.content: wl比较大，难好🐢
reviews.translated_content: The workload is quite heavy, and it’s difficult to get a good grade.

reviews.content: 课程内容挺有意思的，需要有长期的组队project
reviews.translated_content: The course content is quite interesting, but it requires a long-term group project.

reviews.content: 不错的课程，颇为有意思但是总体来讲需要对课程以及其理论有兴趣才能学好。最终的project和midterm大部分的资料都需要自己去找。
reviews.translated_content: A good course, quite interesting, but generally you need to be interested in the course and its theories to do well. For the final project and midterm, you have to find most of the materials yourself.

reviews.content: 课程内容比较有趣，assessment中group work占比不小，如果被分配到freerider多的小组，workload巨大还会烂龟
reviews.translated_content: The course content is quite interesting. Group work makes up a significant portion of the assessment. If you are assigned to a group with many free riders, the workload becomes huge and the grading harsh.

reviews.content: 总结:wl超级超级大，龟一般，课很好 详细说说:对刑侦+法医尸检感兴趣又不介意大wl和很一般的龟的话非常推荐！上课都是干货满满，lecturer和tutor都是超级大牛，能学到非常多的东西！但是给龟很一般...而且因为是接近10个人的大组，所以可能无法避免的会有各种麻烦的情况。wl非常大，很多个report都是十几页二十几页的写，要生啃各种法医报告和刑侦报告，还有视频要做(期末报告视频要求3-40min)。我们组的报告在最后阶段当时是得到了tutor非常高的认可和肯定的，案件和找到的真实案件内容也几乎是还原了，但是最后还是给了个B，总之想要轻松又好龟的话不建议选
reviews.translated_content: Summary: The workload is huge, the grading is average, but the course is excellent. In detail: If you’re interested in criminal investigation and forensic autopsy, and don’t mind a heavy workload and merely average grading, this course comes highly recommended! The lectures are packed with substantive content, and both the lecturer and tutors are top experts, so you can learn a great deal. However, the grading is just average... Also, because it involves large groups of nearly 10 people, various troublesome situations are unavoidable. The workload is very heavy: many reports are 10–20+ pages long, requiring you to digest forensic and investigative reports, and there are video assignments (the final report video must be 30–40 minutes). Our group’s report received very high praise and affirmation from the tutor in the final stage, and the case we presented was almost a faithful reconstruction of a real case, but we still ended up with a B. In short, if you want an easy ride and a good grade, I wouldn’t recommend this course.

reviews.content: 超爱这门课，lecture 质量高且没有 gp，点燃了我对天文学的兴趣。第一次作业没摸到头脑连 mean 都没上，但后来认真学很快赶上来了。final 有点难，相对来说比较偏文科。最后出分 a。对科学史以及基础天文学感兴趣的无脑冲
reviews.translated_content: I love this course. The lectures are high quality and there is no group project, which sparked my interest in astronomy. I didn’t get the hang of the first assignment and didn’t even reach the mean, but after studying seriously, I caught up quickly. The final was a bit difficult and leaned more towards the humanities side. I ended up with an A. If you are interested in the history of science and basic astronomy, go for it without hesitation.

reviews.content: 真的对天文学感兴趣的还是别上这门了…虽然也收获了一点insights 但感觉一半时间都是在讲人文科学的内容 final考试的内容也是那种“这门课给你什么启发”之类的比谁能bb的问题
reviews.translated_content: If you’re genuinely interested in astronomy, don’t take this course… Although I gained some insights, it felt like half the time was spent on humanities content. The final exam also consisted of questions like “What inspiration did this course give you?”—basically a competition to see who could bluff or talk their way through it best.

reviews.content: 虽然这门课总体上是挺理的，很多知识过硬，但毕竟可以学会。个人高考大文，前三分之一基本是高中地理讲过的内容，后面的科学史比较考验文科能力（？）最后A
reviews.translated_content: Although this course is generally quite logical and the knowledge is solid, it is learnable. My background in the Gaokao was humanities-focused, so the first third basically covered content from high school geography. The later part on the history of science tests your humanities skills (?). I got an A in the end.

reviews.content: 不实名呕吐，lecturer上课就是paraphrase PPT，assignment要求什么的就不说清楚，课程内容也很无聊，总之不推荐。
reviews.translated_content: I’m vomiting without naming names. The lecturer just paraphrases the PowerPoint slides in class. Assignment requirements are not explained clearly, and the course content is boring. In short, not recommended.

reviews.content: 教授会从最早人们如何观星开始讲起，没有物理基础也完全可以上！没有group project，但是有final，最后龟还挺好的，感觉社恐人可冲
reviews.translated_content: The professor starts from how people observed the stars in ancient times. You can take this course even without a physics background! There is no group project, but there is a final exam. The grade turned out quite well. I feel that people who are very uncomfortable with social participation should go for it.

reviews.content: 讲天文学历史以及天文学概念的演变，以及感受人如何从认识宇宙到认识自己。 非常硬核的一门课，天文学知识挺考逻辑的，而且比较天马行空一点，会给你一些奇奇怪怪的设定去推演历法、季节、月相等，本人逻辑不是特别好所以选了PF workload适中吧，每节课都有quiz，难度不高
reviews.translated_content: It covers the history of astronomy and the evolution of astronomical concepts, exploring how humanity moved from understanding the universe to understanding itself. This is a highly rigorous course. Astronomy knowledge tests your logic quite a bit, and it involves some imaginative scenarios where you deduce calendars, seasons, moon phases, etc., based on strange premises. My logic isn’t great, so I took it on a pass/fail basis. The workload is moderate; there is a quiz every class, but the difficulty is not high.

reviews.content: 个人觉得对文科生不太友好555，本来期待是一门讲天文理论知识的课（比如如何观星之类），结果是讲天文史orz。感觉整学期和老师的逻辑都不在一条线上，上得不太快乐。
reviews.translated_content: Personally, I feel it’s not very friendly for arts students (crying). I originally expected a course on astronomical theory (like how to stargaze), but it turned out to be about the history of astronomy. I felt like my logic was never on the same wavelength as the teacher’s throughout the semester, so I wasn’t very happy.

reviews.content: 真的要很熱愛天文才選 不然就像我一樣感覺努力了也學不到東西
reviews.translated_content: You really need to love astronomy to choose this; otherwise, you’ll end up like me, feeling that even with effort, you don’t learn anything.

reviews.content: 纯纯烂课 别选
reviews.translated_content: Purely a terrible course. Don't choose it.

reviews.content: A+. 4 short q assignments. test and exam allow cheatsheets. no need to do calculations. humorous lecturers. very friendly course for introverts.
reviews.translated_content: A+. 4 short q assignments. test and exam allow cheatsheets. no need to do calculations. humorous lecturers. very friendly course for introverts.

reviews.content: 给分不好

reviews.content: 龟是挺满意的，但是对于教授，Tutor的态度很不满意。除了他们对于教学的不负责任之外，教授在一次作业中，备选的Topic包括 “衡量水炮车对于环境的影响”与“衡量催泪弹对环境的影响”，有加入政治因素的感觉。在网课这一学期，Workload中等，Midterm和Final的题目需要好好看PPT准备，一个Environmental Project和Infographics都需要花2-3天准备

course_info.title: Science and Music
course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content:
A range.
如果对音乐和科学都比较感兴趣的还挺推荐的，一开始会学一些声学wave什么的，发声原理和传声，后面会无聊一些学各种乐器的分类和构造，最后还有挺多比较抽象的历史，不过final是全选择题而且开卷，基本上ppt看个透然后花点时间记一下重点词，开卷考试应该能做出来一半以上（prof说final可以用chatgpt但据我的经验基本没用，按照ppt原话来选择是最稳妥的）；然后gp和essay只要做的不太烂，不要太摆烂感觉应该就有好结果，注意essay要更多的将自己的观点而不是堆积citation！强推tutor Kar Man Leung人特别好很nice，然后要跟tutor多沟通能改进的地方；总体来说只要认真去学ppt上的内容，再稍微花点时间去整理和理解ppt肯定能a range！
最后prof是谁不知道名字但是讲话很小声讲的也不太好，不过不靠prof也是可以滴！
reviews.translated_content: A-range grade. If you are interested in both music and science, it’s quite recommended. At the beginning, you learn some acoustics, waves, principles of sound production and transmission. Later, it gets a bit boring as you learn about the classification and structure of various instruments. Finally, there is quite a bit of abstract history. However, the final is entirely multiple-choice and open-book. Basically, if you go through the PPTs thoroughly and spend some time memorizing key terms, you should be able to get more than half right in the open-book exam. (The prof said you could use ChatGPT for the final, but in my experience, it was basically useless. Choosing answers based on the exact wording in the PPTs is the safest strategy.) Also, as long as your group project and essay are not too bad, and you don’t slack off too much, you should get a good result. Note that for the essay, you should express more of your own views rather than just piling up citations! I strongly recommend tutor Kar Man Leung. She is very nice. Communicate with your tutor more about areas for improvement. Overall, as long as you seriously study the content on the PPTs and spend a little extra time organizing and understanding them, you can definitely get an A-range grade! Finally, I don’t know the professor’s name. He speaks very quietly and doesn’t teach very well, but you can manage without relying on the professor!

reviews.content: 不是对音乐真爱的最好别选，对music nerd强烈建议选的一门课。比较偏向物理声学的方向，内容cover了声波，各种乐器的工作原理，concert hall design，不同的temperament（律制）等等，对我的音乐学习帮助非常大。配合一些音乐系的课一起学会有bonus的效果！但是纯看个人兴趣，对了解律制、声学等等内容不感兴趣的朋友们就快逃吧，但如果有和我一样对音乐真爱的朋友的话，我相信你能学到很多。lecturer和tutor（Shum Shengyun Alex)都超有趣，都是物理专业但是非常爱音乐会很多乐器的有趣的灵魂。但是quiz很难，特别难，回到被高中物理课支配的恐惧……group project是向layman解释一个自己挑选的音乐物理原理，我和一个朋友碰到两个local free rider，final的时候真的非常痛苦了，不过后来tutor给我们组每个人分开打分还问我们是不是碰到了free rider，人真滴超好
reviews.translated_content: If you don’t truly love music, it’s best not to take this course, but I strongly recommend it for music nerds. It leans more towards the physics of acoustics, covering sound waves, the working principles of various instruments, concert hall design, different temperaments, and so on. It was extremely helpful for my music studies. Taking it alongside some Music Department courses gives you a bonus effect! However, it really depends on personal interest. If you’re not interested in learning about temperaments, acoustics, and similar topics, run away. But if you’re like me and have a true passion for music, I believe you’ll learn a lot. The lecturer and tutor (Shum Shengyun Alex) are both super interesting; they are physics majors but have fascinating souls who love concerts and play many instruments. However, the quizzes are hard—really hard—bringing back the fear of being dominated by high school physics classes... The group project involves explaining a chosen physics principle of music to laypeople. My friend and I encountered two local free riders, which made the final period really painful. Later, the tutor graded each of us separately and even asked if we had encountered free riders. They are genuinely super nice.

reviews.content: A+ / 几乎没学到什么有意思的东西。Final quiz出题扣ppt细节，只要认真复习不会有差错，而且开卷考试。gp选题一定要和tutor好好交流，选的主题大于一切，scientific的部分要有意思。只要能impress tutor会得到很好的分数。
reviews.translated_content: A+. I learned almost nothing interesting. The final quiz questions focus on PPT details; as long as you revise carefully, you won’t make mistakes, and it’s an open-book exam. For the group project, you must communicate well with your tutor when choosing a topic; the theme is everything. The scientific part needs to be interesting. As long as you can impress the tutor, you will get a good grade.

reviews.content: 两个字，快逃
reviews.translated_content: Two words: stay away.

reviews.content:
这个课需要做两次group presentation（一次practise一次final，两次都打分）；还要交两篇文章，考期末。这些assessment就特别的零散，deadline一个接一个的，就很烦。而且presentation找好队友很关键，要不然会有点不愉快。

reviews.translated_content: This course requires two group presentations (one practice, one final; both are graded) and two essays, plus a final exam. These assessments are very scattered, with deadlines coming one after another, which is annoying. Also, finding good teammates for the presentations is crucial; otherwise, it can be unpleasant. The lecture content is quite interesting; both lectures and tutorials include many demonstrations to help you understand physical phenomena. I think the course content is decent, and you can learn something. However, I really can’t stand this assessment structure of presentations + essays + final exam. It causes a huge pile-up of deadlines at the end of the semester, and juggling all three aspects is quite exhausting. If you can handle scattered due dates, I think the experience is okay.

reviews.instructor: Ng, Tuen Wai,  Zheng Hua,  Edmond K.M. Leung (导师)
reviews.content: 课程内容： 我们 2020 - 2021 第一学期首先讲了有疫情背景的 SIR 模型，相关的一些参数，它们之间关系和疫情模型的简单演示和计算。之后讲到博弈论的纳什平衡（Nash Equilibrium），讲到合作博弈过程中各方利益分配计算的沙普利值（Shapley Value）及其在多个场景下的运用等等。课程后半期显得无聊一些，讲了密码学一些算法，本福特定律（Benford's Law），以及人工智能一些基本数据处理方法等。  课程任务： 主要有每节课的小作业（难度不大，尽情对答案），习题课参与考评。一个小组项目：基于一个生活中可以使用到数学情境的地方来做分析，要求做经济学、游戏学中一些相关理论的文献调研等。也可以自行创设生活情境，运用先前学习过的纳什平衡、沙普利值等对情境中问题答案进行探索。小组项目四人一组可以找到内地生朋友一起做；本地生层次各异有努力做的也有只是划水的，关键要在 WhatsAPP 等社交空间中积极跟进每位成员的进展。项目呈现：草案（5%）+ PPT 讲演（10%）和最终项目报告（20%）。  课程考试： 因为疫情原因本身好好的有纸笔 Past Paper 考试（30%）的一门课改为线上 6 个填空题的考试容易一招不慎满盘皆输，填空题虽然不难，但一旦做错就没了整门课5%的分数，这里是有些坑的地方。其它作业和项目我们做的都很好估计我就是在这门考试上栽了，没拿到预想中的 A+ 或者 A。  课程老师： 第一位本地老师 Leung 教学风趣课堂互动也比较多，但是后边的 Zheng Hua 等教课受吐槽率比较高，因为课程内容本身就有些无聊的情况下，老师上课也没有创设很好的互动。导师人很好，一节课可以流畅、饱满地带领大家一起做几个 Tutorial 习题，或者在课程后期做小组项目的展示  课程总评： 总体而言这门课可以给我们带来一些生活中数学理论的启蒙。由于其 workload 不大，给分又相对可以，很适合用来作为大一练手入手的 CC。
reviews.translated_content: Course content: In the first semester, we started with the SIR model in the context of the pandemic, covering related parameters, their relationships, and simple demonstrations and calculations of pandemic models. Then we moved on to Nash Equilibrium in game theory, discussing the Shapley Value for calculating benefit distribution in cooperative games and its applications in various scenarios. The latter half of the course felt a bit boring, covering some cryptography algorithms, Benford's Law, and basic data processing methods in artificial intelligence.  Course tasks: Mainly small assignments after each class (not difficult, feel free to compare answers) and participation in tutorial sessions which were assessed. There was one group project: analyze a real-life situation where mathematics can be applied, requiring literature reviews on related theories in economics and game studies. You could also create your own life scenario and use previously learned concepts like Nash Equilibrium and Shapley Value to explore solutions. For the group project, teams of four could include friends from Mainland China; local students varied in effort, with some working hard and others just coasting. The key was to actively follow up on each member's progress via social platforms like WhatsApp. Project presentation: Draft (5%) + PPT presentation (10%) and final project report (20%).  Course exam: Due to the pandemic, what was originally a proper pen-and-paper past paper exam (30%) was changed to an online exam with 6 fill-in-the-blank questions, making it easy to lose everything with one careless mistake. Although the fill-in-the-blank questions weren't hard, getting one wrong meant losing 5% of the total course grade, which was a bit of a trap. We did well on other assignments and the project, so I estimate that I stumbled on this exam and didn't get the A+ or A I had expected.  Course instructors: The first local instructor, Leung, taught in an engaging way with plenty of classroom interaction. However, Zheng Hua and others who taught later received more complaints because, given the already somewhat boring course content, they didn't create good interaction in class. The tutor was very nice; in one session, they could smoothly and comprehensively lead everyone through several tutorial exercises, or help with group project presentations in the later stages of the course.  Overall evaluation: Overall, this course can provide some enlightenment on mathematical theories in daily life. Since its workload is not heavy and grading is relatively fair, it is very suitable as a introductory Common Core course for first-year students.

reviews.content: 建议新生的话最好高中接触过基础数学竞赛或者数学很好的国际生才学，个人数学bg alevel普数高数A*，step grade2，tutor是tim感觉还可以不像评价写的那样啊😂 gp扣10，quiz漏做两次，作业扣两分，final比原来难很多而且跟assignment的题型也不是很相似（作业的数论和概率都像是小学生做的，final数论考了要求证明11的整除特征和一个很像高考数列题的概率题还要用到求极限）发挥的还行，预估B+最后A-。
reviews.translated_content: For freshmen, I’d recommend this only if you have some background in basic math competitions from high school or are an international student with strong math skills. My math background: A-Level Pure Math and Further Math both A*, STEP Grade 2. The tutor is Tim; he’s okay, not as bad as the reviews suggest 😂. I lost 10% on the group project, missed two quizzes, and lost 2 marks on assignments. The final was much harder than before and the question types weren’t very similar to the assignments (the number theory and probability in assignments felt like elementary school level, but the final tested proving the divisibility rule for 11 in number theory and a probability question resembling a Gaokao sequence problem that required limits). I performed decently, predicted B+ but ended up with A-.

Be extremely careful when choosing your topic, otherwise you’ll end up with a bare passing grade. I missed one question on the final, my group project score was just above passing, and everything else was full marks, but I still only got a B+.

reviews.content: 课程的内容本身很有意思，里面讲 数学和很多有趣的东西结合，比如说数学与爱情，数学与离婚等。 但是平时的作业比较难也有点多，并且最后需要完成论文和考试，总体不算非常容易，但上的很开心。

However, the regular assignments are quite difficult and numerous, and you ultimately need to complete an essay and an exam. It's not very easy overall, but I enjoyed the class.

reviews.content: gp搞得很烂（基本没见过比我们低的，虽然也不太能拉开差距但是gp总共占35分呢），因为本人数学还好最后final相比去年难了很多导致有了一些区分度，fianl基本全会也拿了A range

Since my math skills are decent, and the final exam was much harder than last year’s, creating some distinction, I managed to get an A-range grade despite basically knowing all the final exam questions.

reviews.instructor: Prof. T. W. Ng., Dr. Yung, Dr. Hua etc.
reviews.content: 如果对game theory，数学小游戏等话题感兴趣的的话很推荐选这门课，assignment由难变易，第一partPatrick教的挺好，Group Project中规中矩给分也不错，期末考虽然在最后一天（当然网课时代嘛肯定就不是了）但是在网考时代是本人唯一一门加入了防作弊机制的随机题库考试，题目也不会太难，对理科生来讲A+是一个不难的事情，文科生可以试听一下最难的前几节课再看看啦
reviews.translated_content: If you’re interested in topics like game theory and mathematical games, this course is highly recommended. The assignments go from difficult to easier. Patrick teaches the first part quite well. The Group Project is standard, and the grading is decent. Although the final exam was on the last day (though of course that didn’t apply in the online era), it was the only course where I encountered a randomised question bank with anti-cheating measures during the online exam period. The questions weren’t too difficult, so for science students, getting an A+ is not hard. Humanities students might want to audit the first few hardest lectures before deciding.

course_info.requirement: 无前置要求或未提供相关数据

reviews.content: （怎么看不到其他评价了）课程本身挺有意思的，题目看上去和生物相关其实没太大关系，实际上是地球史和天文相关，需要一点高中化学和初中物理。前半部分是kono，讲得很有意思但是容量也大。最后几节课是liyiliang，和前面的内容有点重合也有点无聊。开学说的是每节课结束前都有小测（需要复习讲义），但是执行情况看kono是不是讲high了刹不住车了。。anyway最后小测成绩去掉两次最差记的分。还有两次线上quiz（超简单），一次debate（打分按个人和小组两部分，本人拿了13/15），一次ai相关作业（选题比较关键，18/20），一次小组poster pre（主包大一高考生不知道什么是poster最终喜提21/30）。最终拿A。
reviews.translated_content: (Why can’t I see other reviews?) The course itself is quite interesting. Although the title seems biology-related, it’s not really; it’s actually about Earth’s history and astronomy, requiring some high school chemistry and middle school physics. The first part was taught by kono, who lectured in an engaging way but covered a lot of material. The last few classes were taught by liyiliang, which overlapped slightly with earlier content and was a bit boring. At the start of the term, it was said that there would be a small quiz at the end of each class (requiring review of the handouts), but whether this happened depended on whether kono got too carried away to stop... Anyway, the two lowest quiz scores were dropped in the final calculation. There were also two online quizzes (super easy), one debate (graded based on individual and group components; I got 13/15), one AI-related assignment (topic selection was key; I got 18/20), and one group poster presentation (as a first-year student with a Gaokao background, I didn’t know what a poster was and somehow ended up with 21/30). I ultimately received an A.

reviews.content: Digital devices are not allowed during lectures, and no chatting too. Would say the workload is big (with weekly non-open-book quizzes, essays, debates, group projects…), so really be ready to dedicate some time into studying. They talked more about planets and stuff, and though i know only a little Chemistry + Physics, I got an A at last. (but really used a lot of time in studying)
reviews.translated_content: Digital devices are not allowed during lectures, and no chatting either. I’d say the workload is heavy (with weekly non-open-book quizzes, essays, debates, group projects…), so really be ready to dedicate some time to studying. They talked more about planets and stuff, and although I only know a little Chemistry and Physics, I got an A in the end. (But I really spent a lot of time studying.)

reviews.content: 别上，体验感奇差。我的评价是如果你抢不到又好又好龟的cc课，这门可以勉强顶一下，毕竟它给龟还行。但你要问上课体验完全就是拉屎。
reviews.translated_content: Don’t take it; the experience is terrible. My verdict: if you can’t snatch a Common Core course that is both good and GPA-friendly, this one can barely serve as a substitute, since its grading is acceptable. But if you ask about the class experience, it’s absolutely awful.

search_summary.title: Understanding Climate Change

course_info.title: Understanding Climate Change

reviews.content: 今年好像是换prof了，课程内容又少又简单wl巨小，教的基本都是常识，初中生来学都完全没问题。给分个人觉得还不错，蛮松的，一起上的朋友都是A range（好像不咋curve？）非常满意。
reviews.translated_content: It seems like they changed the professor this year. The course content is sparse and simple, and the workload is extremely light. What’s taught is basically common sense; even a middle-school student could handle it without problems. Personally, I think the grading is quite good and rather lenient. Friends who took it with me all got A-range grades (it doesn’t seem to be curved much?). Very satisfied.

reviews.content: 有啲難，因為要用英文學地理咁對於高中唔係英文嘅同學真係唔容易
reviews.translated_content: It’s a bit difficult because you have to learn geography in English, which is really not easy for students whose high school education was not in English.

reviews.content: 总体而言还不错，最后拿了最高的A（这门课不给A+，但用点心拿个A range问题不大）。wl在cc中算中等程度，每周lecture就是一些科普讲座（可能有点无聊 但有一节课是电影）tutorial的话占分多比较重要，前两三次都是模拟lab，要用excel分析数据做各种表，但是只要跟着tutor的节奏一步一步走基本能拿满分。后面会要做一个group game，难度不大但占分很高。然后整个sem要求做一个photo或video essay，在🇭🇰各地考察气候变化，不要拖到最后。外加一份scientific report，本大一新生0基础也能轻松handle。期末会有一个开卷当堂quiz，基本都是ppt里的内容。⚠️提醒：有一些bonus point千万要争取 能拿的尽量拿，不拿bonus的话可能连B都拿不到（一个朋友的血泪教训）。还有 有个tutor是大陆人 Liu Jiacheng，英语水平真的…….一言难尽
reviews.translated_content: Overall, it’s not bad. I got the highest possible A (this course doesn’t award A+, but if you put in some effort, getting an A-range grade is not a problem). The workload is moderate for a Common Core course. Weekly lectures are basically popular science talks (maybe a bit boring, but one session was a movie). Tutorials carry more weight and are quite important. The first two or three sessions were mock labs where you use Excel to analyze data and create various tables, but as long as you follow the tutor’s pace step by step, you can basically get full marks. Later, there’s a group game, which isn’t difficult but carries high weight. Then, throughout the semester, you need to produce a photo or video essay investigating climate change across Hong Kong—don’t leave it until the last minute. There’s also a scientific report, which even a first-year student with zero background can handle easily. At the end, there’s an open-book in-class quiz, mostly based on content from the slides. ⚠️ Reminder: Make sure to strive for those bonus points; take whatever you can. If you don’t get the bonus points, you might not even get a B (a friend’s painful lesson). Also, one tutor is from Mainland China, Liu Jiacheng, and his English level is really… hard to describe.

reviews.content: 因为online导致field trip取消，趣味少了一些。总体无功无过。
reviews.translated_content: The field trip was cancelled because of online delivery, so it was a bit less fun. Overall, it was neither good nor bad.

reviews.content: 感觉要理科比较强的同学才适合，以为是对天文地理有兴趣就报了。但发现course 的内容包含了更多数学的运算，会用excel算数做统计图的选比较划算
reviews.translated_content: I feel that only students with a strong science background are suitable. I enrolled because I thought I was interested in astronomy and geography. But I found that the course content involves more mathematical calculations. It’s more worthwhile for those who are comfortable using Excel for calculations and making statistical charts.

reviews.content: Online 课程取消了field trip 和film discussion有些可惜，但还是会有一些alternative project。听了课，在做project的时候多跟老师沟通就没什么问题。印象最深的是利用南极冰川分析气温和温室气体变化的project，蛮有意思。最后的quiz有点小难，需要仔细复习slides，龟的话付出和收获成正比吧，wl不小。这门课由多名老师一起上，其中Jess非常nice，很容易看出她对climate change这个议题的热情，问问题解答得很清楚，回邮件也快！本人是热爱地理的文科生，对这门st感到满足。
reviews.translated_content: It’s a pity that the field trip and film discussion were cancelled for the online version of the course, but there were some alternative projects. If you attend the lectures and communicate more with the instructor while working on the project, you’ll be fine. The most memorable part was the project analyzing temperature and greenhouse gas changes using Antarctic ice cores, which was quite interesting. The final quiz was a bit difficult and required careful review of the slides. As for the grade, the outcome is proportional to the effort you put in; the workload is not small. This course is taught by multiple instructors. Jess is very nice; you can easily see her passion for the topic of climate change. She answers questions clearly and replies to emails quickly! As an arts student who loves geography, I felt satisfied with this ST course.

reviews.content: um 网课感觉跟没上过这课一样 感觉这课的灵魂在于fieldtrip吧 建议还是有得线下的时候选
reviews.translated_content: Um, the online classes felt like I hadn't even taken this course. I feel like the soul of this course is the field trip. I'd recommend choosing it when there are in-person options available.

reviews.content: A+龟巨好，wl很小，老师可爱，但学到的东西感觉没有很多（可能我平时也比较关注这方面？）对气候变化不太了解的同学应该能学到不少
reviews.translated_content: An A+ is very attainable, the workload is light, and the teacher is cute, but I feel like I didn’t learn that much (maybe because I already pay attention to this area?). Students who don’t know much about climate change should be able to learn quite a bit.

reviews.content: 非常inspiring
reviews.translated_content: 非常inspiring

reviews.content: 容易又好龟
reviews.translated_content: Easy and generous grading.

course_info.title: Sustainable Development of the Built Environment
course_info.requirement: Your enrollment must comply with the requirements of Common Core (CC) and your programme. Contact commoncore@hku.hk for enquiries."

reviews.content: 讲的东西我不是很感兴趣，纯抱着想找一个好龟cc的心态选了这门课，平时作业wl很小，上课讲的知识点比较多且杂，group project占比35%所以找到几个好的队友很重要，如果认识大佬的话建议和大佬选同一个tutorial time slot因为这样子分到同组的概率比较高，整体来说还行吧就是期末前要背的东西很多，建议考试前刷past paper因为这次期末甚至考到了18还是17年的原题，总之考试的出题风格没有什么大变化，最后A。
reviews.translated_content: I wasn’t very interested in the topics; I chose this Common Core course purely hoping for a good grade. The regular assignment workload was light. The lectures covered many scattered knowledge points. The group project accounts for 35%, so finding good teammates is crucial. If you know any very strong students, I suggest choosing the same tutorial time slot as them, as this increases the chance of being grouped together. Overall, it was acceptable, but there was a lot to memorise before the final exam. I recommend practising with past papers, because this year’s final even included original questions from 2018 or 2017. In short, the exam style hasn’t changed much. I got an A in the end.

reviews.content: 谁跟我说这课好龟的.jpg   这门课三个部分，第一部分侧重香港交通的历史，但是考试会要求从stakeholder、professionals什么角度分析某个交通项目；第二部分可以看成是要求背记更多技术细节的高中人文地理（可持续发展）；第三部分比较杂，可持续发展科技、能源之类的。最后的考试很……大致三个部分出四道默写，有信心背300+页PPT就选吧。除此之外还有field trip、presentation和撰写报告，强制随机组队，随缘吧。最后B+
reviews.translated_content: Who told me this course has generous grading? .jpg This course has three parts. The first part focuses on the history of transportation in Hong Kong, but the exam requires you to analyze a transportation project from the perspectives of stakeholders, professionals, etc. The second part can be seen as high-school-level human geography (sustainable development) that requires memorizing more technical details. The third part is quite miscellaneous, covering sustainable development technologies, energy, and so on. The final exam is... roughly four dictation-style questions drawn from the three parts. Choose this course only if you are confident enough to memorize 300+ pages of PPT. In addition, there are field trips, presentations, and report writing, with mandatory random team formation—just leave it to fate. In the end, I got a B+.

reviews.content: 比ECON1210还难！全是简答题，tutorial和lecture顺序全是乱的，考的也是乱七八糟的，给的learning outcome根本看不完，花了一堆时间什么用没有，差评！！！！！！！！high workload！
reviews.translated_content: Harder than ECON1210! It’s all short-answer questions. The order of tutorials and lectures is completely messy, and the exams are chaotic too. The provided learning outcomes are impossible to finish reading. I spent a ton of time for nothing. Would not recommend!!!!!! High workload!

reviews.content: 这门课有点抽象期末要背的好多 而且有一位tutor真的很不supportive影响了我对这门课的观感（不过其他tutor们人还是不错的） 期末太忙了只背完了一半最后b+…
reviews.translated_content: This course is a bit bizarre; there is a lot to memorise for the final. Also, one of the tutors is really unsupportive, which affected my perception of the course (though the other tutors are quite nice). I was too busy at the end of the semester and only managed to memorise half of the material, ending up with a B+...

reviews.content: workload相对较小，平时没什么作业就每节课前预习一下就好，最后的group presentation和group report 可能会稍微多花一点时间，如果对于城市规划建设，可持续发展之类比较感兴趣的话，lecture会涉及很多内容，tutorial感觉比较无聊基本都是重复lecture的内容，最后考试之前要多背一些ppt上的内容，最后拿了A，目前为止龟最好的一门CC
reviews.translated_content: The workload is relatively light. There’s hardly any homework; just preview before each class. The final group presentation and group report might take a bit more time. If you’re interested in urban planning, construction, or sustainable development, the lectures cover a lot. The tutorials feel rather boring and mostly repeat the lecture content. Before the final exam, you need to memorise a lot of content from the PowerPoint slides. I ended up with an A; so far, this is the Common Core course where I’ve achieved the best grade.

reviews.content: workload 一般 grade不错 tutorial感觉一般
reviews.translated_content: Workload is average, grades are good, but the tutorials feel just so-so.

reviews.content: 真的是惊了，拿了A-，一堆知识点我根本背不完。考试考的我全不会，我在那里拿可怜的知识储备量硬扯瞎编，居然拿了A-，我以为这课要拿C呢。我考试旁边一个哥们考到一半突然唉声叹气，然后就趴下去睡觉了。因为好多题我根本没复习到，我就想到啥写啥，居然A-
reviews.translated_content: I was genuinely shocked to get an A-. There were so many knowledge points that I couldn't possibly memorize them all. I didn't know how to answer any of the exam questions, so I just relied on my limited knowledge base to bluff and make things up, and somehow got an A-. I thought I would get a C in this course. A guy sitting next to me during the exam suddenly sighed heavily halfway through and then put his head down to sleep. Since I hadn't reviewed many of the topics, I just wrote whatever came to mind, and surprisingly got an A-.

reviews.content: 嗯，m可以来尝试一下这门课，呵呵，宝子你继续。谁不想每周急头白脸既复习了ppt又看了reading，reference paper也写满了，然后对着问得莫名其妙又很controversial的quiz上的一堆医学生物专有名词挠头。好吧，我确实reading只是浏览（ppt确实是每个角落都看了），但是期望一个学生每周看完lecture大约有40-50页的ppt又看完2篇每篇有20页左右的生物学术论文不太好吧。CC不是主课而且并不是所有学生都是学生物的。嗯对，大概就是也有简单一点的quiz吧， 可以3/4或者得满的，但是多数quiz不是。我不知道为什么那么多人给好评，因为本人它不好龟罢 （好吧，如果每次quiz都是平均水平但是靠gp work也能得A range当然也很好龟了）只不过我现在没出分，也不知可否靠gp力挽狂澜（我已经尽一切所能得软性分数了，如果真靠gp得A range了，当我没发这段话）。只是单纯觉得这课完美继承了CC特有的玄学特点，quiz莫名其妙而且可能还会钻牛角尖，local朋友也觉得这门课体验感差，wl大。其实这门课是本人在adp末期很多CC都被选完的时候加上的，嗯对，这课那个时候还有位置（有位置的CC不知道有没有10个哦。。。）什么意思不用我多说了。（为什么大家都避雷了呢？好难猜啊？）好吧，最后不管结果好不好只是我对这个课的看法，不会因为它给我A就翻脸，因为它本来就不简单。（本人还学MATH的课，我觉得比MATH还麻烦）
reviews.translated_content: Well, med students might want to try this course, seriously... keep going, dear. Who doesn’t want to spend each week frantically reviewing PowerPoint slides and readings, filling up reference papers, only to scratch their head over a quiz full of obscure and controversial medical-biology terminology? Okay, I did skim the readings (though I did examine every corner of the PPTs), but expecting students to get through roughly 40–50 pages of lecture slides plus two biology academic papers of about 20 pages each every week isn’t reasonable. This is a Common Core course, not a major requirement, and not all students have a biology background. Sure, there are some easier quizzes where you might get 3/4 or full marks, but most quizzes aren’t like that. I don’t know why so many people give positive reviews, because personally, the grading wasn’t great. (Well, if your quiz performance is average but you can still get an A-range grade through group project work, then the grading can be generous.) I haven’t received my final grade yet, so I don’t know if the group project will save my grade (I’ve done everything I could to secure the soft-score components; if I do end up with an A-range grade thanks to the group project, please ignore this post). I simply feel this course perfectly inherits the opaque and unpredictable nature typical of Common Core courses: the quizzes are baffling and may even nitpick details. My local friends also had a poor experience, citing heavy workload. Actually, I added this course at the end of the add/drop period when most Common Core courses were already full. Yes, there were still spots available then (I doubt there were even 10 Common Core courses with vacancies...). I think you know what I mean. (Why is everyone warning others to avoid it? Hard to guess, right?) Anyway, regardless of the final outcome, this is just my view of the course; I won’t change my opinion even if it gives me an A, because it’s inherently not simple. (I’m also taking MATH courses, and I find this one more troublesome than MATH.)

reviews.content: 平时assignment给分挺好的。gp的话选到了比较好的队友，所以觉得体验还可以，建议大家可以tutorial上留意那些积极发言的人！我选到了一个超好队友她carry我们全组，感觉我都freeride了笑死。gp也不算麻烦，做一个group poster，然后每一个组是3~4个人，一组上去present十分钟吧好像是。期末考试我感觉source真的对我帮助比较大，考试的题目跟我买到的source里面有一个是题目一样的，因为我看过思路，所以就可以比较快和有信心地写出来。教授的PPT感觉重点不是很清晰，一节课可能有个七八十面的基础上字太多太小了，期末考试的时候根本就看不完。不过教授讲课挺风趣。
reviews.translated_content: Grading for regular assignments is quite good. For the group project, I got relatively good teammates, so the experience was okay. I suggest paying attention to those who speak up actively in tutorials! I got a super good teammate who carried the whole group; I felt like I was freeriding, lol. The group project wasn’t too troublesome: make a group poster, with 3–4 people per group, and each group presents for about ten minutes. For the final exam, I found the study materials really helpful. One of the questions in the materials I bought was identical to an exam question. Because I had seen the approach, I could write it out relatively quickly and confidently. The professor’s slides don’t highlight the key points very clearly; with 70–80 slides per lecture, the text is too dense and small, and you simply can’t finish reading them all during the final exam. However, the professor’s lectures are quite humorous.

reviews.content: Tutor太不负责任了，给分很差，而且永远不会回复电邮，group project只拿了B+。但岂料final grade 有A-。可能因为final考得好。
reviews.translated_content: The tutor was too irresponsible, graded poorly, and never replied to emails. We only got a B+ for the group project. But unexpectedly, the final grade was an A-. Maybe because I did well on the final exam.

reviews.content:
Lecture: 大部分單元由Parker任教，非常生動有趣，喜歡和學生交互；小部分單元由專精各自專業的教授任教，水平不一。可以不上，PPT會在課後才在Moodle發佈（理由是鼓勵學生課上參與，但我尋思你課後還是會發啊，不想上課的學生就等Moodle發佈自己看不就行了）

Tutorial: 由George任教，很犀利的一個人，評價非常的尖銳，邏輯能力恐怖。他真的很忙很忙，如果他不回你Email請繼續轟炸他郵箱或者Office堵門（）

Workload: 正常。兩次Essay，一次Final（需要複習PPT），一份小組poster + presentation。George稱他更在意poster design（like font size），presentation skill倒是其次（儘量脫稿，我只能說那麼多）

整體評價: 適合對科學史有一定了解，邏輯能力好的同學，需要主動複習Lecture PPT才可以衝很高的Grade，可在tutorial class面對面堵George問assignment意見和提示。本人最後拿了A+。
reviews.translated_content: Lecture: Most units are taught by Parker, who is very lively and interesting and likes to interact with students. A small number of units are taught by professors specialising in their respective fields, with varying levels of quality. Attendance is optional. PPT slides are posted on Moodle only after class (the stated reason is to encourage in-class participation, but since they are posted afterwards anyway, students who don’t want to attend can just wait for the Moodle release and study on their own). Tutorial: Taught by George, a very sharp person with extremely incisive comments and terrifying logical ability. He is really busy. If he doesn’t reply to your email, keep bombarding his inbox or block his office door. Workload: Normal. Two essays, one final (requires reviewing PPTs), and one group poster + presentation. George says he cares more about poster design (e.g., font size), while presentation skills are secondary (try to speak without notes; that’s all I can say). Overall evaluation: Suitable for students with some background in the history of science and strong logical skills. You need to proactively review the lecture PPTs to aim for a high grade. You can corner George face-to-face in tutorial classes for assignment advice and hints. I finally got an A+.

reviews.content: 总的来说课程有些无聊，wl看起来不大但也不小。总共12堂lecture，前五节讲一些科学史的理论（科学方法的结构，归纳和演绎推理的区别，范式变化的结构，为什么可证伪性是科学的标准），其实总结下来内容不多，能水出五堂lecture也是蛮神奇的。后七节讲了几个科学革命的例子（达尔文理论，元素周期表，哥白尼革命，相对论）。wl是一篇600字essay一篇800字essay，小组海报+presentation，还有期末考试。最后莫名奇妙拿了个b，生气
reviews.translated_content: Overall, the course is a bit boring. The workload doesn’t look huge, but it’s not small either. There are 12 lectures in total. The first five cover some theories in the history of science (the structure of scientific methods, the difference between inductive and deductive reasoning, the structure of paradigm shifts, why falsifiability is the standard for science). To sum up, there isn’t much content, so it’s quite amazing that they could stretch it out over five lectures. The last seven lectures cover several examples of scientific revolutions (Darwin’s theory, the periodic table, the Copernican Revolution, relativity). The workload consists of one 600-word essay, one 800-word essay, a group poster + presentation, and a final exam. In the end, I inexplicably got a B, which made me angry.

reviews.content:
比较推荐！能学到很多有趣的生活中 不理性的现象和原理，理解起来也不困难。老师有点压分（说好的cc不curve呢），但认真学考试多写就问题不大。a range在70+左右。非常自闭、难得没有gp的cc课。
Weekly Workload: 较小！2hr lecture 一学期4次tuto 课余2.5hrs上下。
Assessment: 需要注意的是20%的tuto是20分的四次讲完就考小测验 题不难但不认真写扣一分就是1%，得认真听+完全理解tuto。25% Midterm和35% Final都比较常规 全是讲过的理论的应用 需要完全理解ppt。 有个10-15%的research hw需要看4篇research paper回答问题 介意慎选。
reviews.translated_content: Recommended! You can learn a lot of interesting irrational phenomena and principles from daily life, and they are not difficult to understand. The instructor grades a bit harshly (what happened to the promise that Common Core courses don’t grade on a curve?), but if you study seriously and write more in the exam, it should be fine. An A-range grade is around 70+. It’s quite isolating and rare for a Common Core course to have no group project.  Weekly Workload: Light! 2-hour lectures, four tutorials per semester, and about 2.5 hours of extra-curricular work.  Assessment: Note that the 20% tutorial component consists of four 20-mark sessions followed by quizzes. The questions aren’t hard, but failing to write carefully costs 1% per mark, so you need to listen attentively and fully understand the tutorials. The 25% Midterm and 35% Final are fairly standard, applying theories covered in class; you need to fully understand the slides. There is also a research homework worth 10–15% that requires reading four research papers and answering questions. If you mind this, choose with caution.

reviews.content: 讲各种heuristic和bias，原理、应用，最后有讲到研究方式。大概是行为经济学，我没接触过，觉得大多还挺好理解的。wl一般般，有moodle和tutorial的quiz、期中期末两场考试和一个final的analysis form。涉及的内容很多很广，不过lecture讲得有点散容易分心，我都是靠ppt学东西的_(:3」∠)_，*完全吸收*ppt的内容已经足以应对考试的了，就是final需要多读几篇论文。认真学就能搞定的课，能学到东西，挺不错的～
reviews.translated_content: It covers various heuristics and biases, including principles, applications, and finally research methods. It’s roughly behavioral economics. I hadn’t encountered it before, but I found most of it quite understandable. The workload is average. There are quizzes on Moodle and in tutorials, two midterms/finals, and a final analysis form. The content is extensive and broad, but the lectures are a bit scattered and easy to lose focus in. I relied on the PowerPoint slides to learn _(:3」∠)_. *Fully absorbing* the PPT content is enough to handle the exams, though the final requires reading several more papers. It’s a manageable course if you study seriously, you can learn something, and it’s quite good~

reviews.content:
我的人生cc 原因如下 
1. no grp project no presentation（這對我很重要）甚至還沒有essay（好像這課之前是有essay的 這兩個學期開始取消了）   
2.wl真的很小 lecture都去聽了理解了的話final前背ppt沒啥壓力 tutorial也比較輕鬆（tutor小姐姐笑嘻嘻的超級可愛！）每節下課之前有一個小quiz算tutorial分 答案全是剛講過的內容 readings在做online quiz的時候有極少量的題需要refer一下 除此之外我沒咋看  
3. 內容主要學怎麼用一些心理學的concept解釋簡單的behavioral economics現象 然後還會講一些和數學(probability/logic)有關的paradox 感覺把我major學的的東西全串在一起了 然後用心理學的角度去解釋 非常有意思  
4. 好🐢！！
reviews.translated_content: This is my life-changing Common Core course. Reasons below: 1. No group project, no presentation (this is very important to me), and not even an essay (it seems this course had essays before, but they were cancelled in the last two semesters). 2. The workload is really small. If you attend and understand the lectures, there’s little pressure memorising the slides before the final. Tutorials are also relatively relaxed (the female tutor is always smiling and super cute!). There’s a small quiz before each class ends that counts towards the tutorial grade; the answers are all content just covered. Readings are rarely needed, except for a very small number of questions in the online quiz. Apart from that, I didn’t really read them. 3. The content mainly teaches how to use psychological concepts to explain simple behavioural economics phenomena, and also covers some paradoxes related to mathematics (probability/logic). It feels like it connected everything I learned in my major and explained it from a psychological perspective, which is very interesting. 4. Generous grading!!

reviews.translated_content: At the end of last semester, my evaluation of this course was ‘stay away’. reviews.translated_content: I barely read the assigned readings, unless a quiz question used an example from them, in which case I would go back and check specifically. The workload mainly comes from the Research Analysis. This time I wrote about [REDACTED_PHONE] words, answering 6 small questions based on 6–7 readings. I do recommend reading these properly. The analysis requires some thought, such as extracting and summarising the similarities and differences between articles. The final exam this semester lasted two and a half hours. It was quite painful writing it, feeling like I was just rewriting the same things over and over haha. But it wasn’t actually difficult! There were also two additional short essays, adding another ~800 words. The good thing is that the essays for this course don’t seem to require high literary flair; writing clearly and accurately is basically enough. The course content is very interesting! It can be applied to life to explain many phenomena! Overall, I was quite happy. I ended up with an A.

reviews.instructor: Dr. Karen Mak, Prof. D.L. Phillips, Dr. B.L. Lim
reviews.content: ●课程简介   理学院开的CC，比较简单的”法医学“（本质上是生物，化学的大杂烩）。Lecture主要包括法医人类学(解剖学)，指纹及DNA鉴定，毒品毒药学，伪造文书鉴定以及纵火爆炸鉴定。内容偏向于对于证物的科学鉴定手法，对法医，人体解剖，化学鉴定感兴趣的同学可以考虑选这门课。 ●Assessment 1. Labs (30%) 2. Tutorials (10%) 3. Mini-mock quiz (5%) 4. Quizzes (30%) 5. Group project (25%) Lab有两次，涉及毛发鉴定和指纹鉴定，不太涉及实验操作技巧，完成后要交一份回答问题形式的报告。Mini mock quiz白给分的项目，自己根据lecture讲过的内容出选择题，一定要看清楚范围和要求，final会考同学们出的原题。期中的Quiz只要认真总结Lecture的内容，临时抱佛脚也可以全答对，但是一定要复习！！Group project要求写一个侦探小故事，但是个人感觉剧情并不重要，重要的是对于物证的化学分析！能自圆其说即可。 ●个人经验 Grade:A+ 因为楼主是生物专业并且学过人体解剖所以感觉内容比较基础，生物或者化学专业的同学可以考虑一下哦。一两节课上会展示尸体的图片所以如果实在接受不了可以回避。除了Group project外，其他几项assessment是可以拿满分的，group project不推荐临时赶工，最好在tutorial分好组后就开始构思。虽然这个学期因为停课，更改了一部分assessment比例，但是对于成绩的可控性影响不是很大。 最后的经验：认真总结每节课的内容（整理笔记）+Lab&tutorial认真完成+Group project多与tutor交流+基础的生物和化学知识（可以抱大腿）=好龟
reviews.translated_content: ● Course Introduction  A Common Core course offered by the Faculty of Science. It’s a relatively simple “Forensic Science” course (essentially a hodgepodge of biology and chemistry). Lectures mainly cover forensic anthropology (anatomy), fingerprint and DNA identification, toxicology and pharmacology, document forgery identification, and arson/explosion identification. The content leans towards scientific methods for identifying evidence. Students interested in forensics, human anatomy, or chemical identification might consider this course.  ● Assessment  1. Labs (30%) 2. Tutorials (10%) 3. Mini-mock quiz (5%) 4. Quizzes (30%) 5. Group project (25%)  There are two labs, involving hair and fingerprint identification. They don’t involve much practical lab skill; after completion, you submit a report in a Q&A format. The mini-mock quiz is almost free marks: you create multiple-choice questions based on lecture content. Make sure to check the scope and requirements carefully, as the final exam will test the exact questions created by students. For the mid-term quizzes, if you summarise the lecture content seriously, you can get everything right even by cramming at the last minute, but you must revise!! The group project requires writing a short detective story, but personally, I feel the plot isn’t important; what matters is the chemical analysis of physical evidence! As long as you can justify your reasoning, it’s fine.  ● Personal Experience  Grade: A+  Because I’m a biology major and have studied human anatomy, I found the content quite basic. Biology or chemistry majors might want to consider it. Images of corpses are shown in one or two classes, so if you really can’t handle it, you can look away. Apart from the group project, full marks are achievable in the other assessment components. I don’t recommend rushing the group project at the last minute; it’s better to start brainstorming right after groups are formed in tutorials. Although class suspensions this semester changed some assessment weightings, it didn’t significantly affect the controllability of the grade.  Final advice: Summarise each lesson’s content seriously (organise notes) + complete labs and tutorials diligently + communicate frequently with tutors for the group project + basic biology and chemistry knowledge (you can rely on strong teammates) = generous grading.

reviews.content: kenneth人真的超级好 非常喜欢他的英式口音 虽然觉得tutorial没什么意义但是他人实在太好了一定要给点面子请大家一定要去他的课 本人很不喜欢主动发言但是在他课上发言很自在 回邮件非常的及时 处理事情让人觉得很nice pick他
reviews.translated_content: Kenneth is a really nice person. I really like his British accent. Although I felt the tutorial was rather pointless, he’s so pleasant that you should definitely show some respect and take his class. I’m not someone who likes to speak up voluntarily, but I felt very comfortable participating in his class. He replies to emails very promptly and handles matters in a way that feels very nice. Pick him.

reviews.content: Run quiz就是考记忆力，无聊且折磨 quiz1考了的名人名言和历史（“以下那句话是xx说的”和“在19xx年的案子中，……”），lecture讲了很多种毒品都要背过，quiz2有15%裸问xx毒品属于什么类型。并没有标题看上去有趣
reviews.translated_content: The run quiz is just a test of memory—boring and torturous. Quiz 1 covered famous quotes and history (e.g., “Which of the following was said by XX?” and “In the 19XX case, ...”). The lecture covered many types of drugs that all had to be memorised. Quiz 2 had 15% bare questions asking what type a specific drug belongs to. It’s not as interesting as the title suggests.

reviews.content: 24-25 sem1. Dropped the class in the first lecture. It seemed that the professor was even more nervous than me, which means, he could hardly speak a complete sentence. Boring lecture.
reviews.translated_content: 24-25 sem1. Dropped the class in the first lecture. It seemed that the professor was even more nervous than me, which means, he could hardly speak a complete sentence. Boring lecture.

reviews.content: 没有想象中的有意思，lecturer差距很大。有两节课的lecture说英文整一个支支吾吾的。quiz1没好好背，6/10，quiz2背了两天，18/20。gp和三个local做的，presentation认真，小说乱搞。lab认真。最后A-。
reviews.translated_content: Not as interesting as I imagined. There’s a big gap between lecturers. In two lectures, the lecturer spoke English very hesitantly. I didn’t memorize well for Quiz 1 and got 6/10; I studied for two days for Quiz 2 and got 18/20. For the group project, I worked with three local Hong Kong students. We took the presentation seriously but slacked off on the fictional case study. I was serious in the lab. Final grade: A-.

reviews.content: 说实话真的不知道这么有趣的一个领域是怎么讲成这样的。workload大：虽然没有作业，但是一个学期一共有两次随堂quiz，分别是10道和20道选择题占10%和20%（共30%）；三次lab，第一次fingerprint and hair patterns、第二次fingerprint detection、第三次chromatography，结束之后分别要填写发的worksheet report，还算简单；一个group presentation，选一个forensic TV show 介绍里面用到的forensic techniques并criticize any discrepancies between the show and real life；一个group essay，几个人编一个crime story并选一个technique着重介绍和分析。因为有两个group project所以前期选择靠谱的组员特别重要，tutorial不重要可以不去（但是Kenneth人特别好tutorial也比lecture有趣很多很多）。最终成绩是A，虽然拿到好🐢不难但是由于实在是太麻烦太无聊了还是不推荐
reviews.translated_content: Honestly, I don’t know how such an interesting field could be taught like this. Heavy workload: although there are no assignments, there are two in-class quizzes during the semester, consisting of 10 and 20 multiple-choice questions, worth 10% and 20% respectively (total 30%); three labs (first on fingerprint and hair patterns, second on fingerprint detection, third on chromatography), each followed by a worksheet report, which is fairly simple; one group presentation where you choose a forensic TV show, introduce the forensic techniques used, and criticise any discrepancies between the show and real life; and one group essay where you create a crime story and focus on introducing and analysing one technique. Because there are two group projects, choosing reliable teammates early on is crucial. Tutorials aren’t important and you can skip them (but Kenneth is very nice, and his tutorials are much more interesting than the lectures). My final grade is an A. Although it’s not hard to get a good grade, I don’t recommend it because it’s too troublesome and boring.

reviews.content: Large workload. Teamwork played improtant role
reviews.translated_content: Large workload. Teamwork played an important role.

reviews.content: 对课程内容挺感兴趣，而且感觉workload不重，还不错
reviews.translated_content: I’m quite interested in the course content, and the workload doesn’t feel heavy. It’s pretty good.

reviews.content: 对法医刑侦感兴趣的同学们快冲。wl一般不算很大，对gp比较敏感的同学们慎选，因为最后大作业是写一篇侦探小说，不过真的挺有意思的
reviews.translated_content: If you’re interested in forensic science and criminal investigation, go for it. The workload is average, not too heavy. Students who are sensitive about their group project grades should choose with caution, because the final major assignment is to write a detective novel, though it’s actually quite interesting.

reviews.content:
烂死了 本来预计A+的课最后只有B 本人有生化基础 全部毁在烂组员上了 第二天pre前一天晚上组员才回消息开始搞 可以找非freerider人一起选 要不然碰到差劲组员都得死
课程没想象中好玩 wl不大 gp。。呵呵
reviews.translated_content: It’s terrible. I was expecting an A+ but only got a B. I have a background in biochemistry, and it was all ruined by terrible group members. One member only replied and started working the night before our presentation the next day. Choose this course with non-free riders, otherwise, you’ll be doomed if you get bad teammates. The course wasn’t as fun as I imagined. The workload isn’t heavy. As for the group project... what a joke.

course_info.title: Making Sense of Science-related Social Issues

reviews.content: 很水的课，lecture就是吹水看一会儿PPT，tutorial一学期就上三四节吧，workload的话一篇initial essay ，一篇final essay,每周200字关于lecture的reflective，小组做一份poster。initial essay和final essay的topic一样，如果initial essay🐢好可以完全copy，但经过一学期学习多多少少会有一些思想上的变化吧，不建议大一新生上，因为根本不会写essay,拉低了我的🐢，如果比较会写essay上这门课挺轻松拿🐢也会更好一点吧。
reviews.translated_content: It’s a very lightweight course. Lectures are just chatting and looking at PowerPoint slides for a while. There are only three or four tutorials in the whole semester. In terms of workload, there is one initial essay, one final essay, a 200-word weekly reflection on the lecture, and a group poster. The topics for the initial and final essays are the same; if you get a good grade on the initial essay, you can basically copy it for the final. But after a semester of study, your thinking will change somewhat. I don’t recommend first-year students take this course because they won’t know how to write essays yet. It dragged my grade down. If you are better at writing essays, this course is quite relaxed and you’ll likely get a better grade.

reviews.content: Good grade course, not very in depth but discuss a wide range of science related social issues. Also friendly to those who have little knowledge about natural science.
reviews.translated_content: Good grade course, not very in depth but discuss a wide range of science related social issues. Also friendly to those who have little knowledge about natural science.

reviews.translated_content: This is an ST course particularly suitable for humanities students. The course content combines basic scientific knowledge with social issues, analyzing these issues using journalistic methods.

reviews.content: Great!!!
reviews.translated_content: Great!!!

reviews.content: boring lessons but grade ok, got A-. need full attendance thi
reviews.translated_content: Boring lessons but the grade is ok; I got an A-. Full attendance is required though.

reviews.content: 学不到东西，但是非常好grade,拿了A+ （不过我觉得不具有普适性因为prof有公布excel sheet可以看所有人的grade我全部的分都是比较高的，特别是我们的group project是全班最高）所以我的建议是要是真的想学东西不要选，不过作为非理科人不想学technical的科学想水了一个cc也是勉强能选。workload真的小，我initial essay grade不错final essay我只用了半个小时把一些小问题改了，整个hku都没有那么轻松的final…
reviews.translated_content: You don’t really learn much, but the grading is very generous—I got an A+. (However, I don’t think this applies to everyone, because the professor published an Excel sheet showing everyone’s grades, and my scores were relatively high across the board, especially since our group project was the highest in the class.) So my advice is: if you truly want to learn, don’t take this course. But if you’re a non-science student who doesn’t want to tackle technical science and just wants an easy Common Core course, it’s passable. The workload is genuinely small. My initial essay grade was decent, and for the final essay, I only spent half an hour tweaking some minor issues. There was no easier final exam in all of HKU…

reviews.content: 每個禮拜寫一篇200字左右的reflection memo/ 期末有一篇essay題目跟最一開始上課繳交的essay (在總成績外extra 5%)一樣/期末還有一個group presentation 做了個poster。個人覺得課程不難，但也不到很有趣，普普通通大家有興趣再選。
reviews.translated_content: Write a reflection memo of about 200 words every week. The final includes an essay with the same topic as the essay submitted at the very beginning of the course (an extra 5% outside the total grade). There is also a group presentation where we made a poster. Personally, I feel the course is not difficult, but it’s not very interesting either. It’s just average; take it if you’re interested.

reviews.content: 无敌好龟课 我身边朋友都比我高 我是最菜鸡一个 可见龟有多好 workload说大也大说小也小 每周要写reflective memo（占比20%） 所以必须要去听lecture不然写不出来 开学和结课时要写两次paper 有group project 总体来说评分内容比较丰富 但是每一个component都真的不难 只要你用一点心 就绝对不差
reviews.translated_content: An incredibly GPA-friendly course. My friends around me all scored higher than I did; I was the weakest one, which shows how generous the grading is. The workload can be seen as either heavy or light. You have to write a reflective memo every week (worth 20%), so you must attend the lectures; otherwise, you won’t be able to write them. You need to write two papers, one at the start and one at the end of the semester. There is also a group project. Overall, the assessment components are varied, but none of them are truly difficult. As long as you put in a little effort, your result will definitely not be bad.

reviews.content: 非常适合文科生上的一门CC，给分很好WL小，一个prez+一个initial essay+一个final essay（在initial essay的基础上改），每周还有一个十几分钟就可以完成的小reflection。
reviews.translated_content: This Common Core course is very suitable for humanities students. The grading is generous and the workload is small: one presentation, one initial essay, and one final essay (revised from the initial essay). There is also a short reflection each week that takes just over ten minutes to complete.

reviews.content: 我逢人就安利啊 文科生友好ccst 自爆 是A Lecturer是教物理的 东欧那旮沓的帅气女老师 然而 生物化学啥都会点  Lec前几节课都在介绍sci-fi 都比较小众 老师真的读过很多 这些都是在帮助选prez 和essay 的小说 后面的课讲一些 科幻小说里的逻辑问题 科学错误 还有很多社会问题什么的 有一个『in class test』 一半考科学概念解释 一般考结合现实例子分析科幻小说 满分25分我只得了12.5 依旧A了 大家别担心 【总结！lecture不用听😂】  接下来讲tuto Tutor推荐Alex 人非常好 tuto 『participation占分』 但是他会让每个人都发言 不用抢答什么的   『Presentation』和组友一起 从老师给的书单里选一本sci-fi 老师给的list会标注好 没本书的长度 可讨论的点多少 建议1.选一本短一点的 2.可讨论点多的 3.有中文版的［笑哭］ 抱一个思想有深度的文院大佬就好 我组友是一个很强的文院local小姐姐 帮我改prez发言稿 带我飞  『essay』挺短的 好像就1000字 和prez同一本书 tutor给分也好 就扣了4分［大家想想essay的评分标准 怎么也得没项扣一分吧］  反正就wl小 grade好
reviews.translated_content: I recommend this to everyone I meet. It’s a Common Core course friendly to Arts students. Full disclosure: the lecturer teaches physics and is a handsome female teacher from Eastern Europe. However, she knows a bit about biology, chemistry, and more. The first few lectures introduced sci-fi, which is quite niche. The teacher has read a lot; these introductions help with choosing novels for the presentation and essay. Later classes covered logical issues in sci-fi novels, scientific errors, and many social issues. There was an ‘in-class test’ worth 25 marks, half testing explanations of scientific concepts and half testing analysis of sci-fi novels combined with real-world examples. I only got 12.5 but still got an A, so don’t worry. [Summary! You don’t need to listen to the lectures 😂] Next, about tutorials: Tutor Alex is highly recommended; he’s very nice. Tutorial ‘participation counts towards the grade’, but he ensures everyone speaks, so there’s no need to fight to answer. For the ‘Presentation’, work with your group mates to choose a sci-fi book from the list provided by the teacher. The list indicates the length of each book and how many discussion points it offers. Suggestions: 1. Choose a shorter one; 2. One with many discussion points; 3. One with a Chinese version [laughing/crying]. Just partner with a deep-thinking Arts expert. My group mate was a very strong local Arts student who helped me revise my presentation script and carried me. The ‘essay’ is quite short, seemingly just 1000 words, on the same book as the presentation. The tutor grades generously, deducting only 4 marks [think about essay grading criteria; surely it’s at least one mark deducted per item]. Anyway, the workload is light and the grades are good.

reviews.content: 🐢很ok 但不可否認 是個神煩的課 表面看是一個小組報告一篇essay一個in-class test 報告和論文都是圍繞一本書來做 但是報告和essay真的很花時間 有預備報告 Q&A環節 essay草稿評分 essay peer editing評分 我們組當時報告整個重新打掉修改了三次 最後終於滿足tutor Alex嚴格的要求 這還不是最煩的 考試是最煩的 文科人理解題目很費勁 理解完了也不懂怎麼回答 最後考試59/100 考試佔15% 所以能A真的是essay和小組報告做得很好 還有課真的很無聊 我是一節課都沒聽過的 對sci-fi有興趣的就當我沒說 選就完事！！！
reviews.translated_content: The grading is OK, but admittedly, it’s an incredibly annoying course. On the surface, it consists of one group presentation, one essay, and one in-class test. Both the presentation and essay revolve around a single book, but they really take a lot of time. There are preparation checks, Q&A sessions, essay draft grading, and peer-editing grades. Our group had to completely redo and revise our presentation three times before finally meeting tutor Alex’s strict requirements. And that wasn’t even the most annoying part; the exam was the worst. As humanities students, we struggled to understand the questions, and even after understanding them, didn’t know how to answer. I ultimately scored 59/100 on the exam, which accounts for 15%. So getting an A really depends on doing very well on the essay and group presentation. Also, the class is really boring; I didn’t listen to a single lecture. If you’re interested in sci-fi, ignore what I said and just enrol!!!

reviews.translated_content: I’ve never taken a worse Common Core course. The content is boring, the instructor just reads off the PowerPoint slides the whole time, and the grading is terrible.

reviews.content: William很可爱，不过rw左右有几节课是LI Yiliang上的，此人和我们描述差的老师常说的“念ppt”不同，而是直接把ppt甩给学生，不闻不问，上课的时候zoom上脸也不露，讲了两句话，让我们有问题问他（很自然地，没有学生问），旋闭麦走人。不过除开占所有课时中的三节（应该是这个数）之该老师外，这节课没有任何槽点，wl很杂但是不大（而且因为杂而分散，用的时间其实很少），虽然quiz presen essay exam占尽，但是都很小，presen是一共三次每次五分钟（一个人讲最多两分钟）很容易做，essay是按instruction做一个实验（记录自己睡眠）并且只要写几百字，quiz是每次几个小问题，做之前翻看几下ppt就行（我甚至有一次忘了有quiz，靠手速和文件内查找做完的）。总之是一个很好的课。要注意的一点是tuto分组，分一次组之后的每次prez和期末的海报（工作量也不大）都是这些组友，所以最好找好队友先（我运气很好，分到了一些非常好的组友）。上这节课那个sem我生了很大的病，精神状态极差，不过最后的龟仍然不错，是我至今所有cc中最好的。
reviews.translated_content: William is very cute. However, around Reading Week, a few classes were taught by LI Yiliang. Unlike the typical “reading off PowerPoint slides” complaint about bad teachers, this person simply dumped the PPT on the students without any explanation or engagement. During class, he didn’t even show his face on Zoom, said just two sentences, told us to ask him if we had questions (naturally, no students did), then promptly muted his microphone and left. Aside from those three classes (I think that’s the number) taught by this instructor, the course had no drawbacks. The workload is varied but not heavy (and because it’s scattered, the actual time spent is quite little). Although it includes quizzes, presentations, an essay, and an exam, each component is very small. The presentation consists of three sessions, each five minutes long (each person speaks for at most two minutes), so it’s easy to do. The essay involves conducting an experiment according to instructions (recording your own sleep) and writing only a few hundred words. The quizzes are just a few short questions each time; flipping through the PPT a bit before doing them is enough (I even forgot about one quiz once and finished it relying on speed and in-file search). All in all, it’s a very good course. One thing to note is the tutorial grouping: once groups are formed, all subsequent presentations and the final poster (which also doesn’t involve much work) are with the same group mates, so it’s best to find good teammates first (I was lucky and got some very good group mates). That semester, I was seriously ill and in very poor mental state, but my final grade was still quite good—it’s the best among all my Common Core courses to date.

reviews.content: wl还好，一个月的数据记录，两周一次小组presentation，一共三次课上小quiz（填空题和排序题，就几分钟的那种），最后有一个小组poster和一个test
reviews.translated_content: The workload is manageable: one month of data recording, a group presentation every two weeks, three short in-class quizzes (fill-in-the-blank and ordering questions that take only a few minutes), and finally a group poster and a test.

reviews.content: 超简单…wl小而且tutor人很好龟也很靓！
reviews.translated_content: Super simple... the workload is small, and the tutor is very nice with generous grading!

reviews.content: 吹爆William!太可爱了~把lecture讲成诗。第一节课有惊喜!只要好好背知识点quiz基本每次满分，期末一张自制A4纸笔记开卷考，最后给grade A－还不错。Problem-Based Learning随机分groupmate，最后一次poster presentation自己组队。topic有趣，讨论跟时间有关的一切，时间旅行、时间的文化与社会意义、人类与动植物对时间的感知、古代西方哲学家的时间观、地质学意义上的"deep time"、地球演化历史、宇宙历史……有个assignment记录自己起床和入睡时间规律一个月，report蛮有警醒自己的意义的……不过wl其实不小
reviews.translated_content: Cannot recommend William highly enough! He's so cute~ He turns lectures into poetry. The first class was a surprise! As long as you memorize the key points, you'll basically get full marks on every quiz. The final is an open-book exam where you can bring a self-made A4 cheat sheet. I ended up with an A-, which is not bad. Group mates for Problem-Based Learning are assigned randomly, but you form your own team for the last poster presentation. The topics are interesting, covering everything related to time: time travel, the cultural and social significance of time, human and animal/plant perception of time, ancient Western philosophers' views on time, geological 'deep time', Earth's evolutionary history, cosmic history... One assignment involved recording your wake-up and sleep patterns for a month; the report was quite a wake-up call for me... However, the workload is actually not small.

reviews.content: WL不大，小組project有趣。quiz有點難要復習復習，但是最低分的一次不算。
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t heavy, and the group project is interesting. The quizzes are a bit difficult and require review, but the lowest score is dropped.

reviews.content: piece of shit
reviews.translated_content: piece of shit

reviews.content: 被评论里workload小骗去上了这门课，wl是上过所有cc最大的之一！（跟我总选水课和对data science一窍不通有关？ 前半段lecture还偏水，后面开始讲数据结构，一堆陌生至极的名词和内容。tutor都很好，tuto内容设计精心不是复习lectur，算是本课的亮点，但tuto上有一次debate，还有两三次小prez，每次都要提前准备。有一个midterm，大家几乎都接近满分，如果不好好听lecture（like me，cheatsheet就要做一天。有课程中间的小小essay，可以随便写写。project分为一个不超过8分钟的prez和10+pages的report。当时，碰到的一个local组友不freeride但不靠谱，工作成果没办法直接用，还要再帮他改。overall的wl真心不小，tuto要准备，lecture要去听，有midterm，还有project。给分fair，用心了一学期最后拿了a。感觉cs or double E or data science相关的专业大佬学起来应该很简单，非专业人士wl较大，能学到不少干货。
reviews.translated_content: I was tricked into taking this course by comments saying the workload was light. The workload is actually one of the heaviest among all the Common Core courses I've taken! (Maybe because I always choose easy courses and know nothing about data science?) The first half of the lectures was rather lightweight, but then it started covering data structures, with a bunch of extremely unfamiliar terms and content. The tutors are all good; the tutorial content is carefully designed and isn't just a review of the lectures, which is a highlight of the course. However, there was one debate in tutorials, plus two or three small presentations, each requiring advance preparation. There is one midterm; almost everyone scored close to full marks. If you don't listen carefully in lectures (like me), making the cheat sheet will take a whole day. There is a short essay during the semester that you can write casually. The project consists of a presentation of no more than 8 minutes and a report of 10+ pages. At the time, I had a local teammate who didn't free-ride but was unreliable; their work couldn't be used directly, and I had to revise it for them. Overall, the workload is genuinely not small: you need to prepare for tutorials, attend lectures, take a midterm, and complete a project. The grading is fair; after putting in effort for the semester, I finally got an A. I feel that experts in CS, Double E, or Data Science-related majors would find it easy to learn, while for non-majors, the workload is heavier, but you can learn a lot of substantive content.

reviews.content: 和Big Data没啥太大的关系，能学到的知识很少，毕竟只是CC。wl较高（有可能是网课的原因），一共做了三次prez，一次辩论，两次test和一篇15页的 group project report。test考前一晚回顾一下ppt就好，班级平均分都接近满分了。但是prez和report给🐢相对较严格。如果抱着想学到比较hard core的知识的想法，多半会失望，所以请慎重考虑。
reviews.translated_content: It doesn’t have much to do with Big Data, and you learn very little—after all, it’s just a Common Core course. The workload is relatively high (possibly due to online classes). We did three presentations, one debate, two tests, and a 15-page group project report. For the tests, just reviewing the slides the night before is enough; the class average was close to full marks. However, grading for the presentations and report is relatively strict. If you expect to learn hardcore knowledge, you’ll likely be disappointed, so please consider carefully.

reviews.content: 关于复杂系统的一门cc，虽说是cc但讲的内容实际上是个比较专业的研究领域（至少本文科生是这么看）。考核的assignment有五次练习，一个视频的project，还有一个小组作业（pre+report)。每次的tutorial一定要参加，会记participation。Tim讲的东西很多（分形、混沌、网络学、二八定律），但主要围绕一本特定教材（可不买）。由于我并没有仔细听lecture，平时作业做的不是很好，最后成绩B...不过还是坦然接受了。 以及，找靠谱队友很重要（感谢厉害队友帮助）！！！
reviews.translated_content: A Common Core course on complex systems. Although it’s a CC, the content is actually quite specialized (at least from my perspective as an arts student). The assessments include five exercises, a video project, and a group assignment (presentation + report). You must attend every tutorial, as participation is recorded. Tim covers a lot of material (fractals, chaos, network science, the 80/20 rule), but it mainly revolves around one specific textbook (which you don’t need to buy). Since I didn’t listen carefully in lectures and didn’t do well on the regular assignments, I ended up with a B... but I accepted it calmly. Also, finding reliable teammates is crucial (thanks to my awesome teammates for the help)!!!

reviews.content: 大爱Tim！教的非常用心，课程内容数学相关，涉及neural network，genetic algorithm，ABM，Fractal，urban planning，genetics，entropy etc 对激发学习理工科的兴趣非常有效。就是wl大，一个视频，一个gp with 2000 words report。
reviews.translated_content: Big love for Tim! He teaches with great care. The course content is math-related, covering neural networks, genetic algorithms, ABM, fractals, urban planning, genetics, entropy, etc. It’s very effective at sparking interest in STEM subjects. The workload is heavy, though: one video and one group project with a 2000-word report.

reviews.content: 我觉得wl虽然有点大但是非常有趣，lec没怎么听tut也摸鱼但是quiz assignment好好做都是可以拿高分的，gp需要找好队友好好准备。Tim人非常好的可以多问问他对gp的建议。我们组最后prez分数一般但是report和video都没有扣分，拿了A+
reviews.translated_content: I felt that although the workload was a bit heavy, it was very interesting. I didn’t pay much attention in lectures and slacked off in tutorials, but as long as you do the quizzes and assignments properly, you can get a high score. For the group project, you need to find good teammates and prepare well. Tim is a very nice person, so feel free to ask him for advice on the group project. Our group’s presentation score was average, but we didn’t lose any marks on the report and video, and ended up with an A+.

reviews.content: 感觉还可以但lecture真的不是特别有趣，前半段还是在学校的就记得空调开的特别冷两个点失去知觉lol，平时的assignment要好好完成，认真有理有据应该就好，解答不需要写太多，因为占的分数比不算小，正常还会有一个video assignment而且记得当时第一版的topic被打回来了，还是得和他聊吧hhhhhh，期末应该是一个小组report和presentation,sem1 因为改线上变成了部分选做，但感觉也是需要选对题并付出精力的。tutorial上是lecturer手把手教，但是有的时候不太知道自己到底搞了个什么（（
reviews.translated_content: It was okay, but the lectures really weren’t particularly interesting. In the first half, when we were still on campus, I remember the air conditioning was set so cold that I lost sensation in two spots lol. You need to complete the regular assignments properly; if you’re serious and provide well-reasoned arguments, you should be fine. You don’t need to write too much in the answers. Since the weight isn’t small, there’s usually also a video assignment. I remember my first proposed topic was rejected, so you probably need to discuss it with him hhhhhh. The final assessment should be a group report and presentation. In Sem 1, because it moved online, part of it became optional, but I feel you still need to choose the right topic and put in the effort. In tutorials, the lecturer guides you step by step, but sometimes I wasn’t quite sure what I had actually done ((

reviews.content: 良心好课，推荐对数理科学感兴趣的人上。Tim相当好，很愿意讨论问题。不需要读教科书。workload有些大，但感兴趣的话也没什么。最后A+
reviews.translated_content: A genuinely worthwhile course. I recommend it to those interested in mathematical and physical sciences. Tim is excellent and very willing to discuss problems. There is no need to read the textbook. The workload is somewhat heavy, but it’s fine if you’re interested. I got an A+ in the end.

reviews.content: workload不算大，给分就一般
reviews.translated_content: The workload isn’t too heavy, but the grading is just average.
